links.title: La Receta Incierta: Cuando el Pan que Amas se Convierte en Duda
links.body:
![La Receta Incierta(1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jocksy/23wgMX4RVEtEvXBSBuTo7Kh6cBaQY6e2LUShUcbEzKzi9XnSsuKaFbTcSMvpcTNBE4Wng.png) Versión español En el silencio de la madrugada, cuando el resto del mundo aún duerme y comienzo a organizar mi logística diaria, mi mente suele perderse en la preparación de los alimentos para mi familia. Sin embargo, lo que antes era un acto mecánico de cuidado, hoy es un campo de batalla mental. Entiendo que el tiempo es un ingrediente que nadie ve, pero que lo decide todo, y hoy mi tiempo se va en descifrar cómo alimentar sanamente a mi familia en un mundo lleno de atajos artificiales. Soy panadera de oficio e ingeniera de profesión. Mi formación me empuja a buscar la causa raíz, a analizar cada variable que pueda estar alterando el entorno de mi hogar. Sé cómo los elementos se transforman bajo el calor y entiendo que la paciencia es vital. Sin embargo, en estos últimos meses, esa capacidad de análisis se ha visto puesta a prueba de una forma que nunca imaginé: no en un plano o en mi cocina, sino en la piel de mi hija. Todo comenzó con un rastro rojo cuando ella apenas tenía dos añitos. Recuerdo la angustia de ver su piel, tan tierna y frágil, marcada por los brotes en los pliegues. En aquel entonces, el camino pareció despejarse con una rapidez que hoy añoro. Un diagnóstico, un cambio en la dieta y la eliminación del Cerelac y otros alimentos, fueron suficientes para devolverme la paz. Sentí un respiro, como el que se siente al sacar un pan perfecto del horno; creí que habíamos descifrado la fórmula y que la dermatitis atópica, sería solo un recuerdo borroso de su infancia. Pero a los trece años, el fantasma regresó. Ahora, a sus quince, nos encontramos en la etapa más difícil de este largo camino. Ver cómo los brotes rojos han reclamado sus codos, sus nalgas me genera una impotencia que se me queda grabada en el pecho. No es solo el dolor físico que ella sentir es la incomodidad persistente; es el peso emocional de una adolescente que busca su lugar en el mundo mientras su propio cuerpo parece traicionarla. ![1000460471.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jocksy/23yTfFjuKrDVNnwjFgjeJsv3WZmHoY4qnGw8kF8r1gQxBnMan1Xn13DCWaHEKKUL11sRR.jpg) Lo que más me desvela es la duda. En una casa donde el pan es parte de nuestro sustento y es uno de los primeros alérgenos de una lista de alimentos que pueden hacer daño algunas personas, vivo con la pregunta constante si es el enemigo a la hora de comer. Me pregunto si este oficio que tanto amo es, en realidad, el origen del malestar de mi hija. Es una encrucijada dolorosa, sospechar que este tipo alimento es el que pueda aumentar su brote. ![1000460470.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jocksy/23y8vA662Z1QEYgLnqTU8jZiL9nwK7NGTyST3QJ5RhMNJDQnf3RRmD2VrLC61VDusifTb.jpg) No puedo seguir permitiendo que la duda sea el ingrediente principal en nuestra mesa. Por eso, finalmente, tenemos una cita con el alergólogo. ![Gemini_Generated_Image_8s7hhc8s7hhc8s7h.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jocksy/23vsHwG44S6Q2f6og8fJWgiN6oDPLVsX9eJkZ2G5jJWYGMb8M2AuhuMpRv47k2v5MZQ7Z.png) Imagen generada por IA Confío en que sea él quien logre poner fin a esta incertidumbre que me desvela. Necesito que alguien nos oriente, que me ayude a descifrar si realmente el pan que amaso con tanto amor es el que está afectando la piel de mi hija. Al final, no hay ingrediente más poderoso para sanar que la presencia constante de una madre que no se cansa de buscar el bienestar de su hija.
Inglish version(clik aqui)

![La Receta Incierta(2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jocksy/23wgMX4RVEtErhtQrz9kKjBYchDpRWmKhWr8s1ypM79xsNhHtXfF9XcneQGoGXmcuXNQw.png) In the quiet of the early morning, when the rest of the world is still asleep and I begin to organize my daily routine, my mind often wanders to the task of preparing meals for my family. However, what used to be a routine act of care has now become a mental battleground. I understand that time is an ingredient no one sees, but one that decides everything, and today my time is spent figuring out how to feed my family healthily in a world full of artificial shortcuts. I am a baker by trade and an engineer by profession. My training drives me to seek out the root cause, to analyze every variable that might be disrupting the environment of my home. I know how elements transform under heat, and I understand that patience is vital. However, in recent months, that analytical ability has been put to the test in a way I never imagined: not on a work surface or in my kitchen, but on my daughter’s skin. ![Gemini_Generated_Image_icsl4nicsl4nicsl.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jocksy/23u5vaZG2FatMa2PCZuWoZKMcnVy1ka9ctAazvWAzWz5QsG81idxuw4Fv3gxSysK2rky1.png) It all started with a red rash when she was just two years old. I remember the anguish of seeing her skin—so tender and fragile—marked by rashes in the folds. Back then, the path ahead seemed to clear up with a speed I long for today. A diagnosis, a change in diet, and cutting out Cerelac and other foods were enough to restore my peace of mind. I felt a sense of relief, like the feeling you get when you take a perfect loaf of bread out of the oven; I thought we had cracked the code and that atopic dermatitis would be nothing more than a faint memory of her childhood. But at thirteen, the specter returned. Now, at fifteen, we find ourselves at the most difficult stage of this long journey. Seeing how the red rashes have taken over her elbows and buttocks fills me with a helplessness that weighs heavily on my chest. It’s not just the physical pain she feels or the persistent discomfort; it’s the emotional burden of a teenager trying to find her place in the world while her own body seems to be betraying her What keeps me up at night is doubt. In a home where bread is part of our daily diet and eggs are the top allergens on a list of foods that can harm some people, I live with the constant question of whether they are the enemy at mealtime. I wonder if this profession that I love so much is, in fact, the source of my daughter’s discomfort. It’s a painful dilemma, suspecting that this type of food might be what triggers her flare-ups. I can’t keep letting uncertainty be the main ingredient on our table. That’s why we finally have an appointment with the allergist. I’m counting on him to put an end to this uncertainty that’s keeping me up at night. I need someone to guide us, to help me figure out if the bread I knead with so much love is really what’s affecting my daughter’s skin. In the end, there’s no more powerful ingredient for healing than the constant presence of a mother who never tires of seeking her daughter’s well-being.

links.title: Is iPhone & Samsung the New AI kings?
links.body:
![269816.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/48bWgPpEAAZ7dg1nThQAPsDT8csmrnzWwW1SsadKK4yTXgsQ5hapPSZaa3tKdC53wJ.png)




> **Look at the after effect lol**



<hr>

Recently I started talking about CHATGPT, Gemini, Grok, Claude and other AI, this is solely because of two reasons; for the sake of SEO and using my content experience to put Hive on the Google ranking. 

My second reason is also because I've been doing some heavy research on a particular venture in trying to embark on **(will share it if it becomes a success)**. I also think that people wants to read real life experience of AI usage from some specific point of view and not from the POV of paid KOLS and marketers. 

I also talkes about ONEUI 8.5 coming to Samsung in my last post, so I'll just continue in this post. 

### Why I didn't upgrade my iPhone 12

iPhones have led when it comes to usability and functionality, but android and Samsung have provided more everyday functionality. I like to say that Samsung copies iPhones in hardware and software. 

iPhone came up with the dynamic island thingy and Samsung copied it on the latest s26 series.


 The switch from titanium to aluminium was also done by the iPhone firstly and then it was copied by Samsung, then Samsung in the latest updates with the new 8.5 has again copied iPhone with the way it arranges the whole gallery thingy: you can now view people who has appeared a lot in your pictures from the gallery, I think this feature was already there from 2020 on tnt iPhone and Samsung has been copying it, but the latest update was like a fork or clone of that UI, and the good thing is that we all love it. 



This isn't to say iPhone hasn't copied Samsung, infact there was a rumor that iPhones once used Samsung lens and all that, but this has to be a rumor because iPhones still have better camera hardwares than Samsung.


 This isn't to say the Samsung is completely defeated by iPhone in this area, infact the Samsung s26 matched the 17 pro max at every level and still defeated it in many photography areas, but iPhone still continue to take it when it comes to nighttime videography. 

### The AI kings 


This isn't a phone about Samsung and iPhone, but I guess we cannot talk about AI without talking about these two powerhouses. 

I've not used AI on the latest iPhone powerhouse *(from the 15 to 17)* my last flagship iPhone was the iPhone 12 and I never even thought of buying another iPhone, this was simply because the iPhone was seriously limiting.


 I work a lot online and must times the internet is better accessed with an Android and that's why I currently use a Samsung. In 2019 Samsung was the best android phone out there, but today, not anymore. 

### Value for money 


Devices like Oppo, Xiaomi and many others packs massive hardware for even cheaper prices and in 2026 the Vivo, especially with it's flagship device, the Vivo x300 ultra. Infact this device is 30 to 40% cheaper than the s26 ultra, and over 50% cheaper than the iPhone 17 pro max, but rivals them in quality and even does better than them in so many areas. 


Samsung is solid, no doubt but we also have to remember that Nokia was king back in the day and today the brand is dead. 


### Value for long-term 


Samsung understands the importance of remaining relevant and that's why they've packed a lot of AI gestures, and these updates are what makes it worth the money. 

I think this device might be my last Samsung though, because obviously I want to also buy stuffs for cheaper and get the best value for money.


 I haven't used the latest iPhones so I don't know about their AI capabilities, but I'm sure Samsung must've copied it too. 


### Check these out. 

This doesn't mean I'm not blown away by the value Samsung offers, infact these features are actually great and I don't know if Vivo will continue offering this for long-term. 

Check out a few pictures, I've remade using their AI features, infact the S25 Fe can even shoot in the HDR10+ in the main lens and these are the type of the updates that makes the S25 series true flagship levels. What do you think of these pictures I remade?

links.title: I got some new Epic cards in Splinterlands, opening 20 Fundation Packs
links.body:
>

Hello friends, I'm back again to share with you the opening of 20 Foundation card packs. Most of them, as you know, are duplicates and are usually common cards, but now and then I get special cards like the ones I'm sharing here.

> Hola amigos, me tienen de nuevo por aquí para compartir con ustedes la apertura de 20 paquetes de cartas de Fundación. La mayoría de ellas, como bien saben, me salen repetidas y suelen ser cartas comunes, pero de vez en cuando salen cartas especiales como estas que les comparto aquí.


<center>

![IMG-20230909-WA0010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/culebro/EonosK9htPi7qwPGjS5zrY6stuEZAAChBap5CJDbgn1v4ThLrvoLEonRCoyGPMkoVTr.jpg)

</center>

|![Sin título2.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmS9B2DtoUQQQEPiX3sgoEJ9dehQwfFV9yC6NApjY1pBsw/Sin%20t%C3%ADtulo2.png)|![7.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/culebro/23tbK2FBoRXCzkFUE6JicnoNEtvEZJe95wQsqfgf99VDeQYPwjJDaK5WxP5ktpaVyh5Sh.png)|
|-|-|

<div class=\

>

But before I show you the cards I liked the most, let me show you how my progress in the game is going. As you can see, I'm making good progress in the Gold I Frontier rank, and I'm also in Bronze III and Silver II in the Modern and Wild modes, respectively.

> Pero antes de mostrarles las cartas que más me gustaron, les muestro cómo va mi progreso en el juego. Aquí pueden ver que voy a buen ritmo en el rango de Oro I de Frontera y además, estoy en Bronce III y Silver II en las modalidades Moderno y Salvaje respectivamente.

<center>

![IMG-20230909-WA0010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/culebro/EonosK9htPi7qwPGjS5zrY6stuEZAAChBap5CJDbgn1v4ThLrvoLEonRCoyGPMkoVTr.jpg)

<div class=\

>

Echelon was one of the first epic cards I got, and the best part is that I didn't get just one of these, but three. So I'm going to take advantage of that and level it up immediately, since at its base level, it's not that powerful.

> Echelon fue una de las primeras cartas épicas que me salieron y lo mejor de todo es que no me dieron una sola de este tipo, sino 3. Así que voy a aprovechar de subirla de nivel inmediatamente, ya que, teniéndola en su nivel básico, no es tan poderosa.

<center>

![IMG-20230909-WA0010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/culebro/EonosK9htPi7qwPGjS5zrY6stuEZAAChBap5CJDbgn1v4ThLrvoLEonRCoyGPMkoVTr.jpg)

</center>

<center>![Saltwater Mage.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/culebro/244xPKVr1JgvdaU1L3XxRMiuC3wfrSD3YL7cwQVmyfmPXA9ZnRURzoejzhxA5SRdDATZZ.jpg)</center>

<div class=\

>

Another surprise was receiving the Saltwater Mage water card. A Tideborn that deals significant damage and has enough health to be useful in some battles. She's one of the best cards I use and has saved me thanks to her attack power and the amount of health she provides.

> Otra de mis sorpresas fue recibir la carta de agua de la maga Saltwater Mage. Una Tideborn que hace bastante daño y tiene bastante vida para usarla en algunas batallas. Ella es una de las mejores cartas que uso y que me ha salvado gracias a su poder de ataque y a la cantidad de vida que trae.

<center>

![IMG-20230909-WA0010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/culebro/EonosK9htPi7qwPGjS5zrY6stuEZAAChBap5CJDbgn1v4ThLrvoLEonRCoyGPMkoVTr.jpg)

<div class=\

>

Another card I wasn't expecting to get is the Sorrow Harvester elf mage. She's usually my favorite elf when I use Death Summoner. She's a must-have in my games, and of course, thanks to her, I've gotten to where I am today. For now, I'm continuing to collect her in this version so I can level her up when the time is right.

> Otra carta que no me esperaba que me saliera es la de la elfa maga Sorrow Harvester. Una elfa que suele ser mi favorita cuando uso al invocador de la muerte. Ella no puede faltar en mis partidas y por supuesto que gracias a esta elfa he logrado llegar a donde estoy. I get them quite often, and the one I have the most of so far is the human mage called Water-Logged Wizard. I have so many of them that I can finally level them up and make them more powerful. And yes, it's one of the water cards I use a lot, which is why it's my favorite. > Como les mencioné en mi post anterior, las cartas raras son las que se me hacen más fáciles de obtener, además de las comunes. links.title: The Bastille Market: Part One
links.body:
<center>
![IMG_8700.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23wCE5wp691JxqZHwWDRBx6xcHLb823fwdeUakXY14vR5LjhQpWHBpcwAvqJn9HJJoAca.jpeg)
</center>



<center>![paw divider transparent.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/48KZyd16wthLszaeq8fk7G1E4ouNCTPmsydXQQeMc23jdxuFbbxjwqu3LKfLB9x6LQ.png)</center>

----------

On my recent ramble through Switzerland and France, I had the opportunity to do so many cool things! One of my absolute favorites was our visit to the Bastille Market right in the middle of Paris.

I had the pleasure of meeting my nephew's boss, a wonder of a woman who is a nuclear scientist and chairperson of nuclear criticality things. I had an absolute blast with her, talking reactors, tomato varieties, and about all things food. She was the one who wanted to show us the Market, as she visits it every time she is in Paris, which, due to her occupation is a quite frequent happening.


![IMG_8682.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23yTeoFYp2eJNwcovha7AuhHpPd1aSjsVwr776XxohJj3Amqju9uFJreCPYa2cFusDniU.jpeg)


As we were staying over in the lovely part of Paris that is known as Boulougne-Billancourt, the nephew and I hopped on the metro and headed toward the center of the city where the Bastille is located. The Marche Bastille is an artisan market containing food and flowers of such high quality that it almost overwhelmed my little homesteading hobbit brain.


But I get ahead of myself. Before we even got there, we had to meet our cohort, and even beyond that, an entire Paris marathon and blocked off streets greeted our eyes as we emerged from the Metro tunnel. 

After a bit of participant dodging and running back under the streets through the underground tunnels, we finally arrived at the center square in front of the Bastille statue that had culinary and agriculture sights galore.


![IMG_8699.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23uFU9fFAAxoaoLcRnrtQLFNJ1ALLiCc72VeLwftmuLmVSAVRjvqxDXPk23tGXK4uWVzp.jpeg)
-----------------------



![IMG_8696.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/Eoc7wrbzjuN1YyeUFGh98TGbp4Xjz65QFqWysX4bz4uG28dVkXw3zD18v6qWq1ZgCcg.jpeg)

--------------------


![IMG_8691.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/EonkaCZgsLznGUDWHt5DWdHJ3SzLRKEwdfLGCQmv5M8sc23qtXZ48zEkwgsb5vKcq8k.jpeg)




The first thing I saw was endless beautiful flowers! The diversity of the blooms warmed my heart. Here in the states you see a lot of the same, standard varieties most of the time. Not at the Marche Bastille. My face broke into the most adoring smile.


![IMG_8687.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/Ep3foLQryvt4urqdM2eXaoP9mZRB8YJwSp2ESYS5D7KWXxvySJLK8QxDyLAdhSmzX49.jpeg)

-------------------------


![IMG_8688.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23w2iyUiAix2gRL1PHUfRCXa7yNUvcytz7PFUXqk8rgZ3D3rSLC4Dq5ZKQdnXSKf4et6q.jpeg)

--------------------


![IMG_8689.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23wMcoHjKXAMtii2qAAnUdBM2FZzL3PG7u22myzWEVZ8h3bJhkkj874E57BqVmsLiDMpW.jpeg)



My eyes lit upon vibrant ranunculus, glistening fish, and proud asparagus spears. The lover and producer of food in me beamed as I oohed and awed over all the glorious comestible offerings!


![IMG_8685.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23wMaCKbYBV9NknqgkLgphdUEcsu9BNYqddzqCVDtSmPpjxnB14CWYVXzxdBq4PcbzAYp.jpeg)


The produce absolutely captivated me, because not a watery nitrogen plumped, glyphosate abomination was in sight. Each bit of produce that my eyes lit upon was alive and blessedly diverse. I just couldn't believe my eyes and my joy often reflected back from the vendors themselves at me as I just couldn't keep such joy from spreading. I so admired everything about their lovingly, good stewardly raised wares. 


![IMG_8686.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23wCE9LWFkv7zdS6WaPJp9PgMXBw6U8jq4wV8CwGBgbgJwkjTv9FRYHhNn91F38HTojWn.jpeg)


In my next post I will focus more on the food, this post was for the flowers. Lisianthus, azaleas, lilacs, statice, roses of every hue, peonies in bud, every kind of flower conceviable lined vendor stall after vendor stall. I have never seen anything like the flowers of Paris, it was like the love of the floral bloom permeates the make up of the city.

And I sure wasn't complaining. 


My happy nose will recount my delighted taste buds and ocular region when it comes to food in the next post. The market's comestible offering absolutely didn't disappoint, in fact, our lunch was a lifelong dream of mine, ever since high school French class to be exact.

Til next time!





--------------




<center>![paw divider transparent.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/48KZyd16wthLszaeq8fk7G1E4ouNCTPmsydXQQeMc23jdxuFbbxjwqu3LKfLB9x6LQ.png)</center>

------------------
<center>*And as most of the time, all of the images in this post were taken on the author's envious it doesn't come in the scent of the Bastille Market  iPhone.*</center>

-----------

links.title: My Onboarding Strategy to Catch New Fishes
links.body:
Remembering the first day I learnt about Hive and how my onboarder @vickoly explained things to me in a way that attracted me fully to the blockchain that I opted in immediately and signed up, makes me think thoroughly about the prompt for the week on how I would convince someone to be onboard on Hive. 

![1000687854.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/23tbK28QByCMm33ydYHvSzYmcoxceXRMTzQvqdTo1ypm6Yiw4Uz8FCVRE6Axuo8SzZJXN.jpg)

It is so clear and vivid that I can't step in my onboarder's shoes of the dialogues and pattern he used because the situation back then is way very different from now. Back then I was seriously in need of a steady and stable source of income, so much that I had opted in for a writing platform where by i could only cash out when I have a hundred followers and a particular range of blog articles on my dashboard for me to be able to monetize my account. 

He saw my post on that, asked me a few questions and then introduced Hive to me as a platform where I can write and get money almost immediately, showcase my talent as a drawing artist, meet people as a form of networking and the likes. Of course it was a very far better offer than my present conditioner platform so I opted to be onboard on Hive immediately.

Right now, we all know the price of Hive and obviously the monetization can't be a forerunner of my dialogue to a new user I want to onboard which should have been the point of enticement since everyone is on the lookout for ways to survive the bad economy now. 
However, here is still how I would convince him or her to come on Hive:

Aside the whole monetization part, there's this part of Hive that allows you to express yourself the way you deem fit with no concern or discrimination about how good you are as a writer, and there's no one to hunt you for your story just because you shared it. 

The fact that Hive is also a decentralized platform whereby you're involved in almost everything and nothing is hidden with the process makes it a trusted platform to be in. 

![1000687860.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/afrikens/23wWki4ZC6v93GsMqBVukuZk3gsoptxPh34QVhsJ3WK46KFuUj9WSccBwUSDd4DwZfxwH.jpg)

It gives room to show your creativity as there is almost a community for every craft you feel you are into. You get appreciated for what you do, reach more audience and increase your network of those who knows about what you do and at the end of the day, you still get paid for just showcasing what you do and what you write as a whole.
Though hive price may not currently be catchy but just like every other coin in the crypto space that pumps or dips, hive also have its own dipping period which we are currently in.

The sweet part is that once the price pumps and price rises, every hive rewards you've acquired before then are affected with the increase and you can always harvest your rewards just like the crypto traders in crypto world and you can as well delegate your rewards or stake it as a means of investment.

Hive has a lot of benefits depending on what part you want to hold unto andi know this is more than enough to convince someone on coming on Hive.

I'll be dropping my 🖊️ here on the Indiaunited community prompt.

Thanks for reading through 🤗

links.title: The Engine Turns, But It’s Hardly a Car
links.body:
I can sincerely say, with no risk of exaggeration, that working on Hive projects over the past year has been a crazy journey. Feeling uncomfortable, sometimes unqualified, has been the common theme throughout — and yet, the work is <u>never truly done</u>.

![b7485e5f-ee47-47da-a5b1-2a795535f0ca.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQWkyXo4Th3kfxoiAo355mTLpvvriah1FiJarPu4Zwekc/b7485e5f-ee47-47da-a5b1-2a795535f0ca.png)

For a while now, ideas have been put forward on how to improve uploads on 3Speak and speed things up. It’s no secret that the process is slow, and although we’ve tweaked and *tweaked* the levers, it’s still not quite there. The embed system — the video service used for Shorts — relies on a different upload approach that, while making the codebase more maintainable, slowed the process down even further.

The obvious solution for those familiar with this space is to remove IPFS from the beginning of the chain. Instead, you use the now-standard S3 technology everyone and their mother relies on, and leave IPFS at the end for long-term storage, so to speak.

It’s a good idea. A very good one, actually.

But it would also require a refactor of the sort that can age a man five years in a matter of weeks. I’m not entirely convinced I have the stamina for that battle at the moment.

With all that said, my experience with S3 buckets wasn’t exactly extensive to begin with. I’ve used them — specifically Wasabi — but I never really looked under the hood, so to speak.

Today marks a bit of a turning point, because I’ve been playing around with MinIO. I successfully deployed an instance and, what do you know, the darn thing works well.

I wish I could say the foundational rock for the future was laid today, but I’m now — and I mean this literally — beginning to understand just how much more needs to be built for a transition like this.

The best analogy I can give is this:

I got the engine to turn on. It works well. It takes fuel and converts it into torque.

But it’s hardly a car.

Multi-tenancy, statistics, load distribution, backups, scaling — none of those challenges are remotely solved yet.

It’s easy to look at the mountain of work ahead, the sheer size of the challenge, and say: **“Not me.”**

But I’m not insane because I want to be. It’s a feature and a bug all rolled into one.

So I’m going to start building something around MinIO.

Do we need it? Maybe not. Maybe yes. But it also can’t hurt, and I’m certain I’ll learn a ton along the way.

Madness and happiness for dinner…

*What can I say?*

MenO

links.title: Un paso más a la meta: Revelación de Chemises de 5to año / One step closer to The goal: 12th Grade Shirt Reveal
links.body: > Saludos, comunidad, especialmente a **#Gems** Hoy quiero compartir con ustedes un momento que llena el corazón de cualquier padre: la revelación de las camisas de la promoción de 5to año de la **U.E.N. Paula Correa de Zamora**, aquí en mi querido pueblo de **Villa de Cura**. Greetings, community, especially **#Gems**! Today I want to share with you a moment that fills any parent's heart: the shirt reveal for the graduating class of **U.E.N. Paula Correa de Zamora**, here in my beloved town of **Villa de Cura**. *** | *Orgullo de padre / Father's pride* | *Celebración en Villa de Cura / Celebration in Villa de Cura* | *** El pasado lunes 11, el salón parroquial se llenó de alegría y nostalgia. Ver a los estudiantes de las secciones A, B y C reunidos marcó el inicio de la despedida de una etapa maravillosa. El evento fue sumamente emotivo; cada madre tuvo el honor de entregar la camisa a su hijo o representado, un gesto que simboliza todo el apoyo y el esfuerzo que hemos hecho como familia para llegar hasta aquí. Last Monday the 11th, the parish hall was filled with joy and nostalgia. Seeing the students from sections A, B, and C gathered marked the beginning of the end of a wonderful stage. The event was deeply emotional; each mother had the honor of handing the shirt to her child, a gesture that symbolizes all the support and effort we have made as a family to get to this point. La celebración estuvo a la altura del esfuerzo de nuestros muchachos. Contamos con la música de los **Mariachis Costeños**, quienes pusieron a todos a cantar, y la gran sorpresa de la tarde: un robot animador que llenó de energía el salón mientras ayudaba en la entrega de las camisas. Ver sus caras de felicidad al lucir sus nuevas prendas fue el mejor regalo para nosotros. The celebration lived up to our kids' hard work. We had music from the **Mariachis Costeños**, who got everyone singing, and the big surprise of the afternoon: an entertainer robot that filled the hall with energy while helping deliver the shirts. Seeing their happy faces wearing their new shirts was the best gift for us. Como padre, me invade un sentimiento de orgullo profundo. Sabemos que el bachillerato es un proceso largo, lleno de retos y aprendizajes, tanto para los estudiantes como para nosotros los padres. Ver a mi hija y a sus compañeros triunfar me confirma que con perseverancia y esfuerzo los sueños se cumplen. Ahora se preparan para la universidad, una nueva meta donde estoy seguro de que seguirán brillando. As a father, I am overcome with a feeling of deep pride. We know that high school is a long process, full of challenges and learning, both for the students and for us parents. Seeing my daughter and her classmates succeed confirms to me that with perseverance and effort, dreams do come true. Now they are preparing for university, a new goal where I am sure they will continue to shine. Felicidades a todos los nuevos bachilleres de la Paula Correa Congratulations to all the new graduates of Correa --- ▶️ [3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=solorzanot/8d9818b5)

links.title: [ESP-ENG] Celebrando el día de Las Madres con mis compañeras de trabajo 🌹/Celebrating Mother's Day with Coworkers 🌹
links.body:
>
 
 Buenos dias amigos de hive, un gusto saludarles y compartir nuevamente por acá con ustedes,  hoy les quiero mostrar como estuvo mi día de compartir con compañeras de trabajo, un dia de esparcimiento y sana diversión.

> Good evening, Hive friends! It's a pleasure to greet you and share with you again. Today I want to show you how my day went with my coworkers—a day of relaxation and wholesome fun.



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZhW91PWJozDn7UaxAhRtLzdgHdpHxh2gGNN7BFWG9zGo/1778682583608.jpg)


Y este día 08 de mayo nos fuimos de paseo, salimos de la oficina a una posada ubicada en el municipio Antolín del campo, conocida como Rancho los Niños, el autobús salió de nuestro lugar de trabajo a las 10:00 am, fuimos en total un grupo de 40 mujeres y madres hermosas para disfrutar de un día diferente.

> On May 8th, we went on an outing. We left the office for an inn located in the municipality of Antolín del Campo, known as Rancho Los Niños. The bus left our workplace at 10:00 am. In total, there were 40 beautiful women and mothers who went to enjoy a different kind of day.

Al llegar a la posada había otro grupo de personas Celebrando un cumpleaños de una niña, Pero fue un grupo que estaba lejos de nuestra zona, a nosotros nos tocó la churruata, dónde no había sol 😎 y estaba muy cerca de la piscina, un excelente lugar.
> When we arrived at the inn, there was another group of people celebrating a little girl's birthday. They were farther away from our area, so we ended up in the \

(a covered area), where there was no sun 😎 and it was very close to the pool—an excellent spot. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR528Dr7kXZFBAKkycTDeXEgCcvkqwPbecuxmzyTZ2NEg/1778682619121.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPS7LyJb5uUWqtUXd5eDcDgptxaGkdV44ywU84LFfQgew/1778682619183.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPhgxsfeJwguWFyB9GXPpNbd2C1Kx5E1P2rAks4XFwcNH/1778682619423.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmackLcUXmvDYzfKTDkp3EMjxqGvg1ZKcQRc22XE4sDUVR/1778682619789.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNUck7EqqyDz73CeNukWKYD9THqVYP4s9BoUj1o5P2mdi/1778682619913.jpg) Allí comenzamos nuestro compartir, dónde fue amenizado por 2 compañeros que pertenecen al grupo musical del trabajo, así que hubo también música en vivo, estuvo bastante movida la tarde, llegó la hora de comer un buen almuerzo y luego comenzó la rifa, dónde todas ganamos un lindo detalle, los premios fueron: cafeteras, planchas, tostadora, secadores de cabellos, tazas, entradas al cine y pare usted de contar, hubo toda clase de premios, todas salimos contentas y esperando que se repita siempre. > There we began our get-together, enlivened by two colleagues from the work band, so there was live music too. The afternoon was quite lively. Then it was time for a delicious lunch, and afterwards the raffle began. We all won a lovely little gift. The prizes included coffee makers, irons, toasters, hair dryers, mugs, movie tickets, and much more. There were all sorts of prizes, and we all left happy and hoping it will happen again. El autobús para el regreso llegó casi a las 6:00 pm, ahí si se nos hizo un poco tarde, ya estamos un poco agotadas de todo el día, y la mayoría tenían que tomar otro bus pata ir de regreso a sus casa, gracias a Dios todo salio bien y llegamos temprano a nuestras casas, adi que este día fue un gran agasajo a las madres de nuestra institución y muy agradecida por ello, saludos y bendiciones a todas las madres en este dia, todo estubo hermoso, agradecimientos a todos a ños que hicieron posible este paseo, gracias. > The bus for the return trip arrived around 6:00 pm. We were a little late, as we were quite tired from the day, and most of us had to catch another bus home. Thankfully, everything went well, and we arrived home early. So, this day was a wonderful treat for the mothers of our institution, and I am very grateful for it. Greetings and blessings to all the mothers on this day. Everything was beautiful. Thank you to everyone who made this outing possible. Muchas felicidades Madres hermosas! 🌹 > Happy Mother's Day to all the beautiful mothers! 🌹 Hasta aquí mi publicacion de este día, espero les haya gustado, muchas gracias a todos por el apoyo brindado. Saludos 🌹 > That's it for my publication today, I hope you liked it, thank you all very much for the support provided. Greetings 🌹 #### Todas las imágenes son de mi autoria por @mariarodriguez, tomadas especialmente para esta publicación. > #### All images are my own by @mariarodriguez, taken especially for this publication.

links.body: En tus palabras se resume una problemática de las que pocos son conscientes y que ha ido mermando la calidad de los productos, no solo los que quedan para el consumo local, sino en líneas generales.\nDesde la aparición pública de los documentos y pruebas de los alimentos transgénicos y toda la maquinaria de modificación genética que se ha activado para \

la calidad de las semillas, y evitar las plagas, eliminando el ciclo normal de la naturaleza, todo el equilibrio del proceso se ha visto modificado, quizás más para mal que para bien.\nDe alguna manera, yo siento que vamos cavando nuestras propias tumbas, entre esas mejoras para la industria y la producción, que nos han llevado a desarrollar alergias y resistencias a ciertos alimentos, por lo que la ventaja que tiene una mandarina sin semillas, por ejemplo, va más para la comodidad de su consumo, que para los nutrientes que otrora aportaba a quienes lo comían.

description.title: When all my Classes got cancelled in one day
description.body: > Good day everyone and welcome to another edition of my Daily Diary Game entry. Receive warm greetings from my part of the world. I hope you are all doing well today.

> https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmWkzN9s3zdji8Qv6Wi3Wn6ju2ABi1DchTEodG6EfL5GpV/IMG_20260512_073402_741~2.jpg
My morning look

My day started early at about 6:00am when my alarm rang. I managed to turn it off and stayed on my bed for a while since I was to have class by 10:00am. I began my morning with prayers (morning rosary), and after that I spent some time watching a movie titled Mission Impossible, which I had started the previous night but couldn’t finish due to sleep.

> https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmavqb4NfKxMMN8HRhB5pgCjnn7wk2SKWTvQDZKshg9aEu/IMG_20260512_113842_973~2.jpg
On my way to the lecture hall

At about 8:50am, I began preparing for my 10:00am lecture. I took my bath, brushed my teeth, and got dressed. I didn’t feel like eating in the morning, so I only drank water before heading out. On my way to the lecture hall, I met some of my coursemates and we all walked together to the hall.

> https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmc2tkUt5KQwquC8DXdhfHt8HSMf5d3MqT6tCvrBh3VHJF/IMG_20260512_113907_725~2.jpg
Heading back after cancelled class

When we arrived, we waited for the lecturer to come in as it was already past 10:15am. While waiting, we engaged in friendly discussions and shared memories from our 100 level days. However, we later received a message through the departmental representative that the lecture had been cancelled.

> https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmc1YjRpXiGyKSVxWZKrtHhx91XF1VnFFxDL1dCyJTc17k/IMG_20260512_125952_590~3.jpg
At the next class venue

Since I was charging my phone, I stayed back until around 11:50am before heading to my next class scheduled for 12:00 noon. We gathered at the department where our practical class was expected to hold, but after waiting for almost 40 minutes, the class was postponed again by the departmental representative. I still waited briefly, hoping it would hold, but unfortunately, the lecturer did not show up.

> https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmWLvXCLdLfwThWLaRPbhzQ7CW5CAokcYpMTyzQ86KzXfo/IMG_20260512_170341_794.jpg
Afternoon moment

After all the delays and cancellations, I had no lectures for the day. I returned to my department to charge my phone since I would be going to church by 6:00pm for our FED WEEK activities. Later, the weather changed and strong winds started blowing. I quickly rushed back to my lodge because my window was open, and I didn’t want rain to damage anything inside. Fortunately, it didn’t rain. While resting, I parboiled some rice since I had stew available. I ate when it was ready, took my evening bath at about 6:02pm, and then headed to church to participate in the FED WEEK program. That marks the end of my day.

Most of the rulers was fail to establishe justice. We know about Genghis Khan and his grandson Halaku Khan. Both are known as dangerous and dreadful leaders of Mongolia. The great wall of China, The Taj Mahal of Agra, the pyramids of Mishor are some of the greatest landmark of ancient era. Still now the making  of Pyramids is mysterious to the scientists. If I born in that time I will see the making of Pyramids and it would be hilarious. I have a dream to visit all over the world and enjoy the landmarks of ancient architect. Though it is hard to fulfil my dream but I will try to travel many countries as I can. I got two different types of era. One is 90's and other in 2020's. The 90's memory is so cool and sweet. On that time most of the families were joint families. We share our emotions with our neighbours and relatives. We share our foods with them. We played in the afternoon.  Went to school by group. In winter our mother's made various types if cakes from rice, milk and molasses.

Now a child of 1 year to an age of 80 years almost 99 percent people are affected by internet through smartphones. Children now passing yheir times with mobile and for this reason their communication skill is hampered and they can't soeak orooerly. They learn speaking after a long time. The oarents are also passing their leisure with mobile insted of passing time with family members. The people are becoming intolerat because the play video games with full of destruction theme. Thevrich send their old oarents to the old home where a poor villegers never do this even if he have to beg. 

Total ethical system collapsed but some sky scrappers built like Burj Khalifa. Some unwanted wars are still continuing.  It is high time we should change our characteristics. Majore  countries should  come forward to stop wars and killing innocent children ad ladies. We should change your habit to use internet. we have to make our world as a flower garden to the next generation. We have to free them like a bird from the invisible cage of smartphone and internet.

links.title: Television Review: Oathkeeper (Game of Thrones, S4X04, 2014)
links.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/2h2dtlA6U0Imc3VSq5YlpAif9Qz.jpg)


**Oathkeeper (S4x04)**

Airdate: 27 April 2014

Written by: Bryan Cogman
Directed by: Michelle MacLaren

Running Time: 55 minutes



The adaptation of George R.R. Martin’s sprawling literary saga *A Song of Ice and Fire* into the television phenomenon *Game of Thrones* was, from its inception, an exercise in necessary compromise. The book and the television series are two distinct media, with differing narrative economies and audience expectations. It was therefore impossible for the show to be a completely faithful transliteration of Martin’s dense, multi-perspective novels. Creative shortcuts were inevitable: multiple minor characters were fused into single composite figures, and elaborately explained political machinations were streamlined for the screen. However, by its fourth season, the series under showrunners David Benioff and D.B. Weiss began to move beyond mere condensation. They started to actively insert characters, plotlines, and entire scenes that had no direct precedent in the source material. This marked a subtle but significant shift from adaptation to augmentation, a process whereby what readers had consumed in the books and what viewers witnessed on screen began to diverge into two distinct narrative entities. One of the earlier and most telling examples of this new creative direction is Season 4’s fourth episode, pointedly titled *Oathkeeper*. Whilst functioning as a competent piece of episodic television, it serves as a crucial case study in the show’s growing willingness to fill narrative silences with invention, for better and for worse, and highlights the first faint tremors of the creative exhaustion that would later become more pronounced.

The episode continues to meticulously chart the ripple effects of King Joffrey’s murder at the Purple Wedding. A central mystery—the identity of the perpetrators—is neatly resolved through two confessional scenes. Aboard ship, the duplicitous Petyr Baelish finally reveals to Sansa Stark his role in the regicide. He explains that, despite a fruitful alliance with the Lannisters, Joffrey had become too volatile an obstacle for his “new friends.” Those friends are confirmed in King’s Landing, where the formidable Lady Olenna Tyrell calmly informs her granddaughter Margaery that she used poison concealed in Sansa’s necklace. This dual revelation is handled with typical series efficiency, though it arguably robs the event of some of the lingering ambiguity Martin favoured. With Joffrey removed, the narrative pivots to the political manoeuvring of the newly widowed Margaery. Her attempt to seduce the boy-king Tommen in his chambers shows cynical calculation. Finding him too young for overt sexual manipulation, she swiftly recalibrates, appealing instead to his sheltered sense of adventure and his poignant desire for genuine friendship. This scene is a highlight, showcasing Natalie Dormer’s ability to convey razor-sharp intelligence beneath a veneer of gentle concern, and it establishes the dynamic that will define her next political marriage.

Simultaneously, the episode delves into the moral rehabilitation of Jaime Lannister. Forced to practice one-handed swordsmanship with the mercenary Bronn, Jaime is shamed into visiting his imprisoned brother, Tyrion. Their conversation reveals Cersei’s vindictive demand for Sansa’s head and her offer of a knighthood for her return. This sparks in Jaime a memory of the oath he swore to the late Lady Catelyn Stark—to return her daughters safely. Hamstrung by his new duties as Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, he cannot fulfil this vow personally. In a moment of resonant symbolism, he performs the next best thing: he entrusts his magnificent new Valyrian steel sword, forged from Ice and named “Oathkeeper,” to Brienne of Tarth. Assigning Podrick Payne as her squire, he sends this most honourable of knights on a quest to find Sansa and protect her. This sequence is emotionally potent, cementing Jaime’s complex redemption arc and providing Brienne with a purpose worthy of her formidable virtue. It is a clear example of the show successfully streamlining book material (where the sword’s bestowal and mission have different nuances) into a powerful, character-driven beat.

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys Targaryen continues her crusade in Slaver’s Bay. The conquest of Meereen is achieved by subterfuge and insurrection. Grey Worm infiltrates the city via its sewers, distributing arms to the slave population with the instruction to rise up. Once they do, Daenerys makes her triumphant entry. Here, the episode presents a pivotal moral test for the Mother of Dragons. Advised by Ser Barristan Selmy to be merciful, she instead chooses a brutal, eye-for-an-eye justice. Commanding that 163 Meereenese masters be crucified in retribution for the 163 slave children crucified on the road to the city, she delivers a stark lesson in the perils of absolutist rule. This moment is chillingly effective, complicating her liberator image with a thirst for vengeful violence.

However, this plot strand also contains one of the episode’s most jarring creative missteps. The graffiti daubed on the city walls, reading “Kill the Masters,” is rendered in modern English. This is a baffling failure of world-building. The characters speak in High Valyrian, a constructed language audiences hear consistently, yet they are apparently literate in contemporary English. David J. Peterson, the linguist who crafted Valyrian and Dothraki, later revealed he was prepared to develop a functional writing system, but producers demurred, believing it would alienate viewers. This decision, aimed at simplicity, severely undermines immersion. For an audience by now deeply accustomed to the textured detail and linguistic depth of Martin’s world, it feels like a lazy concession, a betrayal of the show’s own established standards for verisimilitude.

North of the Wall, the narrative introduces a subplot almost entirely of the show’s own devising, which exemplifies the new strategy of narrative invention. Jon Snow, preparing an expedition to deal with the mutineers at Craster’s Keep, notices a new recruit: the formidable Locke. Posing as a former gamekeeper who took the black to avoid losing a hand, Locke’s true mission—to find and capture Bran Stark—is known only to the viewer. This insertion of a character from the Northern storyline (where in the books he serves Roose Bolton) into the Watch is a clever, if contrived, way to raise stakes. The expedition itself heads to Craster’s, now a hellish stronghold held by the vicious Karl Tanner and his fellow mutineers. This segment exists to fill a blank space in the books. In Martin’s narrative, the fate of Craster’s Keep after the mutiny is left obscure, and Bran Stark never ventures there. The show uses it to create a tense, if gratuitous, set-piece. The mutineers are depicted engaging in rape and sexual abuse of Craster’s widowed daughters, a scene reportedly filmed with disturbing graphicness using pornographic film actresses before being toned down for broadcast. Whilst intending to portray the depths of their depravity, it risks feeling exploitative. Karl Tanner is given lengthy, self-mythologising monologues about his past as a “fookin’ legend” in Gin Alley, dialogue that feels less like natural characterisation and more like exposition hastily plastered over a thin plot contrivance. It is here that one first detects a whiff of creative exhaustion—a willingness to insert violent, sensational filler to maintain momentum and tie up loose ends, rather than trust the slower-burning political and mythological threads.

The episode’s final sequence, however, is great and that justifies much. In the frozen wastes of the Far North, a chilling figure—a White Walker later codified as the Night King, portrayed with eerie stillness by Richard Brake—receives a male infant from Craster’s sacrifices. In a silent, glacial ritual, he touches the baby’s cheek, its eyes turning a piercing, icy blue. This single, wordless image is profoundly impactful. It answers a haunting question about the Others’ origins and methods, transforming them from mere supernatural threats into a species with a perverse biology and culture. It is a stark, brilliant reminder that whilst the southern kingdoms squabble over crowns, the true existential menace is methodically building its army in the eternal winter.

Written by Bryan Cogman and deftly directed by Michelle MacLaren, *Oathkeeper* is, on a technical level, a generally solid piece of television. MacLaren’s direction is assured, particularly in the intimate scenes of political intrigue in King’s Landing and the haunting finale. Yet, tonally, it is an uneven and largely transitional episode. Its primary function is to connect dots and prepare the ground for future confrontations. For every successful element—the poignant conclusion of Jaime’s gift, Margaery’s cunning, the terrifying implication of the final scene—there is a corresponding misstep or compromise. The clumsy English graffiti breaks the spell of Essos, and the Craster’s Keep subplot, whilst tense, feels like a manufactured conflict designed to give Bran and Jon something to do in the absence of book material. It represents the show’s early foray into significant narrative invention, revealing both its strengths (generating iconic mythological moments) and its emerging weaknesses (a tendency towards contrived, violence-driven filler). As such, *Oathkeeper* is a fascinating inflection point: the moment where *Game of Thrones* began to consciously walk its own path, for better or worse, and where the first cracks in its meticulously built world began to subtly show.


RATING: 6/10 (++)

links.title: Chapter 1: The Move
links.body:
/>

The black taxi pulled up with a soft screech in front of number 42 **Prinsengracht**. The Amsterdam sky, tinged a leaden gray, seemed to weigh down on the pointed rooftops of the houses lining the canal. For **Tom**, that dark brick building with disproportionately large windows was the trophy of his recent promotion; for **Ana**, it was a structure that seemed to watch them with an uncomfortable fixity.  
\
Tom said, stepping out of the car with a smile that didn't quite reach his eyes, hiding the exhaustion of months of paperwork. \

\n**Ana** climbed out of the vehicle, tightly holding little **Laura’s** hand. The girl, barely six years old, wasn't looking at the facade. Her eyes were fixed on the dark water of the canal, where the reflections of the houses seemed to distort like elongated faces beneath the surface.  \n\
Laura whispered, huddling into her mother’s wool coat.  \n\

Ana replied, though she felt a shiver herself that had nothing to do with the weather.

### Entering the New Home

As they opened the heavy oak door, they were greeted by the smell of old wood, candle wax, and something else—something metallic and rancid. The house was narrow, and the steep, winding spiral staircases disappeared into the gloom of the upper floors.  
Shortly after, **Elli** arrived, the local nanny they had hired to help with the transition. She was a young woman with a lively gaze, but as she crossed the threshold, her step faltered.  
\
Elli commented, though her voice sounded hollow. \

### Shadows Among Boxes

As the movers brought up the boxes, the family began to explore. Tom moved with energy, measuring spaces and planning where to set up his study. Ana, on the other hand, felt a tightening in her chest every time she entered a new room.

> \

Ana thought as she walked down the second-floor hallway.

In the room intended for Laura, the girl stopped dead in her tracks in front of a small service door at the base of the wall.  
\
the little girl asked, pointing to the decaying wood.  \nElli crouched down, forcing a smile.  \n\

However, when the nanny stood up, she noticed something that turned her blood cold: in the fine dust covering the floor near the small door, there weren't just the prints of Laura’s shoes, but also small marks, like long, thin fingers coming from inside the wall.  
As evening fell, while Tom and Ana toasted with wine among stacked boxes, the sunlight suddenly vanished behind the buildings. At that moment, a violent slam echoed from the attic, followed by a hiss that ran through the pipes of the entire house.  
The move was over, but the true inhabitants of the house were only just beginning to wake up.

links.title: Back on the keys
links.body:
![Inline Image](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYGqKUUaEYhmzvfGeViPXtboaGj1oBL1Xhq5g9i1wNwnB/ai-image-1778701329860.jpeg)




Sitting here browsing hive and checking on a few small wallets after what feels like far too long. Not that I've disappeared, because I have still been around in the background, but I have definitely not been giving hive my full attention over the past few weeks for a bunch of different reasons.

There have been weddings, funerals, sick kids, sick me, matches won and lost, and all of that on top of the usual day-to-day life that keeps ticking along whether we like it or not. None of it is unusual on its own, but when it all seems to land in the same stretch of time it can feel relentless. It's honestly hurting my head just thinking about how busy the last six weeks have been.

Because of that, hive and crypto in general has had to take a back seat to everything else going on. That is just the reality sometimes. As much as we might want to stay on top of every little thing, there are only so many hours in the day and only so much mental energy to go around.

It is a shame in one way, but at the same time crypto has been pretty flat all year, so it doesn't really feel like I have missed some huge moment by stepping away for a while. If anything, it has probably been a decent time to reduce the noise and focus on real life without feeling like I'm constantly looking over my shoulder at charts and notifications.

I do miss writing and posting though. That part of it always stays with me, even when I am not actively doing it. There just can't be time for everything we would like to do, and that becomes even more obvious when summer arrives, the days get longer, and there are more chances to get out, see people, and end up with even more on the calendar than expected.

At this point I feel like I just need a few quiet days to reset, get back on track, and organise myself properly. That sort of breathing room helps more than people realise. When you get hit with so much, so fast, it can be hard to catch your breath, let alone think clearly about what comes next.

So this post is not really designed to set the world alight. It is mostly just me checking back in with one of my favourite activities and getting my fingers back on the keys again. Even calling it a post is probably being generous to what I have written so far, but that is fine. The important thing is getting back into the game and reminding myself how good it feels to create something again, even if it's only a small start.

Hopefully my next attempt will bring a bit more color to recent events and a little more structure to my thoughts as I get my head back into a writing mentality.

links.title: Branch supports, and raising the water hose...
links.body:
Last year I made a ladder to support the branches of a fig and a pear tree, so that the branches would not break under the weight of the fruit.
And this year I have to make a support for the branches of an apricot tree.
It is partly my fault, when I pruned the tree I did not want to remove many fruit buds. I was afraid of frost because last year we were left without a single apricot. The frost destroyed everything in bloom. So, taking that into account, I did not remove the fruit buds.
This apricot tree has certainly \

a little, and it is difficult to bring it back into a shape that meets the rules of pruning. And I do not want to make large cuts because that can harm it. So now I am forced to support a few branches and help them with the weight.


![20260513_173512.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AK2C8Mpq5s7t47mZcNw2Uhk7GqvBcJZTdGBQnfp2ERfV49KhpaPd27KtQ2rMvSu.jpg)



For this purpose I used (recycled) old used battens and a few nails.
For each bracket I measured how long it needed to be, cut it with a hand saw and added another batten on top of the batten, making a kind of fork.

![20260513_173533.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AK6X3i8PPgsCC31eP3hMZNfxbupCF4cXzB9QEyYjBgETou6Whk22f7xAgBoKoej.jpg)![20260513_174308.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AJms2yaDkBrwrELNrkeq95fjGhS2yEVk1TaiBrq2P4aBzrcSZ3ZJJ2K2eZcSNjL.jpg)

I made four branches and supported the more critical branches. I may need more, I'll have to monitor the condition of the apricots as they grow.I have removed and am removing every overly damaged , stunted or bad apricot . But I am sorry to remove healthy apricots .
![20260513_174511.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AK2DMyGgmZ6UpncLnQKAMqhWRtqZ1MAoR8NJRd8hNbFpEua7fDkqhsuiz4Z7NWb.jpg)
Since I had already worked with slats, I made five smaller slats for the orchard.I stuck them in the ground and raised the main hose from the irrigation system. The grass has grown in the orchard and the neighbor is coming tomorrow to mow the grass with a trimmer.
In order not to damage the hose and not to bother him, I decided to raise it. I removed the individual hoses of the drip system and removed them from the orchard. I know that this is not the best solution for watering and instead of this trick with drips, it is better to have a more decorative hose with drippers that goes to the orchard. And it is attached to the fruit trees themselves. That is all I have at the moment, so I have to make do.
![20260513_180852.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AJkRoQ5bVFSsW2LSM1EnGr4TehdxPyxZ9LXt1p8UAYtfbV9Dw93hyqz62YKgACP.jpg)

![20260513_181053.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AKKQx4BZh7aFGa82gU7MJuph38rbTY7eUr7jLMFPaq8FTfhGFK32rsJ3pq2qbKy.jpg)


![20260513_181146.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/markone85/AK6XiJJUHuUN1FrEwHpFzecJYXcoUEoLix9b7QdA6niHmjCgS9Y3V5tYXc7p1ac.jpg)

---
Thanks for reading.
Until next time.
Stay healthy.
Markone85.

links.title: Would I Still Use Hive Without Rewards?
links.body:
Honestly, this is a really interesting question because rewards are one of the main reasons many people join Hive in the first place including me, if you ask me this question some years back, my answer will be no. When I first joined Hive, I just became a mum then and I need something to do to make money. I searched online for apps that I can get money from but find none not until I was introduced to the hive blockchain. Immediately I heard that I will be getting paid for posting, commenting, or curating content got me interested because it was attractive. But if rewards disappeared completely, would I still use Hive? I think my answer now would be yes.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQfau3DKXpvE2nbPUciEncH7YvqzBpFmwdfAGMMjWJLCd/1000214986.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/man-think-young-thinking-male-1276384/)

Of course, things would be different. I probably wouldn’t post as often as I do now, and I’m sure many users would lose motivation. But at the same time, ever since I joined Hive, I've got to understand that Hive is more than just earning tokens. After spending time on the platform, I started realizing that there are other things that make it more valuable.

For me, one of the biggest things is the community. I’ve seen people from different countries connect, support each other, and share ideas in ways that feel more genuine than most social media platforms today. On apps like Facebook or Instagram, everything feels rushed and focused on trends, likes, or going viral. Hive feels different because people actually take time to read and interact with content.

Another reason I would still stay on Hive is because of the freedom it gives users. On other platforms, you don’t really own anything. Your account can get restricted, your reach can disappear overnight because of an algorithm, and the platform controls almost everything, I've got restricted on a platform for what I had no idea on, just because someone tag me with the content they said violated their community rules. With Hive, it feels like users have more control over their content and identity. That decentralized aspect is something I appreciate a lot.

I also enjoy the blogging side of Hive. Writing posts, sharing experiences, and reading other people’s thoughts can still be enjoyable even without rewards. In a way, rewards are like a bonus, but they are not the only reason to create content. Some people genuinely love writing, photography, gaming, or sharing knowledge, and Hive gives space for all of that.

At the same time, I won’t pretend rewards are not important because they definitely are. Rewards help keep users active and motivated. They encourage consistency and participation. For many people, especially those in countries with weaker currencies like mine, Hive rewards can actually make a real difference financially. If rewards disappeared, I think a lot of users would leave because the earning opportunity is what brought them here.


In my opinion, Hive works best because it combines both community and rewards. The rewards attract people, but the community is what makes many stay long term. Without rewards, Hive would definitely become smaller, but I don’t think it would completely die.But nevertheless, I would still use Hive without rewards, even if my activity level changed a bit. Because at the the end of the day, the platform still offers freedom, connection, and a place to express yourself, and those things still matter.



**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

links.title: O.S.M.A.N.D. all' undicesima ora ENG/ITa
links.body:
![CH 12.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zumzulik/23xyp3t95FoLqaQhBMRRrdgUwYUkVVSphB12PgahPJXDHwta2AH4gjH8PA2emqYWN3VWp.png)

Versione in Italiano subito dopo

Hive community, good morning.
Today I want to introduce you to one of my passions: writing. Below, I am posting a review I received from a specialized website; further down you will
also find the link to the blog, Les fleurs du mal 2016.
It was my first literary adventure, and this review gave me the strength to keep going.
The book was released in 2023 and is titled O.S.M.A.N.D. all’undicesima ora (O.S.M.A.N.D. at the eleventh hour), published by Gruppo Albatros.
I want to be clear, because those who are familiar with this world know that reviews are often paid for, but Alessandra and Barbara do it solely out of
passion and not for mere profit.

Il blog 
https://lesfleursdumal2016.wordpress.com


## The Review ##


In the preface of this pleasant tale, Barbara Alberti speaks of books as friends who can be lovers or confidants, and she quotes Dickinson's highly famous
lines:
There is no Frigate like a Book
To take us Lands away
Nor any Coursers like a Page
Of prancing Poetry –
This Traverse may the poorest take
Without oppress of Toll –
How frugal is the Chariot
That bears the Human Soul –
Finding one's own soul in a book is every reader's dream, but to achieve it, we must prepare ourselves for the journey with deep respect, cultivating humility
and listening. Silence is a good friend in this case, but certain melodies work well too.
Osmand tells us his story in the first person. It is the story of a lonely man, taken into a military base and trained to fight, to be cynical and ruthless.
But can a man's nature truly be warped?
It is not so much what he did that struck me, but rather the mechanism that led him to feel the need to move away from the only place he had ever known.
An old man, Mariuccio, used to tell him about his retirement dreams, and so, all of a sudden, the walls started to feel tight.
Another person's dream, his voice, his stories, triggered in Osmand the desire to escape, the necessity to achieve freedom.
Freedom, however, comes at a price—a steep price that left me in disbelief, as if watching a movie that starts from the ending. Beauty arrives in small
steps in this strange tale, which is finely interwoven with the escape.
Indeed, at a certain point, I no longer knew whether this boy was running away from freedom or reaching for it. Ultimately, it is a very subtle difference
for someone raised \

for whom time can turn out to be the worst of enemies.
Time is a rather strange dimension when reading; it flows, flies, stops, keeps you waiting, demands admiration, and embellishes with its coils the pages
that slip away, only to return in the form of dreams, hopes, plans, and imagination.
If life has no value, then Osmand is right: he has nothing to lose, he does not have to abide by any rule, and any weapon is good enough. The only variable?
Feelings, which are the protagonist's weak point and, at the same time, his only true hope of redemption.
Actions do not become right just because institutions tell us they are. We should always be put in a position to decide for ourselves what is right and
what is wrong. Yet behind it all, there is a reason, and the true reason is that Osmand…
I swear it will leave you speechless.



It all started as a joke, it was an escape route and a pastime at the same time; now, it is a genuine passion: writing.

Thank you to those who took some time to read this,

Yours,
zumzulik

---   ---

Popolo di Hive, buon giorno.

Oggi voglio presentarvi una delle mie passioni, la scrittura. Posterò di seguito una recensione ottenuta da un sito specializzato, sotto troverete anche il link del blog, Les fleurs du mal 2016.
Era la mia prima avventura letteraria, e questa recensione mi ha dato la forza per continuare.
Il libro è uscito nel 2023 e si intitola O.S.M.A.N.D. all’ undicesima ora, edito da Gruppo Albatros.
Voglio esser chiaro, perché chi frequenta questo mondo sa che le recensioni sono a pagamento, ma Alessandra e Barbara, lo fanno solo per passione e non per mero profitto.

Il blog 
https://lesfleursdumal2016.wordpress.com



## la recensione ##

Barbara Alberti nella prefazione di questo simpatico racconto parla di libri come di amici che possono essere amanti, confidenti e cita i versi famosissimi della Dickinson:
Non esiste un vascello come un libro
per portarci in terre lontane
né corsieri come una pagina
di poesia che si impenna.
Questa traversata la può fare anche un povero,
tanto è frugale il carro dell’anima
Ritrovare la propria anima in un libro è il sogno di ogni lettore ma per raggiungerlo dobbiamo prepararci al viaggio con profondo rispetto e coltivare l’umiltà e l’ascolto. Il silenzio è un buon amico in questo caso, ma anche alcune melodie si prestano.
Osmand ci racconta la sua storia in prima persona ed è la storia di un uomo solo, accolto in una base militare e addestrato per combattere, per essere cinico e spietato, ma si può stravolgere la natura di un uomo?
Non è tanto ciò che ha fatto a colpirmi, quanto il meccanismo che lo ha portato a percepire la necessità di allontanarsi dall’unico luogo conosciuto. Un vecchio, Mariuccio, gli raccontava i suoi sogni per la pensione così all’improvviso le pareti cominciano a stargli strette.
Il sogno di un altro, la sua voce, i suoi racconti, hanno innescato in Osmand la voglia di fuggire, la necessità di raggiungere la libertà.
La libertà ha però un prezzo, un prezzo salato che mi ha lasciato incredula come davanti ad un film che comincia dal finale. La bellezza arriva a piccoli passi in questo racconto, strano, intrecciato finemente con la fuga.
Sì perché ad un certo punto non sapevo più se questo ragazzo stava scappando dalla libertà o la stava raggiungendo. In fondo si tratta di una sottilissima differenza che per uno cresciuto “in cattività”, per il quale il tempo può rivelarsi il peggiore dei nemici.
Il tempo è una dimensione assai strana quando si legge, scorre, vola, si blocca, si lascia attendere e ammirare e impreziosisce con le sue spire le pagine che scivolano via per poi tornare sottoforma di sogni, speranze, progetti, fantasia.
Se la vita non ha un valore allora Osmand ha ragione, non ha nulla da perdere, non deve sottostare a nessuna regola e qualsiasi arma è buona. Unica variabile? I sentimenti, che sono il punto debole del protagonista e allo stesso tempo la sua unica, vera speranza di riscatto.
Le azioni non diventano giuste solo perché le istituzioni ci dicono che è così. Dovremmo sempre essere messi nella condizione di dire da soli cosa è giusto e cosa è sbagliato. Eppure dietro a tutto c’è un motivo e il vero motivo è che Osmand…
Vi giuro che vi lascerà a bocca aperta.

------    -----

Era iniziato tutto per scherzo, era una via di fuga ed al tempo stesso un passatempo, ora una vera e propria passione, la scrittura

Grazie a voi che avete avuto un po' di tempo da dedicarmi,

Il vostro 
Zumzulik

links.title: Splinterlands - Opening 5 Foundation packs, winning 1 Gold foil and 2 Epic Cards, and an unpredictable Battle with Equalizer Modifier
links.body:
Hello everyone,
How are you all? I hope everyone is fine and doing great in their life.



I am back with another Splinterlands blog, and this time I am going to share a very interesting battle that I played today.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUQHduyLjCN2UgZ9D517LPhH9nYAfDSWN2rer6MJmBPvm/image.png)

But before that, let me first take you all to the mana well because that is where we open our Foundation chests.

This time, we only had five Foundation chests left, as you can see in the screenshot below, and I decided to open all of them. I was unable to play the game for the last two days, so I did not get the chance to earn more chests. Maybe I will buy more later, but for now, let us see what we got from these packs.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRocySowAzMiu5GtKuHbKtTB8dUciS7aBNK6jK5ukMvUH/image.png)

In the screenshot below, you can see all the cards I won, and honestly, I am happy with the opening even though I did not get any legendary card.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQHbXckY86sDTPUUauAYJidYbjjvT8cvszocZnmocNq6V/image.png)

The very first thing that made me happy was the gold foil card named New Beluroc Aegis, which you can see in the screenshot below. I already own this card, so now I might be able to upgrade it to the next level.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeYUhsBBbesGmpkyb1HuRotQca7iwVRgW5BCRd1SeWKD1/image.png)

Apart from that, I also won two epic cards.

The first epic card can be seen in the screenshot below. Its name is Lenore Nevermore, and this card is really useful in battles because I have personally used it many times.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQzrdYcBf4Vda6PGmohSMSwqUWsW4gUUnBnC5SXAzdp6q/image.png)

In the  screenshot below, you can see the second epic card that I won. This monster is also very useful in many battles, and I would love to max it out someday. So I was happy to get this card as well.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYBGjmAGZWa25nixSpukEcyopanDLUdFefMbt4vU3FwJZ/image.png)

Now let us talk about the battle, which was quite interesting.

In the screenshot below, you can see the battle lineup. I used the Fire element while my opponent went with the Dragon element. The battle had the Equalizer modifier, which means all monsters start with equal health.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfJf8xCTxKYp3A5qC41NpXfDqyUipJjpvcH5wpFakr2vD/image.png)

The battle began, and by Round 2, I was already worried about losing because, as you can see in the screenshot below, my team was struggling badly.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUVxC34BcBmZzJYS5oerBt5NR7mQXZpTM4k47CNAZNoyW/image.png)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXPv76JNkrvaeP9KtdJFYYgcoKUH8UF28Fk6eszMV2wRr/image.png)

Finally, in Round 5, the battle went down to 3 vs 1, and I managed to secure the victory.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcKvDYFJuYrxmQBz34FSTevtogUp52EC4eqwYBYNcj7Kn/image.png)

So this was a really interesting Equalizer battle. At first, I thought I was going to lose, but in the end, the battle completely turned in my favor.

Now let me share some Terracore activity as well because that is the second game I play regularly.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPVuYp3c21MaEAym5avkAHkyxihTmasPcqRXtpcxDQs3a/image.png)

In the screenshot above, you can see the seven attacks I used in my Terracore base. This time, the attacks went quite well. Even though two of the attacks were dodged, I still managed to earn around 1000 scrap tokens.

That is all I did in Splinterlands and Terracore today.

links.title: What Modern Viewers Expect From an IPTV Service
links.body:
Viewer expectations have changed dramatically in the digital entertainment era. Traditional television models no longer satisfy audiences who want flexibility, convenience, and instant access to content. As IPTV continues to grow in popularity, users now expect services that deliver more than just live channels.

Modern IPTV platforms are expected to provide reliable performance, personalized experiences, and seamless accessibility across devices. These expectations are shaping the future of home entertainment and pushing providers to improve their services constantly.

## Flexible Access to Content

One of the most important expectations modern viewers have is flexibility. People no longer want to organize their schedules around television programming.

IPTV allows users to watch live TV, movies, sports, and on-demand content whenever it suits them. This convenience makes entertainment more accessible for viewers with busy lifestyles.

Flexibility has become a standard feature rather than an added benefit.

## High-Quality Streaming Performance

Streaming quality plays a major role in user satisfaction. Modern viewers expect HD and 4K playback with minimal buffering and stable performance.

Reliable IPTV services use adaptive streaming technology to maintain smooth playback even when internet speeds fluctuate. Consistent performance is especially important during live sports events and popular broadcasts.

Users are less willing to tolerate interruptions than ever before.

## Multi-Device Compatibility

Today’s audiences consume content across multiple devices. Viewers expect IPTV platforms to work seamlessly on smart TVs, smartphones, tablets, laptops, and streaming devices.

This allows users to continue watching content from different locations without interruption. Multi-device support has become essential for modern entertainment experiences.

Convenience and accessibility strongly influence viewer preferences.

## Personalized Entertainment Experience

Modern IPTV services are expected to offer personalized recommendations based on viewing habits and interests. Instead of browsing endless channels, users want quicker access to relevant content.

In the middle of this evolving market, many viewers look for an [IPTV provider](https://monstertvs.net/) that can combine personalization, smooth performance, and broad content availability in one service.

Tailored experiences improve engagement and create stronger user satisfaction.

## Wider Content Variety

Viewers now expect access to more than local channels. IPTV platforms are increasingly valued for offering international entertainment, live sports, movies, documentaries, and niche content.

This wider content availability gives users more freedom to choose entertainment that matches their interests.

Diverse programming is one of the strongest advantages IPTV has over traditional cable systems.

## Easy-to-Use Interface

A simple and organized interface is another key expectation. Users prefer platforms that make navigation quick and intuitive.

Complicated menus or slow-loading systems can negatively impact the viewing experience. Modern viewers want entertainment platforms that feel smooth and efficient from the moment they log in.

Ease of use plays a major role in long-term customer satisfaction.

## Affordable and Transparent Pricing

Traditional cable systems often frustrate users with hidden fees and expensive bundled packages. IPTV viewers now expect more transparent pricing structures.

Flexible subscription plans that match viewing preferences are becoming increasingly important. Users want better value without paying for unnecessary channels or features.

Cost efficiency strongly influences service selection.

## Reliable Customer Support

As IPTV services become more advanced, customer support also becomes more important. Modern viewers expect quick assistance when technical issues occur.

Responsive support helps build trust and improves the overall user experience. Reliable communication is an important factor in maintaining customer loyalty.

Strong service quality goes beyond just content delivery.

## Conclusion

Modern viewers expect IPTV services to deliver flexibility, high-quality streaming, personalized recommendations, and seamless access across multiple devices. These expectations reflect broader changes in digital entertainment consumption and user behavior.

As IPTV technology continues to evolve, providers that focus on convenience, reliability, and user experience will remain ahead in a highly competitive market. For today’s audiences, entertainment is no longer just about watching content, it is about having complete control over the viewing experience.
