links.title: Back When Happiness Was Simpler.
links.body:
I often hear adults say that the past was much quieter. When I was a child, I thought that maybe they were just saying this out of nostalgia for the past. But over time  I also started to understand that there is some truth behind the words.

The difference between today's life and the past is not just technology or modernity  but also the difference in people's lifestyle, mental peace, and relationships. In the past, people may not have had so many opportunities. There were not so many smartphones, internet, social media, or modern technology, but people were much closer to people then. In the evening, the whole family would sit together and talk, relationships with neighbors were deep, and joy could be found in small things.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrarhat/23wC7dwpyDg6iXxx5vT859Yuqw7W812YKCjwDENAuHTpuJfgdbUEVynXFw9FoUZS83Vog.png)

[Image Source](blob:https://gemini.google.com/8d15c380-c61a-44ea-b6fa-148ff6af5f80)

Now we have everything in our hands but no time. Before, people lived with less things, but their minds were perhaps a little calmer, and now, even though we have a lot, we always live with the fear of losing something. Seeing the lives of others on social media, feeling small, always feeling pressure to prove ourselves, worrying about the future, these have become a part of life today.

I sometimes notice that people may not have been so busy in the past, but they lived a lot, and now we are so busy that we don't get time to experience life properly.

Earlier, family meant eating together, spending time together. Now, even in the same room, everyone is busy on different screens. There are relationships, but conversations have decreased. People are connected but emotionally disconnected.

However, it would not be right to say that everything was good before and everything is bad now. The present time has given us many advantages. Medicine, communication, education, job opportunities, everything is much better than before. But with this improvement, the mental stress in our lives has also increased a lot. I think the main reason why the past time seemed more peaceful was that people viewed life relatively simply then. Their demands were lower, expectations were lower, and real relationships were stronger.

links.title: Rethinking Free Trade Assumptions
links.body:
There's been a strong free trade narrative around at least since Reagan and Thatcher, with the 'free' standing broadly for 'tariff' free - the neoliberal theory being that government interference in global markets would be bad for economic growht. 

But Trump's Tariffs have put an end to that and lo the doom-mongering about economic downturns hasn't come to pass, in fact things look surprisingly stable a year or so into his time in office. 

So maybe that economic of theory of neoliberalism was just a tiny bit flawed!?!

What's actually happened as a result of Trump's tariffs is maybe a marginal restructuring of global economic power in the US's favour, with many other countries being worse off, and a massive political gain for Trump, at least in the short term, as he looks like he's negotiating hard for those American workers left behind by 40 years of neoliberalism. 

Trump's policies aren't just economics in action; he's about power, negotiation, and using leverage. Policy doesn’t exist in an empty room—politics shapes every decision.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23wC5GUC86nwBcSHzcJGFQ2MqaxEuSocxTobcuVWsGX1kMgaxya7Mc9yPGSuYJbRxk1zd.png)


### All change.... 

It's actually quite refreshing to see a politician having a crack at policy, rather than leaving it up to the technical so-called experts - neoliberalism hasn't worked for everyone, after all, so time for a change, time for something different! 

And that's what Trump is about - poking holes in previous economic 'certainties' 

You may not like what he's doing, but it's probably better than just the same old, maybe?!?

links.title: KISS BLOG IDEAS: WEEK #211/ The type of person I am 😊
links.body: >The type of person I am

> There are things people I don't know have said to me that I've almost immediately forgotten, but there are other things, said by people who know me, that I'll never forget. And it's not because they're good or bad, but because I hold onto them because those words act as a mirror, showing me how others see me, how they perceive me, how much they see that I don't. I remember that before, at university, I had an office where students, more than seeking academic help or looking for a particular book, would just come to talk to me, to share their family and romantic problems, but also to share their joys or ask existential questions. There, spontaneously, students from all semesters would gather every day. Over cookies, coffee, and candy, I learned about their first relationships, their failed romances, their doubts about identity, as if I were the closest friend they could have or the town priest they could confess to.

/> I listened to them attentively, without prejudice, without complaint, without retaliation. If I had to offer my opinion, I did so if they asked me to, but otherwise, I simply remained silent and let that chest, heavy with feelings and words, unburden itself. No one can imagine the number of secrets I will take to my grave and the many times I had to be more than a teacher; I had to be a friend, a confidante, an accomplice, and even a mother—I, who never had a child of my own. But just like those students, it has happened to me that I have sat next to a stranger and, out of the blue, they have told me their life story. I have been sitting in the park, for example, and a woman has sat next to me to tell me her sorrows, her doubts, how her family treats her. Of course, many times I have wondered: What is it about me that makes people open up, that makes them have the confidence to open their hearts and show me without shame what they carry inside?

/> I don't know what it is about me, but I do know what other people see in me. Some have told me that I inspire trust and respect; others have even said they know I'm not prejudiced, and that's why they confide in me. But what has always surprised me is that some people tell me they've never shared that secret before and don't know why they told me. For many, my mere presence gives them confidence, calm, the courage to express themselves, to be themselves. I give them a positive vibe that allows them to open up and speak frankly and openly with me.

/> I like to think that my spontaneity, my way of seeing the world, my spiritual strength, that magnetic energy that's sometimes invisible to the eye, makes me a refuge for some people. That there are things that disappear when I appear. It's a gift or a superpower that brings me great joy, but it's also a responsibility.
>All images are from my personal gallery and the text was translated with Google
>Thank you for your support, for reading, and for your comments, friends. Until next time\n\n

links.title: The Blessings and Challenges of the Modern Era
links.body:
People born in different eras have different experiences, and when you try to compare many of these eras to themselves, you'll come to realize almost everyone has what they wish they had in their own era that other eras have. Many of us born into this era are actually pleased with the era we were born in because of the numerous benefits we're blessed with, ranging from technology to different devices that have made life easier, coupled with the peace of mind unlike those born during the era of war. So in light of that, I'll be stating if I'm pleased with the era I was born in or not. ![1000357297.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickoly/EpJa4suZKkJAJVivSUUkXKBvDeWGJMHhS1Jn7yHqvUrcCxafgeVbAQkkC7fcThMdhy3.jpg) Personally, in my opinion, I think I'm living in the very best era in human history, and that's because of the various benefits associated with this era. Alongside many of these dangers, evil of the previous eras are now a thing of the past in my era, and that's why I feel like it's the best era ever. I just can't imagine what people go through during the slave trade era, during the civil war era, during the military reign era, among many other eras. I've read and heard a lot of terrifying things about those eras, and I'm always thankful I wasn't born in them.I can't even imagine walking a long distance because there are no vehicles to transport me from one destination to another. Imagine the impact technology and social media are having on lives, how they pay people, and the like. How it helps one connect with the outside world and how various technology devices have made life easier and enjoyable. I love this era, and I think it's the best there is among all the eras there ever were. I know we've our own lapses, but then it's still quite better than others. There might come another era in the near future that's better than ours, but for now we're the best to date. If I can pick something from another era to add to ours for a better life, I'll pick the agricultural abundance of eras of the past, given the level of scarcity in this present age and inflation that has left on the economy. I'd also love to have the community spirit that was available back then and the peace it had on the people; now the world is plagued with hate, greed, and numerous other abnormalities that weren't in the past era. So having such kinds of peace, contentment, and the like are a good way to make this era better. But aside from that, this era is amazing; it's the best among all of the eras the world has witnessed. I'm a big fan of this era because of the convenience the technology has given us in this era. Ease and several other things to name but a few. If I were asked to pick any of the previous eras, including ours, I'd definitely pick this profile, and that's because of how awesome it is. I'm sure if our ancestors see what we're enjoying presently, they'll also wish they were born in this era. *** All photos are mine. ***

Сегодняшняя прогулка была просто невероятной! Я решил исследовать один из знакомых маршрутов в горах, и, как всегда, это принесло массу приятных сюрпризов. На середине пути я встретил семейную пару с детьми, которые гуляли с собакой. Мы разговорились, и они рассказали мне о своих любимых местах для прогулок в этом районе. Оказалось, что они недалеко живут и часто приходят сюда, чтобы наслаждаться природой. Это было здорово — обменяться рекомендациями и услышать новые истории о горах. По пути я также заметил несколько интересных видов растений, которых раньше не встречал: ярко-желтые цветы, которые выглядели как дикие ромашки, и необычные мхи, которые мирно растерялись на камнях. links.title: Every Era Has Flaws, But This One Feels Right
links.body:
When I saw the prompt, I thought up something out of fun. When we talk about era, I think of all the eras that has lived since the world began and that begins from Adam and eve era to Abraham to Moses to Jesus christ era before civilization era and then technology era, it's been a long one. And the whole point of this is, there was no era that wasn't without it's ups and downs. Humans lived in all these eras and humans are no perfect beings, they will always make mistakes, do the wrong things that will pass on as history. There was even eras with wars and slavery unlike now. It's a crazy world indeed, we can't have the good and not have the bad from it as well, we just choose our bad and live about it. So the question asking if we are living the best era, my answer is a very simple one and it is, **Yes we are.** I mean, are there other era we could choose from to live? Let's be honest, we are tempted to compare to past times because there are histories and stories about how that time was. Luckily for some alive today, they experienced it first hand and tell the story but if those were not available, we won't be where we are today and there would be no need to make comparison between eras. ![file_000000004dec720a8094091dd3b041f8.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/merit.ahama/EpXMwtEkLu688aTxR14TXJTSqGGvvU1TWZAAUgkgNCPSTVAW63cJHUEkdEaRDgBdsMr.png) I honestly can not imagine living in a world of no technology *(the past before advancement in technology)* and the reason is clear, I've never lived in those times. Even some who were opportune to live in both era, they would agree that life is more easier today than before. Of course, there are also downsides just like before. No era is free of downsides, moments that people would wish they could go back to an era that has passed. What we should be focused more on is how to make our era work more in our favour than against us. Technology has come to stay and the sooner we accept it, not compare with other era and grow with it, the better for us. So yeah, you can guess that I am happy and grateful to be born in this era. It was God's perfect plan so I won't dare question that. Every era comes with it's own challenges and best parts, we just need to balance up in our individual lives and try not to let ourselves be controlled by the technology we created with our own brains. Of course, there is no harm in picturing my life in the days of my ancestors, how closely I am to nature than I am today. That is one beautiful aspect of the past I love so much but it can be done in this age and time too so it still goes down what we do with our present era because there is no going back into another era anyways.
**Image used are AI generated.** Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@merit.ahama/every-era-has-flaws-but-this-one-feels-right-3tp)

links.title: A rainy dawn (Eng/Esp)
links.body:
> ![Post de Instagram horóscopo minimalista azul_20260513_152045_0000.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeXW9nwLYbhyY24HH9bcfXz5Bq2sQ4ci6MP8JQrMAC7JQ/Post%20de%20Instagram%20hor%C3%B3scopo%20minimalista%20azul_20260513_152045_0000.jpg) Rainy days are my favorite. First thing in the morning, I woke up to the sound of falling rain. It was pounding loudly on the roof and the pavement. When I woke up, it was still raining, and the temperature had already dropped a bit, which made the atmosphere very pleasant. This is the second tropical wave to hit the country during this rainy season, which is just beginning. After months of extreme drought, heat, and wildfires, many are eagerly awaiting the rain. >Los días lluviosos son mis favoritos. En la madrugada me desperté con el sonido de la lluvia al caer. Se escuchaba fuerte sobre el techo y el pavimento. Cuando desperté todavía llovía y ya la temperatura había bajado un poco, haciéndola muy agradable. Esta es la segunda onda tropical que llega al país en esta temporada de lluvias que esta apenas comenzando. Después de meses de extrema sequía, calor e incendios forestales la lluvia es esperada por muchos.
![20260513_090809.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVYGXYWWk1ARATqDdwDqUrLU1MtKsudNPJkYeff43Wq2o/20260513_090809.jpg)
After having a nice hot cup of coffee and breakfast, I went outside to watch the rain. It had already let up a bit, so I took the opportunity to snap a few photos. >Después de tomar un cafecito bién caliente  y desayunar salí a ver la lluvia. Ya había escampado un poco y aproveche de tomar unas fotografías.
![20260513_090833.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaGiFkQCfkKPXGjyVsvibuw5ELKhxgH3hAgNVznbcnGDX/20260513_090833.jpg)
![20260513_090942.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVhEt2bfjXiriZCqJmjo6gRUco9SNsCofXgDXH49VtDW3/20260513_090942.jpg) Across from the building where I live stands a large tree with lush foliage and a trunk covered in thorns. We call it Jabillo. Its outstretched branches are dripping with water. It must feel happy about this gift from nature. >Enfrente del edificio donde vivo está un gran árbol, de follaje frondoso y tronco con espinas. Le decimos Jabillo. Sus ramas extendidas están llenas de agua. Debe sentirse feliz de ese regalo que la naturaleza le dio.
![20260513_090753.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbhkQiqyQtn4r3j2kTrKP59iLUgdikmgNM6VaKzMAw6Um/20260513_090753.jpg)
The ground was flooded, and in some places water had pooled, so I had fun, just like I did when I was a child, watching the raindrops fall and create ripples. I took several photos of this effect of the raindrops on the water. >El suelo estaba anegado y en algunos lugares se había acumulado el agua y me divertí como hacía cuando niña , observando las gotas caer y formar ondas. Tomé varias fotografías de este efecto de las gotas en el agua. ![20260513_090910.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUNfMPBxq7dh1BnjVFjcWygKWzrafLt8DF49PSqFbJLN2/20260513_090910.jpg) I went out to the backyard, and my turtle, Lolita, took advantage of the open door to slip out. She’s very agile; she hopped down the step and started exploring, walking among the plants, climbing up and down the remains of dry branches from some trees that had fallen during a stormy night.
![20260513_091506.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbnFPmAsJQybUtDHQwBczxjuTukV9k82tLxLcnMhTAWXV/20260513_091506.jpg)
I like how the leaves look with the water droplets on their surface. Some insects were flitting over the plants.
![20260513_091753.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUFe7Z5eRk9gUaajBySvQoecaMf5DhstVwys83oTpNPGi/20260513_091753.jpg)
>Salí al patio de atras y mi tortuga Lolita aprovechó que la puerta quedó abierta para salir. Es muy ágil,  bajó el escalón y empezó a explorar, caminando entre las plantas, bajando y subiendo entre los restos de palos secos de unos árboles que se cayeron en una noche de tormenta. Me gusta como se ven las hojas con las gotas de agua sobre su superficie. Algunos insectos sobrevolaban las plantas.
![20260513_091421.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQEW4ap5E4e9ANcEB2eEJphb1aA71MAheRU9euKhmqHS8/20260513_091421.jpg)
![20260513_091815.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR6moqt6JmggSxsnqucWSLW86272u8RWr4JWHmNQSmKK6/20260513_091815.jpg)
Even the mango tree, heavy with fruit, looked radiant with the rain that came to wash its leaves and quench its thirst. >Hasta el árbol de mango cargado de frutos se veía resplandeciente con la lluvia que vino a lavar sus hojas y a saciar su sed.
![20260513_092019.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc56Hbncs4nriJ1R3Dt77pJiv15GhmSiBkCD3FtX9nMqJ/20260513_092019.jpg)
The sky is still cloudy, even though the rain has stopped falling.  >El cielo todavía esta nublado aunque ya la lluvia a dejado de caer.  ![20260513_091108.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdwD25VbggdKYTtJppwSmGp1zgJDuXvPocjCoGbnoZ3EX/20260513_091108.jpg) ![Ingredientes_20260110_153742_0000.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXzmGnv9jVDz8aMkc4eM3youZE6wEgPKaF87bCw198N1T/Ingredientes_20260110_153742_0000.jpg)
Thank you so much for reading
![17786994193816222287264290644099.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdK2vhwCfaF1Hu7BuA64Dm5cxGFb1ZyE5rSLNP2sKmYQT/17786994193816222287264290644099.jpg) All the photos were taken by me using a Samsung A15 smartphone. I used www.deepl.com to translate this into English.

# ෴ ᴡʜᴏ

## Cranio

![DSC09084.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tvY8jE6geC9RVwauyArZkyAppRG3zEeAP1aHShpXQubSWxwj1eyAqz5M5pfc3Z8TXsg.JPG)

[**Cranio**](https://www.instagram.com/cranioartes/) is a self-taught Brazilian artist from **São Paulo** active since 1998. In his work, he highlights the issues of our current society such as overconsumption and the environment with a Brazilian touch.

> *[**Cranio**](https://www.instagram.com/cranioartes/) est un artiste autodidacte brésilien de **São Paulo** actif depuis 1998. Dans son travail, il souligne les enjeux de notre société actuelle comme la sur-consommation, l'environnement avec une touche brésilienne.*

<div class=\

/> His works are easily recognizable by the presence of his favorite character, a blue native in traditional dress. The color blue comes from his cultural heritage as an indigenous person of the **Xingu** region in Brazil. > *On reconnait facilement ses œuvres avec le présence de son personnage favori un autochtone bleu en tenue traditionnelle. La couleur bleu provient de son héritage culturel en tant qu'autochtone de la région du [Xingu au Brésil](https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xingu_(peuple)).* ![DSC09082.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23uFPgLBV8Kn8ZaFi84gX1DGwYiasM5WY1vVN6aZ7LhJ6Buy2UBhSgDrxvcCtvq6mvFjM.JPG) This mural depicts the effects of progress on nature, with deforestation in the background. The characters are trying to tame technology; one is using a cell phone (?) which is criticized by the leader but sparks the interest of the younger ones. Really interesting, there's a lot to see on this wall. I especially like the character with the fanny pack and frog costume. > *Sur cette murale, on voit les effets du progrès sur la nature avec le déforestation en arrière plan. Et les personnages essaye d'apprivoiser la technologie, un avec un téléphone portable (?) critiqué par le chef mais suscitant l'intérêt des plus jeunes. Vraiment intéressant, beaucoup à voir sur ce mur. J'aime bien le personnage avec son sac banane et son déguisement de grenouille.* ![DSC09081.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tvVw242qgKEqFtDhDCkcHtYKVenKi5T4m57BKyKuCf6djfHuoWpwuT6b5Dh8How1yMq.JPG) **What do you think of this work? *Que pensez-vous de cette oeuvre ?*** *** ![Cranio](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/23tbif9o3voCJZcDH3inzYQP8MVsNWsBTtc75KdPXi38eE1yU64dB8xc4QSeUJGxyJ36s.JPG) I found this little guy on another street in Wynwood (25th Street if I remember correctly). I don't know if this is the only character left or if he's crawled out of the mural to explore the neighborhood too 😀. > *J'ai trouvé ce petit bonhomme dans une autre rue de Wynwood (la 25ème rue si mon souvenir est correct). Je ne sais pas il ne reste que ce personnage ou il s'est enfoui de la murale pour lui aussi visiter le quartier* 😀. # ෴ ᴡʜᴇɴ ![line_hive.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/heroldius/xoycoMPQ-line_hive.jpg) * **2022/2023**. ![line_grey.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSj2ThUhewrAjDZMFsx4UjSaXuS84cwHR2anDzyq9KWVh/line_grey.jpg)

/> **෴ ꜱᴏᴜʀᴄᴇꜱ** **Instagram** : [Cranio](https://www.instagram.com/cranioartes/) **෴ ᴘʀᴇᴠɪᴏᴜꜱ ᴘᴏꜱᴛꜱ** [#883 SKE, Ismo, Luke & Mwanel (Miami Part V)](https://peakd.com/hive-184784/@heroldius/street-art-883-wynwood-miami-part-v--ske-ismo-luke-and-mwanel)  **>** [#882 Mufa & **Tristan Easton** (Miami Part IV)](https://peakd.com/hive-184784/@heroldius/street-art-882-wynwood-miami-part-iv--mufa-and-tristan-easton) [StreetArt Contest #299 Hefster & Pilot...](https://peakd.com/hive-184784/@heroldius/cccs-street-art-contest-299-wynwood-miami-part-iii--hefster-and-pilot-and-bert-and-loomit) [#881 **Quake & Hiero** (Miami Part II)](https://peakd.com/hive-184784/@heroldius/street-art-881-wynwood-miami-part-ii--quake-and-hiero) [#880 El Mac & DFace... links.body:
**Strong point:** high EQ absolutely makes life smoother. It won’t make someone magically right all the time, but it **does** help them read people better, regulate themselves better, and avoid a lot of unnecessary drama. That part of your post lands.

I’d tighten one thing: **high EQ doesn’t mean rarely doubting yourself**. Sometimes the opposite is true — emotionally intelligent people can be more reflective, which means they notice their own blind spots. The real marker is not “no doubt,” it’s **self-awareness + self-control + empathy + good communication**. That’s the combo that keeps relationships from turning into chaos. [Simply Psychology](https://www.simplypsychology.org/emotional-intelligence.html) and [Verywell Mind](https://www.verywellmind.com/components-of-emotional-intelligence-2795438) frame it pretty much that way.

The image works well with the idea too. It shows one calm central figure surrounded by different social interactions, which fits your point that EQ helps someone stay balanced while reading the emotional energy around them. Nice visual choice — simple, clear, and not trying too hard.

One small writing upgrade: your post gets stronger if you also mention that **EQ can be developed**. Otherwise it can sound a bit fixed, like people either have it or they don’t. A line about practicing listening, managing reactions, and paying attention to body language would round it out neatly.

links.title: My Actifit Report Card: May 13 2026
links.body:
> Rower, rower, rower. Wczoraj sobie uświadomiłem, że jeden z tych rowerów przejechał już ponad 22 tysiące kilometrów. Wczoraj wrzucałem screena że stravy, ale dzisiaj dotarło to do mnie ile to jest. Dzwoniłem dzisiaj do serwisu i pytam zaczepnie czy nie wcisną mnie na jakiś delikatny serwis roweru. W słuchawce pracownik serwisu odpowiedział gromkim śmiechem i, że z moim rowerem to nigdy nie jest drobny serwis, ten rower nie ma lekko. Taka jest prawda, nie chce być inaczej. Małżonka przyznała mi się, że oglądała nowe rowery i w sumie sam zajrzałem na stronę producenta tego mojego i upgrade kosztowałby jakieś 3100 zł. Może podjadę do salonu i się pokręcę i popytam - można się śmiać, że ten mój Northtec to trochę frankenstein z wieloma przeszczepami, ale na tyle kilometrów popełnionych przez osobę, która średnio umie dbać o rower, to wydaje się, że zakup był jak najbardziej uzasadniony. Bike, bike, bike. Yesterday I realized that one of those bikes has already done more than 22,000 kilometers. I posted a Strava screenshot yesterday, but only today did it really hit me how much that actually is. Today I called the bike service shop and jokingly asked whether they could squeeze me in for some minor servicing. The guy on the phone burst out laughing and said that with my bike it’s never a minor service — that bike has a hard life. And that’s the truth, I wouldn’t want it any other way. My wife admitted that she had been looking at new bikes, and I also checked the manufacturer’s website for mine. An upgrade would cost around 3,100 PLN. Maybe I’ll stop by the showroom, take a look around, and ask a few questions. People can laugh that my Northtec is basically a Frankenstein bike with countless transplanted parts, but considering how many kilometers it has done in the hands of someone who isn’t exactly great at taking care of a bike, it really seems like a very justified purchase. ![1000016816.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sk1920/EpT5gmQexNhv7Dw1kLCNa63j1BYLEXQRX4RyUkBgZrmocJBWt88AFX8EwaWKUdduaYU.jpg) ![1000016821.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sk1920/23tbHAHHXeD6zRx7YdnitGbaomFTeEk5ewFLpsAeAVzAtv36N1kWUCUQ6cGouUWGDFqnt.jpg)

links.title: High EQ is good
links.body:
>

Humans are smart, and using their intelligence, they dominate the world. When it comes to intelligence, there is no other creature besides humans. Emotional intelligence, which is also known as EQ, plays a very important role in human life. Having a high EQ can save us from lots of trouble. In a word, it helps us keep human relationships simple by eliminating complexities while communicating with others. On the other hand, having low EQ makes things complex and troublesome. So, having a good EQ is necessary. ![Inline Image](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRiw5bjoSE3dTVnYvxLw2UdV3DePgJmLudWvU7yd4XwmW/ai-image-1778699916478.jpeg) picture generated by rafiki Having high EQ means one person has the ability to understand his own emotions, and the person knows what he actually wants from himself and what he expects from others. Because of it, he has a clear vision about himself and, in rare cases, he doubts himself as well as his expectations and destination. Such a thing is indeed good for anyone as it ensures the smooth growth of a person. It not only gives a better understanding of oneself, but it also helps to understand others. High EQ helps to improve the relationship between others, as it makes communication much better. A person with high EQ can communicate with others easily and make things interesting, for which staying connected with them is not so difficult. It doesn’t matter where they go; they can make friends easily as long as they want. So, life seems to be in their favor. Such a person has a good understanding of others, and just by observing for a while, they can understand if one person is upset, happy, or angry. If they find someone feeling irritated by his presence, he can understand it easily. They don’t need any warnings to understand it. Just the actions or body language are enough to make them understand what’s actually going on. A person with high EQ will always be self-aware and have good control over their emotions. Even if they can’t avoid being angry, frustrated, and upset all the time, they can take control of the situation most of the time, and they also know how to balance and protect themselves from negative emotions. They also make mistakes, and it’s quite natural, and nobody can avoid it, but those people acknowledge the situation pretty well and understand what their mistake was, and as fast as possible they try to correct it, and if they need to apologize, they can do it quite fast. As humans, they can live their life in interesting ways, and they can also chase success as they can read the situation well.

links.title: We wish to go back to the 90s
links.body:
/>

The truth is that people who were born in the 80s and 90s always wish to feel again what life was like during those times when compared to how life is now because it appears that life was better in those days than it is now, and that is very true. I am among those born in the 90s, and I had a better life back then compared to this era that we are currently in.

I have this elderly man in his 80s who's a neighbour in my workplace, anytime we have conversations about life, he always likes to throw me back to how life was sweet for them in their early days. These are the people who bought lands with just 1naira. Some of them even acquired lands for free by clearing the forest. This man always tells me how they don't buy fish or meat for their food because their traps in the backyard of their house always give them bush meat.  
Oh yeah, I experienced a good part of that life too because I was born in the 90s.

Do you know how beautiful life was before this era?
===================================================

Some time ago I made a post on how we enjoyed good music and I had people who couldn't just get enough of how entertaining music was in those days. Back then, only good music was the one that made it to the limelight, there was nothing like using digital means to push and force it into the ears of people. Although they were marketers back then, they pushed music to the public but only the good ones came out. Talking about the albums of P-Square, Omg! Those albums sold out effortlessly. But now, the music digital flow and means of forcing people to listen to songs have spoiled the fun. It's so hard to separate well-crafted works from the shallow ones.

Should I talk about how we had a good family bonding in those days compared to now?

Although back then, things were very tough for us as a family, we bonded very well during those moments. We would go to the farm, work until our bodies were worn out, and even in the midst of that, we cracked jokes with our siblings and parents while doing those jobs on the farm. Dad was always the chef, and eating together from the pot and mortar was simply unbeatable. Back then, the thought of the delicious “poor-rated” food we were going to enjoy at the farm would make us eager to go.

The bonding never stopped. Whenever we returned home and were done with dinner and chores, the family would gather to watch movies either on VCD or on the antenna-powered television. There were no phones to distract us. Even when we had phones back then, the distraction was very minimal, and that was because the phones of those days were not as advanced as the ones we have now.

But now, it is rare to see a complete family seated together and watching movies. The last time I went home, I tried to stay put and watch movies with my mom and other siblings, but it was not interesting at all. Lol

Thanks for reading.

_The photo used is mine_

This is the video series for an oil painting 'Wisteria' I did from 2016-2020.  The painting was destroyed in 2021 due to a number of reasons, but mainly: the painting's faulty experimental linseed-epoxide substrait, Covid-19 crushing lockdowns, extreme poverty, family attacks and ongoing US government (Big Tech + Big Media) censorship of me and my 30 years of artwork.

Its not ideal to not be able to show this piece, but I still gained the knowledge of how to do it and invented several useful oil painting mediums & varnishes used in its creation which never yellowed and still cannot be bought anywhere.

I am posting these videos for posterity and for people that are interested in seeing an oil painting created from start to finish in the Baroque style evolved for the 21st century.  I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

title.title: A Steel Cocoon - Part 4 (Short Story)
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQJ4NzbozJWY5U6wNKj9JMDuX2NmDr3aoDX9apoVeoHzn/dpdajlxnh4jfho6ovuqi_3_1km1w.jpg)

[Source](https://creator.nightcafe.studio/creation/DPdaJLXnh4JFHO6OVuqI)

Five blips on his monitor. Five blips, flying in formation toward their vessel. Another alarm. Five more came towards them from the other ship. They were little more than streaks on the video feed. Min'canari readied his turret. He had switched to burst fire and was just waiting for an opportunity to strike.

\
Captain Naash's voice came in unexpectedly. He retained an air of confidence, but there was a slight panic to his tone.\n\n\
Captain Naash's voice was clear over Min'canari's shoulder. \
His voice trailed off as footsteps receded.\n\n\

Min'canari singled out the leader and watched as they grew in the distance. He recognised the model, but not the decals or colour scheme. They were flying an older model ship. Pre-war. Human. Confederation. They seemed to have undergone some retrofitting. He noticed the one behind the leader had some damage. Cosmetic. These fighters had seen battle, but that didn't mean the pilots had seen conflict. Being outgunned was a problem. An enemy without experience, though, was enough to sway the outcome. 

Harrit moved rapidly in his seat. His fingers worked overtime while attacking. Out of the corner of his eye, Min'canari could see points rising. As the number grew, it seemed like Harrit gained composure. His eyes darted from his score to the targets. If he were to warrant a guess, he was more concerned with the score than actually winning this battle.

The leader was well within firing distance before Min'canari pulled the trigger. Pull, release, pull, release. His shots were controlled. Suppressive fire. The ship evaded. Weaving from side to side. As it banked, missed shots landed on those behind. The fighters began to fire. Many of the shots landed. The shields flashed to life as they reflected incoming fire. He tracked the leader. His fingers moved faster. His turret unleashed a hail of blue orbs. Sparks. Emergency lighting. He could see the pilot flailing with each new impact. A flash of light. In a beautiful display, the leader's fighter had been destroyed. 

\
\n\nMin'canari noticed Harrit glancing at his score, which was quickly catching up. Those stupid numbers. He could see the appeal to something like this. It made the process \

but there shouldn't be fun in this. It is not a sport. Combat. Death. This battle was about survival. Defense. The lives of those on board. A points system stripped that away. Yet another peculiar thing that Humans do.

The fighters retreated and regrouped. As they moved away, the three turret gunners let off many more shots. One of the ships was destroyed. Many now seemed worse for wear. It didn't stop them from coming again. Another pass. Min'canari continued to fire at them. His target was worn down and damaged. It limped along. Slower than the rest. Its pilot maintained control of his ship, but he must have felt the eyes watching him. Fire. A flash of light. Another explosion. All that was left was debris that rained in all directions. If the room was quiet enough, he may have been able to hear the ping of fragmented steel against their hull.

No more shields. The familiar blue shimmer has stopped. They were depleted. The video feed showed another fighter. Another target. It was no longer firing; it was just flying. Then a dot of red light appeared on it. It grew over the course of a few seconds and launched. The orb of red light flew beyond the video feed. He could feel a tremor. He continued to fire, but it manoeuvred in such a way that it disappeared. He tried to track it. As he turned right, a ship would come and go from the left. As he rotated the turret up. Another would pass below. He was too slow to keep up with them. He fired wildly out of frustration, knowing he wasn't going to hit anything.

\

Another tremor punctuated her sentence.

Min'canari rotated the turret. There was nothing but the blackness of space. No trial of an engine. No receding shots. Nothing. He continued to move. A red ball off light appeared. It grew rapidly. He didn't even have time to fire. Flash. His monitor lit up. He shielded his eyes too late. He couldn't see. The ground hit him hard as he landed.

title.title: Bonpland's Croton  (Croton bonplandianus)
title.body:
| Latin Name | Observation Date | Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ***Croton bonplandianus*** | May 13, 2026 | Purulia, Natore, Bangladesh |


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ3W3ycJ7CXxmST5iAe4gJLnkH2iJ2mxj83oW55ntWkVR/mix_20260513_203449.jpg)



There are many unknown wild plants scattered in nature. I came across this beautiful wild plant while walking along the road on the evening of May 13. Since its structure is quite interesting, I took a few pictures of it.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbp7HmSkRERLaoNVBPWgWTNMmEfzDkZ4MXW6yG1EF4EeU/mix_20260513_225338.jpg)

With the help of the iNaturalist app, I found out that its common name is **Bonpland's Croton**. Its scientific name is ***Croton bonplandianus***. In terms of species, it is a plant of the Euphorbiaceae family.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRMGjKWUfzF3Q5t49ChscnAhbEiNiKiWWndcLUQgJJ41w/mix_20260513_225524.jpg)

Habitat: This plant usually grows as a weed along roadsides, in wastelands, and around crop fields. They are found almost everywhere in our country.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYRqZQTx1hQWymgbEK4UY4HSzLLDPYhAZTgGZAqh2JFGc/mix_20260513_202845.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT6n2vyX5hX9UmKkciY89nKhZLAjgsec8zJmUaUL2W1jV/mix_20260513_203134.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTezXV43ZXKWtbqmSRYURuujcKpVyCT1SBnsJnTjx1LMc/mix_20260513_210002.jpg)

Benefits: Although it is basically a weed, it has some medicinal properties. In rural areas, its leaf juice is often used to treat common cuts, wounds, or skin diseases.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNwFVCd72S648ARU5NysivRqUmAW2V9frFEQko8iZTJ3x/20260513_180432.jpg)

Disadvantages: It is quite harmful to farmers. It is an aggressive weed that spreads quickly and sucks nutrients from cropland. It can also be quite toxic to livestock if they accidentally eat too much.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZDYR5dpQqUjNuEz4zV5c3PXgYwwJZpUizkHvA2ijjHBU/mix_20260513_202952.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRXUgmYbAZWaYtnnTEsNQbDpYD47WmaFjBhajCtLLEWPV/20260513_180413.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSRdt779HYrwASWXCkezDcHzs2G1MNNxo7fyojfyDaj29/mix_20260513_205822.jpg)

Although it is a weed, the beauty of these tiny elements of nature is truly worth enjoyithe 

I learned about them from various sites including iNaturalist, Wikipedia and Google.

(All posts are written in Bengali and translated into English using Google Translate.)

title.title: What I Planted Without Knowing
title.body:
I was chatting with one of my friends from secondary school, and she told me that I told her something back then when we were still in school that changed a lot of things about how she sees herself. I have even forgotten I said something to her. But whatever it was, I believe that it is helping her, because it has left me in a way. I didn't bother myself asking her because our conversation left me thinking deep about all the seeds I had scattered without any awareness of where they landed. A lot of us, or lemme say some of us, always believe that we always need preparation and intention when planting. Some people always wait for the perfect time until they think they are ready. But in the real sense, seeds don't always fall that way. From our conversation, in the way we turn up for others, in that little help that we render when no one is paying attention, yeah! That is how seeds scatter. ![235432.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenproject/235432.png) Just as we have the good side of this. We also have the bad side. The careless words also scatter. That negative talk, the harsh words, those comparisons, and dismissal or even offhand comments, they all have where they land when scattered. And this is why all those gentle, loud, and quiet moments can define the types of seeds that we are planting. And at the end of the day, we never can tell where those seeds landed and where they are growing. --- Thank you for reading. >

title.body:
![IMG_20260511_062903.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/shikumi5/23yJEPAzMJp6nmwhqhxpsrUvTLgg2NEfT7e6knSNvPoo8fYP6QoMU5anAq9HNhAZ9uJr6.jpg)
I

Sometimes, we subconsciously train our minds to focus more on burdens than blessings.
Every conversation becomes about lack, pressure, stress, disappointment, or things not working out yet. Yes those struggles are real, but constantly dwelling on them can slowly shape and eventually change your mindset without you realizing it.
Make it a habit to speak more about your blessings too.o9
There’s power in the tongue. The things you repeatedly say, think about, and meditate on eventually begin to influence the kind of person you become. If your mind feeds wholly on negativity, fear, and frustration, it becomes difficult to see growth even when progress is happening quietly. It becomes difficult for you to see it. 
This doesn’t mean ignoring reality or pretending life is perfect. It simply means learning to balance your perspective. Replacing negativity with positivity. 
Be grateful for the little wins. Be grateful for growth. Be grateful that you’re still trying. Be grateful that despite everything, you’re still standing. Be grateful particularly over small things. 
What you constantly dwell on has a way of expanding in your mind. That is why protecting your thoughts and words are important.
Speak life . Speak growth. Speak hope. 
Over time, your mindset begins to follow the direction of your words. Stay positive

@shikumi5

#mindset#selfimprovement#positivity #growth#inspiration

title.title: A story of two love birds
title.body:
In the peaceful town of Zaria, where the sound of church bells mixed gently with the early morning call to prayer, two teenagers unknowingly began a journey that would change their lives forever.
Amina was a sixteen-year-old Muslim girl known for her intelligence and kindness. She loved reading novels under the mango tree behind her father’s house and dreamed of becoming a doctor someday. Her father was a respected Islamic teacher, and her family valued discipline, honor, and faith above everything else.

Across the street from Amina’s school lived David, a seventeen-year-old Christian boy whose laughter could brighten even the dullest classroom. He played the guitar in his church choir and hoped to study engineering one day. Unlike many boys his age, David was calm, respectful, and hardworking.
Although they attended the same secondary school, they rarely spoke to each other. Their worlds seemed separated by invisible walls built from religion, tradition, and family expectations.

One afternoon during a heavy rainstorm, Amina forgot her umbrella in class. Students rushed out while thunder echoed across the sky. As she stood helplessly near the corridor, David walked toward her quietly.
“You can share mine if you want,” he said nervously.
Amina hesitated for a moment before nodding softly.
That short walk home became the beginning of something neither of them expected.
Days turned into weeks. They started talking after classes first about schoolwork, then about books, dreams, fears, and life itself. Amina discovered that David respected her religion deeply. Whenever it was time for prayer, he waited patiently for her. David also noticed that Amina never mocked his faith or judged his beliefs.

Slowly, friendship grew into love.
But love in their town was not simple.
Rumors spread quickly among students. Some classmates mocked them, while others warned them that such relationships never ended well. One day, Amina’s older cousin saw her speaking with David outside the school gate and reported it to her family.
That evening, her father’s face was filled with disappointment.
“Amina,” he said firmly, “our ways are different. These things only bring pain.”

On the other side of town, David’s mother also warned him carefully.
“People may not understand your feelings now,” she said, “and hatred can grow where understanding is absent.”
The pressure became unbearable. Their families restricted them from seeing each other. At school, they avoided eye contact to prevent more trouble, but silence hurt them more than words ever could.
One evening, during the town’s cultural festival, fate brought them together again near a quiet riverside away from the crowd and music.
“I never wanted to hurt anyone,” Amina whispered, tears gathering in her eyes.
“Neither did I,” David replied. “I just wanted us to be accepted.”

For a long moment, neither of them spoke. The river moved gently under the moonlight as if carrying away their worries.
Then Amina smiled sadly.
“Maybe love is not always about being together forever,” she said softly. “Maybe sometimes it teaches people understanding.”
David looked at her with pain in his eyes, yet he understood.
Before they parted that night, they made a promise not to allow religion turn into hatred inside their hearts. They would respect each other’s beliefs no matter where life took them.
Years later, Amina became a medical doctor, while David became an engineer. Though life separated them, neither forgot the lessons they learned from each other.
Whenever people spoke carelessly about religion and division, they both remembered a simple truth:
Love had once shown them that humanity comes before difference.
And somewhere deep inside their hearts, the memory of their young love remained like a quiet song carried by the wind of old Zaria nights.

links.title: Every 11th of May is My Day 🎂 | Birthday Vibes at the Jollof Bay Buka with a Bowl of Amala 😊
links.body:
>Every 11th of May is my day. Happy Birthday to Olamide, aka justola1 on hive. Aka Creator of Hive Studio ⭐\n
\n

/>

Dear Gentle Readers, So I am 25 years old now. Wow, I am still pretty young but yet feel so old, LOL.

There were times when I was lost, confused and wasn't really sure what I was doing with my life. Older readers would undertand what I am saying because you probably went though this phase.

Well, cheers to this age and I hope it comes with a deeper sense of purpose, growth, peace of mind, and beautiful opportunities.

/>

So, I was supposed to write a post on my birthday but after I went out to have my fun, I caught a flu so it delayed sharing this post.

Honestly, the celebration was small but it was fun. It's the most fun I've had in a long time. I got calls from family, friends hyped me on their social media and I even got treated my favorite meal (Amala and Ewedu).

Lets give you a quick gist:

So, I spent most of the night at the Jollof Bay Buka. It was my first time being there and I enjoyed my night. I ate Amala and Ewedu with goat meat. It was the best meal I have had in a while now.

/>

I am not a fan of taking beverage while eating, I prefer to just drink water.

/>

The environment was calm and aesthetically pleasing. I went on to take pictures and even videos, here are some I took:

/>

Here are 25 things I have learnt in the last 25 years of my life:

No.Lesson
1.Brilliance(1) X Bad character(0) = 0.
In summary, build a good character. 🧠✨
2.Always be open to learning 📘. Only a fool thinks he knows it all.
3.Listen More, talk less. 👂
4.In every new phase of your life, read a book. It reduces the number of mistakes you make 📚
5.Networking is easy. Ask yourself, what can I give? 🤝
6.Empathy 💞
7.Your mindset determines your growth. Always think positively 🧠🌄
8.The best investment you can have is on yourself 💡
9.Sleep more. That's an underrated Medicine 🛌💤
10.Have a mentor 🧓
11.Be principled ⚖️
12.Discipline > motivation 🔥
13.Never be idle, always pick up something to learn 🛠️
14.Budgeting and financial literacy shouldn't be ignored 💰📊
15.Progress > Perfection. Start where you are, use what you have. ⏳
16.People come and go, cherish those who stay, but don't force anyone to remain. ❤️‍🩹
17.Guard your Mental Health 🧘‍♂️
18.Learn to rest, not quit 🌙
19.Growth is uncomfortable, embrace it 🌱
20.Be curious. Ask questions. ❓
21.Comparison is a thief of joy. Run your own race 🏁
22.Pray, even when things feel good. Not just when they're bad 🙏
23.Good communication saves relationships. Talking saves both parties a whole lot of stress🗣️
24.Every year won't be the same, but it comes with a lesson worth learning.✨
25.Be patient. A lot of good things happened this year and I wished I was more patient instead of overthinking and worrying all the time.
>If you're reading this, please send me a kind word 🤗 or a prayer. No pressure, just positive vibes 🌤️. Here's to 25, a year of better discipline, quiet wins, and louder gratitude 🥂.

links.title: Tears of Zainab
links.body:
In the ancient city of Kano, where the evening breeze carried the smell of suya and roasted corn through the narrow streets, there lived a young woman named Zainab. She was known for her quiet beauty, gentle voice, and the respect she showed to everyone around her. Many people admired her, especially when she walked gracefully to the market with her hijab flowing behind her like soft silk in the harmattan wind.
Zainab was married to a man named Musa, a trader who sold grains in the busy market. At first, their marriage looked peaceful. During weddings and naming ceremonies, people pointed at them and said, “Allah ya ba su zaman lafiya,” meaning, “May God give them a peaceful home.” But behind the mud walls of their small compound was a different story.

Musa was a man filled with anger. Whenever business was poor or life became difficult, he poured his frustration on Zainab. He shouted at her for little things food with too much salt, water not cold enough, or clothes not washed quickly. At first, the shouting turned into insults. Then insults became slaps. Soon, the slaps became severe beatings.
Every night, Zainab cried silently on her prayer mat after Musa slept. She hid her bruises beneath long veils and fake smiles. In Hausa society, many women were taught to endure suffering in silence because they feared shame, gossip, or being called a failed wife. So whenever her mother asked, “Zainab, lafiya kuwa?” she always replied softly, “Alhamdulillah, everything is fine.”
One rainy evening, Musa returned home angry after losing money to dishonest business partners. Without listening to explanations, he accused Zainab of disrespecting him because dinner was not ready on time. His rage became uncontrollable. He pushed her violently against the wall while their little daughter, Aisha, cried in fear from a corner of the room.

That night changed everything.
As Zainab looked into her daughter’s frightened eyes, she realized the violence was no longer affecting only her. It was destroying the innocent soul of a child. She remembered the words of an elderly woman in the neighborhood who once said, “A home without peace is like a well without water.”
The next morning, with tears in her eyes but courage in her heart, Zainab visited the local women’s support group near the central mosque. The women welcomed her warmly. Some of them had suffered similar pain. For the first time in many years, Zainab spoke openly about her suffering.
The community leaders and elders later invited Musa for counseling. At first, he denied everything. He believed beating a wife was a sign of authority. But after hearing the words of the imam about kindness, patience, and how Islam condemns oppression, Musa became silent with shame. The imam reminded him that a man’s strength is not in violence but in compassion.

Change did not happen overnight. Trust broken for years cannot heal in one day. Musa attended counseling sessions and slowly began to understand the damage he had caused. He apologized to Zainab sincerely, though the scars remained in her heart.
Zainab also changed. She was no longer the frightened woman who hid her pain behind smiles. She began teaching young girls in the neighborhood that marriage should never become a prison of fear. She encouraged women to speak up, seek help, and protect themselves and their children.
Years later, people in the community still spoke about Zainab not because she suffered, but because she found the courage to break the silence.

And in many homes across the city, mothers began telling their daughters:
“Patience is good, but silence in the face of violence can destroy a family.”

links.title: 🌍 Cotonou in Motion — Between Lagoon, Sky and Street Life
links.body:
Today, I crossed the new bridge near Dantokpa Market, and once again, Cotonou reminded me why this city never sleeps.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR5Wygrmh9yucYLuLyQH97p95LZ8h1KcHUSKG3uf3tGE9/1778694382896.jpg)

From the road of a Zémidjan, the city unfolds differently.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXzKgDFs2cDT5C6SLoeVhqEU6AqvKfgLMd1ETiWLs8gMi/1778694403811.jpg)

The lagoon breathes beside the traffic, reflecting the blue sky and the moving clouds above. Small wooden boats quietly cross the water while the streets vibrate with engines, voices, and daily hustle.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVmDCw5yfvGYKktG3SUL2KSTSzXqAuDrq4hytFfkcQeuE/1778697557350.jpg)

Along the bridge, life appears in many forms at once:
a street vendor searching for customers under the sun, a man asking for help at the edge of the road,
motorcycles weaving through the city’s rhythm, and in the distance, the silhouette of a mosque rising calmly above the urban movement.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdcaE2yDFTgEmYvmjYhT9JzAFmeYTjAuHLRE2CXdPwm8P/1778697954097.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV5GmShVnLQTdje2yWh75jeZ68VZVs3Y4z8hKV9LFsF5u/1778697954247.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSDo5FbYQRx8JRvwWkwhbpdBNhU7bRTvkdw1ZM1FaiytY/1778697954356.jpg)

This is Cotonou.
Raw. Fast. Beautiful. Alive.
What I love about this city is its contrast.
Water and concrete.
Silence and noise.
Struggle and hope.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVQHYBR4Lqu12FAbVvvoS8eWhAKAtpwMXpafbfAmfEgT7/1778698027213.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbVNpSstdSVPA8jtcXT6ycZ41doLTqfJUVUFcKQL2x38M/1778698027368.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR5Wygrmh9yucYLuLyQH97p95LZ8h1KcHUSKG3uf3tGE9/1778698027500.jpg)

Modern bridges connecting deeply human stories.
The clouds today carried a special light, and the lagoon reflected the full energy of the city like a giant mirror of movement and resilience.
Cotonou is not only a place.
It is an atmosphere.
An African pulse constantly in motion.
— Dr JPEG

links.title: Cauliflower burgers [ENG/ESP]
links.body:
> Since it’s about learning, about trying new recipes, today I bring you another invention. For some time I wanted to make something new with this vegetable, but I hadn’t been able to get it. Can you believe it’s an odyssey to find a good cauliflower in my city? Well, at least one that’s close to me hahaha... Anyway, now that I have it, I had to make the most of it, so I went to look for my recipe with the ingredients and said to myself, let’s do it. Today’s recipe is about some delicious **Cauliflower Burgers**.
![post hive (52).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/243MDyBbENU12Xv97ow1XNKa4vgHKwy2jmRyfZTLFdUoqiYJ2LNAY3dRWAhDYnWdzpHDQ.png)
--- The ingredients are as follows: ## Ingredients: - 3 tablespoons of whole wheat flour - 1 small cauliflower - 1/2 onion - 1 egg - 2 tablespoons of grated white cheese - pepper, salt, and oregano
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EowFbsg51Y5pegwghGGPuFcKhHR1wAbzvGLuL9pKb3wLA8LEBp65q5JticmC1EY2hY9.png)
## Preparation: The first step to make these hamburgers is to wash our cauliflower well, with vinegar. Once this is done, we cook it with a little water until it softens. Once done, we are going to mash it with a potato masher; you can blend it if you want. I found it more practical this way. The idea is for it to turn out well like a dough.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoChfqQtwtctQcdDg7YtRqrhJxQ1ENwMFAAQXqZgGkSmc645MZsAZuWGQjDi7ura6kE.png)
To this, we will add a little salt, oregano, and pepper, with the onion previously chopped into small pieces.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGxvkWiiXVQgp6k35zEtYwTZ9SouLkgc1CXosfSBF6LQgVzBFC9YJtrwg5Sb7F1H6o.png)
Now we add the flour, which by the way I used whole wheat, but I sifted it, finally we add the cheese.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EogMJTdWoCMxvXaDbKyBgy5GZ8E3N8xPC1Tc1Kj69VuZQmbcsSd6pgMfdH1dneoTFbu.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EonjyN8hBYVFca8eTZFbfJsAtK4fLSRx4gc69PrzfnboYT3jvtcwS27pgBYhiZ2Jwai.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGwsvgwYxbMRCyhYm3G9gKbp4AR296hogrEATMHKKKfsYMHHaPYXYdR9CLcYeMhjtF.png)
Now we mix everything, we will get a dough like this, soft, we just have to make small round cookies, and put them in the oven.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoAafLrMDGj6oF2C1XEDCboRujE5kUQhkUzh39q1azRPee8TykDqkv2ujDQ8HYfizCB.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/Eoc7zgtVGNj6oxQ5c76EhSv4C6cH1Gjp2kGi81wPKwbkWC5xovZNBQUDSgtR2u8btC9.png)
I left it for 20 minutes, then I took it out, flipped them over and left them for another 20 minutes, and that's how they turned out. You can leave it longer, on low heat, but they're fine, they're tasty, and as you can see, easy to prepare.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EouB9QP2t61vticYfjhc13pnvQD2cZX8bNP23qtMWfhXKcVv5nPLcwzS5v8VP6VUQnp.png)
I hope you like this recipe, and that you feel encouraged to prepare it. What do you think? I look forward to reading your comments.
SPANISH VERSION

Como de aprender se trata, de probar recetas nuevas, hoy les traigo otro invento, desde hace un tiempo que quería hacer algo nuevo, con este vegetal, pero no lo había conseguido, pueden creer que es una odisea encontrar una buena coliflor en mi ciudad, bueno por lo menos que me quede cerca jajaja... En fin, ahora que la tengo, tenia que aprovecharla, así que fui a buscar mi receta, con los ingredientes y me dije, vamos hacerlo, la receta de hoy se trata de unas ricas **Hamburguesas de Coliflor**.

![post hive (52).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/243MDyBbENU12Xv97ow1XNKa4vgHKwy2jmRyfZTLFdUoqiYJ2LNAY3dRWAhDYnWdzpHDQ.png)
--- The ingredients are as follows: ## Ingredients: - 3 Cucharada de harina integral - 1 planta de coliflor pequeña - 1/2 cebolla - 1 Huevo - 2 cucharadas de queso blanco rallado - pimienta, sal y orégano
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EowFbsg51Y5pegwghGGPuFcKhHR1wAbzvGLuL9pKb3wLA8LEBp65q5JticmC1EY2hY9.png)
## Preparation: El primer paso para hacer estas hamburguesas es lavar bien nuestra coliflor, con vinagre, una vez hecho esto, la llevamos a cocinar con un poco de agua, hasta que se ablande. Una vez hecho hecho, con un pisapapas vamos a triturarlas, pueden licuarlas si quieren, a mi me resulto mas practico así, la idea es que nos quede bien como una masa.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoChfqQtwtctQcdDg7YtRqrhJxQ1ENwMFAAQXqZgGkSmc645MZsAZuWGQjDi7ura6kE.png)
A esto le añadiremos un poco de sal, orégano y pimienta, con la cebolla previamente picada en trocitos pequeños.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGxvkWiiXVQgp6k35zEtYwTZ9SouLkgc1CXosfSBF6LQgVzBFC9YJtrwg5Sb7F1H6o.png)
Ahora le agregamos la harina, la cual por cierto use la integral, pero la cerni, finalmente le colocamos el queso.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EogMJTdWoCMxvXaDbKyBgy5GZ8E3N8xPC1Tc1Kj69VuZQmbcsSd6pgMfdH1dneoTFbu.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EonjyN8hBYVFca8eTZFbfJsAtK4fLSRx4gc69PrzfnboYT3jvtcwS27pgBYhiZ2Jwai.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoGwsvgwYxbMRCyhYm3G9gKbp4AR296hogrEATMHKKKfsYMHHaPYXYdR9CLcYeMhjtF.png)
Ahora mezclamos todo, nos quedara una masa así, suave, solo queda crear pequeñas masitas redondas, y llevarlo al horno.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EoAafLrMDGj6oF2C1XEDCboRujE5kUQhkUzh39q1azRPee8TykDqkv2ujDQ8HYfizCB.png)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/Eoc7zgtVGNj6oxQ5c76EhSv4C6cH1Gjp2kGi81wPKwbkWC5xovZNBQUDSgtR2u8btC9.png)
Yo lo deje 20 minutos, luego la saque, las voltee y deje otros 20 minutos, y así me quedaron. Pueden dejarla mas tiempo, a fuego lento, pero están bien, quedan ricas, y como ven fáciles de preparar.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ikigaidesign/EouB9QP2t61vticYfjhc13pnvQD2cZX8bNP23qtMWfhXKcVv5nPLcwzS5v8VP6VUQnp.png)
Espero les guste esta receta, y se animen a prepararla, que les parece, los leo.

---

This is the video series for an oil painting 'Wisteria' I did from 2016-2020.  The painting was destroyed in 2021 due to a number of reasons, but mainly: the painting's faulty experimental linseed-epoxide substrait, Covid-19 crushing lockdowns, extreme poverty, family attacks and ongoing US government (Big Tech + Big Media) censorship of me and my 30 years of artwork.

Its not ideal to not be able to show this piece, but I still gained the knowledge of how to do it and invented several useful oil painting mediums & varnishes used in its creation which never yellowed and still cannot be bought anywhere.

I am posting these videos for posterity and for people that are interested in seeing an oil painting created from start to finish in the Baroque style evolved for the 21st century.  I also must have deleted some of the initial videos when I did the quick underpainting, but what still exists, I give to you.

I hope this can be an educational experience as no gallery will show any of my controversial art even today.

Hoy, mi caminata por la ciudad fue realmente inspiradora. Comencé mi recorrido en un parque cercano, donde vi a un grupo de niños jugando al fútbol. Sus risas y gritos llenaban el aire, y me recordó la energía contagiosa de la infancia. Hablé brevemente con uno de los padres, que me contó que sus hijos estaban entrenando para un torneo local. Fue genial ver a la comunidad reunida alrededor de un evento tan positivo. A medida que avanzaba, pasé por una pequeña galería de arte al aire libre. Muchos artistas locales estaban exhibiendo sus obras, y me detuve a observar un mural colorido que representaba escenas de la vida urbana. Conocí a una artista que estaba pintando en vivo; me habló sobre su proceso creativo y la importancia del arte en la vida cotidiana. Fue fascinante ver cómo ponía su pasión en cada trazo. En general, fue una caminata no solo física, sino también emocional y cultural. Me encanta cómo cada día en la ciudad me ofrece la oportunidad de conectarme con personas y descubrir algo nuevo. _This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). I’m not seeing a recent official thread specifically about the purple crown bug from [@leofinance](https://inleo.io/@leofinance) or [Khal](https://inleo.io/@khaleelkazi), so this looks more like a stale entitlement/display issue than a mystery extra subscription. links.title: Witness Townhall, Sunday May 17 at 12pm EDT
links.body:
![Townhall May 17.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/shadowspub/23vsJ52fkhdpyHjT1Jy6LVokVaRJzoPkEwgVa1qbKyPJPE8UV3wkW3w2WAA1jFxv9PPQM.png)

It’s almost time for the third Witness Townhall of 2026 taking place in in the official Hive discord. 

It will take place on Sunday May 17th at 12pm ET in the [official Hive Discord](https://discord.gg/3sUqmmxwWm). That would be 4pm UTC 

It  is an opportunity to meet the Witnesses: 

- find out what they do on the chain 
- what projects are important to them
- how they feel about topics of interest on the chain 
- for them to share about upcoming developments or possible developments

At the Townhall on April 18th Witness attendance was down. I was asked to do weekend Townhalls. We’ll try them and see how the attendance works out. 
 
Those who participated were given opportunity to weigh in on their opinions about factors that could be influencing the price of Hive. Not everyone agreed but the conversation was respectful. 

Here is the recording from the Townhall: 

https://youtu.be/qopjjg3MKdM

By hearing the Witnesses, community members get a sense of who the Witnesses are and can make better informed voting decisions. 

The townhall is meant to be a two way discussion between Witnesses and the rest of the community. The text is monitored for people to be able to put questions and concerns to raise. 

I’m your host for the event. For those who don’t know me, I’ve been on Hive since August 2016. I host the long running Pimp Your Post Thursday (PYPT) and am one of the co-hosts on the Hive Thrive show held each Tuesday. On the legacy chain I hosted a monthly Witness Chat, so this is returning to that format on Hive. 

It doesn’t matter if you’re new to Hive or been here forever, your vote counts. So come on out and listen in, ask questions and learn.

links.title: Wednesday walk from Brunlanes to Bøkeskogen
links.body: ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPzQdW8ZSfTrcB4tz1itqreFAj2ZK2V3EqicT8bm3jPSh/ff.jpg) Hello, friends and the #WednesdayWalk community! Happy Wednesday to all of you. We’ve recently traveled from the tropics to the Northern Hemisphere, where spring is just beginning. When we were in India, we heard that spring was arriving early this year. However, upon our arrival here, it seemed to be progressing quite slowly. Normally, by the end of April, cherry trees, pear trees, and apple trees are in full bloom, and various wildflowers surround the landscape. This year, though, aside from the anemones and the bright yellow carpet of dandelions and marsh marigold, there are only a few blossoms available. Most trees are still waiting for their leaves to bud, and some beech trees are just starting to sprout. The lingering effects of last year's cyclone, Amy, are still felt in the forest. We went to visit the Brunelness Forest, where the white anemones bloom like a beautiful white carpet—an ideal spot for a lovely walk among the tiny flowers. However, we were disappointed to see broken trees scattered throughout the forest, which created quite a mess and made it less enjoyable for photography. We then headed towards Helgeroa Road and were delighted to see the greenery there. Some trees have developed soft, beautiful green leaves, enhancing the landscape's charm.

> The Brunalaness didn't appear very interesting. The forest has lost many trees from last year's Amy hurricane, making it look quite sparse. This is not a very good feeling, but we couldn't have control over nature.
> But as we headed towards Helgeroa road, things changed very quickly. The view of green, lush trees with soft leaves, those flowers of anemone, dandelion, and marsh marigold, gave us a happy smile.

> The lush greenery of the forest was truly refreshing for the mind. After spending some time playing with the flowers and taking pictures, we continued toward Larvik. My husband was driving while I captured the scenery through my camera. Each time we visit, experiencing the natural beauty here feels unique and delightful.
> The Bridge over the River Logan on E18 highway, and the view of the Silver Sea from Longestrand Hill is stunning.

> As soon as we reached the Bøkeskogen forest, after seeing the condition of the forest, we were again emotional. The forest, which was full of trees, had become very sparse, Amy's feat. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeQksmFs8wYAxi7rfVH1tHeK6MUcb5qDVPq4Thj3yRJUH/p1060295.jpg) ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmU6362Qe9pd4bWf2GhtmKazfaBAgkELBHkZnbrwdKBcDP/p1060235.jpg) These two photos are from a couple of years back; this was the condition of Bøkeskogen exactly on 13 May, when we were walking there.

> But we continued our walk, and finding some good spots, were content with whatever was available and seeking the best. We couldn't find a lush of anemone flowers, normally it blooms every year, or the very green feeling while walking around. Last year's damage was unforgettable, which is an example to see in the spring.
>\nBut after walking around, we came across the other part of the forest. It is nice and green and has not much damage here. \n

>
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYxUeDTxKPg6vyiSpL7o4FmJBcP4rbwp15nev1tvbw3zG/20260502_120429.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQaHWqDRiyp1BWuHU5VYdArwbDcq9HPiLBrDqLgX4MZ6F/20260502_120547.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZdh3EfJc7mr34667ZHbjYEDf8YGH8JSBihwAt5QPBeVc/20260502_120606.jpg)
After exploring this part of the forest, we felt very happy. After spending some time in the greenery and fresh air, we headed back home. This was my Wednesday walk from Brunnala to Helgeroa and Bøkeskogen. I'm pleased to share this experience with you through the community initiative #WednesdayWalk by @tattoodjay. Thank you very much!

links.title: Childhood memories (Recuerdos de infancia) [EN/ES]
links.body:
> My three life companions, those who accompanied me in my younger years. In the town where I was born, of white houses with gardens in each one, clean and meticulously neat streets and a tranquility that ran through every space, where children ran around playing, yes, playing in an era where cell phones were a crazy idea of a dreamy guy. In that neighborhood we met with our friends, on those summer evenings and holidays, the most anticipated time for us, where we could enjoy full freedom, games, sleep late, walk through the small forests, sell lemonade for a few cents to quench the thirst generated by the inclement sun. And how to forget the summer love, those loves that were innocent and pure, that moved our hearts and minds, that at that stage of our life began to experience new sensations and feelings. I remember Lili, my beautiful neighbor, with blond hair like the sun's rays, blue eyes like the sea itself, freckles that adorn her snow-white complexion and that thin mouth with a beautiful pink hue. That girl was my weakness when I saw her passing by anywhere, I can't blame myself for the shyness that came over me when I saw her, it was too much for my inexperienced mind. I think many felt those butterflies in the stomach, the cold sweat, the head about to explode and the desire to run out when that person we liked came from in front, a total terror. But thanks to my friends I was able to find the courage to talk to Lili, on an afternoon where the sunset had made the sky have a beautiful orange color, under that splendid sky, Lili gave me a kiss, a short, fleeting kiss, but I felt my whole world move, faint before a new feeling blooming, like water in a fountain. I can say that it was one of the most wonderful experiences of my life, something that is engraved like a tattoo on the soul and I will take it to the end of the road through this world. There was no shortage of crazy things with my three friends, my cronies, almost infinite experiences, personal growth, experiences built every day, those days that defined us as adults. I remember the first cigar, the first drink, the first night getaway under that full moon, all with those cronies, and despite all the crazy things we took care of each other, like brothers, because our souls had combined as we will never do with another person before. And how to forget the wonderful walks, excursions into the unknown, to the small forest where it was easy to get lost in so much beauty, squirrels roaming the trees, the little birds flying and singing incessantly, the big trees to which we climbed like monkeys and at the top we felt like the kings of the world. The tours of the caves, those mysterious caves, that's what we called them. The terror and emotion they generated, looking at that huge hole and dark as night, but that with my friends we had the courage to enter and travel to a totally unknown and incredible world, we felt Indiana Jones, explorers looking for treasures, which were often treasures of beautiful memories, that as adults we value more than anything. Finally, how to forget the dips in the river, those refreshing dips in those summer times, where the sun punished the bodies and the river that source to cool us down. The water was murky from the river's contact with humans, but that didn't matter. We were young and we enjoyed everything without thinking about the consequences, we just immersed ourselves in that water, feeling the embrace of freshness before the heat, it was a pleasure that we did not miss on every day of the summer. Of course, I will not forget, the fat Polisky, with his famous cannonballs, which seemed to take all the water out of the river and the laughter and cheers we gave him. I will not forget the skinny Norman, at first afraid when entering the river and with my help we managed to get him to dive between screams of excitement. I will not forget the blond Lucas, the most intrepid of all, the one who always goes ahead of everyone and is not afraid of new experiences, the one who first dived in and came out with a big smile. Memories I will never forget with my best friends and experiences that made me who I am today. Those times that will not return and that revive with every breath, like one of those eighties movies. ![bannerhive.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVHP6CkxhCEAu67zAoPbfRAJc6QCPZdGNXvJLHraenhgL/bannerhive.jpg)
Español #### Recuerdos de infancia

> Mis tres compañeros de vida, aquellos que me acompañaron en mis años juveniles. En el pueblo donde nací, de casas blancas con jardines en cada una, calles limpias y meticulosamente aseadas y una tranquilidad que recorría cada espacio, por donde los niños corrían jugando, sí, jugando en una época donde los celulares eran una loca idea de un tipo soñador. En aquel vecindario nos reuníamos con nuestros amigos, en aquellas tarde de verano y vacaciones, la época más esperada por nosotros, donde podíamos disfrutar de una plena libertad, juegos, dormir hasta tarde, pasear por los pequeños bosques, vender limonada por unos centavos para calmar la sed generada por el inclemente sol. Y como olvidar el amor veraniego, aquellos amores que eran inocentes y puros, que movían nuestros corazones y mente, que en esa etapa de nuestra vida empezaba a experimentar nuevas sensaciones y sentimientos. Recuerdo a Lili, mi bella vecina, de cabellos rubios como los rayos del sol, ojos azules como el mismo mar, unas pecas que adornan su cutis blanco como la nieve y aquella boca delgada con un bello tono rosado. Esa chica era mi debilidad cuando la veía pasar por cualquier lugar, no puedo culparme por la timidez que me embargaba al verla, era demasiado para mi mente inexperta. Creo que muchos sintieron aquellas mariposas en el estómago, el sudor frío, la cabeza a punto de estallar y los deseos de salir corriendo cuando aquella persona que nos gustaba venía de frente, un terror total. Pero gracias a mis compinches pude sacar el valor para hablar con Lili, en una tarde donde el ocaso había hecho que el firmamento tuviera un hermoso color anaranjado, bajo ese firmamento espléndido, Lili me dio un beso, un beso corto, fugaz, pero que sentí mover todo mi mundo, desfallecer ante un nuevo sentimiento que florecía, como el agua en una fuente. Puedo decir que fue una de las experiencias más maravillosas de mi vida, algo que se graba como un tatuaje en el alma y lo llevaré hasta el final del camino por este mundo. No podían faltar las locuras con mis tres amigos, mis alcahuetas, vivencias casi infinitas, crecimientos personales, experiencias construidas en cada día, aquellos días que nos definieron como adultos. Recuerdo el primer cigarro, la primera bebida, la primera escapada nocturna bajo aquella luna llena, todo con aquellos compinches, y a pesar de todas las locuras nos cuidábamos, como hermanos, porque nuestras almas se habían compaginado como nunca antes lo haremos con otra persona. Y como olvidar los paseos maravillosos, excursiones hacia lo desconocido, hacia el pequeño bosque donde era fácil perderse en tanta belleza, ardillas recorriendo los árboles, los pajaritos volando y cantando sin cesar, los grandes árboles a los que trepábamos como micos y en la cima nos sentíamos como los reyes del mundo. Los recorridos por las cuevas, aquellas cuevas misteriosas, así las llamábamos. El terror y emoción que generaban, el mirar ese hueco enorme y oscuro como la noche, pero que con mis amigos teníamos la valentía de entrar y viajar a un mundo totalmente desconocido e increíble, nos sentíamos Indiana Jones, exploradores buscando tesoros, que muchas veces eran tesoros de recuerdos hermosos, que de adultos valoramos más que ninguna cosa. Por último, como olvidar los chapuzones en el rio, aquellos chapuzones refrescantes en esas épocas de verano, donde el sol castigaba los cuerpos y el río esa fuente para refrescarnos. El agua era turbia por el contacto del rio con los humanos, pero eso no importaba. Éramos jóvenes y disfrutábamos de todo sin pensar en las consecuencias, solo nos sumergíamos en aquella agua, sintiendo el abrazo de la frescura ante el calor, era un placer que no nos perdíamos en cada día del verano. Eso sí, no olvidaré, al gordo Polisky, con sus famosas balas de cañón, que parecían sacar toda el agua del río y las risas y vítores que le hacíamos. No olvidaré al flaco Norman, al principio temeroso al entrar al río y con mi ayuda lográbamos que se zambullera entre gritos de emoción. No olvidaré al rubio Lucas, el más intrépido de todos, el que siempre va adelante de todos y no teme a las nuevas experiencias, él que primero se zambullía y salía con una gran sonrisa. Recuerdos que nunca olvidaré con mis mejores amigos y experiencias que me hicieron lo que soy hoy. Tiempos aquellos que no volverán y que en cada suspiro reviven, como una película de esas de los ochentas. ![bannerhive.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVHP6CkxhCEAu67zAoPbfRAJc6QCPZdGNXvJLHraenhgL/bannerhive.jpg)
