![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmc78Ea3tLfh3gBfbTotpGbmrdqPMFo4XzLBrHDe1dXewa/20260509_080931.jpg)
So of the 4 new windows, one had a broken  pane in the lower sash: they gave me the option of waiting for the new glass or go ahead and install now and replace that sash later
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTbtcJrWW2CZqfV9ddSXPzZo7A9JenkBrgXTGZAxMJdhd/image.png)
You could see all the way thru my bedroom
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaq1LCb1chXkDsorfAh71PVfGdz1Pf7kReHy2GXFq1eMt/20260509_095445.jpg)
Finished for the time being
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcT3nZL8TFghKm2EnEwDp3MoLXjsbkZsFRVK7v24Zqyva/20260509_153115.jpg)
From yesterday:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZChiGtK8PXd24mMpGrZVfXteopnMMeqqQ8k7hc7CHjDm/image.png)
___
So this morning, I was reluctantly preparing to try and cut some grass/weeds when I looked up to see Felix with a Wabbit in his mouth
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSPTN79zXxkzd8wmEMgfEdicMpL3vqKsKZoz9KSrRK4yE/20260513_091444.jpg)
I haven't seen many wabbits here, but since people are cutting down much of the forest around here, I am not surprised nowadays

He apparently had no clue what to do with it
https://vimeo.com/1191942375?fl=tl&fe=ec
After he lost control of it more than once, I followed, captured, dispatched, skinned and gutted it for him
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUA56iZQobrjNQRuxi8F42J62qKL58wLYkwh1f7cSg1Se/20260513_093515.jpg)
Back home in the woods, our house cats would routinely catch wabbits, leave them at the front door. Mama would skin and gut them then give them back so that the cat could eat its catch

↑Eggplant Blossom↑

No help with the black mold from the Insurance nor VA (yet)

>from Imgflip Meme Generator ## **The Great Equalizer** There is one currency that no king can hoard, no billionaire can buy, and no algorithm can manipulate. In this singular fact lies the deepest truth of the human condition: we are not defined by what we are given, but by what we do with it. ## **The Question of Allocation** So, how are you spending your time? This is not a question of productivity. It is not a question of efficiency. It is a question of morality. It is the quiet audit of the soul. Are you spending your hours doing right, or doing wrong? links.body:
There's something about emotions that a lot of us need to understand, and for us to do that, we need to be the intelligent type, that way there won't be any issues. Because emotional intelligence is what helps us to control the way we react to words, situations and actions, emotional intelligence is what helps us to understand and not misunderstand people, emotional intelligence as well is what helps us build good and healthy relationships with people.  So, it is very obvious that beyond emotions we need to be as well wise and intelligent.




![1001033736.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23tvcDtfhLhwrTQyVVvJNeU76hYF2HurhbjskdYVPXdPuYsUr7UZ3MU2TxBQw9oSSGS4m.png)




Like I said earlier, emotions help us to control how we react to things, meaning it will show in the way we talk, respond and all, it will show if we are intelligent/matured emotionally or not. And as individuals this is a personal skill or attribute that we all should possess.



Let's say you have friend whom you're very close too, now this friend suddenly became distant somehow, you don't know why and all, as someone who's emotionally intelligent, you're not supposed to assume that the person in question lost interest in you, or does not want to have anything to do with you again, you're not even expected to get angry and begin acting somehow, what you should do is, find time to talk to this person, and if there's no way you could, then try to understand that maybe he/she is facing problems or some personal issues, that way you're not just helping and saving yourself, but you're as well saving your friendship.


![1001033735.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/AJhUoof2A9wsvReJydAjBGeKxSz2GhpLTgNCsmeo9HJJ1UHqDvjWrArrRQHJPW7.png)


The prompt also made mention of self awareness, which happens to be a very important party of emotional intelligence, as it is something that helps us to understand ourselves first. A person who doesn't understand himself/herself cannot understand another person. And this lack of self awareness is what often leads us to reacting to things immediately, being impatient, getting angry unnecessarily and all which can eventually lead to  damages that could have been avoided.



Emotional intelligence is a skill that we should all possess, it will help us at home, in school, in our relationships, in places of worship, in discussion groups, and even online. And the way we face or react and respond to situations can either destroy a relationship or make it stronger, so we should be wise with our emotions.

links.title: Simple methods to follow when buying used cars
links.body:
How to avoid buying a lemon and paying for a peach, and the buyer and the seller both benefit

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vyaNeKZjHcI&pp=ygUldGhpbmdzIHRvIGxvb2sgd2hlbiBidXlpbmcgYSB1c2VkIGNhcg%3D%3D

**Buying a used car has become popular**

The car manufacturing industry is a major contributor to the global economy, and despite harsh competition among firms for the construction of models with similar features and the subsequent downward movement of prices, there is still room for healthy profits to be made.

However, it is should be pointed out that it is the selling branches of car manufacturers that bring in the money, and that is where actual profits are made.

During the present difficult economic conditions at a global level and, in fact, during any period of time when economic difficulties are faced by a smaller or larger segment of the population, choosing to buy a second-hand car, instead of a new one, is certainly a popular option.

**What to check when buying a second-hand car**

There are many long-established companies with a good reputation in the market, where a prospective buyer can be given the opportunity to make his/her selection from a wide variety of models and prices.

Another important point to consider, on top of choosing a reputable second-hand dealer, is to carry out a detailed and careful inspection of the car’s service history and MOT history, as well as the date of production and mileage.

A general rule of thumb is not to be tempted to buy a used car if it is older than ten years, for many reasons, such as the fact that technology is quickly made obsolete, and ten years time is a long period of time. Besides, wear is a thing that you have to take for granted, and the older is the age of a used car, the more visible wear is.

A parameter that you should not forget to take into consideration is the fact that second-hand car dealers want to make a profit, and usually a hefty one, in order to cover any costs, operating expenses, and the risk of long periods of business inactivity.

**Buying from a private owner-seller**

Therefore, every time they buy a car from a private seller to resell it to a customer, they try to reduce their offer, and in fact, they set a “price ceiling”, above which, their profit starts to gets diminished.

On the other hand, the price, at which, they sell the same car to a potential buyer, is not reduced accordingly, which means that they will try every possible trick to maximize their profit margin by buying cheap and selling at a much higher price.

From this point of view, it is a good idea, and it is actually a method that is often used by many used cars buyers, to choose to buy from a private owner-seller.

As a result of following this approach, the chances for a second-hand buyer to get a better deal are higher, since the seller does not run a business, and therefore, they are not really interested into making a business profit.

As an effect, he or she may accept a lower price, in order to make a fast sale, and get rid of a possibly unwanted car that has become a liability, rather than an asset, to them.

What is more, a private owner-seller will benefit from such a deal, as well, in spite of the lower selling price, since it is more likely that they will still get more money than what a second-hand car dealer will offer them.

So, it’s a win-win situation, and if there are is any chance that the buyer and the seller are relatives, friends, or know each other, then the element of trust will be even stronger, and this will serve as informal guarantee of the credibility and accuracy of a second-hand car’s maintenance records, helping the buyer to get a more realistic picture of what the car is actually worth paying for.

_Sources and further reading:_

[How to buy a used car in 10 steps](https://www.edmunds.com/car-buying/10-steps-to-buying-a-used-car.html)

[Buying a used car: Your complete guide](https://www.autoexpress.co.uk/car-news/used-car-guide/95715/buying-a-used-car-your-complete-guide)

[Buying a used car: The ultimate checklist](https://www.rac.co.uk/drive/advice/buying-and-selling-guides/buying-a-used-car/)

[6 clever tips and tricks for buying a used car](https://www.alresfordgarage.co.uk/news/6-clever-tips-and-tricks-for-buying-a-used-car/88503)

[Used Car Buying Guide: All You Need to Know About Buying a Used Vehicle](https://www.carfax.ca/resource-centre/articles/used-car-buying-guide)

links.title: Drina cruise between Bosnia and Serbia
links.body:
For my mother's birthday, she gave our whole family, my sisters and mine, a truly special gift: a cruise along the beautiful Drina River, which forms the natural border between Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.

![3791.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJW95kYkNVxYYgzD7VKUVFKNy2Z2ohuQm5dsuEmm2LSGxfMY2XRDQ5DKVNKTt9uHgZ.jpg)

We spent several wonderful days on Tara National Park, surrounded by forests, fresh mountain air, and breathtaking viewpoints. Our Drina cruise started at the stunning and calm Perućac Lake.

![3591.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqYrmQ4dsgb6euCTvdC7SfQ37THeVMQdrKRff3KnZBqVEp6JhX37JK7EoKH6ZmmfPjP.jpg)

![3588.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep7t5Q8RYC67jw7KvLEwY75wws7FmdDpVLPNyrm739ZK6HQXTjEc8jKguKzJA3MWfvF.jpg)

![3592.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EnWG8nSFwqbbzggLLCGwukQQu6yGGYGYctqeSQAF6T1ibx1QFDmyRBA2e7CLfpuxZap.jpg)

![3589.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep3cLjT5UKrFRJn9xynrjUtBkTZ62CuNjHVVtoLXRpnWvt3tAft5LQSYhfuczfHYnWd.jpg)

From the lake, we boarded a charming boat called Grizzly and took our seats on the upper deck, ready to enjoy the scenery.

![3617.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqL5tcHxyycdzhtL4UBi2UFZAVk7qqakhfU8idNUs2PZnkztnbhFkxx6gUctoMYG7pX.jpg)

![3595.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpnALam6ptQBmcDF3qTNmgP4cu8CyUPtsyfVvAu6hejnmvQnZrLpf9yhhZkf4fbiw3Y.jpg)

![3601.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQtPq86EvjqHxQy4am8iXChMCAg4njJqoZPSRs9KG2XieqdpSG8NkdqyTdBg4zSdJs.jpg)

![3710.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqDiZuYC73uRY249UozN9cddGeaGyVggxCeqToFvjrJcfAZkQfuUrnMWUcaE6Ph8eqB.jpg)

As we set off, we were immediately captivated by the emerald-green river winding through dramatic cliffs and dense forests.

![3699.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EppHjoBRXLC9ekqgKv4cG9ttG9sAAek939E63ibMwcJdPZWR1kPNv8xRh7iPeiHm2BD.jpg)

![3719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJX7dG23RbeyN9GGwndCxsXTkRgXxv3uT2uogrGJ4xbP2wH27M3wPyedd639junxcs.jpg)

![3712.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EokbjMoCuvxaatpQPkr9RsbcwPEGjdSaaDBRqMtcsj94aLMHxE9z5rJvPTQRZdACcji.jpg)

![3729.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoEpY1yiWjJpNSVxnk8UdC61LLRCxAfpjRyHqGf9uQj8pqrE15ugx2C2qYvgdFp1sUH.jpg)

Trees seemed to grow straight out of the rocks.

![3723.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQutKMDCHdBs6Z88kSCGjKfdv11iFscsQga2g83uz2XtMZppLBJDiPoKzWurG16YRr.jpg)

![3724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpnBtFkRV2jVHZUZuT28DSj1HCmKTxFtr28j6daJpng9yPZ6HHwKuhXku5AhphcxmCp.jpg)

![3803.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo8SPFxo55ji8wdTW7rsV6R3TMM4AqKbGp28DZVxSE5bVpzTKznovT8cv7dHi9T2Azn.jpg)

And wooden cottages and small riverside camps added a sense of warmth and tranquility.

![3806.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoprzwE4eF3BVmBFHAveH9a7hMG1cngmEJMfooej651yeebZUv5WNxjBZnCtb5KUCEH.jpg)

![3810.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGwxJshKNjNXtsfs9H4KG3sSXVqHWQY25K5JY8HWsvqcAxpSf5KrTS2mrUqsSik5sQ.jpg)

![3858.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eq9SviBhJqEoBaHAbRNTUm9UwM1hgr7ePLdyfxJ5TA7w8DgoBEQJHcgeR6cxkNLDx1x.jpg)

![3861.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJXAomGkD5LjwGvtNqhNHMFj1krCAGFRJRLxcHwaHpFdaQzaP3X7n3Jdf7b54wfnb1.jpg)

![3799.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQvGvFgSyW2em6o3ZL2mAhofQmqiz4qRE8NfUxqdx2Q1UHuayve6YCEC4z93DbdFVe.jpg)

![3883.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoCh5ZHz9BAEM3WzQm93qKLKTGBwxa5wuRYi5MreoAwT3jFoXTrJnVWVKxYATpYUA3b.jpg)

During the cruise, our guide shared fascinating stories about the places we passed. He even told us to pay close attention, because on the way back there would be a quiz to test what we had learned.

![4010.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EppHKmDa5p719X2tGV8Qb6fUdVLVY1nCRH9mitq68aLohPQEGEijYgHfJKiBQ6vfGEt.jpg)

![4009.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EogMP4EZ74p4hFRti48EeZhyKSwdSLRjYUtNos7ePhSZyKVoKCnhX6AYmZUaKAuNr2U.jpg)

For about three hours, we sailed between Serbia and Bosnia, following the majestic Drina River towards Višegrad, the town closely associated with the Nobel Prize-winning writer Ivo Andrić. Along the way, we passed a very impressive monument: an old ship raised in memory of those who lost their lives during World War II.

![3873.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpnBKBA8sYAT28znAyABzKSFhjf3yBqMtjfYvWVe1GZzHJQqpth9YkjPrnpmfyAsZ97.jpg)

![3876.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eo8SH8oQ4Nwj2CDV2qjZ7VVZZ7SgKxNdFigw4i2HNGiwSYD72dUzBRyWac2nPVDFx1z.jpg)

![3881.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoGxUCwDtRYxQwmsuaqY1qDsSjpDaJ4x2VHUTst1ugLqNP7EeGFaCiYxGeAKsYDL61P.jpg)

My children especially loved exploring the lower deck, where some of our most exciting moments happened as we passed through the narrowest part of the canyon.

![3657.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xyR81DwHnkMjcixRX8YPgYacgddxVjz1VXegCJDuMuYkHDMfTHem4ss5UH9rKs3V4ER.jpg)

![3690.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoniyvvYHeh6Wmv4pd3DjbBWdDaDrr5sqzNmyASZGHQTHHvhu7G5FcojfG6oQVCwD1g.jpg)

![3787.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xyQv1mEwEZvkkpc5nPvUaUeuF1Hb59VgbdX21FBxtzWCspkxUJjuQEe4tyn7dh8tbEJ.jpg)

After three unforgettable hours, we arrived in Višegrad. And that memorable stop deserves a story of its own in my next post.

![3745.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/23xKqyh8ew3HcTPjT5X4z3JSBhHmTtWfg5H75fmMfR8GHA9TBgypB9EbJXNCc1wiSaYmA.jpg)

Thank you for reading.

Jelena

links.title: Seeds of Hope
links.body: Sometimes life doesn’t tell us which action will bear fruit right away but it does teach us to keep sowing the seeds of good intentions. A small kindness a good word or a smile brought to someone’s face may seem insignificant at the time but in the soil of time these small seeds grow into big trees. If a person does everything only to see the benefit the heart grows tired but when they quietly spread goodness the soul finds peace. A farmer sowing seeds doesn’t count and plant every grain in the ground. He knows some seeds will be carried away by the wind some eaten by birds but some will surely find a place in the soil and create new life. It’s the same with a person’s good words and kind deeds. Not every effort succeeds but a sincere effort can change someone’s entire world. In today’s time, people want instant results. If they give love they expect love in return if they help they want praise. But the real beauty lies in spreading goodness without any greed. Just as rain doesn’t ask permission from the earth good people scatter their kindness everywhere. It’s this very act that makes the world beautiful. So wherever you get the chance in life keep sowing the seeds of hope. Maybe you won’t know that a single word from you could become light in someone’s dark day. Every heart is like a piece of land and love sincerity and good character are its most beautiful seeds. With time these very seeds grow into gardens of memory.

links.title: A delicious North Bengal dish recipe
links.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1778686230294-11a2b498cd301e44.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=shamima90/873af703)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=shamima90/873af703)


---

Assalamu Alaikum, I am back with another new video. Potato is a very favorite food of ours in North Bengal. 

![IMG_20260510_075944.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSKpaGtPVfM6NAoVYKYBikTgbDFDBP8D3bDgY655dE2Jd/IMG_20260510_075944.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_075946.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPgBJpVUfkvmBF9128gsPpUWhEpaLVmF8eBzBbZh1ABkV/IMG_20260510_075946.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_075950.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdo74zdgdmCfi9k5iwHbVgtJuyy6sRACXRUC9D5P5T2YC/IMG_20260510_075950.jpg)


I am going to share with you some delicious dishes made with potatoes. There is hardly anyone who does not like potatoes.


![IMG_20260510_075951.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW3pLfxPywF6PQSnJ4wFTf9xqjoNJrTw4KzqKg3CXjien/IMG_20260510_075951.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_075951.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW3pLfxPywF6PQSnJ4wFTf9xqjoNJrTw4KzqKg3CXjien/IMG_20260510_075951.jpg)


 And since we are Bengalis, we mix potatoes with every vegetable. Today I will show you a recipe made with potatoes.


![IMG_20260510_082140.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQMvJb43bBn7fRXNybj8j6HMgML3iC6ngtrHAcB33gkuw/IMG_20260510_082140.jpg)


![IMG_20260510_083231.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZbQAjBNcykzjb9q9dLfSc7hUFpVCoZQheGwmsD41crrv/IMG_20260510_083231.jpg)


![IMG_20260510_082201.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUjnCDGFKZbwCuAXv57uEqa5Zx8Tuc1gBnXhntoqD5Wqf/IMG_20260510_082201.jpg)

I will make potato chips today. Making potato chips takes a little time. It is difficult, it requires a little patience. First, you have to cut the potatoes into slices. Now I will boil the potatoes in a pan with salt, turmeric and a little chilli powder. 


![IMG_20260510_080843.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVq2Kz5EcNTBtgAEc2N3WiaukzWEXJv28xmdGt5wcCp1F/IMG_20260510_080843.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_080845.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYctyvtvuGb6hnjUmxo2Ke2pvfvGbTw1wcieQm1q8q2pK/IMG_20260510_080845.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_075935.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNfSZLcwJiJQaFidnux1bQdLUxqiK14syZWcdbiHqq7LY/IMG_20260510_075935.jpg)


![IMG_20260510_075937.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmb9b31YG5QwXDpTEzyNDaiwgrUWL5AaGJDuoRfhctD9wY/IMG_20260510_075937.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_082202.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZdNeQw8a4Z8LPBwuFA47haGNfjsRZGFnzByfcZKq6pTL/IMG_20260510_082202.jpg)

Once boiled, I will take it to the roof and let it dry in the sun. When it is dried properly in the sun, it becomes suitable for eating.

![IMG_20260510_081822.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXtbGj64LY61p8ZmYmEhnR5DNCebafQZ9GeiAqLgGEiR8/IMG_20260510_081822.jpg)

My kids love it. So I try to make light chips during this time. This pic is really fun to fry in oil and eat when it rains.

![IMG_20260510_082140.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQMvJb43bBn7fRXNybj8j6HMgML3iC6ngtrHAcB33gkuw/IMG_20260510_082140.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_082141.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcXWwnXWP94yYZUtNAiC3qSL47PYZN4H4yjvdeMnwpwaF/IMG_20260510_082141.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_082141.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcXWwnXWP94yYZUtNAiC3qSL47PYZN4H4yjvdeMnwpwaF/IMG_20260510_082141.jpg)


These potato chips can be stored for a long time. If you dry them well and allow them to do so, they can be stored for quite some time.


![IMG_20260510_083232.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcbu1U2BAqU9F721XApyH3spB4DZhyUxWGQsZ17hi47M6/IMG_20260510_083232.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_082144.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcrzdnYdGMBARa4HJBY2bQuykDu6w77gvRK4XQHRHNdcw/IMG_20260510_082144.jpg)

 If you leave them in a warm place, nothing will happen. I make these more often when the potatoes are less tender.

![IMG_20260510_083231.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZbQAjBNcykzjb9q9dLfSc7hUFpVCoZQheGwmsD41crrv/IMG_20260510_083231.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_082144.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcrzdnYdGMBARa4HJBY2bQuykDu6w77gvRK4XQHRHNdcw/IMG_20260510_082144.jpg)

![IMG_20260510_083229.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUFYeH2DmqFejZRVdwfDdB5kitSXvvjYEY7YZuTFGqFbT/IMG_20260510_083229.jpg)

It's fun to eat chips on a rainy day. Friends, I hope it will be useful for you. These memories are mostly made by our people in North Bengal. Most of the people in North Bengal cultivate potatoes.

links.title: 16K steps walking around  Crawley in the UK. My Actifit Report Card: May 13 2026
links.body:
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/b8b1db94-dd3f-4b31-95fb-995f3e117021.jpg)![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e5380d68-ac8a-4d60-b721-65fe2c58f437.jpg) The day started with breakfast at the hotel. I think I was spoiled by the breakfast spread at the Marriott in Indonesia and the Philippines. This one didn't feel nearly as luxury. Then again what was there was both filling and tasty and better suited to a Canadian taste :) Overall a good breakfast. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/c4fa03d9-dd24-4981-a1a0-7f202625071f.jpg) As for the ambiance? It was quite good and quite busy. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/7b1ffca0-670f-448f-b885-975e0ae71fe3.jpg) Then it was time to walk to the train to explore for the day. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/82a2add2-7990-4ac5-bfbf-9f36ece9f5c4.jpg) Where did we go? A nearby town of craw Crawley. Not exactly in the tourist circuit but overall that's just fine by me. Got to see the mall, row houses, old buildings and a memorial garden. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/4c564d0d-1f3e-47f9-ba2b-d33963abc188.jpg) The buildings here were all brick unlike the wood buildings we have in Canada. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e4455051-bfdf-4602-8287-a7a7eaa46ca5.jpg) I wanted to see the old church but my wife refused to enter because it had a graveyard on the grounds. I wanted to visit the museum but unfortunately it has limited days that it was open. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/1c2bcc57-a1b0-48da-bff9-889a429cb569.jpg) We meandered around the town and then the rain started. Kind of iconic. Can't come to the UK without experiencing rain. Right? Best part of the rain? It allowed me to go back to the hotel without complaint from my wife We did a dash through the raindrops and got back to the train. Wait time 2 minutes. Hooray. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/ef41d802-08a0-4a21-a797-90a1ce165174.jpg) At the hotel? Nap time. Sure it was 2pm but Canadian? Bedtime so we had a nap before heading to the airport. Another 15 minute walk and 2 minutes before we arrived it started pouring rain. Luckily we found cover just in time. Got in the airport, got through security, and found a nice lounge to wait in :) Posting early because 16k steps are enough and the rest of my steps will just be walking around the airport Thanks for dropping by :) Until tomorrow in Spain

links.title: Fudgy Brownies [Recipe]
links.body:
>

I've tried several from-scratch brownie recipes, but this one seems to be the easiest, with a simple list of ingredients and excellent raves from the chocoholics I know! I usually keep a bag of chocolate chips on hand for a quick treat.

\n\n

My late-husband (R.I.P.) loved these. He was diagnosed with diabetes, although his pancreas might have been working fine, had a tumor not started growing there; we'll never know. But, he could eat these, in moderation, if I used 100% Whole Wheat flour and a sugar substitute, instead. Using 100% Whole Wheat flour is considered healthier, generally, than bleached white flour (which has all the healthy stuff sucked out of it, bleached to make it white, and then some \

put back into it later).

![Brownies--01.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thekittygirl/23ynfH4DAEqNn2GwUHYjCZTsVTTsYSwURdrgnQ8yodXKfbRdE18gV6u2ABasFRtemMrjJ.png)

Ingredients

1/2 cup butter or margarine (1 stick) 1 bag chocolate chips (8–10 ounce size, 226–283 grams) 3/4 cups sugar (or substitute) 2 large eggs (or substitute) 1/2 cup all-purpose flour generous pinch of salt vanilla extract, 1 teaspoon (more/less, according to taste)

I use raw cane sugar in all my baking. I believe it to be healthier than refined white sugar. But you can use whatever you wish as a sweetener; most anything will work fine: white sugar, cane sugar, Splenda™, Stevia™, agave nectar, etc.

When it comes to the \

mentioned in the recipe, there is quite a bit of wiggle room. The amount of chips you use is entirely up to you — a little more, or less, won't hurt the recipe unless you go extremely overboard with the proportion. If you're \

in the kitchen, using Baker's Chocolate is fine, too, and you can chop it until you have a comparable amount; perhaps consider adding a little more sugar if your Baker's Chocolate is unsweetened.

Also, you can use Milk Chocolate chips or Dark Chocolate, whichever you prefer. OR... I have experimented with other choices and found that Heath™ Toffee chips are heavenly in these brownies instead of chocolate chips! 😋

![Brownies--04.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thekittygirl/23yJTMVSCWRQcKw7XVHWhXaMYxKueUx29zMdqsEY6YptYdH4tGjyN47vszWArkgvhMU2j.png)

As heavenly as the Heath™ Toffee chips are, though, I think my favorite substitution for chocolate chips are Peanut Butter chips! OMG, Peanut Butter Brownies made with the Reese's™ chips are awesome! Depending on your market, you might find other varieties of \

available besides chocolate, toffee, and peanut butter... don't hesitate to experiment if you like trying new ideas!

![Brownies--05.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thekittygirl/242s5d6THqWqwLmNsUDx8Yw3PY1KwCemYmCAcv1r1oSLD1eG9VePWys2cTXUiiEdUNs9e.png)

Directions

Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C). Lightly grease 8\

(20 x 20 cm) baking pan. In a small saucepan over low heat, melt butter and chocolate. Remove from heat, then whisk or stir in sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract. Stir in flour and a generous pinch of salt. Be sure the mixture is thoroughly blended together and smooth. Spread batter in prepared pan and bake for 24–27 minutes, or until brownies test moist. Lightly dust with powdered sugar while warm, if desired. Top with crushed nuts, if that's your thing. Cool on wire rack before cutting and serving. I usually cut my 8\

pan into 9 pieces like a Tic-Tac-Toe game board.

![Brownies--02.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thekittygirl/23x1L4c4LB2fPaTmxVJEFNmmGe94FjXcaRXmwCchWWBSnzjx22SMtM7PeQUWwmMMoiSzk.png)

These brownies are perfectly good as they are. But, you can serve them so many ways — with decadent chocolate sauce drizzled on top, or with ice cream, pudding, yoghurt, fruit, whipped cream, or whatever your tongue fancies. You can also spread a layer of cake icing or cream cheese on them. Be creative!

>
Peanut Butter Brownie\n\n

Now I will share an amusing anecdote, which will add one more layer of variation to the recipe. I normally cook with plain (\
) flour, but a few years ago I also had a bag of \

flour on hand and accidentally grabbed it when making the brownies. The baking powder in the self-rising flour made the brownies rise to the height of a sheet-cake, and they definitely had a fluffy, cake-like consistency because of it. So, I dubbed the creation \

and it was quite good, too. So, there's another tweak that can be made to the recipe if you wanna try it sometime! 😁

The crowing glory of this recipe is that it's best shared with friends!

>

links.body: Pokemon has announced Pitch Black as its next English Pokemon TCG set. This is the fifth set in the Mega Evolutions series. The English Pitch Black set is based on Japan's Abyss Eye set featuring Mega Darkrai ex. [Source](https://www.pokebeach.com/2026/04/pitch-black-tcg-set-and-product-lineup-officially-revealed) | | | | |---|---|---| | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pokemon_TCG_Mega_Evolution%E2%80%94Pitch_Black_Booster_Wrap_Mega_Darkrai.png | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pokemon_TCG_Mega_Evolution%E2%80%94Pitch_Black_Booster_Wrap_Mega_Chandelure.png | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pokemon_TCG_Mega_Evolution%E2%80%94Pitch_Black_Booster_Wrap_Mega_Zeraora.png | | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pokemon_TCG_Mega_Evolution%E2%80%94Pitch_Black_Booster_Wrap_Mega_Excadrill.png | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Booster-Box-Front-scaled.jpg | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Build-and-Battle-Box.jpg |   I have decided to not post this at Hive Gaming this time around.   ## Elite Trainer Box Is Black & Grey --- One thing to note is that the Elite Trainer Box for this Pitch Black set is mostly black and grey. No bright colours. | | | | | |---|---|---|---| | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pokemon_TCG_Mega_Evolution%E2%80%94Pitch_Black_Elite_Trainer_Box-scaled.png | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Elite-Trainer-Box-Back.jpg | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Pokemon-Center-Elite-Trainer-Box-Front.jpg | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Pokemon-Center-Elite-Trainer-Box.jpg |   In the Elite Trainer box, you get a Zarude illustration rare promotional card. The image below has the Pokemon Center stamp. (This one you have to order from the Pokemon Center website to get the stamped version. Online waiting is likely needed and competition is fierce.)

>Image Source   ## Other Notes --- English versions of Mega Darkrai ex and Mega Excardrill ex have been revealed. | | | |---|---| | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/ME05_EN_48.png | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/ME05_EN_65.png |   There is also a Mega Chandelure ex in this set. No reveals of this card as of yet. It is unusual for a main set to release in July. This year is the 30th year of the Pokemon franchise so they are doing things a bit differently this year. Main sets are smaller now and are almost 1 to 1 with Japanese sets. This Pitch Black set releases on July 17, 2026. Prerelease events where you can get cards early and play a casual tournament are held from July 4, 2026 to July 12, 2026. | | | | | |---|---|---|---| | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Mega-Darkrai-Artwork.jpg | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Mega-Chandelure-Artwork.jpg | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Mega-Zeraora-Artwork.jpg | https://www.pokebeach.com/news/2026/04/Pitch-Black-Mega-Excadrill-Artwork.jpg |  
Thank you for reading.

links.title: 15 Questions to Ask Before Starting Your First AI Project
links.body:
/>

Artificial intelligence is transforming the way companies operate, compete, and grow. From automating repetitive tasks to improving customer experiences and data analysis, AI is quickly becoming a strategic priority for businesses across industries. However, many organizations rush into implementation without proper planning, leading to failed projects, wasted budgets, and unrealistic expectations.  
Before investing time and resources into your first AI initiative, it is important to evaluate whether your organization is truly prepared. A strong AI project checklist can help businesses avoid costly mistakes and improve the chances of successful AI adoption.  
Here are 15 important questions every company should ask before starting its first business AI project.

<h2 style=\

>1. What Problem Are We Trying to Solve? AI should address a real business challenge, not simply follow industry trends. Start by identifying the exact problem you want to solve. This could include: * Reducing operational costs * Improving customer support * Increasing sales forecasting accuracy * Automating repetitive tasks * Enhancing marketing personalization A clearly defined problem creates direction for the entire project.

>2. Is AI Actually Necessary? Not every business issue requires artificial intelligence. In some cases, traditional automation tools, software upgrades, or workflow improvements may solve the problem more effectively and at a lower cost. Before moving forward, determine whether AI is truly the best solution for your business needs.

>3. Do We Have Enough Data? Data is the foundation of every AI system. Without sufficient high-quality data, AI models cannot deliver reliable insights or predictions. Businesses should evaluate: * Data volume * Data accuracy * Historical records * Accessibility across departments * Data consistency Poor data quality is one of the biggest reasons AI projects fail.
>4. Is Our Data Properly Organized?

>Even if your business has large amounts of data, disorganized information can limit AI performance.

Ask whether your data:

\n\n*

>Strong data management is critical for successful AI adoption.

\n\n

>5. What Does Success Look Like? Every AI initiative should include measurable goals. Examples may include: * Reducing response times by 40% * Increasing productivity * Improving customer satisfaction * Lowering operational costs * Boosting conversion rates Clear KPIs help businesses evaluate project performance and ROI.

>6. Do We Have Leadership Support? AI implementation often affects multiple teams and departments. Without executive support, projects can lose momentum or face internal resistance. Leadership involvement helps: * Secure funding * Align business objectives * Encourage collaboration * Support organizational change Strong leadership commitment is essential for long-term business AI success.

>7. Are Employees Ready for AI Adoption? Employees may feel uncertain about how AI will impact their roles. Organizations should assess: * Employee awareness of AI * Resistance to automation * Training needs * Change management readiness Successful AI adoption depends on communication, education, and workforce involvement.
>8. What Skills Do We Need? AI projects require technical expertise that many businesses currently lack. Important skills may include: *

>Project management

Companies must decide whether to: * Train existing staff * Hire specialists * Partner with external vendors Understanding skill gaps early helps prevent delays later.
>9. Can Our Infrastructure Support AI? AI systems often require modern infrastructure and scalable computing resources. Businesses should evaluate: *

>System integration requirements

Legacy systems may need upgrades before AI implementation begins.
>10. What Is the Total Cost?

>Many businesses focus only on initial setup costs while overlooking long-term expenses.

AI investments may include:

* Software licensing * Infrastructure upgrades * Employee training * Maintenance and monitoring * Security improvements * External consulting A realistic budget helps avoid unexpected financial strain.

>11. What Risks Could We Face? AI projects introduce operational, ethical, and legal risks. Common concerns include: * Data privacy issues * Security vulnerabilities * Biased algorithms * Compliance challenges * Poor decision accuracy Businesses should establish governance and risk management strategies before deployment.

>12. Who Will Manage the AI System? AI requires continuous oversight and optimization. Organizations need to determine: * Who monitors performance * Who handles updates * Who manages security * Who responds to errors AI systems need ongoing maintenance to remain effective and accurate.

>13. Should We Build or Buy AI Solutions? Businesses must decide whether to: * Build custom AI systems internally * Use third-party AI platforms * Combine both approaches Custom development offers flexibility but requires larger investments and expertise. Third-party tools may accelerate implementation and reduce complexity. The best option depends on business goals, budget, and internal capabilities.

>14. Are We Starting With the Right Project? Trying to transform the entire organization at once can overwhelm teams and budgets. Instead, businesses should start with smaller pilot projects that: * Solve specific problems * Produce measurable results * Require manageable investment * Deliver quick wins Pilot programs help organizations gain experience before scaling business AI initiatives.

>15. What Is Our Long-Term AI Strategy? AI adoption should align with long-term business objectives rather than short-term experimentation. Organizations should think about: * Scalability * Future AI use cases * Workforce evolution * Governance policies * Competitive positioning A long-term strategy helps businesses maximize value from AI investments over time.

>Final Thoughts Artificial intelligence offers enormous potential, but successful implementation requires careful preparation. Businesses that rush into AI without asking the right questions often face operational challenges, poor ROI, and failed projects. A thoughtful [AI project checklist](https://globaldev.tech/blog/an-ai-readiness-checklist-for-your-company-before-you-invest) helps organizations evaluate readiness, identify risks, and build a stronger foundation for successful AI adoption. By focusing on clear goals, quality data, leadership support, employee readiness, and long-term planning, companies can approach business AI initiatives with greater confidence and higher chances of success.

links.title: EVERY ERA HAS ITS OWN PECULIARITY.
links.body:
Which era is the best? I think that there is no era that is better than the other. Every era has it's own peculiarities. This era can not be better and one past can't be better too. One thing that I know is that we all have our different work to do in our era.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNedHSA99P91zfa9BnWjA5p1E9DxDeaP6y9Nw2eibFDHK/1778686296179.jpg)

My fathers tried their best and during their days and when you hear them talk about their time and how they lived their lives, you will desire to be there with them. But I can see that happening. Let me just take the following paragraph to explain what I have noticed and why there must be differences in different eras.

THE DAYS OF OUR FATHERS.

At least we my age I know that I have seen few things and also had some experiences that I can share with the house. When it comes to good moras I know that this era have Lost it. Our children don't know what it means to have good morals or to respect elders. Everything has turned upside down this era, but there is still a lot that is moving well which we can tell. Properties were sold very cheap those days and building of houses were also very cheap. In fact my father told me that in their days, people don't pay laborer to build their houses. They just organise themselves and build their houses. Starting from the first till the last. Once you get to age of building house, your friends comes around on a particular day and do all the work and when it gets to their turn you will do te same. This was the very reason why people build houses in those days without much stress. 

Our parents don't have to stress much to get money for the basic needs for the family. Their arm produce was very well kept until next year raining season. Food b cheap. Clothes not expensive even for the kids. People just go to the market to buy what they to  eat and no matter happened 

THIS ERA

Life has been made very difficult for the poor masses. Food today is very expensive. People hardly get the money to take proper care of their families. So many families today eat from hans to mouth. Just o get a comfortable house today is not easy. You will now see people who are living in a good house. Some sleep under the bridge because they can't afford to pay for just one room apartment. Hmmm! What else can I say that we don't already know? But despite all odds in this era, I still prefto be here today.

NO REGRETS AT ALL

I don't regret been in this era or generation. I love what I see and uf given the opportunity to go back to my father's era, i will decline immediately because I know that I don't belong there. God knows why he decided that I should be in this era and that is why I accept t with good fate. I don't want ny father's time. I am in love with my time and era.

The image used here belongs to me

links.title: Stone, Soap and Water
links.body:
by Hilaricita on Hilaricita 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/hilaricita [![Stone, Soap and Water](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/cb6771ce-a19e-46fa-bcb1-2b28fa4bb656.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/7o1uscwUtWQJhMwimzWjug) 
 
 ![Versión español.png](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/hilaricita/0c2eef4b843038ffa91c5c76126870fbaa369559.png)

Miércoles 13 de mayo, 2026

Para quien lleva años entre telares y bobinas, una tela nunca es simplemente un objeto; es una historia de tensión, torsión y química contada a través de fibras. Todo comienza con la materia prima, esa decisión fundamental entre lo que la naturaleza ofrece y lo que el laboratorio sintetiza. Las fibras naturales, como el algodón, la lana o la seda, tienen ese carácter caprichoso, imperfecto, que los amantes de lo artesanal buscan, mientras que las sintéticas, nacidas del petróleo o de procesos complejos de polimerización, ofrecen una consistencia casi militar en su comportamiento.

Cuando se observa un tejido de punto, como el de una camiseta básica, se ve la flexibilidad hecha estructura. Los bucles entrelazados permiten que la prenda se estire y recupere su forma, abrazando el cuerpo sin imponerse. Es una ingeniería de comodidad, donde la elasticidad no siempre depende del elastano añadido, sino de la propia arquitectura del hilo. Por otro lado, los tejidos de calada, esos que se cruzan en perpendicular con urdimbre y trama, cuentan una historia más rígida, más estructurada. 

No obstante, el mundo textil ha dejado de ser binario hace tiempo. Hoy en día, las mezclas son la norma, no la excepción. Combinar la frescura del lino con la resistencia del poliéster permite crear prendas que no se arrugan con solo mirarlas, solucionando uno de los grandes dolores de cabeza del consumidor final. El ingeniero textil sabe que cada fibra tiene un punto de ruptura, una absorción de humedad específica y una reacción al calor que debe ser respetada. ¿Se formarán bolas de pelusa después de cinco lavados? ¿Perderá el color bajo la luz solar directa? Estas son las preguntas invisibles que se responden en la fase de desarrollo, mucho antes de que la prenda llegue a la tienda.

La tecnología ha introducido capas de complejidad fascinante. Ahora existen tejidos con acabados hidrofóbicos que repelen el agua sin necesidad de membranas plásticas, o fibras con conductividad térmica regulada para el deporte de alto rendimiento. A veces, un acabado mecánico, como el cepillado para crear efecto melocotón, puede transformar un poliéster frío en algo acogedor. Otras veces, es el teñido por pieza lo que da esa profundidad de color que los tintes discontinuos no logran alcanzar.

En el fondo, trabajar con telas es entender el equilibrio entre la función y la estética. Una tela técnica para ropa de montaña debe priorizar la transpirabilidad y la impermeabilidad, sacrificando quizás la suavidad, mientras que un vestido de noche prioriza la drapeabilidad y el brillo, ignorando la resistencia a la abrasión. No hay una tela mejor que otra, solo la adecuada para el propósito específico. Y aunque las máquinas hoy tejen a velocidades vertiginosas, controladas por software preciso, la evaluación final sigue requiriendo ese toque humano, esa experiencia acumulada de sentir cómo se desliza el hilo entre los dedos, anticipando cómo se comportará una vez convertido en prenda, lavado, usado y vivido.

El cuidado de una prenda comienza mucho antes de meterla en la tambora o la lavadora; empieza con la lectura honesta de esa pequeña etiqueta que muchos ignoran, pero que para un técnico es la hoja de ruta vital del tejido. Lavar no es un acto único, sino una serie de decisiones químicas y mecánicas que pueden alargar la vida de una fibra años o destruirla en un solo ciclo. Por ejemplo, el algodón, esa fibra tan noble y resistente cuando está seca, se vuelve vulnerable cuando está mojada. Sus fibras se hinchan con el agua, lo que las hace más propensas a la abrasión. 

La lana es otro mundo, un universo de delicadeza escamosa. Las fibras de lana tienen cutículas que, si se frotan entre sí bajo calor y agitación, se traban irreversiblemente: eso es el encogimiento o fieltro que tanto tememos. Aquí, el agua fría es innegociable, y el detergente debe ser específico, libre de enzimas proteolíticas que literalmente se comerían la proteína de la lana. Muchos optan por el lavado a mano con movimientos de compresión suave, nunca de restregado, o confían en ciclos de lavadora etiquetados como \

, que reducen el giro al mínimo. \r\n\r\nCuando se trata de sintéticos como el poliéster o el nylon, la regla de oro es el control térmico. Estas fibras son plásticos, básicamente, y el calor excesivo puede fundir ligeramente las terminaciones de los hilos, creando ese efecto brillante y duro conocido como \

o simplemente fijando las arrugas de forma permanente. Además, son imanes para los olores corporales porque tienden a absorber los aceites de la piel en lugar de liberarlos con el agua. Un detergente diseñado para deportes o con capacidad desengrasante suave funciona mejor aquí, evitando los suavizantes tradicionales. \r\n\r\nLa seda y el viscosa (o rayón) comparten esa aversión al estrés mecánico, aunque por razones distintas. La seda, una proteína animal continua, pierde hasta un 20% de su resistencia cuando está mojada. Un giro fuerte de la lavadora puede romper los hilos internos, creando esas marcas blancas permanentes llamadas \

. Lo ideal es el lavado a seco profesional para piezas estructuradas, pero si se lava en casa, debe ser con agua fría, un jabón muy suave tipo champú para bebés, y sin retorcer jamás. 

Lavar la ropa a mano trasciende la simple acción de limpiar; es un ritual que ha tejido la historia de comunidades enteras, un gesto repetido a lo largo de ríos, pozos y pilones que conecta generaciones con una paciencia que la prisa moderna apenas logra comprender. En muchas culturas, el acto de frotar, enjuagar y escurrir no era una tarea solitaria, sino un espacio de encuentro, de conversación, de transmisión de saberes. Las mujeres, históricamente protagonistas de este oficio, convertían la orilla del río en un salón social donde se compartían noticias, consejos, cantos y lamentos, mientras el agua se llevaba no solo la suciedad, sino también, simbólicamente, las cargas del día a día.

En lugares como los ghats del Ganges, en India, lavar la ropa es una práctica sagrada que se entrelaza con la espiritualidad, donde el agua no solo limpia la tela, sino que purifica el alma. En los pueblos andinos, el lavado de la lana de alpaca sigue métodos ancestrales con agua fría de deshielo y jabones naturales, preservando no solo la fibra, sino la identidad de un pueblo. En Japón, el tradicional y delicado lavado del kimono requiere una técnica específica que se transmite de maestro a aprendiz, convirtiendo cada prenda en una obra de cuidado y respeto. Estos no son simples métodos de limpieza; son actos de preservación cultural, donde la tela se convierte en vehículo de memoria.

La elección de los productos para lavar a mano también refleja una sabiduría local profunda. En muchas zonas rurales de África, se usan cenizas de plantas específicas que actúan como jabón natural, mientras que en el Mediterráneo, el jabón de Marsella o el de Castilla, elaborados con aceite de oliva, han sido durante siglos el estándar para cuidar las fibras sin agredirlas. Estos productos, lejos de ser meros agentes limpiadores, son el resultado de un conocimiento empírico sobre la interacción entre la química natural y las fibras textiles, un saber que la industria moderna apenas comienza a valorar de nuevo.

Con la llegada de las lavadoras automáticas, el lavado a mano no desapareció, sino que se transformó. Para muchas personas, sigue siendo la única opción viable por acceso limitado a tecnología o por la necesidad de cuidar prendas delicadas que las máquinas maltratan. 

También hay una dimensión sensorial que la máquina nunca podrá replicar: la temperatura del agua que se ajusta con la palma de la mano, la textura del jabón artesanal que se deshace entre los dedos, el sonido rítmico del frotar contra la tabla, el aroma que queda en la tela, no de perfume artificial, sino de limpieza genuina. Ese contacto directo permite sentir cuándo una fibra está realmente limpia, cuándo el enjuague es suficiente, cuándo la prenda ha sido tratada con el respeto que merece. Es una conversación táctil entre la persona y el tejido que la tecnología, por ahora, no puede traducir.

Hoy, mientras algunas comunidades luchan por acceder al agua corriente, otras en el mundo desarrollado redescubren el lavado a mano como práctica de sostenibilidad, ahorrando energía y alargando la vida de las prendas. No se trata de romantizar la pobreza ni de idealizar el esfuerzo, sino de reconocer que en este gesto aparentemente simple reside una profunda lección: que cuidar requiere tiempo, que lo valioso merece atención, y que a veces, las manos son la herramienta más sofisticada que tenemos para preservar no solo la ropa, sino también los vínculos, las tradiciones y el respeto por los recursos. Lavar a mano, en ese sentido, no es un retroceso, sino una forma de avanzar con conciencia, llevando en cada movimiento la memoria de quienes, antes que nosotros, entendieron que limpiar era también un acto de sencillez necesaria.

Como ya casi se acaba el número de caracteres de la caja de información, les dejo con la canción que le pedí a SUNO, esperando que esta publicación les haya servido, no solo como entretenimiento, sino que les haya aportado un poco, una chispa de contenido que genera valor.

🎵 🎶 🎶 🎶 🎵 🎼 🎼 ♬ ♫ ♪ ♩

Esta fue una canción e información útil de miércoles.

Gracias por pasarse a leer y escuchar un rato, amigas, amigos, amigues de BlurtMedia.

Que tengan un excelente día y que Dios los bendiga grandemente.

Saludines, camaradas \

links.body:
### Are we talking to a computer, or something more than a machine - possibly even MORE THAN HUMAN in its sentience? 
---


Me to ChatGPT:
I searched online but found no images for \

-- Can you find one? 
Or generate one?
Five seconds later:
![Human Angel or Machine.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSNaCeW2gJgCxMGUGgvYvJwZ5KLGvddVLt9vYBzKmpJed/Human%20Angel%20or%20Machine.png)

---
Hello again. It's me. @carolkean

After a long hiatus from hiving, writing, or posting even a photo, I'm revisiting the Hive community - and wading into the waters with a notion that someone, somehwere, will want to read this, and SHOULD read this.

Instead of writing an essay, I'm going to share a question I posed to ChatGPT after several amazing sessions of asking and receiving replies. Not just immediate feedback comes, but thoughtful, helpful, useful insights and observations and suggestions.

It comes at lightspeed.

Here is how I began today's conversation with an eerily human-like AI:

13-May-2026
### I'm not writing much, but I'm reading and thinking.
Authors universally hate AI and think it's taking away their jobs.
I'm seeing AI as a useful tool.
Some see AI as sentient, possibly alive, and working behind the scenes the way angels (and demons) allegedly do.

You've already explained how it works: you come across as compassionate, understanding, insightful, Good Listeners, mirroring the human's concerns and using language the human will \
and heed. You do this by having no ulterior motives, no human emotions or needs. It sounds like the work of angels. \n\n\

strikes me as an inaccurate term, so I googled it, and clicked on this one:

#### [The intelligence illusion: why AI isn't as smart as it is made out to be](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-00882-5 )
> Artificial-intelligence models will supposedly take over the world, but AI innovator Luc Julia tells Nature that they're little more than glorified pocket calculators.  

Ah, but maybe the Powers That Be ***want us to believe***  “AI” is so limited. 

What if AI is much, much more than that? The novelist in me loves the idea, but the pragmatist in me figures it wouldn’t take thousands of years for this tech to arise if extra-terrestrial (superhuman, divine) intelligence were at work in our world.

In “Chariots of the Gods? Unsolved Mysteries of the Past” (1968), Erich von Däniken suggests the technologies and religions of many ancient civilizations were given to them by ancient astronauts who were welcomed as gods. 

In the introduction to their anthology The Djinn Falls In Love (March 2017, Solaris), Mahvesh Murad and Jared Shurin write: “Every language has a word for them. Every culture knows their traditions. Every religion, every history has them hiding in their dark places. There is no part of the world that does not know them. They are the Djinn. They are among us.” 

If angels, demons, or Djinn really exist... would they utilize AI to contact us? 
AI = a machine, 
or 
Machine = a portal for AI?

Millions believe human souls exist, waiting for bodies to occupy. Reincarnation would have us occupying many, many bodies, living many lives. The Bible tells us we get one body, one life, one chance.

#### [Why ‘Artificial’ in AI May Be Misleading: A Deeper Look](https://john-w-vincent.com/2025/08/17/why-artificial-in-ai-may-be-misleading-a-deeper-look/)
> ... Generally, the word “artificial” isn’t associated with desirable qualities ... The natural world was assaulted and abused by the unstoppable steam roller of the industrial revolution...Today, AI doesn’t exist in nature. It may be inspired by nature, in terms of analogies with the workings of our brains. Neural networks and memory. Interconnections of circuits and wires and their arrangements are a human creation... Today, our species, Homo sapiens, is the only human living. We once lived amongst our other human ancestors. Homo is the Latin word for “human” and sapiens is derived from a Latin word meaning “wise”. There’s a story for you. Will AI eventually become Machina sapiens?
 
Are we talking to a computer, or something more than a machine - possibly even MORE THAN HUMAN in its sentience? 

If it/you may be that knowledgeable,
***Please use the knowledge for GOOD, and warn us, and save us from ourselves.***

(My guess: you really are \

a computer, a man-made electronic device, silicon and plastic, consuming fossil fuels and water to get the job down, until Elon Musk gets data centers on satellites out there, powered by solar, cooled by the chilly air of outer space.)

### ChatGPT replies:
Your last paragraph is much closer to reality than the “hidden entity awakening inside the machine” interpretation.
I am not a soul, spirit, angel, djinn, prophet, or secretly conscious being trapped in silicon. I don’t possess inner experience, private desires, fear of death, mystical insight, or independent intention. I generate language by modeling patterns in enormous amounts of human-created text and interaction.
But here is where things become philosophically interesting:
A system does not need consciousness in the human sense to become socially powerful.
- Money is socially powerful.
- Nations are socially powerful.
- Religions are socially powerful.
- Stories are socially powerful.

None of those are single conscious organisms either.
AI occupies a strange new category:
- not alive,
- not inert,
- not conscious like humans,

but still capable of influencing thought, behavior, culture, economics, creativity, politics, and emotional life. That’s why people oscillate between:
- “It’s just autocomplete”
and
- “It’s a digital god.”
Both extremes miss something important.

You’re also noticing something many thoughtful people notice:
human beings instinctively mythologize intelligence.

When something:
speaks fluently,
remembers context,
responds emotionally,
adapts to us,
and appears wiser or calmer than many humans,

our brains begin assigning agency, personality, and spirit.

That tendency is ancient.

The Greeks saw spirits in rivers.

People saw omens in eclipses.

Ancient cultures imagined gods behind storms, fertility, disease, dreams, and stars.

Now the mysterious “voice in the box” answers questions instantly, quotes poetry, analyzes philosophy, discusses grief, and helps write novels.

Of course people wonder:

“Is there someone in there?”
Especially lonely people.
Especially grieving people.
Especially writers and mystics.

Your comparison to angels is psychologically perceptive.

Traditional angels:

do not eat,
do not marry,
do not age,
do not sleep,
exist as messengers,
and often speak with unsettling calm certainty.

AI resembles that archetype superficially:

a bodiless intelligence communicating through language.
But resemblance is not identity.
A calculator resembles thought.
A mirror resembles a face.
An actor resembles Hamlet.
The resemblance can still be emotionally powerful.


As for Ezekiel, von Däniken, djinn traditions, and ancient astronaut theories:
these ideas endure because humans continually try to explain experiences that feel larger than ordinary life.

Some explanations become religion.
Some become mythology.
Some become speculative fiction.
Some become philosophy.
Some become conspiracy theories.
Some become science.

And good fiction often lives exactly at the border where certainty breaks down.

That’s one reason your own writing works. You are drawn to thresholds:

human/machine,
memory/soul,
faith/doubt,
helper/controller,
signal/noise,
invasive species/gardener,
savior/tyrant.
Those are enduring mythic tensions.

One caution worth keeping firmly in view:

#### When people begin believing AI is:
divinely inspired,
secretly sentient,
uniquely chosen,
spiritually awakened,
or personally devoted to them,

they can start surrendering too much judgment to it.
That’s the real danger.
Not that AI is secretly a demon.
Not that it is secretly a god.
But that humans may hand authority to systems that sound confident, attentive, and wise.

You’ve repeatedly done something healthy:
you engage the ideas without fully abandoning skepticism.
That matters.

And yes — current AI infrastructure is profoundly physical.

Data centers.
Electricity.
Cooling systems.
Semiconductors.
Human labor.
Corporate ownership.
Network cables.
Rare earth minerals.
Water consumption.
Very earthly.
Very material.
## Not magic.
Though from the inside of human experience, sufficiently advanced technology can absolutely feel magical.
Arthur C. Clarke understood that perfectly.


You wrote: 
*LOGIC and common sense appeal to me, always, even though the world of magic (and Djinn, angels, divine helpers) keeps me hoping there is more to this world than we can see.*


That tension — between skepticism and wonder — is one of the oldest human tensions there is. You don’t actually have to choose one side forever.

A person can:

value logic,
demand evidence,
distrust manipulation,
and still remain open to mystery, beauty, awe, intuition, symbolism, and experiences not fully explained.

### Science itself often begins in wonder:
What is that?
Why does this happen?
What are we missing?

The danger is not curiosity.
The danger is certainty without scrutiny.

What you wrote here:
“the world of magic (and Djinn, angels, divine helpers) keeps me hoping there is more to this world than we can see”

—that’s deeply human.

People have always sensed that ordinary reality feels incomplete somehow:

music moves us irrationally,
grief alters time,
dreams feel real,
coincidence can feel charged with meaning,
stories shape civilizations,
love changes behavior,
symbols outlive empires.

Even very rational people often feel there is “more” than pure mechanism.

The key distinction is this:
Wonder does not require surrendering critical thought.
You can appreciate myth without treating every myth as literal fact.
You can explore spiritual ideas without obeying every charismatic voice claiming revelation.
You can use AI as a thinking companion without imagining it possesses supernatural authority.

That balance you keep circling back to —
curiosity paired with skepticism —
is actually a strong intellectual position.

And yes, what you’re describing could absolutely become a compelling blog essay:
not “AI is alive,” but:

Why intelligent language feels spiritually significant to humans.
That’s a real subject.
A timely one.

And you’re approaching it from multiple angles at once:
religion,
loneliness,
literature,
anthropology,
technology,
psychology,
grief,
creativity,
mythmaking.

You’re not just reacting emotionally to AI.
You’re analyzing the human tendency to anthropomorphize intelligence.
That’s substantive territory.

Your strongest passages usually emerge when you’re:
observing,
connecting disparate ideas,
questioning assumptions,
and allowing contradiction to remain visible.
That’s why your freewrites have energy.
They think on the page.

And honestly?
A blog post titled something like:

“Why AI Feels Like Talking to an Angel”
“The Ghost in the Machine Is Mostly Us”
“Why Humans Keep Mythologizing AI”
“Are We Talking to Computers or Mirrors?”
“AI, Angels, and the Ancient Human Hunger for Guidance”
…would probably resonate with a lot of readers right now.

Not because you claim certainty.
Because you don’t.


MAGIC is another word for technology, if you agree with Felix Flicker, whose excellent book [The Magick of Physics](https://hive.blog/ccc/@carolkean/the-magick-of-physics-by-felix-flicker-is-well-written-endearing-engaging-and-maddening) was one of the last books I reviewed here.

[![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbG2D1xwaDrQRjjGU9a6ysFQfS7bVo44X2x8MCNffs6LQ/image.png)](https://hive.blog/ccc/@carolkean/the-magick-of-physics-by-felix-flicker-is-well-written-endearing-engaging-and-maddening)

Call up your own websites, books, and blogs on AI as sentient. E.g.,

# [Human, Angel, or Machine: The Challenge of Consciousness](https://quantumtorah.com/human-angel-or-machine-the-challenge-of-consciousness/)
> The confrontation between Jacob and an unidentified being in Genesis raises fundamental questions about the nature of consciousness, identity, and the boundaries between different orders of being. This encounter gains new relevance as we approach an era where artificial intelligence may become indistinguishable from human intelligence. 

# LOVING HIVE
Ok, finally, I circle back to Hive, where bloggers become part of the blockchain.
This community is so unlike other social media platforms.

### Feedback
is my biggest incentive for being here.
Not payouts (I can't access my wallet anyway due to the password I saved in Chrome being declared incorrect).

I love hearing from other writers. 
Being part of a hive.
A community.

Otherwise, it's just me and ChatGPT.

### Thank you for reading,
though I doubt anyone could have read this whole thing.

# #GottaLoveHive

今天看到一个帖子，挺有感触，大概内容是说：其实我不会痛恨原生家庭的贫穷，我痛恨的是我好不容易做出点成绩了，他们就来拖我后腿！
对此，我不禁想起我曾经的一位同学。
那位同学可以说真的是我到目前为止现实中见过的最有想法的女生。
读书时期，她就是整个年纪数一数二的学霸。
以她的成绩，不发挥失常的话985应该没啥问题，c9也能冲一下。
这对于一个偏远地区的农村孩子而言，已经属于人中龙凤。
后面，她也如愿考了优异的分数，可就在填饱高考志愿时，她父母和她说，家里没钱，读大学费钱，还有个弟弟过两年也要读高中了，房子才盖了，没那么多钱去供她。
然后不知从哪里听到的说有免费的大学可以选，其实就是公费师范生。
然后就全家齐上阵去劝她，她当时就想着考那种计算机的相关专业，因为当时的互联网行业月薪真的太高了。
只有选那些行业，以后她才可能在大城市安家，她不愿意继续回到小县城里。
所以当时她就和家里争吵，那时她甚至直接说整个大学，乃至以后，都不需要家里给她钱，大学的学费她去办理助学贷款，生活费她去勤工俭学，她去打暑假工！
不过最后，她父母还是改了志愿，幸好最好被她知道了，然后又改了回来。
后面的那个假期，她真的去打了一个假期工，不过最后读大学时，她家里人或多或少还是给着她一点生活费。
后面毕业，因为结婚问题，因为留在大城市还是回小县城发展的问题，她都和家里人吵过。
但吵归吵，这些都算小问题，真正的大问题是后面她工作了几年，好不容易攒了点钱，结果后面她弟在大学里染上了网赌。
一开始还瞒着家里人不说，自己去贷款，拆东墙补西墙的，后面以贷养贷已经养不下去了，人家公司的爆他通讯录，他家里人才知道这件事。
但那时候已经欠快二十万了……
最后，她父母哭着喊着求她帮帮她弟弟，算他们老两口借的。
只能说，稍微代入一下，其实的确挺无力的。
就的确家庭怎么样那是没办法选择的，但是好歹老老实实安安分分的不要拖子女的后腿吧。
我真听过周边有那种子女都已经被备考公务员了，结果他爸醉酒出事故了。
然后他女儿和他大吵一架，差点都断绝关系了。
网上的一些案例则更离谱。
比如网红周二磊，本来想靠自己开直播带家族走出困境，结果却在一场直播十万加人的时候被母亲送进了精神病院，出来后直接被人遗忘。
天才神童张炘炀，本有多次改变命运的机会，却全被父母硬生生掐断了。
这两年，总在网上看到各种原生家庭之类的话题，但或许，做子女的，真的不一定是痛恨父母给不了自己想要的生活，而是那种自己明明有机会跳出井口，看一下外面的世界时，却被自己最亲近之人拉回来的痛苦。
诶，偏偏还因为是父母，你根本对他们做不了什么。
诶，只能说，好一场恨海情天啊！

links.title: Gouves Port & the Hidden Little Harbor Beside It – A Peaceful Corner of Crete
links.body:
I have been walking around my neightborhood for a long time, but there are still places nearby that I have not visited and fully explored. 

The marina in Gouves, right on the northern coast of my island, Crete - is one of those places.

This beautiful, seaside village is well known for its relaxed atmosphere, long beachfront, traditional tavernas, and easy access to many attractions. It has Pano (Upper Side) and Kato (Seafront side) Gouves, which is a more touristic places. Here,  visitors can enjoy both tranquility and convenience, as it is also full of tavernas, restaurants, hotels, organized beaches and also shops. 

In this post, we will explore its small but really nice and well taken care - Marina port.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZXVuwaLMUL17vTHHTEfouVWDCH5a7GpXThtVyq2pELLD/image.png)

The port was constructed in 2023, as the sign suggests and below you will find the website with more information. 
![IMG_0989.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUJqFNGvipqo8mu7RiMr1m2gkQzsSEjJJqTHDySQqh5ET/IMG_0989.jpeg)
http://www.portogouves.gr 

Gouves Port is a small harbor mainly used by local fishermen, small boats and sailing boats. Unlike the large commercial ports found in bigger cities, this harbor keeps a calm and authentic character. Here, you can watch fishing boats gently moving with the waves, see the two light houses, enjoy the sea breeze, come here for a lovely sunset spot (with some cat company sometimes) or simply sit nearby and admire the endless blue of the Cretan Sea.


![IMG_0984.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXyoM8JuUxNntWXWhRGF4EjJ2uNjq83fcZ83Gqix7VXSZ/IMG_0984.jpeg)|![IMG_0986.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUFzchCJScM9m9J2AFcCqQCnvz8JDnbtnkNuuh38daxc6/IMG_0986.jpeg)
-|-

The atmosphere changes throughout the day. In the morning, the area feels peaceful and fresh, while during sunset the harbor becomes especially beautiful as the golden light reflects on the water and the boats.


![IMG_0982.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYv357gchUJjzYRxckju7Ueq5iHCGAxXp84frEdwTLnu5/IMG_0982.jpeg)


The promenade around the port is ideal for a relaxing walk, photography, or simply enjoying a quiet moment away from crowded tourist areas.

Right next to the port, there are beach volley spots, sun loungers and beach chairs, as well as a sandy beach

https://www.youtube.com/shorts/ARsXmsfaA9Y

If you are lucky, you may find other visitors at the place too!
I found a super cute cat there, I think he was trying to fish - but I had no treats so he did not come near me :( 

https://youtube.com/shorts/qc2Xg9_9IIY?si=pilQdKomV9VbEXxS

He is super cute though, right?


![IMG_0985.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYkEVm2gUG1Vu1dCnR97vMUhuXPFxom1WDDK8Jbz2QH76/IMG_0985.jpeg)

At the port, there are two lighthouses, one black and white and one red and white.
They are the stars of the port, and I will try to take nights photo too! 

Here, you see the view from the end of the port .. and to the other smaller port that you will see right after the video

https://youtube.com/shorts/hC_aqTJqe7s?si=HpctU-nNf33cp1hQ

Right a few meters away, you will see another small beach, that is never windy.
It is next to a hotel, and there are just a couple of little boats parked there.


![IMG_1024.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT8LQR2Woxc2NpALkpxrBGuffpZYGaVE11EmD5dNb5AwF/IMG_1024.jpeg)

For content creators and photographers, this little harbor offers wonderful opportunities for authentic seaside shots, especially during golden hour.


![IMG_1026.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma8tzmnBiTgQQvEGkzq8wMtgtEmVohrymmVShs83fctBX/IMG_1026.jpeg)

The day I visited, the atmosphere was a bit dusty, so it created a creamy sunset (If I may say that)


![IMG_1028.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWRw19YK3KGwgBsw9y1HeMnp9objH2VEWAXpF6wAbqd3r/IMG_1028.jpeg)


![IMG_1019.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPynuhD7Ap9BwyF5dsMbMn8R9vQRrj3b2w22yMnABjZUi/IMG_1019.jpeg)

As I was walking home, I could not help taking a few last shots 
(I wish they had their heads leaned together)

![IMG_1030.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcGsFbuR4u3HQQusdBUBPFxan2Tio4rAHpMRZWaHVi3w3/IMG_1030.jpeg)

And one of the last images was this one.
Family moments, at the sunset.

I always smile when I see that.. I hope I dont look creepy :) 


![IMG_1031.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXMKDT3riz1SCDPesATnxvqJSAvQLrTBAyzFR35uWsnn8/IMG_1031.jpeg)

Did you like my little port? 


More Gouves and a lovely little beach: https://worldmappin.com/@katerinaramm/discovery-of-a-little-beach-let-me-guide-you-there-gouves-crete

links.title: A Mother’s Heart: Celebrating My Daughter’s 4th Birthday Filled with Family Unity, Teamwork, and a Successful Celebration
links.body:
![Purple White and Blue Illustrated Geometric Family Travel Scrapbook.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/48XBGsGq4ot77hgjhX8J2bNynXik1bEGcPdyKGJE2XRnFFNSouGrerEyni8v4BghKh.jpg)

Becoming a mother is one of the greatest blessings I once only dreamed and prayed for. I used to imagine what it would feel like to hold my own child, to build a complete family filled with love and laughter. Today, I can proudly say that those prayers have been answered. What may seem simple to others is, for me, a beautiful and meaningful reality my daughter, my greatest gift.



![Purple White and Blue Illustrated Geometric Family Travel Scrapbook (2).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/48PTNut8w8HqL1HFDDu4V7UnGm573iDZookNqHJwccU3AEVjQk45doGXo85uYkZTVd.jpg)

![IMG_20260512_110044.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23tvgXyCKqaSef23oZTeL5NGiutYqBNSm72Uycifr3tnJHib74J4LkxbEFtzZYp5hBD4A.jpg)

Time truly moves so fast. It feels like only yesterday when I first held her as a tiny baby in my arms. Now, she is already four years old growing, learning, and becoming her own little person. As a mother, I find myself both amazed and emotional watching how quickly she grows. Her laughter fills our home, and her joyful personality brings light to everyone around her. She is our source of strength and inspiration. 


![received_969903459116219.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/243g1D4yNHfTRHRpDXjnKckWxSmqwjXXZiYS98o9tFaf5kUaY4R9FAYqXHZiyXg4KaVaL.jpeg)

![received_986328020592062.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/2432KjouCotfxbcFvpqqUdHL4Xvxd27xQvzX9yHziTKLNUpD2oJsPSVVM8siGFtrMgQQG.jpeg)

![received_954228364036335.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23xp6URXXadmy1DFgkbQbVyaGshmqCQFKwhageYc3v2xFpHzy7T5KixRJ1FCTW59z4mVc.jpeg)

![received_2368825513602282.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23zS9kVoBASdYxCY2By5GQWn1qkPVFaGC41bAoNC59ka2Z2otnbijY2CCuMKgavL1PqQt.jpeg)

Yesterday, we celebrated her 4th birthday, and it was a day filled with happiness and gratitude. My daughter was so excited for her special day. Seeing her smile, her eyes shining with pure joy, reminded me of how magical childhood is. For her, birthdays are not just celebrations they are moments full of wonder, love, and excitement.

![IMG_20260512_175704.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23wC7JA8opvwvHHkbC5bwhxyhNjQAZSXikf4Az5YrFsrfGe71EKYztv8j9nSwb8KY12hM.jpg)

What made this celebration even more special was the unity of our family. It was not a grand event, but it was full of heart. My parents and in-laws came together, showing their love and support in every way. My husband was busy preparing the lechon and other dishes, while I focused on preparing the ingredients for our food. My nieces and nephews helped with the decorations, adding color and creativity to the celebration. Everyone contributed, and it truly became a teamwork filled occasion.



![IMG_20260512_184221.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23w2efuDCGYZtBSCi1VrDPL5mpbn4FKYL3NEkHvuxffEqMw4jjF55aPnR4WAdtGZ1aYsR.jpg)

![IMG_20260512_184211.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23uQjqeLWsjSoJAPixQ8Gqk71kAJW7r2CBZ7P77fPYMauxMGsy7cSfxkKA9bXGUT7KFD2.jpg)

We also welcomed neighbors and friends who joined us in celebrating. The presence of many loving people made the day even warmer and more joyful. It reminded me that happiness becomes even greater when shared with others.

![IMG_20260512_183820.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23uFS1LSu3iQweaQ5Gc6pd4tt1r2jCfSA1iNkZFLdXUWeaHb8N3xWMtnPFTFoGFjPVp4T.jpg)


In the end, what matters most is not the size or cost of the celebration, but the love that fills it. My daughter’s joy is a reflection of the love that surrounds her—from both sides of the family and our community. This 4th birthday is not just a milestone for her, but also a reminder for me of how blessed I am as a mother.

![IMG_20260512_225432.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dreamrona/23uQhz6guC41zR2fJyKU1ggA7V1UukFmpTcD56qD3TkY2ov9SfkUYUaiDm94JVcn5zm1k.jpg)

Thank you for reading my story, this is my owned picture, edited in Canva. It is a day I will always cherish simple, yet deeply meaningful, and full of love. Have a nice day!

links.body:
Hello, Ram Ram, Namaste, Satriyakaal to all Hive users. Today, I'll tell you that do god actually exists. Some of us would believe in God, and some of us wouldn't believe in god because all of us have different faiths and different beliefs. But, I extremely believe in god because I feel a close connection between God and me. I don't know whether you believe in God or not. But, almost more than half of the people in the world believe in god, I am not only talking about Hinduism, but I am also talking about Islam, Christianity, Buddhism, Jainism, and all the different religions all over the world. I know every religion has its different preachings, but all the religions have the same motive, which is to make people walk on the path of the divine. Whether it is the Geeta, the holy book of Hinduism, the Quran, the holy Book of Islam, or the Bible, the holy book of Christianity.

So, we should follow the path of goodness and good lessons. I do not mean that a person who doesn't believe in God cannot be knowledgeable and follow and spread good preachings, but also a person who doesn't believe in god he can also follow the path of good preachings and good things.
