body.title: Hive Open Days: El viaje de regreso a casa // Hive Open Days: The Journey Home
body.body: ![IMG_2547.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Ep3foEthWCcyvC8DYDNeKudq6qWrB86tbRhUjj2ht2o4rYgsxe2FZxBJrhAiM2Ha1zt.JPG) [Click here to read this post in **English**](#english)

> Hola querido hiver. Los viajes de regreso a casa siempre parecen más cortos. Cuando salí de mi casa iba con la maleta llena de expectativas, soñando con esos encuentros tan deseados y esperando pasarlo fenomenal en compañía de personas a las que considero amigos. Todo eso se cumplió y hoy me apetece escribir cómo fue el regreso para poner el broche final a la loca aventura que ha sido preparar y disfrutar de los Hive Open Days en Alicante. ![IMG_2536.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoiY7FSGbQuaGw64DSEt9EAa5fjxYBjQvjmxmys6RwnzSvrE1wNuAS4XrMP6ZPsUwAk.JPG) De camino a la estación de tren tomé un desayuno clásico de café con leche y tostada con mantequilla y mermelada. Madrugué con tiempo suficiente para disfrutarlo de forma lenta, saboreando cada bocado como tratando de aferrarme a lo que acababa de vivir en los días previos. ![IMG_2538.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoGyx5K94p5oS6cKWnw3Cb3PVJhS31g3QHtngUzDY2txZnWTTpW3hjERt1brQrw2uar.JPG) ![IMG_2537.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoptwyoRbvRWdCTSqEB5XPKQ93FF2sJzZC9F4mpyB6oCAUtnFcfGMditpy3EH31QEUQ.JPG) Me despedí de Alicante con la satisfacción de cumplir con mis propias expectativas, algo que mi autoexigencia siempre me pone difícil. Sin embargo, esta vez ha sido diferente y mucho más positivo. Hablar en público de nuevo tras varios años apartada de este tipo de eventos me daba algo de miedo por no saber si sería capaz. Lo fui, y lo mejor es que han sido más de una y de dos las personas que me han dicho que les gustó mi intervención. ![IMG_2539.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoiY7M6xKbmKpUatbnKafFySLBAGsfCnhCqsuHdE19x1TFmdyyGvKxfkxP2LCeKFu6M.JPG) ![IMG_2541.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqDhaTjKPuxzHgri4PykqPoZoao6ZLSpEXpYdLZDrp9YTw9SMQktr1E6hPr4L5Go87o.JPG) En este viaje no hubo incidencias, todo salió como estaba previsto y fue mucho más tranquilo que a la ida. La experiencia fue tan dulce como los bombones que viajaron desde las islas británicas y que me acompañaron en el bolso de mano durante el trayecto de regreso. Me hizo muchísima ilusión recibirlos de una hiver que me inspira cada día. ¡Gracias infinitas! ![IMG_2543.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9TnGpTXfN77JmwVvpZQzgyH2wHfUNgKhRQWuFrVHVUqjJTYV8jGkLLeX1orZeD4ss.JPG) ![IMG_2544.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EpnAuhdj1e63P6VNFm7eecksvnTFGinKyU8KSZUU9dQofgKymBXb5wQj4Qoe6aqk25H.JPG) Conforme el tren del segundo tramo se acercaba a Zaragoza aumentaban las nubes y la luz del sol anunciaba la tormenta que se estaba desatando en la ciudad. La foto de abajo está tomada unos diez minutos antes de mi llegada, cuando mi marido me decía por WhatsApp que me esperaba en el coche y con el paraguas preparado porque llovía a cántaros. Es increíble cómo puede cambiar el tiempo tan rápido. Cuando bajé del tren el agua y los truenos habían cesado e incluso volvía a salir el sol. ![IMG_2549.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EokeWDTPAn6Kav8iqWpqFZgWazXiZS47mLeezt3HsorbGqQWTRbo1KVxh2ZmajFUuUk.JPG) ![IMG_2550.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoyQTwuUDqr2zLRYcChBn2qxch4YUWzu6EmPiz1ixa539FQgjVxQPqh4crvbVa1qWKS.JPG) Llegué a mi casa agotada, feliz y con la motivación renovada para seguir aportando mi granito de arena en esta increíble comunidad. En la maleta traje recuerdos de estos días, ¡me costó cerrarla! Contaba con una bolsa de merchandising pero no con la que gané en el concurso de Worldmappin. ![d03070b9-097d-4569-aa1c-710ba42f0a53.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/23wCJEYuscZcCg2gHitvtMyAWsvFt9V2FmkQEpdZipbYYBZyLUoK4Vp89wdUxaiYf4se3.jpg) ![IMG_2551.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EopukpRYzQu5rYzSeM4YEuw9SmGEf7HCrVGsUjS1tN2yKsaiC8zCtef3VrCZ3KaVxro.JPG) Hive es como esa caja de bombones: cada uno somos diferentes pero todos aportamos nuestro sabor. Gracias @ninaeatshere por la foto que nos hiciste a @livinguktaiwan y a mí, ese fue uno de los momentos más bonitos y dulces de estos días. Esta es la última publicación de la serie de posts que he escrito sobre los Hive Open Days celebrados en Alicante del 30 de abril al 3 de mayo de 2026, estos son el resto de enlaces: [¿Qué lleva una hiver en la maleta? // What does a hiver pack in their suitcase?](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/que-lleva-una-hiver-en-la-maleta-what-does-a-hiver-pack-in-their-suitcase) [Hive Open Days: Día 1 // Hive Open Days: Day 1](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-1-hive-open-days-day-1) [Hive Open Days: Día 2 // Hive Open Days: Day 2](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-2-hive-open-days-day-2) [Hive Open Days: Día 3 // Hive Open Days: Day 3](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-3-hive-open-days-day-3) [Hive Open Days: Día 4 // Hive Open Days: Day 4](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-4-hive-open-days-day-4) Gracias a todos los que habéis hecho realidad mi sueño en estos días maravillosos. Y ahora, ¡a por el [HiveFest en Barcelona](https://hivefe.st)! Hasta la próxima publicación. Mientras tanto, ¡cuídate!

> Herramientas: Cámara iPhone 13 Pro, editor de fotos Mac. Mis publicaciones en [Worldmappin pinchando aquí](https://worldmappin.com/@palomap3) Si te gusta lo que publico, únete a mi [Fanbase pinchando aquí](https://hive.vote/dash.php?fan=palomap3&i=2) ![B67FB7A6-2E4B-43FD-BE20-57543B8993A2_4_5005_c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/23tmerjFT3bacskjaLCHwJcKiNucG1oEiEzj9BNLMfBBevvri9W4G7eDRveawxvcGY472.jpeg) ©️Copyright 2026 Paloma Peña Pérez. Todos los derechos reservados.

> Hi, dear hiver. The journey home always seems shorter. When I left home, my suitcase was full of expectations; I was dreaming of those long-awaited reunions and looking forward to having a brilliant time in the company of people I consider friends. All that came true, and today I feel like writing about how the return journey went, to put the finishing touch to the crazy adventure that was organising and enjoying the Hive Open Days in Alicante. ![IMG_2536.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoiY7FSGbQuaGw64DSEt9EAa5fjxYBjQvjmxmys6RwnzSvrE1wNuAS4XrMP6ZPsUwAk.JPG) On my way to the train station, I had a classic breakfast of coffee with milk and toast with butter and jam. I got up early enough to enjoy it at a leisurely pace, savouring every bite as if trying to hold on to what I had just experienced in the days before. ![IMG_2538.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoGyx5K94p5oS6cKWnw3Cb3PVJhS31g3QHtngUzDY2txZnWTTpW3hjERt1brQrw2uar.JPG) ![IMG_2537.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoptwyoRbvRWdCTSqEB5XPKQ93FF2sJzZC9F4mpyB6oCAUtnFcfGMditpy3EH31QEUQ.JPG) I said goodbye to Alicante with the satisfaction of having met my own expectations, something my high standards always make difficult for me. However, this time it was different and much more positive. Speaking in public again after several years away from this sort of event made me a bit nervous, as I didn’t know if I’d be up to it. I was, and the best thing is that more than one and two people have told me they enjoyed it. ![IMG_2539.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoiY7M6xKbmKpUatbnKafFySLBAGsfCnhCqsuHdE19x1TFmdyyGvKxfkxP2LCeKFu6M.JPG) ![IMG_2541.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EqDhaTjKPuxzHgri4PykqPoZoao6ZLSpEXpYdLZDrp9YTw9SMQktr1E6hPr4L5Go87o.JPG) There were no incidents on this trip; everything went according to plan and it was much more peaceful than the outward journey. The experience was as sweet as the chocolates that had travelled all the way from the British Isles and kept me company in my handbag on the return journey. I was absolutely delighted to receive them from a fellow hiver who inspires me every day. Thank you so much! ![IMG_2543.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/Eq9TnGpTXfN77JmwVvpZQzgyH2wHfUNgKhRQWuFrVHVUqjJTYV8jGkLLeX1orZeD4ss.JPG) ![IMG_2544.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EpnAuhdj1e63P6VNFm7eecksvnTFGinKyU8KSZUU9dQofgKymBXb5wQj4Qoe6aqk25H.JPG) As the train on the second leg of the journey approached Zaragoza, the clouds thickened and the sunlight foreshadowed the storm that was brewing over the city. The photo below was taken about ten minutes before I arrived, when my husband messaged me on WhatsApp to say he was waiting for me in the car with an umbrella at the ready because it was pouring with rain. It’s incredible how quickly the weather can change. By the time I got off the train, the rain and thunder had stopped and the sun was even coming out again. ![IMG_2549.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EokeWDTPAn6Kav8iqWpqFZgWazXiZS47mLeezt3HsorbGqQWTRbo1KVxh2ZmajFUuUk.JPG) ![IMG_2550.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EoyQTwuUDqr2zLRYcChBn2qxch4YUWzu6EmPiz1ixa539FQgjVxQPqh4crvbVa1qWKS.JPG) I arrived home exhausted, happy and with renewed motivation to keep doing my bit for this incredible community. I brought back souvenirs from these days in my suitcase – I struggled to close it! I waited a goody bag, but not the one I won in the Worldmappin competition. ![d03070b9-097d-4569-aa1c-710ba42f0a53.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/23wCJEYuscZcCg2gHitvtMyAWsvFt9V2FmkQEpdZipbYYBZyLUoK4Vp89wdUxaiYf4se3.jpg) ![IMG_2551.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/palomap3/EopukpRYzQu5rYzSeM4YEuw9SmGEf7HCrVGsUjS1tN2yKsaiC8zCtef3VrCZ3KaVxro.JPG) Hive is like that box of chocolates: we’re all different, but we all bring our own flavour to the mix. Thanks @ninaeatshere for the photo you took of @livinguktaiwan and me – that was one of the loveliest and sweetest moments of the event. This is the final post in the series I’ve written about the Hive Open Days held in Alicante from 30 April to 3 May 2026. Here are the other links: [¿Qué lleva una hiver en la maleta? // What does a hiver pack in their suitcase?](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/que-lleva-una-hiver-en-la-maleta-what-does-a-hiver-pack-in-their-suitcase) [Hive Open Days: Día 1 // Hive Open Days: Day 1](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-1-hive-open-days-day-1) [Hive Open Days: Día 2 // Hive Open Days: Day 2](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-2-hive-open-days-day-2) [Hive Open Days: Día 3 // Hive Open Days: Day 3](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-3-hive-open-days-day-3) [Hive Open Days: Día 4 // Hive Open Days: Day 4](https://peakd.com/hive-148309/@palomap3/hive-open-days-dia-4-hive-open-days-day-4) Thank you to everyone who has made my dream come true during these wonderful days. And now, let’s get ready for [HiveFest in Barcelona](https://hivefe.st)! Until the next post. In the meantime, take care! [//]:# (!worldmappin 38.34490 lat -0.49531 long d3scr)

body.title: The Me You Don’t See After Midnight
body.body:
![migallery23-wendy-7364660_1920 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT1iEVkYFLNWf32nVtYJEfaGt4d26a8piDPjMz8MnrKhx/migallery23-wendy-7364660_1920%20(1).jpg)


Friends, how are you? I hope you're doing well. Today's post of mine is a bit strange—a bit sad—about the silence of the night at the moment. 

When everyone falls asleep at night, the world's noise just stops for me—it simply shifts inside. I lie in bed, no matter which side I'm on, but my mind won't be quiet. I don't know what it is—I keep thinking about all sorts of things. Suddenly, tiny silences all around me become a new guest in my mind. It conjures up old things I've long since forgotten—or the wrongs people have done to me—and suddenly they start flooding back into my mind. 

I'm amazed at how people behave badly toward me and then just walk away. The decisions I confidently make during the day, I doubt at night and think, “What have I done? Should I have made that decision? Should I have done that thing? I should say…” I'd say the midnight hour is the strongest. At night, you're talking to yourself alone; there's no one to disturb you.

So, friends, I've noticed one thing: when you make decisions in the silence of the night, those decisions are always right for you. You're thinking alone, no one is disturbing you. Whatever decisions you make, you make them with your heart and mind. Then in the morning, when you act on those same decisions, So you try to prove yourself extraordinary and right, because the decisions you make are only with yourself—there's no one else there to give you advice; it's just you thinking with your heart and mind about what will happen if I do this or that. What benefit will there be if I behave well with someone? How will they behave with me? What do you think about what I'm thinking in the middle of the night?
Are the decisions a person makes at night better, or are the ones made after consulting friends better?

Source : https://pixabay.com/photos/search/the%20me%20you%20don%e2%80%99t%20see%20after%20midnight/

body.body:
![akk.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/karinanunez/EoptNtSrnJwBuSXwMPW4EjcrSHkP4ws1LpU6HhRiKjJATRRR1CmUZaPAhqM5bZeST5U.jpg)

Hello, my dearest otaku friends; I hope you're all doing well.
A few days ago I drew Akane Tendo, and that inspired me to do a cosplay since I love her character in Ranma 1/2.

I've often mentioned that buying an original cosplay is very expensive, so I prefer to put together pieces from my wardrobe and build the cosplay I want that way. If I don't have everything, I either make it with recycled materials or sew a piece I need.

I love making this kind of cosplay and showing it to all of you, and in this case, I made Akane, a sweet schoolgirl, and I recreated her school uniform as accurately as possible.

I'm sure many of you want to make some cosplay, so go for it! You just need a little more imagination and to start making them at home. You'll love the result, just as I love sharing them with all of you.

>Hola, mis queridísimos amigos otakus, espero se encuentren muy bien.
Hace días hice un dibujo de Akane Tendo, y por tal motivo me animé a hacer el cosplay, ya que me encanta su personaje en Ranma 1/2.

>Muchas veces he comentado que para adquirir un cosplay original es muy costoso, entonces prefiero juntar piezas de mi guardarropa y así voy construyendo el cosplay que quiero hacer y si no tengo todo, pues o fabrico con materiales reciclados o cosiendo alguna pieza que necesito.
Me encanta hacer este tipo de cosplay y mostrarlo a todos ustedes y en este caso, hice el de Akane, una dulce niña de colegio, y con su uniforme escolar la recreé lo más parecida posible.

>Estoy segura de que muchos de ustedes quieren elaborar algún cosplay; pues anímense, solo tienen que poner un poco más de imaginación y comenzar a elaborarlos en casa. Les encantará el resultado, así como me encanta a mí cuando los comparto para todos ustedes

body.title: Shattered Self Image: Abundance Year Episode 1965 (audio: noxsoma.substack.com)
body.body:
Full Metal Ox Day 1900
Wednesday 13, May 2026
Abundance Year Episode 1965
Noxsoma Life Camp:  

Salutations Wellness Warriors, Spirit soldiers, fabulous fam, Eminent emanations of energy, carbon units, beautiful bags of mostly water. Welcome to another, hump day from paradise.  

Your humble vagabond has been standing at the intersection of “interest” and “obsession”, for the better part of this decade waiting for the cosmic traffic light to encourage the vessel to, “make the crossing.” 

The light is blinking, “proceed, with caution.”  

There were at least seven families in my neighborhood with more than seven children. That’s a lot of activity for a row-home. And a lot of talking. All of that talking eventually becomes noise, especially when that talking becomes competitive. Your humble scribe comes from a family of “talkers.” On my Mom’s side. Holiday gatherings were always loud and smokey. Mom and her sibs, as I recall, went on ceaselessly. Some of the in-laws couldn’t get a word in edgewise.  

This is where we are today friends, with media. All media, from personal, to social, to corporate and everything I missed. Everybody’s talking. Breaking News. My personal triumphs. How to be successful. Why you’re sad. The darker side of darkness. The brighter side of gloom. I’m earning $7500 a minute sitting on my ass, and you can too! It’s World War 3, no it’s World War 4, but if you count, this one and that one, it’s World War 5! 

It’s all very, “human.”  

Speaking of humans. Breaking News! Your all-too-human vagabond has been assembling his cosmogonical 7 dimensional puzzle for a very long time, and it’s beginning to resemble something. All of the numbers that keep showing up in all of the myths, biblical accounts and fairy tales are beginning to make sense. This is where interest becomes obsession. When you’re so close. Any moment now. The final puzzle piece unlocks the “secrets of all the ages.”  

Then you get that unexpected knock on the door of your, uber-secure, bourgeois smart-partment. 

“How did Jehovah’s Witnesses get past security? I’m going to report this to HOA!”  

But it’s not the witnesses, Grub Hub, the Mormons, or Amazon Prime.  

It’s the Freemasons. Your independent study has attracted the wrong kind of attention.   

They are impressed with your scholarship, and your ability to connect the dots and assemble the cosmic puzzle. They have an offer for you. Keep your mouth shut, and join the lodge. You’re very close to the truth about the human story, but there are some gaps that need to be filled in.  

Guess what folks. I’m in. 

“Give me second fellas, let me adjust the AI on the smart-partment app.” And I’m gone. No books. No podcasts. No interviews. No, “the public must know!” Just silence.  

I know, (gnosis-know), why secret societies exist. As previously mentioned, before it got state sponsorship, Christianity was a secret society. Various sects, like the Essenes, Manichaens, and Cathars, were “secret societies,” until they attracted the wrong kind of attention. Now they are just tragic consequences of history.  

Mind is not truly worried. What we will be laying out, is a platter of allegory & fiction. Is it even based on a true story? Who knows? It’s something to do.  

Speaking of intersections, we are at the crossroads of  Season 19 and Season 20 of Full Metal Ox. We’ve been doing this series for 1900 days thus far.  And we are not even half way through. It’s been a good lifestyle to this point.  

Check out our content. There may be something that thrills you enough to, you know.  

Stay strong, stay safe, stay sane, stay savvy, stay serene, stay sovereign, stay subscribed.   

PEACE.

Salvation 
Cosmic Fibonacci
Advancing the herd. Investing your soul, in tech that steals your soul.    

![1965.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd3JZZGBJVcLNQ2eYy9UyYbK8Qa59gMBnwj25yBRf3hKR/1965.png)

Today's Episode:    https://odysee.com/@Noxsoma:2/1900_full_5-13-26_1965_selfimage:a?r=47k2ScJsm9Uex9eETqgCCA8q1fukdST9  
Channels: go to noxsoma.substack.com and subscribe. 

 THE LAST CALM

 How Astrology, Apocalypses, Magical Math & Survivor Skills. 

The science of the Universe is not “real” because real would be too complicated.  

You think you know what time it is.

You glance at your wrist. 5:22 PM. Happy hour. That’s fine. That’s useful. That won’t save your life. Unless you’re dying for a cocktail special.

There’s another clock. The big one. The one carved into every stone circle, painted in every cave, and whispered in every flood myth from Mesopotamia to the Mississippi. It doesn’t tick in seconds. It ticks in ages. Each age is exactly 2,160 years. Each age reduces to the number 9. Everything reduces to 9. And that’s what makes it fake. Everything reducing to a single base number? C’mon man! 

You were born in the Age of Pisces. The fish. The age of faith, of redemption, of two roads that never meet. Let’s say it started around the year 1 CE, give or take a murdered carpenter. The latest Sun Deity. Then it ends in 2160 CE. No one really knows. So let’s pretend. 

That gives us about 135 years of the ichthys. That’s Greek for fish. That the word you see in the Jesus Fish metals on the trunks of cars. 

Relax. That’s the good news. 

The bad news is that you don’t know what an “age” actually is. You think it’s a vibe. A personality quiz. “Oh, I’m such a Pisces, I’m so creative.” 

Nope. That was fine for newspapers back in the day, or a barstool ice breaker. But here’s the etymology, if you will.   

An astrological age is a postcataclysm survival manual. And so is the zodiac. But we’ve forgotten how to read it.  Most of us anyway. 



 Festivals should be called,  “Feastivals.” 

Let’s start with the word you actually need: Feastival.

Not festival. Feastival. Because every single holiday on the calendar is about one thing: food at the right time. 

 Easter isn’t about bunnies. It’s about the first fresh meat after a winter of starvation. The lamb. The egg. The spring equinox, when you stop huddling and start planting. 
 Thanksgiving isn’t about pilgrims. It’s about the autumnal equinox, when you slaughter the surplus because you can’t feed them until spring. 
 Christmas isn’t about a savior. It’s about the winter solstice, the darkest day, when you kill the fatted calf and have one last orgy before the famine. 

The stars told you when. Sirius rising over the Nile? Plant. Orion standing vertical? Harvest. The Pleiades setting at dusk? Run. 

That’s astrology. Not psychology. Logistics.

We’ve degraded it into a parlor game because we’ve never actually been hungry. A mudslide in Spain is a “climate catastrophe” to us. A pillar of fire to a Younger Dryas survivor was Tuesday.



The 100 Generations of Hell

Speaking of the Younger Dryas.

That was a 1,200 year period of constant calamity. It started with a comet impact (or something very mean) and ended with temperatures rising 10°C in a few decades. In between? Mud. Flood. Ash. Fire in the sky. Over and over.

That’s not an event. That’s 100 generations of fighting for the survival of the species. No wonder humans are so psychotic. 

Think about that. Your greatgreatgreatgreat (add 95 more) grandmother was born under an ash-choked sky. She died under an ash-choked sky. Her grandchildren’s grandchildren never saw a clear horizon. 

To those people, calamity wasn’t a “crisis.” It was eternity. They built stone calendars not because they were curious about the cosmos, but because the sky was the only thing that didn’t lie. The river lied. The game lied. The ground lied (especially when it shook). 

But the stars? The stars marched in perfect, indifferent time. 

So they carved the rules into stone. When the sun enters Pisces, the rains come. Feastival. When the sun enters Virgo, the grain is dry. Feastival. When the sun enters Capricorn, the days stop shrinking. You made it. Feastival. 

These weren’t “holidays.” They were launch checklists for survival. Maybe those days were more “whole” than “holy.” 

And then the climate calmed down. The Holocene arrived. And we forgot why we wrote anything down in the first place. Those stone calendars became locations for ritual sacrifice. What a difference an age makes. 



When the Language Dies.  

“Who needs a book when you have a PDF?”

Answer: The person who survives the collapse. 

A PDF requires a charged battery and a working screen. A book requires a literate reader. But a book written in a language no one speaks? That’s not a book anymore. That’s a brick. Or an amulet. Or a holy text. Eli had such a book. (The Book of Eli.) 

This is the lifecycle of every technology. 

1.  Utility: You carve a calendar because you will die if you plant too late. 
2.  Convenience: You print the calendar because paper is easier. 
3.  Obsolescence: You put the calendar on your phone because you’re not a peasant. 
4.  Collapse: The power grid fails. The phone is a pretty black mirror. 
5.  Mystification: Your grandchildren find the carved stone. They can’t read the symbols. But they look important. Magical, even. Someone claims to understand them. That someone now has power. 

Congratulations. You’ve just invented religion. 

That’s not cynicism. That’s archeology. The Egyptian hieroglyphs were inventory lists (“300 jars of oil, 50 chariots”) until no one could read them. Then they became sacred magic. The Greek Linear B was accounting until it became a mystical puzzle. The Hebrew Bible was tribal boundary law until it became the unerring word of God. Tens of thousands of Sumerian cuneiform clay tabled of shopping lists, receipts and honeydew lists. (Honey, do this. Honey, do that.)  

When the original purpose fades, we project meaning into the void.  

We’re doing it right now with astrology. We think it’s about “personalities” because we’ve never had to ask the stars when to plant or die. 



 The Math of 9.  

Here’s something we noticed. Something the astrologers don’t like to admit.  

All the numbers of precession reduce to 9.

 The Great Year: 25,920 years. 2+5+9+2+0 = 18. 1+8 = 9.
 One age: 2,160 years. 2+1+6+0 = 9.
 Degrees in a circle: 360. 3+6+0 = 9.
 Precession rate: 72 years per degree. 7+2 = 9.

Only the 30 degrees of each zodiac sign breaks the pattern. (30 reduces to 3, which is just 9 waiting to happen.)  

Here’s the secret they don’t tell you: They fit the stars to the math, not the math to the stars. 

The actual precession of the equinoxes is 25,772 years. A messy, irregular number. But you can’t build a religion on 25,772. You can’t build a calendar. You can’t teach it to survivors standing around a fire, shivering, watching the sky for any sign that the world isn’t over. 

So they rounded it. They made it perfect. They made it sacred. 

The universe isn’t perfect. The universe is a chaotic, wet, indifferent machine. But we are patternmakers. We see 9 in everything because we put it there. 

That’s not a flaw. That’s the only reason we’re still here. 



 The Calm. 

Here’s the part nobody wants to hear.

We are living in the most stable climate in 100,000 years. The Holocene. 11,700 years of mild temperatures, predictable seasons, and sea levels that mostly stayed put.

It’s an anomaly. A geological fluke. But maybe, it has to do with a population of humans on the planet. Maybe we should call this, “human caused global stability.” 

The Younger Dryas survivors couldn’t imagine calm. They assumed fire and flood were eternal. We assume calm is eternal. We’re both wrong.

The difference is that they built monuments to remember how to survive. We built spreadsheets to forget.

 A mudslide in Italy is global news.
 A flood in Spain is a catastrophe.
 A heat wave in Canada is unprecedented.

To a Younger Dryas human, these would be quiet afternoons.

They saw pillars of fire (volcanoes). They saw skies that stayed dark for years (comet dust). They saw deluge after deluge (meltwater pulses). And they looked up at the stars—the only reliable thing left—and they carved the rules into stone.

We look up and check the weather app.



 Happy Hour Bar Talk. 

So here you are. Sitting at a bar. Someone says, “I’m so a Pisces.”

Me, being a smart-ass having recently co-composed this article for my Substack, “Actually, the Age of Pisces ends in 2160. It’s a 2,160 year postal code for survival. The fish meant flood. The fish meant faith. The fish meant two paths: plant or die. Every festival on your calendar is a feastival, and every feastival is a memory of a famine.”

They will stare at you.

Then order another round. (If they don’t throw it in your face, it’s a good sign.) 

Because that’s what we do now. We drink to forget that we ever knew how to read the sky. We outsource our memory to PDFs, and chat-bots, and we assume the power will never go out. 

But the stones are still there. Göbekli Tepe. Stonehenge. The pyramids. Every flood myth. Every harvest holiday. Every time you eat a hot cross bun on Good Friday or turkey on the fourth Thursday of November. 

You are executing ancient code. Survival firmware. Written in a language you no longer speak. 

The sky is not a personality quiz. 

The sky is the oldest clock we have. And it’s still ticking. 

135 years left on the current age. 

That’s not a threat. 

That’s an invitation to remember.  

For the survivor who keeps a stone in their pocket and a PDF on their phone. One of them will outlast the other. You know which.

body.title: Life Then and Now: A Huge Difference
body.body:
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/zoe01/23wMcXHLXUTaRgoNdSDW7byWVz5sLBgaezzhVFrJPgP7pb7G3BAVLuH8d8ubb9ph2BsSY.png)

Sometimes I have thoughts of being born in a different era and it kind of scares me. Because I feel that I will have nothing to do if I try to live in the old era when I'm so used to the modern era. It would be really hard to spend my days. 

So, I personally believe that I am living in one of the best eras in history. To be honest, I do sometimes feel like being born in a different era could have made a few things better for me. I also think that every era has its own beauty, but not only that every era has its own struggles. Yet, I feel lucky to be born in the present time. 

If I was born in the old era then I would be old and gone long ago and wouldn't be able to experience new technologies. Now we have everything advanced, even if we are at home we can still reach people from other countries. Now we have better communication. Moreover, cures for many diseases has been found by modern medicine.

We have more opportunities than what older times offered. Even though life is still difficult in many ways. I compare it to the past, then I would say people didn't have as much freedom back in the day, as they do now. We have freedom and comfort.

I feel bad about our ancestors, the life they used to live. Like my grandmother and my mom's grandmother, they did not have the opportunity to study. Education for girls was considered as a loss project. Before in the past, many parents in Bangladesh used to worry when they found out they were expecting a daughter. Because there was a tradition of giving dowry when marrying off their daughters, which was gonna cost a lot of money. So, the parents used to educate the boys only as boys would stay with their own parents. 

And the women after marriage would move in with their in-laws. So, no one felt the necessity to educate their daughters. Even the girls never felt the urge to study because they were brainwashed by the environment they lived in. And if someone wanted to continue their studies it was not allowed by parents. So, child marriage was very common in Bangladesh. 

Even my grandma was married when she was only 14. Whenever I asked my grandma how she felt and whether the marriage was done without her consent, she replied, \

Then she laughed as if it was a normal thing, she also keeps asking me when I'll get married. I was really shocked as I'm still young. I believe she doesn't even know what she has done to herself, she only knows to cook for everyone, serve her husband and take care of the kids. I am not saying it's a bad thing but I doubt she knows what she likes to do in her free time. To be honest, I felt like I was talking to an NPC. There were many situations where men dominated women in the old era. So, I do not wish to be born in that kind of era. I realize how hard life was for women back then. Not only that a hundred years ago there was no electricity or internet, people used to die because of illness as there was no proper healthcare. If someone wanted to travel from one place to another it would take a long time. Communication was barely possible and very slow. Like if I ever had to go abroad and if I wanted to contact my parents then I would have to write letters and it could take weeks or months to reach them. But in recent times, we can video call our family or friends whenever we want to. Even if I want to meet new people from different countries that is possible within a few seconds. Just like now I'm in Bangladesh but my post would be reaching many international people. This is the most amazing thing for me. My personal favourite is the internet of this era. Because I never feel bored, I can learn languages at home just by watching videos. There are countless videos where teachers are teaching online. I can learn new things every day. I can also learn dancing from online tutorials. Whenever I have a doubt about something or there's something I don't know about, I would search it online and within seconds I'm adding new things to my knowledge. But still I would be lying if I say our era has no problems, well there are many because of social media. Like people can easily spread fake news or there's lots of online bullying. This can ruin one's mental health, but if we learn to control our emotions things can get better. Nothing is good when it's done excessively. So we should not completely become dependent on technology. And again if I had the choice to change my era then I would not. Because I enjoy the opportunities we have today. Women’s empowerment has improved a lot in Bangladesh and I can imagine myself becoming a content creator in the future. But still, no era is perfect or the best. There will be challenges in every generation. ____ The images are created with [Gemini](gemini.google.com) and edited with [Canva](www.canva.con) ____

body.title: The era that made the common man live like a king [EN/PT]
body.body: > At night, if I’m hungry, I grab my phone and order food through an app. I’m not bored, I’m enjoying one of the thousands of entertainment options available on my TV. I know it’s probably going to rain tomorrow afternoon, and I should also bring warmer clothes because it will get a bit colder by nightfall. I settle comfortably into my soft bed, with my warm and nice-smelling blankets, and go to sleep. I wake up, open the garage, and greet my neighbor. I get into my car and comfortably drive to work, and during the drive, I think that in a few years, or rather in just a few months, I might be able to buy a self-driving car. At work, I sit in a chair, passionately talk with my friends about yesterday’s game and about how good the food at restaurant X is. I grab a fresh coffee from the coffee machine and comfortably return to work. It’s 6 PM, and it rained a little, but it’s definitely colder now. Good thing I checked the app and remembered this morning to bring a jacket. Funny, isn’t it? This could be the “exhausting” routine of thousands of people in today’s world, and we’ve become so used to this convenience that we think it’s normal. And yes, it is normal for our era, the era of convenience. So many accessible things, everything is just too easy, and it’s hard to imagine life being any different. That’s why I’d hesitate between calling the age we live in the age of convenience or the age of accessibility. It has never been so accessible to be comfortable, live well, and have so many things. Look back and imagine what the daily life of someone living maybe 100 years ago was like. Completely different. A routine perhaps focused entirely on survival. Difficulties came from everywhere. Today, we are people privileged by modernity. So far, this is the best era, and it seems that every year things become even easier. Look at food. It has never been easier to eat. So many overweight people, and perhaps being overweight was once only a privilege of the nobility during the medieval era. Maybe 500 years ago, only select groups had access to food in excess. Now we have food in abundance, maybe not the best food, because you know industrialization corrupts quality, but we have food. And this same industrialization is what allowed fewer people to go hungry. It’s not just accessibility, and it’s not just food. It’s everything. Everything exists in abundance. You can have almost anything. You can even own a piece of land, like a nobleman in medieval times. You can have multiple professions or change careers whenever you want. We truly are living like royalty. You get sick less often, and when you do, treatments are more accessible and there are cures for almost everything. You can travel to another continent and arrive there the very same day, and if you want to talk to someone on the other side of the world, you can do it instantly. We don’t have feudal lords. It has never been so safe to live. If we are dissatisfied, we can protest, we can exercise freedom of speech, we are not oppressed by power in the same way people were in other eras. I could spend days listing all the things we now have so easily. I love living in these times and, even compared to a few decades ago, today I have far more possibilities. Would I like to live in other eras? Well, that’s a difficult question for a man who loves the medieval age so much and dreams about knights, exploring territories, and defeating enemies. But thinking that I could have been just a peasant with a life expectancy of thirty-something years makes me change my mind, if living in another era were a choice. We live like true nobles of past ages. We possess more knowledge than kings or the wisest men of past civilizations. How can you look at this and not feel lucky? In all the years of human history, you were born here, in the best era possible. --- Credits: Translated: [Deepl](www.deepl.com/pt-BR/translator) Cover: created by [Canva.](www.canva.com) AI-generated image [ Flow]( www.labs.google/fx/pt/tools/flow) --- ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma2XinqppUM2Uvqbsii8ViPirxPmkbLmJ8FkfAbcj9EYN/image.png) Of course, despite all these conveniences, challenges still exist. Not everything is perfect. But imagine walking up to someone living in the 1800s and telling them all this. They wouldn’t even be able to imagine it. Imagine! We are living in the best era, without a doubt. Will it stay this way forever? Since we don’t know if it will, we are even luckier. Maybe all of this will collapse in a few years or decades. Or maybe it will improve even more. Will we even need to work in the future, or will artificial intelligence do it for us? Will we live only on universal basic income, enjoying life even more? Will everything become even easier and more accessible? Wow… so many questions. I wish I could live longer just to see what the future will look like. But I can say that, in all of human history, up until this exact moment, in any area you can point to, we are privileged in almost everything. But of course, easy times create fears. Superficial fears? I don’t know. But I remember the phrase that says easy times are created by strong men, but easy times create weak men, and weak men create hard times. Are we the weak men who will create hard times? Or is that cycle just nonsense? I don’t know, but while I think about it, I’m going to order some food through an app because all this conversation made me hungry. À noite, se estou com fome, pego meu celular e peço comida por aplicativo. Não estou entediado, estou desfrutando de uma das milhares de opções de entretenimento disponíveis na minha TV. Eu sei que amanhã deve chover pela tarde e devo levar também uma roupa mais quente, pois vai esfriar um pouco ao anoitecer. Me acomodo confortavelmente em minha cama macia, com meus cobertores quentinhos e cheirosos, e vou dormir. Acordo, abro a garagem e cumprimento o vizinho. Entro em meu carro e dirijo confortavelmente até meu trabalho e, durante o caminho, penso que daqui a alguns anos, ou melhor, daqui a alguns meses, poderei comprar um carro autônomo. No meu trabalho, sento em uma cadeira, converso acaloradamente com meus amigos sobre o jogo de ontem e sobre como a comida do restaurante X é boa. Tomo um café fresco da cafeteira e volto a trabalhar confortavelmente. São 18 horas, e choveu um pouco, mas realmente está fazendo mais frio. Ainda bem que olhei o aplicativo e me lembrei hoje pela manhã de trazer um casaco. Engraçado, né? Essa pode ser a rotina “cansativa” de milhares de pessoas no mundo de hoje, e nos acostumamos tanto com essa facilidade que achamos que isso é o normal. Sim, é o normal da nossa era, a era das facilidades. Quantas coisas acessíveis, é tudo fácil demais e difícil é imaginar algo diferente disso. Por isso, eu ficaria em dúvida em nomear a era em que vivemos como a era das facilidades ou da acessibilidade. Nunca foi tão acessível estar confortável, viver bem e ter tantas coisas. Olhe para trás e imagine como seria a rotina de uma pessoa que viveu talvez há 100 anos. Totalmente diferente. Uma rotina talvez até mesmo voltada para a sobrevivência. As dificuldades vinham de todos os lugares. Somos hoje pessoas privilegiadas pela modernidade. Até aqui, esta é a melhor era, e parece que, a cada ano, as coisas ficam ainda mais fáceis. Olhe para a alimentação: nunca foi tão fácil se alimentar. Tantas pessoas gordas, e talvez ser gordo fosse apenas um privilégio da nobreza na era medieval, a talvez 500 anos atrás, apenas grupos seletos tinha acessibilidade a comida em excesso. Temos comida em abundância agora, talvez não das melhores comidas, pois você sabe que a industrialização corrompe a qualidade, mas temos comida. Mas essa mesma industrialização é o que proporcionou que menos pessoas passassem fome. Não é apenas acessibilidade, e não é apenas comida: é tudo. Tudo está em abundância. Você consegue ter quase qualquer coisa. Você consegue até mesmo ter um pedaço de terra, como um nobre da era medieval. Você pode ter várias profissões ou mudar de carreira a qualquer momento. Estamos vivendo, sim, como uma pessoa da realeza. Você adoece com menos frequência e, se adoece, tem tratamentos mais acessíveis e cura para quase tudo. Você pode ir para outro continente e chegar lá no mesmo dia e, se quiser falar com uma pessoa do outro lado do mundo, pode fazer isso instantaneamente. Não temos senhores feudais. Nunca foi tão seguro viver. Se estamos insatisfeitos, podemos protestar, podemos exercer nossa liberdade de expressão, não somos oprimidos pelo poder da mesma forma que em outras eras. Poderia ficar aqui dias listando tudo o que temos de forma tão fácil. Eu amo viver isso que estamos vivendo e, mesmo comparando com décadas atrás, hoje eu tenho muito mais possibilidades. Eu gostaria de viver em outras eras? Poxa, é uma pergunta difícil para um homem que ama tanto a era medieval e sonha com cavaleiros, desbravar territórios e derrotar inimigos. Mas pensar que eu poderia ser apenas um camponês, com expectativa de vida de trinta e poucos anos, me faz mudar de ideia, se viver em outra era fosse uma escolha. Vivemos como verdadeiros nobres de épocas passadas. Temos mais conhecimento que reis ou os mais sábios de eras passadas. Como não olhar para isso e não se sentir um sortudo? Em todos os anos da humanidade, você nasceu aqui, na melhor era possível. Claro, apesar de todas as facilidades, existem desafios. Nem tudo é um mar de rosas. Mas imagine chegar para uma pessoa que está vivendo em 1800 e falar sobre tudo isso. Ela nem conseguiria imaginar. Imaginar! Estamos vivendo a melhor era, com toda a certeza. Será que será assim para sempre? Se não sabemos se ainda será assim, somos ainda mais sortudos. Pode ser que tudo isso acabe daqui a alguns anos ou décadas. Pode ser que melhore. Será que vamos precisar trabalhar no futuro ou a inteligência artificial fará isso por nós? Viveremos apenas com uma renda básica universal, desfrutando ainda mais da vida? Tudo ficará ainda mais fácil e acessível? Uau… tantas perguntas, gostaria de viver mais para ver como vai ser. Mas posso dizer que, de toda a história da humanidade, até este exato momento, em qualquer área que você apontar, estamos privilegiados em tudo. Mas claro, esses tempos fáceis geram medos. Medos superficiais? Não sei. Mas me lembro da frase que diz que tempos fáceis são criados por homens fortes, mas esses tempos fáceis criam homens fracos, e esses homens fracos geram tempos difíceis. Será que somos os homens fracos que vão criar os tempos difíceis? Ou esse ciclo é apenas bobagem? Não sei, mas enquanto penso, vou pedir uma comida por aplicativo, toda essa conversa me deu fome. --- Credits: Translated: [Deepl](www.deepl.com/pt-BR/translator) Cover: created by [Canva.](www.canva.com) AI-generated image [ Flow]( www.labs.google/fx/pt/tools/flow) --- ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma2XinqppUM2Uvqbsii8ViPirxPmkbLmJ8FkfAbcj9EYN/image.png)

body.title: Would I stay without a reward or not?
body.body:
>

![4d462ebb51004886af5303460011d63b.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nwaadiaha/23zkpQbs3p5gab327X43mrjkQ37BD1c1K6zcpLA2HHZDs5TkX71qjTWR1imuErCgY4hVz.jpg)

I created my Hive account last year but for some reason, I wasn't consistent, I am still not consistent till now but then, unlike last year when I started blogging, I now engage and join some community contests, to keep my page going, but let's imagine, what Hive would be or look like without rewards, I am sure many people like me, the first narrative we got and made us joined this platform is the \

at least a side pay away from our monthly wages or salary. Our urgent money bank when we have no monthly or daily wages, a bank to fall back to when we are in critical situations, these and more were the reasons many people joined the platform, before they got to enjoy the account growth, circle of friends or bloggers like themselves, and engagement that comes with being here. Truthfully, when I started or joined Hive it was because of the rewards I heard of but it's been how many months now and I have never withdrawn from my wallet to buy anything, but it's something I hope to do someday, although for now, I hope it happens the way I wish it to. ___ ___ ___ The rewards on my post aren't encouraging and as a new blogger, it's discouraging but I still come here to engage and drop a post, just so it doesn't become dormant like it was throughout last year after my introduction post here. The funny part is I would take my time to sit and pen down a long minutes read and at the end of the day, I get no reward on the post, most times I wonder if it is because the post is too lengthy that is why or perhaps it is because I am a new person here but regardless it isn't encouraging. So, based on the prompt question, I have already assumed that I am not getting reasonable rewards, I mean most weeks, my rewards hold no worth, so i am believing this phase is a growing phase, but I am still here, so it automatically means, I am not here anymore because of just the rewards as I had intended from the onset but because I get to have a space where I pour out my heart, most times get rewards other times get nothing for it. The anticipation of the rewards I would be getting if I came back was what fueled my return to this platform. So, maybe if I were told it was a platform that doesn't pay, I wouldn't have joined but I was told it is a platform that pays and it would favour a student like myself who is finding it hard to get a job due to school but I am staying and still here not because of the reward but because I am enjoying it. ___ ___ ___ The image is mine ___ ___ ___

body.title: The price of creative freedom.
body.body: <center>[The Hollywood Reporter](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/rust-spotlight-on-opaque-indie-film-financing-scheme-1235045182/)</center>\nYesterday, I was talking with some friends (also movie buffs, just like me) about the \

that the most daring filmmakers, who defy the natural order of orthodox thoughts and behaviors, pay when they exercise their right to place the weight of their personal viewpoints on their own projects, testing them on a moral and ethical scale that is almost always frowned upon by the more conservative public. This is not a recent dilemma.\nAlthough the movie industry has evolved considerably in dealing with themes involving minorities (globally), the path to full equality (at all levels, so to speak) is still very long. Fortunately, the presence of these filmmakers has become increasingly larger and more relevant, bringing a more balanced weight to a scale that remains very unequal. Basically, because they are the ones who challenge conservative logic.\nOn the other hand, the price they pay is bitter. There is a considerable (and traditionally known) lack of space for movies considered \

to be produced and released, not to mention the fact that there is still a very small percentage of recognition for their work in major awards (for example) and even from the perspective of an audience that often remains unaware of the work they continue to do (and that is just as important, on a much larger scale).\n<center>[The Ringer](https://www.theringer.com/2018/10/18/movies/the-30-best-truly-independent-films-of-the-21st-century)</center>\nThe same creative freedom they have is what ends up keeping them \

in a cage where entertainment becomes a source of reflection for those who want to delve into it, because the big studios are still quite oblivious to these types of more complex approaches in their projects. This is not necessarily bad (quite the contrary), because they break a paradox where cinema is seen only as an \

to get away from reality.\nThus, the price these filmmakers usually pay to maintain their positioning in their movies is almost always very high, and almost always never accepted by those at the top of the \
within this segment. As a filmmaker who likes to think \

, I greatly value these types of filmmakers, because their vision on the themes addressed always presents more challenging lines of thought. Creative freedom matters.\nWithin the *mainstream* cinema (which is largely more traditional) the creative freedom is real, but everything is limited to filmmakers who are already known on an international scale and who have the right to \

against the vision of the heads of major studios (something that doesn't even happen with filmmakers who have their own production companies). Therefore, it is within the well-known independent cinema that the breeding ground for the most transgressive minds resides, and they accept paying the price of \

.
---
<center>**El precio de la libertad creativa.**</center>
Ayer, conversaba con algunos amigos (también cinéfilos, así como yo) sobre el \

que pagan los cineastas más audaces, quienes desafían el orden natural del pensamiento y el comportamiento ortodoxos, al ejercer su derecho a plasmar sus puntos de vista personales en sus proyectos, sometiéndolos a un análisis moral y ético que casi siempre es mal visto por el público más conservador. Este no es un dilema reciente.\nSi bien la industria cinematográfica ha evolucionado considerablemente en el tratamiento de temas relacionados con las minorías (a nivel mundial), el camino hacia la plena igualdad (en todos los niveles, por así decirlo) aún es muy largo. Afortunadamente, la presencia de estos cineastas se ha vuelto cada vez más importante y relevante, aportando un equilibrio a una balanza que sigue siendo muy desigual. Básicamente, porque son ellos quienes desafían la lógica conservadora.\nPor otro lado, el precio que pagan es amargo. Existe una considerable (y tradicionalmente conocida) falta de espacio para que se produzcan y estrenen películas consideradas \

, sin mencionar el hecho de que todavía existe un porcentaje muy pequeño de reconocimiento para su trabajo en los principales premios (por ejemplo) e incluso desde la perspectiva de un público que a menudo desconoce la labor que siguen realizando (y eso es igual de importante, a una escala mucho mayor). \nLa misma libertad creativa de la que gozan es lo que termina manteniéndolos \

en una jaula donde el entretenimiento se convierte en una fuente de reflexión para quienes desean profundizar en él, ya que los grandes estudios siguen siendo bastante ajenos a este tipo de enfoques más complejos en sus proyectos. Esto no es necesariamente malo (todo lo contrario), porque rompen una paradoja donde el cine se ve solo como una \

para alejarse de la realidad.\nPor lo tanto, el precio que estos cineastas suelen pagar para mantener su posición en sus películas es casi siempre muy alto, y casi nunca aceptado por quienes están en la cima de la \
dentro de este segmento. Como cinéfilo al que le gusta de pensar \

, valoro enormemente a este tipo de cineastas, porque su visión sobre los temas que abordan siempre presenta líneas de pensamiento más desafiantes. La libertad creativa importa. En el cine *mainstream* (que suele ser más tradicional) existe una cierta libertad criativa, pero todo se limita a cineastas ya reconocidos internacionalmente que tienen derecho a “oponerse” a la visión de los directivos de los grandes estudios (algo que ni siquiera ocurre con los cineastas que tienen sus propias productoras). Por lo tanto, es en el cine independiente, ya consolidado, donde se gestan las mentes más transgresoras, quienes aceptan pagar el precio de la “invisibilidade”. ---
**O preço da liberdade criativa.**
Ontem, eu estava conversando com alguns amigos (também cinéfilos, assim como eu) sobre o “preço” que os cineastas mais ousados, e que desfiam a ordem natural dos pensamentos e comportamentos ortodoxos pagam, quando exercem o direito de colocar o peso dos seus pontos de vistas pessoais nos seus próprios projetos, testando-os em uma balança moral e de bons costumes que quase sempre é mal vista pelo público mais conservador. Isso não é um dilema recente. Embora a indústria cinematográfica já tenha evoluído consideravelmente ao lidar com temáticas envolvendo minorias (a nível global), o caminho pela equidade plena (em todas as camadas, por assim dizer) ainda é muito longo. Felizmente a presença desses cineastas tem se tornado cada vez maior e mais relevante, trazendo um peso mais equilibrado para uma balança que ainda segue sendo muito desigual. Basicamente, porque são eles que desafiam a lógica conservadora. Por outro lado, o preço que eles pagam é amargo. Há uma considerável (e tradicionalmente conhecida) falta de espaço para que os filmes ditos como “controversos” sejam produzidos e lançados, sem mencionar o fato de ainda haver uma porcentagem muito pequena em relação ao reconhecimento do trabalho deles em grandes premiações (por exemplo) e até mesmo sob a ótica de uma audiência que por muitas vezes ainda desconhece o trabalho que eles seguem fazendo (e que é tão importante, numa escala bem maior). A mesma liberdade criativa que eles têm, é o que acaba mantendo-os “presos” em uma gaiola onde o entretenimento se torna uma fonte de reflexão para quem quer mergulhar nela, porque os grandes estúdios ainda são bastante alheios a esses tipos de abordagens mais complexas em seus projetos. Isso não é necessariamente ruim (muito pelo contrário), porque eles rompem um paradoxo onde o cinema é visto apenas como uma “válvula de escape” para fugir da realidade. Sendo assim, o preço que esses cineastas costumam pagar para manter o posicionamento dele em seus filmes é quase sempre muito caro, e quase sempre nunca aceito por quem está no topo de “cadeia alimentar” dentro desse segmento. Enquanto cinéfilo que gosta de pensar “fora da caixa”, eu valorizo demais esses tipos de cineastas, porque a visão deles sobre os temas abordados sempre apresentam linhas de pensamentos mais desafiadoras. A liberdade criativa importa. Há uma certa liberdade criativa no cinema *mainstream* (que é amplamente mais tradicional), mas tudo fica limitado aos cineastas que já são conhecidos em uma escala internacional e que tem o direito de “brigar” contra à visão dos chefes de grandes estúdios (o que sequer acontece com os cineastas que tem suas próprias produtoras). Logo, é dentro conhecido cinema independente que mora o celeiro das mentes mais transgressoras, e que aceitam pagar o preço de uma “invisibilidade”. Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@wiseagent/the-price-of-creative-freedom-9ni)

body.title: The Message I Never Replied To
body.body:
![samuelfjohanns-pen-4163403_1920 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbxz7fGSmMWBCSCVbnQBxhrF1tDHBTRYHTMJJGWiq8RF6/samuelfjohanns-pen-4163403_1920%20(1).jpg)
image source : https://pixabay.com/

Hello friends, my post today is a bit emotional—messages like these that you and I inevitably remember at some point. 

A kind of silence that eats you up inside, your emotions sometimes don't cooperate, you just don't feel like doing anything. Why does this happen, friends? Can you tell me? 

As far as I think, we also ignore some messages because we get confused; we don't know what to reply. But over time we realize that even a simple reply could have fixed a lot, which we probably ignored at the time out of ignorance. 


Friends, from this we learn that your communication skills should be strong and your mind quick enough to make decisions in time. Many people, myself included, are like this: no matter what you say to them, they don't immediately know how to respond—but by then the opportunity may already be long gone and you won't be able to take advantage of it. is gone, and then you remember, “Oh yeah, I should have said that,” but by then the opportunity has probably slipped far from your grasp and you don't get any benefit from it. 

Now the result of this, friends, is that when it comes to me, I can't leave messages pending for too long, because some special moments never come back and some people don't wait around again. The messages I didn't reply to are still somewhere in my mind, because they're not It was my silence that made it memorable, and that person drifted away from me forever.

Friends, sometimes in life the things we remember most are those messages we simply can't reply to. We see the message—someone's message that they sent us from their feelings—but we ignore it at the time, or we can't read it because we don't have the time. Some messages… Sometimes in life we get so caught up that we don't even realize what's happening to us. In that moment, we forget the special message our loved ones have sent us. Not replying to a message doesn't mean we're rejecting them or ignoring them or… Not talking doesn't mean you don't want to talk to them. It may be that at the moment you don't have an answer to give them, but often it comes to mind later on.

body.title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Treatment for Cancer: Exploring Its Potential Benefits
body.body:
Cancer treatment has evolved significantly over the years, with medical professionals continuously exploring innovative therapies to improve patient outcomes and quality of life. One emerging supportive therapy gaining attention is [Hyperbaric Oxygen Treatment for Cancer](https://www.thewellnesslab.com/hyperbaric-oxygen-treatment-for-cancer/). While it is not considered a standalone cure for cancer, hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) may play a valuable role in supporting recovery and managing side effects related to conventional cancer treatments.

Hyperbaric oxygen therapy involves breathing pure oxygen inside a pressurized chamber. Under these conditions, the lungs absorb more oxygen than they would under normal atmospheric pressure. This increased oxygen supply is then delivered throughout the body via the bloodstream, helping damaged tissues heal more efficiently.

For cancer patients, HBOT is most commonly used to address complications caused by radiation therapy. Radiation treatments, although effective at targeting cancer cells, can also damage healthy tissues surrounding the affected area. This may result in chronic pain, tissue injury, poor wound healing, or reduced blood supply. [Hyperbaric Oxygen Treatment for Cancer](https://www.thewellnesslab.com/hyperbaric-oxygen-treatment-for-cancer/) patients may help stimulate the growth of new blood vessels, reduce inflammation, and support tissue repair in areas damaged by radiation.

Research has shown that HBOT can be beneficial for conditions such as radiation cystitis, radiation proctitis, and osteoradionecrosis, particularly in patients who have undergone treatment for head, neck, pelvic, or prostate cancers. By improving oxygen delivery to compromised tissues, the therapy may accelerate healing and reduce discomfort.

Another reason for the growing interest in Hyperbaric Oxygen Treatment for Cancer is its potential ability to improve overall wellness during recovery. Some patients report increased energy levels, better wound healing after surgery, and improved quality of life following sessions. Although scientific studies continue to investigate its broader applications, many healthcare providers already use HBOT as part of integrative cancer care programs.

However, it is important to understand that hyperbaric oxygen therapy should always be administered under medical supervision. Not every cancer patient is a suitable candidate, and treatment plans should be personalized based on medical history, cancer type, and ongoing therapies. Patients considering HBOT should consult with oncologists and certified hyperbaric medicine specialists before starting treatment.

As research progresses, [Hyperbaric Oxygen Treatment for Cancer](https://www.thewellnesslab.com/hyperbaric-oxygen-treatment-for-cancer/) continues to attract interest as a complementary therapy that may help reduce treatment-related complications and support recovery. While it is not a replacement for chemotherapy, radiation, or surgery, HBOT offers promising potential in enhancing comfort, healing, and overall patient care during the cancer journey.

body.title: When an Old Wagon Suddenly Decides Your Fate in Splinterlands
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmetF6uTit6iKVuiSYNaxcLfXsX67S3vNuCirz1PbF6TBp/escalation_conflicts.png)


What’s up, Splinterlands grinders.

Lately the arena’s been getting crowded as hell. Just when we finally adapt to new rulesets, new skins, new cards—boom, another feature drops. And this one? Feels less like a battle mechanic and more like… straight-up logistics warfare. They call it **Escalation Conflict**.

At first I thought, “Yeah, just another event.”
Stake some cards, chill, wait for rewards to rain down like free loot.

But nah… after digging into it and actually trying to understand the system, it hit me: this isn’t RNG carrying you. This is prep work, strategy, and how deep you’re willing to dive into the Splinterlands ecosystem.

And the wildest part?
This time it’s not about monsters. Not summoners.
It’s about a damn **Mage Wagon**.

---

I’m not gonna lie—I never thought I’d see the day where I’d seriously worry about the condition of a virtual wagon. But that’s Splinterlands for you. Sometimes it’s not the dragon that decides your fate… it’s the wooden wheels.

In **Escalation Conflict**, you stake cards or **Escalation Mini-Set packs** into a Mage Wagon over a 30-day event. That earns you points, and those points decide your shot at pulling a legendary Archon airdrop.

And the first Archon they dropped?
Name goes hard: **MEREDROOL**.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUGeUpCajvSLnjx7ZPfJidny9d26m86zNcT75BzYndsCt/meredrool.png)


The moment I saw that, I was like:
“Yep… this is gonna be a bloodbath.”

---

### Looks Simple… Until You Start Doing the Math

On paper, it’s easy:

* stake cards
* stack points
* wait for airdrop

Done, right?

Yeah… not even close.

One Mage Wagon can only carry **5 cards or 100 packs**.

Want another wagon?

* 2 Wagon Kits
  or
* buy it with DEC/Credits

And don’t forget repair costs—because after you get an airdrop, your wagon can get wrecked.

Yeah. Read that again.

Every time you score an airdrop, there’s a chance one of your wagons gets damaged and needs fixing.

<center>![](https://images.ecency.com/DQma6R7Hj4fPkQ94AnKgH1b8DWyHt52j5QHz26GHHbGhEUc/repair.png)</center>


So it basically feels like a real war sim.
You win the battle, grab the loot… but your ride back home is barely holding together.

---

### My Struggle: Big Ambitions, Small Inventory

Once I saw how the points work, I started checking my own collection.

And as usual… my ambition is way bigger than my stash.

You earn points from:

* your card’s Collection Power
* or Escalation packs (125 points each)

So yeah, whales have a head start. No surprise there.
But that doesn’t mean smaller players are out.

That’s where I had to check myself.

Instead of forcing a full-send play, maybe it’s smarter to optimize what I actually have.

And honestly?
That brought back an old-school Splinterlands feeling—
that long-term strategy grind.

---

### The Real Plot Twist

The craziest part isn’t even the rewards.

It’s how this feature ties EVERYTHING together.

To craft Wagon Kits, you need Land resources:

* Wood
* Stone
* Iron
* Aura

Which means this isn’t just for ranked grinders anymore.

Land owners, traders, collectors, crafters—everyone’s got skin in the game now.

Splinterlands is starting to feel like a living world.
Everything connects.

And I’m all for it.

---

### What I Took From This

If there’s one thing this feature taught me, it’s this:

> Winning isn’t always about who fights the hardest—
> it’s about who’s the most prepared before the fight even starts.

And in Splinterlands?
Preparation often costs more than the battle itself.

Whether I pull **MEREDROOL** or not… one thing’s for sure—

This game is getting way too good at keeping us hooked.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXuXxp6GBhwB1HpXvoabLn8Dt8QaRKSe1WNYDzqX1v6Vk/chaos_logo.png)



Talk about Splinterlands,
If you haven't tried out this fantastic game called Splinterlands yet, I invite you to [**Join**](https://splinterlands.com?ref=rqr4).
It's free, but you'll need to invest in a beginning deck or buy gaming cards to gain real assets like cards and tokens. 

___


If you already joined the splinterlands, and are looking for a place to grow. We need **YOU**. We are a chill, social guild looking for a few more active members! If you think you might be a fit, join us in our [**Discord**](https://discord.gg/5u638vHPVh)

body.title: Tu Bienestar - Mensaje diario de 5 minutos
body.body:
Vivir en paz comienza cuando decides que tu bienestar vale más que tener la razón o guardar deudas ajenas en el corazón. 

Perdona, no porque el otro lo merezca, sino porque tú mereces caminar sin peso. 

Cultiva la gratitud como si fuera un jardín; agradece por lo que fue, por lo que se fue y por todo lo nuevo que está haciendo fila para entrar en tu vida. 

Hoy es el mejor día para ser tu mejor versión, para sonreírle al espejo y decir: 'estoy lista para lo que viene', porque lo mejor siempre está por construirse.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYU7G6GjgjVuiCn2BqUZESNUReuQAf9NBbjGu6iaQSTkb/1778516952774.jpg)

ENGLISH

Living in peace begins when you decide that your well-being is worth more than being right or holding on to other people's debts in your heart.

Forgive, not because the other person deserves it, but because you deserve to walk without burden.

Cultivate gratitude as if it were a garden; give thanks for what was, for what has left, and for everything new that is waiting in line to enter your life.

Today is the best day to be your best self, to smile at the mirror and say, \
because the best is always yet to be built.

We can see alot of things that will make us to believe in God around us. The beautiful flowers, sky and trees we see everyday is enough reason for us to believe that God exists. The Bible affirms this truth, saying that the heavens declare the glory of God, showing His power and wisdom through everything that exists. This gives believers confidence that life has purpose and is not the result of random events.

God guides and protects us everyday of our life and is another reason to believe in God. Many people testify to answered prayers, inner peace during trials, and strength in moments of weakness. The Bible teaches that God is near to those who seek Him and rewards those who trust Him sincerely. This relationship builds faith, as believers grow to know God not just intellectually, but through lived experience and spiritual transformation.

body.title: A Walk & Such
body.body:
Walking is one of the ways for me to go on a mental diet. Sort of a mental detox. It's my way of dialing down whenever I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed or when I can't calm my mind. It rejuvenates me, boosts my mood, and clears my brain fog. My attention immediately shifts to the beauty around, and before I know it, I'm feeling better, lighter, and I tend to forget what was bothering me.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ifarmgirl/EoyR31XNKpLMPLuDmhMi6n4iEHYgFvEt2Qd8L4V19f5JThbLVVudpWBeVwrNYurEmLD.jpg
I was out in the open yesterday morning. Walked in the midst of overgrown weeds, grass, and such. I was lost in my thoughts when, suddenly, a flowering shrub at the edge of the property caught my eye. I quickly moved closer to it, excited like a child who had found a new toy.😁 A bee found its way to them, too! When it sensed my presence (I was trying to photograph it), it flew away before I could take any snaps. Anyway, I spent 10 minutes more there, looking at the intricate details of the pods and flowers. Accordingly, the fruits (inside the hairy pods) are edible when ripe. I didn't dare pick any, though. For me, they are meant for the eyes, not for the mouth, lol!
||| |-|-| |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ifarmgirl/EoK5ocMR5LH68TP5QxSvtmQCXZHqzRZ8ZAXfmFxVy8DVW7Fztz33WykEEG7XmjnKD8L.jpg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ifarmgirl/EowGaTv3G9aTbKPEjh8SsNMeZ24tipqYxyCahc7Dh6JQ9JLvdpqhYxnABsj5BM9YnpL.jpg|

I left the spot and headed back to the house, with nothing much in my conscious mind but food! Funny that the short walk made me hungry. body.title: The Benefits of Group Learning for Children\n
body.body: Hello friends, how are you? Today's post is also about a system through which we want to focus on group learning for children. As you know, education is no longer limited to just books; group learning is also considered important for improving children's learning. Now the question arises: how should group learning take place? When children learn at home, their confidence grows, their communication skills improve, and their understanding becomes stronger. In this way, the children can work as a team. \n \n

/>

source : [https://pixabay.com/](https://pixabay.com/)

You may have also noticed that when group learning takes place, children share things with one another. When they share, they develop a sense of unity—that we have to do things together—and by valuing each other, tasks become easier.

If we look at education, one benefit of group learning is that a team member who knows everything can easily teach another child. If even one person is having trouble explaining, another group member can easily teach the children. This also develops communication skills. They improve, and when you explain things to others, your confidence grows. At the same time, some students feel hesitant to ask their teacher, so group learning also benefits them by allowing them to learn things from their friends in an easy, peer-to-peer way.

Well, it also happens that sometimes during lectures in class, when discipline is being enforced, the kids get really restless. In group learning, when friends sit together and study, their boredom disappears; they can easily discuss with each other and they… They read with mutual interest and try to outdo one another. Ultimately, group learning also plays an important role in the children's personality development, teaching them how to be responsible, cooperative, and how to conduct themselves in school and beyond. They should take seriously and act on what is necessary for their parents, guardians, and teachers.
