title.title: I've been on Hive for eight years now [ESP/ENG]
title.body:
![miniatura de youtube minimalista oscuro amarillo.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23vsLbUakuUjA8Vk5KKWy6u2jbpAEYCHmPp9CN3vbtqdtM3k1AteT4waDLRo13WSZYeUi.jpg)

Hello everyone! How are you? I'm so excited about the reminder I just received from Hive—it's been eight years since I started using blockchain! My goodness, how time flies! However, if I told you those eight years were uninterrupted, I'd be lying, because I actually started when Hive was very different (many of you probably already know that story). Anyway, at a certain point, I became disillusioned with the way many moderators ran some communities and how the blockchain was generally managed. I witnessed injustices and was even a victim of them on occasion, so one day I stopped posting and left. After some time (not much, really), one of my cousins, who was also part of Hive back then, contacted me and told me about the new Hive. In fact, she said it had changed its name and that many things had changed, so I decided to give it a try, and since then (about six years ago) I've been part of this wonderful ecosystem. >¡Hola Hola, gente de internet ¿Cómo están? A mi me embarga la emoción con el recordatorio que acabo de recibir por parte de Hive, y es que estoy cumpliendo ya ocho años con la blockchain. ¡Dios mío, como pasa el tiempo! Sin embargo si yo les contase que esos ocho años fueron ininterrumpidos les mentiría, ya que en realidad yo inicié cuando Hive era muy diferente (ya muchos de ustedes deben conocer esa historia) bueno el caso es que en determinado momento yo me llegé a decepcionar por la manera en que muchos moderadores llevaban algunas comunidades y como en general se llevaba la blockchain, presencié injusticias y hasta fue victima de ellas en algunas ocasiones, así que un día dejé de publicar y me retiré, pasado el tiempo (no mucho en realidad) me contactó una de mis primas que también formaba parte de hive en ese entonces y me habló de la nueva Hive, de hecho me dijo que había cambiado de ombre y que muchas cosas habían cambiado, así que decidí darle y dame oportunidad, y desde entonces (hace como seis años) formo parte de este hermoso ecosistema

![kh.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23sK2sTU4mCHXm18BwXQLDMKG5z4BMTwVAih6VJ6cAvNz4eh3vTngv3PLcrm3gVv6cnZw.jpg)

One of the things I find most appealing about Hive is that it not only has a rewards system, but it's also very fair and, above all, real. There are other platforms that promise you tons of things they can never deliver. Sure, it has its quirks and fluctuations, but the earnings you receive are net, unlike YouTube, for example, where they deduct 30% of your income, and sometimes even more. Hive, on the other hand, allows you to grow, save, delegate, invest—in short, it offers many options. But beyond the income I've earned, there's everything I've learned on this platform, the experience I've gained in content creation. In fact, Hive was my inspiration for taking my gaming career seriously, since I especially loved posting gameplay content on Hive Gaming. Now I don't do it as much, at least not in a live-action format, because work doesn't leave me the time.

>Una de las cosas que más me atrae de Hive es que no solo tiene un sistema de recompensas, sino que es muy justo y sobre todo real, ya que hay otras plataformas donde te prometen miles de cosas que jamás podrán darte, claro que tiene sus detalles y sus fluctuaciones pero las ganancias que recibes son netas, a diferencia de youtube, por ejemplo, donde te descuenta el 30 % de tus ingresos, y a veces hasta más. Hive en cambio te permite crecer, ahorrar, delegar, invertir, en fin, son muchas las opciones que te da, pero en fin, más allá de los ingresos que he logrado obtener está todo lo aprendido en esta plataforma, la experiencia ganada en cuanto a creación de contenido se refiere, de hecho Hive fue mi inspiración para tomarme en serio mi faceta como gamer, ya que sobre todo yo amaba postear contenido sobre gameplays en Hive gaming, ahora no lo hago tanto, al menos no en formato vidao, porque el trabajo no me deja tiempo.
![hf5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23tGVUj8ovq3GP6yJZKdduLYeZwyHExvD74wVaiHHvkQQir5uvW7PCTUkENQYJ2oF44vX.jpg)

Hive has allowed me to be creative by sharing my daily activities and staying active on the blockchain because I'm always thinking about what to upload. Whenever I see something beautiful or interesting, I think about which community to share it with. I believe all of this has helped me become more communicative and expressive. It has also helped with my writing, something I struggled with when I started on Hive, but I feel I've gained fluency now, which is very satisfying.

>Hive me ha permitido ser creativa compartiendo mis actividades diarias, manteniéndome activa en la blockchain porque siempre estoy pensando en que subir, siempre que veo algo bonito o interesante pienso en qué comunidad compartirlo. Creo que todo esto me ha ayudado a ser más comunicativa y expresiva, me ha ayudado también con mi redacción, algo que me costaba mucho cuando inicié en hive, pero siento que ahora he ganado fluidez en eso, lo cual me da satisfacción.
![WhatsApp Image 2026-03-01 at 10.31.55 AM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/23yd5n4ij6gCASifQiahDZBngEZAQtRK7KzmHkZ2LomnDWtCf2yH3ZnnvzLkTNrEFagpk.jpeg)

I am very grateful for everything I have learned from Hive, for all the achievements I have made here, for the opportunities provided, for the support, not only with cures but with guidance and direction whenever I needed it. I am very glad that I returned about six years ago, as I mentioned, and found that what I found was very different from what I left behind.

>Estoy muy agradecida por todo lo que he aprendido de Hive, por todos los logros que he obtenido aquí, por las oportunidades brindadas, por el apoyo, no solo con curaciones sino con indicaciones y guía cada vez que lo necesité, me alregro mucho de haber regresado hace aproximadamente esos seis años que mencioné, y comprobar así que lo que encontré fue muy diferente a lo que dejé.
![dyu.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bethyjade/Eos3Cxu6neGp8Qf6jCJPDWpTX7sD3xm9wQf9f6oMx5kX7qMuBQ9aabU37TiPBesSgnH.jpg)

And well, people, that's all for today's post, I hope you liked it. Thank you very much as always for supporting my work, I welcome new readers, I love you all very much, I send you a hug and I'll see you in another post.

>Y bueno, gente, esto ha sido todo por el post de hoy, espero que les haya gustado. Muchas gracias como siempre por apoyar mi trabajo, le doy la bienvenida a los nuevos lectores, les quiero mucho a todos, les envío un abrazo y ya nos encontraremos en otro post

title.title: Demutskrankheit, Teil 2
title.body:
Ich arbeite seit gestern wieder direkt in diesem Sondermodus, von welchem ich dachte, er waehre ein fuer alle mal verloren.

Das scheint eine Gehirnkapazitaetswillensfrage zu sein.

Ich will das Loswerden, den Rotz.

Das ist aber wie Gummi alles, naja immerhin schon mal.

Ich kann also wieder auf das System zugreifen und spuere wie das Arbeitet. Wenn das stimmt was ich denke, ist weiterhin die Schwerkraft und Haltung das A und O bei dieser Thematik.

Genauso wie Laecheln und Gaehnen, sowie, Muemmelmann mit Nase und Mund zu machen nach vorne im Kreis senkrecht.

So wie der Kreis vom Kiefer zum Ohr eben ich habe es ja bebildert.

Diese gegen den Urzeigersinn arbeitende Netzwerke sind bei mir Verstopft.

Inzwischen habe ich dank der Schulmedizin gelernt, das hier wohl die Verstopfung, an einer Art Haaerchen des Nasensackes sitzen. Diese loest sich Stueck fuer Stueck, mit Hilfe der Kieferruhestellung!

Man stellt den Kiefer locker im Mund und haelt die Position ohne jegliche Anstrengung.

Zusammen mit der Demutshaltung also einer im Zweifel statt geraden und mit dem kopf auf augehoehe waagerechten haltung zur Mutter Erde hin, laesst man den Kiefer Bewusst Locker im Mund sitzen und versucht!!! diese Postion zu halten.

Das wird aber nicht Funktionieren!!!

Weil jetzt der Trick, je nach dem wie man geuebt ist und Masiert und das Gesicht benutzt und eben ausgepraegt an der Krankheit leidet, am Ende weis man das am besten an seinen Zaehnen, wie Stark sie wirklich ist, obwohl die vielleicht alle schon weg sind und man IMMER noch kieferschmerzen hat da wo die Zaehne sind!

Und Am Ohr und Auge und die Nase ist dauernd zu trocken oder zu feucht.

Und im Nacken hat man es auch Beulen am besten die so hart sind das man drauf schmieden koennte.

Das alles vom Haltungsschaden dann.

Also die Haltung halten, minutenlang.

Im Zweifel wird das Schmerzen irgendwann.

Ja das mit dem Schmerzen haben bis man im einem fortschgeschrittenem Prozess der Heilung ist muss ich Extra aufschreiben das ist noch zu viel ungenaues von mir am Wissen.

Die Schmerzen, helfen mir! Wie soll ich das sagen? Die helfen mir einfach zu wissen, das ich an der richtigen stelle in der richtigen postition bin. :-)

Dann! Verharren, mit dem Schmerz zusammen.

Dann faengt des an zu ziepen und zwicken obwohl man den kiefer locker laesst und voellig entspannt da hockt.

Stell dir vor du wuerdest Panzertape wo runterreißen wollen, das ist das gleiche, man trennt zwei Dinge, die viel zu lange miteinander verbunden waren.

Uebrigens kann man sich so auch eine Entzuendung holen, die meiner Meinung nach schon lange vorher wieder vergessen da war immer und immer wieder. 

Ich habe keine Entzuendungen, weil ich einfach weiter in der Therapie bleibe, ich scheue mich nicht mehr vor den Schmerzen sondern mache dann Therapie spaetestens wenn sie immer staerker werden.

Weil, die gehen ja damit nicht weg vor allem wenn das Problem nicht geloest ist im wahrstem Sinne der Worte.

Die werden aber Zeitweise tueckisch weniger bis hin das sie komplett verschwinden.

Man brauch sau viel Ruhe um ueberhaupt in Therapiemodus zu kommen.

Ich hoere mir Podcasts an dabei, oder schau den Voegeln zu. 

Dann einfach verweilen in der Position wo es sich richtig anfuehlt.

Man muss alle Postionen durchgearbeitet haben bin ich ueberzeugt.

Auch, das viele davon vor allem im Schlaf automatisch passieren. Gesunde Menschen haben das also garnicht erst.^^


Wie schoen fuer die.

Salve

Sascha Pürner

title.title: Delighted by the Moment | My Last Day in Auckland, New Zealand
title.body:
> https://images.hive.blog/DQmSsJE53hfbtM1gLKcVNmfbLMERcTfdKcYFpWKeRZppMtw/28.jpg > ## To be delighted by another person, or moved by a landscape or a work of art, requires not being in full control. > -*Meditations for Mortals | Oliver Burkeman* I have always struggled with control. But don’t we all? Because our sense of control is directly tied to our sense of certainty. And who wants to be uncertain? We want to be sure about a lot of things, especially when it comes to our lives. We want to know (for sure) if our money is enough. If we don’t have this worry, then it is because we are certain we have enough. We want to know (for sure) if our time is enough. If our efforts are enough. If other people like us enough. If we are good enough. If we are enough. To have certainty over these things means we can relinquish our worries about them. And until we can become certain, we do all sorts of things trying to control the outcomes, the situations, and even other people. But just as the above quote says (it’s from a book I read a few months back), to be moved and be delighted by other people or a work of art means we have to let go of full control. -----

A Moment in a Museum

----- ![1.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPvT1fbc54EnMb7bGoFpF8jYW8LCtnCSZcFr5sGWjA9fd/1.jpg) So now I’m going to share about my last day in Auckland, where I allowed myself to let go of full control, and how I found delight in it. After seeing the [Sky Tower and the St Matthew-in-the-City Church](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@glecerioberto/tourist-mode-on-or-exploring-auckland-new-zealand), I let my friend take me to wherever she wanted us to go. I had no idea where we were headed. I was already quite satisfied that I was walking around Auckland. The entire city was a tourist attraction for me already. Turns out, she was taking me to the Auckland Art Gallery. She told me it was free, and that was all I needed to know. We climbed up a short hill to get to the museum. It was a massive building. I now know that it is the largest art institution in New Zealand. ![2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmS9uHWo8H255Pj2JZrPHMtwkw3QkboNbE8fJq7b9u3Bc2/2.jpg) ![3.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSwKvZHVxcsQr2RWscmAeguGjFGea5gKqB36oTpzWzXGA/3.jpg) |
![4.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYfwQd4uccMzkut7WqXcuvtTptLEZN9dceeBv9S8wwSYS/4.jpg)
|
![5.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPvLbpfqArky7YLNhNynYSixjf6iQNX2XVW6DYqFY4NjJ/5.jpg)
| ------------- |------------- | ![6-1.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXu4bavbfmCF8k5u2qYeJ5t4Hzpv5qfBe6tF7xWrPKJQ5/6-1.jpg) ![6-2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTYM8HxBEsoM5TBotp5urAHmFzkv9yZjcTseG6Xgzt9SY/6-2.jpg) |
![7.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX4w6poGHpRBTru8ZFpZcYAEEeomGBLTnXig18BQ3VCAR/7.jpg)
|
![8.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaJgsqW1nEM68QNmwuXRcKj4pPKHegvRKkh5BTHEXFG26/8.jpg)
| ------------- |------------- | Again, I let my friend lead the way. We entered a section of the museum and the first things I saw were sculptures. I’m not really an art expert, so I don’t know what I was supposed to look for. I just let the experience of seeing the sculptures be enough. And then I saw the paintings. I thought they weren’t that magnificent. But what made everything work was the collection of the artworks. Everything was just nicely put together. I could imagine sitting in one small gallery and studying each piece of art and trying to figure out the reasons for the curator’s choices to put them together. We moved on to another section. There was a hallway of paintings and some unique pieces, like a hanger with a strip light attached to it and a hanging yellow plastic chain. ![9.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPYTQaaWzr6wnKeS1fL8aR6ANXBhArQd87JENwXSyhqZy/9.jpg) ![10.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR8DPpfE68GAsGpHrxd6abmek8MYjLWybf1AhJL4UgJPZ/10.jpg) ![11.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNeuRuiZf73XXZWqPvhukAP8YUQpCuEuCr9P8eRPgm8Me/11.jpg) |
![12.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSdQG8xyoPdjwJa2xf6AajFXK2a6disCrd1hSc8BC52Ux/12.jpg)
|
![13.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNXDCmnvWcxp7eZBt65i5bWFY1jPZxgU9HwY9RkkSoZfy/13.jpg)
| ------------- |------------- |
![14.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd9dGqPD2qsQsvmpDXdzSeSTksBHoYDmRoD8JHS526FxU/14.jpg)
|
![15.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNnBL1nYDiEfxWGDpYRyFiCRNE8gSNx33cRDyC4ghiRmH/15.jpg)
|
![16.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbYZRs3XPctsF6Ligj9jJt9pRCAGEdVcSszHPt9mQETrw/16.jpg)
| ------------- |------------- | Since we had no itinerary, I had no worries about time. I didn’t even think about worrying if we could see everything in the museum. Looking back, I think we only saw a fraction of the museum. If I was the one planning that trip, I would have spent considerable time planning the entire day to see every inch and corner of the museum. Maybe I would have ‘seen the museum’ more if I did that, but honestly, it is so much better to talk about a visit as a serendipitous and spontaneous excursion rather than a meticulously planned and rigid activity. The timestamps on my photos tell me that we were only in the museum for less than 20 minutes. If ever I get the chance to go back to Auckland, I will definitely make sure to spend more time in that museum. But again, what made that trip so special was that it was fleeting. We were there and then we were gone.
https://images.hive.blog/DQmZhCiUdTdXtDSfjXsRD6dDrrCnbSPhjdCS1DZUyCeuYQM/stars.png
-----

Some Peace in Albert Park

----- ![17.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcDaeENkazo5jBbcLUdmoZA2D6zetMRacSSg68aypwnqh/17.jpg) After a few minutes of walking, we found ourselves in a park in the middle of the city. I’ve been to the parks in Rotorua before, and I thought they were only possible because Rotorua was a small and quiet city. So when I saw Albert Park in Auckland, I was surprised. How could this place be in the middle of the city? How could this beautiful, peaceful, and green place exist and keep existing in the middle of a city that puts so much value on space? Mind you, I haven’t been to Singapore before this trip, so I had no idea how capable a country could be in creating parks like this. We spent a few minutes sitting on the bench, enjoying the view of the deep green grass and the colorful flowers. Sitting there, I realized that if a city as busy as Auckland could afford to give up space for stillness, perhaps I could afford to give up a little certainty for peace. |
![18.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVkcdvNYJwohp2aZRVngvmpk81nj8uzaTbKCktAM2JQvQ/18.jpg)
|
![19.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUa7syVQnwh6kZaD9nqKjEpyw93P8CyqXfdbdAaAMcwk3/19.jpg)
| ------------- |------------- | ![20.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUQHBHj7EtCHpH2XZx2Q87rZpfyaTcr1vtjGLfULon97C/20.jpg) ![22.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmePg5PQS47H74yeNaGbY3jRycvG4u5fb4YLHTkDCzqpNk/22.jpg) Auckland is a major university city in New Zealand. And I saw it for myself when we came across the campus residences and the university buildings when we continued our tour of the city. I was at a point in my life when I was thinking about getting a PhD. I just recently finished my master’s and I was quite sure that I would continue my graduate studies. I was considering what my life could be like if I was studying in a different country. Maybe in New Zealand at The University of Auckland. I had no idea then that I would end up in Singapore a few years later doing my PhD. Maybe I would still get the chance to visit New Zealand. Maybe I would still get the chance to set foot in The University of Auckland. As much as I want to take control of the situation, I know that there is a choice to let go and let things happen. To be delighted by experiences without having to fully plan them. Looking back from my life now in Singapore, I realize that the version of me in Albert Park was so worried about securing a future that ended up happening anyway, just differently than I’d imagined. It was a lesson in letting go that I’m still learning. ![23.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRtLMT23UcvYmkvoB8ybmLN8KoCHCyRT8aJFu2WPTJGrx/23.jpg) ![24.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSSc1BMbVT6h1yvWtu9way8NnUwLHTEsLrCCoV67waNXK/24.jpg) |
![25.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWpcMHJQCdvafG3efTqAXVtmrq8CrMEKVgNfSzcd1w1NB/25.jpg)
|
![26.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUFipop2pEnB5cbyFsi4vSsxFVa2Rm1x9HJyMtpf7kuBv/26.jpg)
| ------------- |------------- |
https://images.hive.blog/DQmZhCiUdTdXtDSfjXsRD6dDrrCnbSPhjdCS1DZUyCeuYQM/stars.png
-----

See You Again, Auckland

----- ![28.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSsJE53hfbtM1gLKcVNmfbLMERcTfdKcYFpWKeRZppMtw/28.jpg) ![29.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ3KjDzinVTpsLu6FYQRu34rbBdXeFgodAX4b4v7Y4Y5P/29.jpg) ![30.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNqrGiDNTu8SDPCZjyzAne767PiXE4jALK4GECwzAM6QE/30.jpg) It was getting quite late in the afternoon when my friend suggested we go back for dinner. It was a bit of struggle to find our way around the city, but even this minor struggle felt different that day. Usually, a wrong turn or a missed stop would feel like a loss of control, a crack in the certainty of the itinerary. But that afternoon, the uncertainty was just part of the experience. The bus eventually came, the restaurant was found, and the meal was hearty. Everything worked out without me having to exert control over it. I got to savor my last day in New Zealand and for a few hours that day, I had no questions about whether money was enough, whether time was enough, or if I was doing enough. I was just there to be delighted by the moment. Good bye Auckland, see you again.
https://images.hive.blog/DQmZhCiUdTdXtDSfjXsRD6dDrrCnbSPhjdCS1DZUyCeuYQM/stars.png
-----

title.title: The best way to live a good teenage life// Mcgi topic review
title.body:
A good teenage life begins with building a strong relationship with God. The Bible teaches teenagers to seek God early, pray often, and study His word daily. When young people allow God to guide their decisions, they develop wisdom, discipline, and a sense of purpose. A teenager who follows godly values is more likely to avoid harmful habits and make choices that lead to peace and success.

Another important part of living a good teenage life is choosing the right friends and showing respect to parents and elders. The Bible warns that bad company can lead people away from good character, while wise and godly friendships encourage growth and good behavior. Teenagers should also learn responsibility, honesty, kindness, and self-control, because these qualities help shape a strong future.
https://youtu.be/5v9TWK6UECE?si=gVU9_hAUqKHGohPp
Every teenager should us their youthful age talent to do something good for God. The teenage years are a time to learn, grow, and prepare for adulthood. Even at a young age, the Bible encourages believers to be good examples in speech, behavior, love, faith, and purity. By living with faith, humility, and obedience to God, teenagers can enjoy a joyful and meaningful life.

title.title: Homemade Dish is a Foodie Vibes: Tasty Sauteed String Beans with Chicken Breast Topped with Roasted Garlic
title.body:
>

![1000036140.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EouC5tsRAuwefMBHucpHnQRKZiQVAvTbhY2BKuQtjy2DdoRtRBSN6gyy9bSk7VtvNR8.png)

I bought a tie of of string beans the other day. Actually, I bought so much vegetable, three kinds of vegetables and I realized that too late. So, I didn't use the string beans and just used the two others. Thanks to that I have vegetable that I can cook today. But the next problem is the recipe I should make. I am really not sure so I search on google like this: \

I didn't get much result but sauteed string beans with garlic. It looks good but I want something with meat so instead of doing a research more I just go to the market with mama to buy chicken and oyster sauce. I'm craving for some chicken today and I want it with string beans\n\n<div class=\

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/Ep1Vx9yL4WefmZoysQBN7RiF5udxXCnSsKMPYyNCUnP2PiXqVfhnb6EKa2oP6rV5YCP.jpg And so here's the string beans. I cut them into small size and soak them in water with salt. I still remember the string beans I soaked in salt water the last time I cook it, I got dead worm after soaking it for 5 minutes. Ewwyyyy! And actually, I do this in every vegetables we cook, just to be sure that no worms can be found in there

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EpGQkiurZ3CqXXeuVxR79YsjfTkzEFSqn8LaKYTVvQTbsZe1qnafcSMaE3YMPTeuFcc.jpg For the chicken, I bought the breast part. I just marinate it with salt and oyster sauce for a few minutes. While letting it rest on the side, I prepared the garlic and onion, I used bigger garlic because I am planning to use half of it for the toppings, inspired by the sauteed string beans with garlic that I found on google, hehe

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/Ep7w2CRoKDn8rf5cMPVLcUCxGS3vgXACoLEab1ju2mTdi3BnxtvbDyfXrXf98guYC2t.jpg Next is sauteeing the garlic and onion, please ignore the color of oil used in there because it is literally a used oil where I fried some chicken joy. Ehe. Its for flavor roo tou know, uwu. And yes, that's our roasted garlic right there. I can imagine it smell, yum, yum, I love it with roasted peanut. Now I want some of it.

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/Eoryq9q7zp6tXcZmfTtwkXVAEcQpqc5JbtLR67SqeugNh3LWfc3fB2wFkqphhwaFsrN.jpg Once the aromatic started to smell, I know it smells even though I can smell it, lolol -we'll then put the chicken meat which I just cut into cubes. A bite size. I also added a cup of water and simmer it for 12 minutes. This is also where I seasoned it with salt, pepper, lots of pepper actually, and some nom nom chu to make it taste better. I love that the oyster is a bit sweet so this taste really good -for me ┏(＾0＾)┛

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/Eopryra8xXCnbuhaC91a9b1anKSfMcPyyGaxCVkgj9WNBgTfBeiz4J5GkhEDNdcydwy.jpg After 12 minutes, I added the string beans. I actually added water in it because it is too dry already. I want my string beans soft and easy to chew so I cooked it for another 10 minutes, because Y not?

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EoiVmoBi1awZJJpMttBoow9CNW26GWZ9xQFoMHEuGTH824rdsBXqM8Yu9dWfir1vKWY.jpg 10 minutes later and its finally done! I sprinkled the roasted garlic that I set aside later and lookie, lookie. I wish we still have spring onion for the color. Sadly Mommy D's plant died or withered already, aigoooo

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EpNoPsHSjeWnH1UPBYbWE91a2eWbQqV7RXSNBzduQuu2veGggEUuznX9ifxuHNB6ENU.jpg Of course, it won't be complete without taste testing it. We still have leftover rice from dinner so I put a spoonful of it in a small dipping bowl and top it with string beans and chicken. I can't say any more words but its GOOD! I think I did good on this recipe. It is a simple one but I cooked it with all my heart and soul, lol. I am so happy with how tasty it bevome. ------ Lead Image Edited in [Canva](https://canva.link/9z2jqqnsai87l71)

title.title: Wednesday Walk enjoying the colorful spring trees in Buttonwood Park
title.body:
# enjoying the colorful spring trees in Buttonwood Park This post if for Wednesday walk challenge Any questions about the challenge read the guide at the Bottom of the post ;) Of recent, I haven't had many days I could get out for early morning walks, its either been to cool for me or like today the temp is nice enough but it is raining, but I have got out for a few day times walks, and a few times to Buttonwood Park, which is pretty close to where I live. Its an awesome park called by many the Crown Jewel of the city, and I feel the same way any time of year it is beautiful but especially in spring when the lovely warm colors come out Now I do not profess to be an expert on tree types infact my knowledge of them is terrible, but i think I know what these are based on a Friend i have met and walked around the park with a couple of times here, who runs a group called the friends of buttonwood park, and that group does a lot to help look after the park. This first one i think is a Kwanzan Cherry possibly part of Sixty trees which were given in 1931 to the city by the Garden Club of Buzzards Bay, or it could be one of the new ones the Group Friends of Buttonwood Park have planted more recently
![WW trees bp.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23uFMbsNgAWYuVXKiCzANL1KZdGAdV7gsJQhPaDDohW49xswBEwDHqfKa9xWuQ57FSn5a.jpg) **Sony A7iv 38mm F8 1/400 second ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23uFMbsNgAWYuVXKiCzANL1KZdGAdV7gsJQhPaDDohW49xswBEwDHqfKa9xWuQ57FSn5a.jpg)**

and this next one could well be a Weeping Japanese Maple, its hard to miss with its lovely warm color
![WW trees bp-4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23uQrdvhKAVMrWdskb1hoqrabxPrtfua7c3JoDJ8XZXeTVWWk9Btxg16WwWf9dD9Ekns7.jpg) **Sony A7iv 35mm F13 1/60 second ISO 125** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23uQrdvhKAVMrWdskb1hoqrabxPrtfua7c3JoDJ8XZXeTVWWk9Btxg16WwWf9dD9Ekns7.jpg)**

and another Kwanzan Cherry I do believe and clearly, well to me one recently added
![WW trees bp-2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23wqY3hTjfouxpTwWRZ668dB7Jwkmd54fn33rkb6LKD6Jw5fTmoG6rvpRv9apVwXuDg7n.jpg) **Sony A7iv 38mm F8 1/320 second ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23wqY3hTjfouxpTwWRZ668dB7Jwkmd54fn33rkb6LKD6Jw5fTmoG6rvpRv9apVwXuDg7n.jpg)**

and possibly a Saucer Magnolia to finish off
![WW trees bp-3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23zRT14tBEcrfk8ifDoswj72STRtNDcNgMmgSTFEQAJFBnnLLhNPbhWpTVAsgo9FmXtNK.jpg) **Sony A7iv 28mm F8 1/500 second ISO 100** **[Click here to view larger](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/23zRT14tBEcrfk8ifDoswj72STRtNDcNgMmgSTFEQAJFBnnLLhNPbhWpTVAsgo9FmXtNK.jpg)**

Wednesday Walk is a challenge started by me, the idea is to get out for a short walk and get some shots of what you can see within a short distance of your home office or wherever you start. And this is my entry for this week, but first, let me explain the challenge. This is my post for the Wednesday Walk challenge hosted by myself, let me first explain the guidelines > Try and get out once a week for a short walk, can be from your office, home or anywhere really and walk for a few blocks or a few minutes looking for things to get shots of. > Your walk does not have to be on a Wednesday I just ask if possible to share your walk photos on a Wednesday. > **Try and get a few shots not just one** > **Add a bit of a write up about where you walked** > **Just one Wednesday Walk tagged post a week** > You can look for anything in general or decide on one subject you want to get shots off. > Make a point of looking around and up and see what you can find to get shots of that otherwise you may miss > Do a post with the shots you get on a Wednesday and tag it with #wednesdaywalk, also if you happen to join, please leave a link to your post in a comment on this post and I will try and visit them all, especially if its not one of the first 5 tags or I may miss seeing it . > Following me and re-Hiving the post so more see it would be appreciated but isn't a rule just a suggestion. > I am not strict on these rules and hence why they are called guidelines and not rules > I will try and visit, and upvote all who take part in the Wednesday Walk. ## I hope a few of you may find this an interesting challenge and decide to join in. *** ## unless stated otherwise all photos used in my posts are taken and owned by myself, if you wish to use any of my images please contact me. ![Wednesday walk footer.jpg](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmYjvvmdLTzDsP1iM8pdowePzr8pSUzgGrWUmQkyBpmxAb/Wednesday%20walk%20footer.jpg) *** ![ ](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/QGGXzaN9-4LQGm7AE-tattoodjay.gif) *** ![TEAMUSA JJ hive.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tattoodjay/so5RKHER-TEAMUSA20JJ20-hive.jpg) ## title.title: Café + Libros: la fórmula de la felicidad
title.body:
Si hay algo que aprendí a valorar con el paso del tiempo, son esos domingos donde el mundo parece haberse detenido, mi taza de café desprende ese vapor reconfortante y tengo un libro abierto frente a mí. Hay algo casi mágico, casi alquímico, en la combinación de cafeína y papel.

¿Alguna vez te has detenido a pensar por qué esta pareja es tan irresistible? No es solo una cuestión de hábito; es una cuestión de atmósfera y paz mental.

**Porque es un ritual de pausa en un mundo acelerado.** Vivimos corriendo. Las notificaciones, el correo electrónico, las exigencias diarias… todo demanda nuestra atención inmediata. Cuando abres un libro y tomas un sorbo de café, estás haciendo algo radical: te estás deteniendo.

El café actúa como el ancla sensorial. Es el calor en tus manos, el aroma que inunda el espacio, el primer trago que despierta tus sentidos. Es el preludio necesario para sumergirse en otra realidad. Por otro lado, el libro es la puerta. Te permite viajar a otros lugares, épocas o mentes sin moverte de tu sillón. Combinar ambos es crear un santuario portátil.

No necesitamos estudios para saber que se siente bien, pero es curioso notar cómo nuestro cerebro reacciona. El café aumenta nuestra alerta y concentración, lo que nos permite retener mejor la trama o los argumentos de lo que leemos. A la vez, el acto de leer reduce nuestros niveles de estrés y nos ayuda a desconectar.

Es la combinación perfecta porque la cafeína nos mantiene presentes; la narrativa nos lleva lejos; el ritual nos calma.

Matemáticamente hablando, podríamos decir que el disfrute es casi exponencial: Disfrute = (Cafeína \* Concentración) Bueno, quizás me lo he inventado un poco, pero se entiende la idea, ¿verdad?

No se trata solo de beber café. Se trata del ritual. Elegir la taza adecuada, sentir el peso del libro en tus manos, el sonido de las hojas al pasar… Todo esto conforma un \

.

A veces, mi café favorito para leer es un Americano simple, sin pretensiones, que me deja saborear la lectura sin distracciones. Otras veces, cuando el libro es denso o un poco oscuro, prefiero un Capuchino con su espuma cremosa, como si necesitara un abrazo líquido para acompañar la historia.

**Es mi momento, son mis reglas.** Busca ese rincón donde entra un poco de luz, pon tu móvil en modo avión (o mejor aún, déjalo en otra habitación) y prepara tu bebida favorita. No hace falta que sea una sesión de lectura de horas; a veces, quince minutos de café y un par de páginas son suficientes para resetear el cerebro y volver al día con otra perspectiva.

Al final del día, los libros nos enseñan sobre la vida y el café nos ayuda a vivirla con un poco más de energía. ¿Qué mejor combinación podría existir? Cuéntame, ¿cuál es tu \
ideal? ¿Prefieres un café negro fuerte con una novela de misterio, o un café con leche suave para acompañar un libro de poesía? Te leo en los comentarios.\n\n

Welcome to my blog, #Freewriters Community. Scatter the seed The best thing we can do in this world is to sow seeds in any environment we find ourselves in. This isn't about religion, churches, or agricultural fields; I'm talking about gestures, words, actions, tone, and the intention behind what we leave in the people we meet. scatter the seed Sowing the seed means leaving beautiful traces in the places we inhabit, in the hearts we touch with our kindness, generosity, respect, love, and empathy. We don't know how long or how short our time in this world will be, but every act, every thought, every word is a seed we sow, planted and engraved in the mind or heart of another human being. Every action bears fruit, which is why we must choose to sow well, to sow truth, to scatter seeds every day, consistent with what we want to experience and what we want to reap. >Bienvenidos a mi blog comunidad #Freewriters Esparcir la semilla Lo mejor que podemos hacer en este mundo, es esparcir semilla en cualquier entorno que nos encontramos, no se trata de religión, de iglesia, de campo de agricultura, hablo de gestos, de palabras, de acciones, de tono, de intención de lo que dejamos en las personas que conocemos. title.title: The Resilient Beauty: A Celebration of the Rock Rose Flower
title.body:
Nestled in rocky terrains from gardens to Mediterranean hillsides, the Rock Rose (Cistus and Helianthemum species) is a small yet striking flower known for its delicate pink, white, or magenta blooms. Belonging to the Cistaceae family, these low-growing shrubs are celebrated not only for their beauty but for their ability to thrive in arid, harsh environments—a true testament to nature’s resilience.

Rock Roses are characterized by their five-petaled, velvety blossoms and leathery green leaves. Though they resemble roses in shape, they lack the fragrance of their more famous cousin.

title.title: Be Wise
title.body:
Good morning, giant friends!

This morning, I will be sharing with you about how your wise friends can make or break you. The Bible says, wise people make you wise, and foolish people make you foolish. The kind of relationship you build with people determines the outcome of your decision and action outwardly. If you speak wisely, people will surround you and they will get to know that you are also surrounded by wise people. 


![Screenshot_20250804-151602.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/peckypeace/23y94cGrq44494gosvQB73H3jBpEog3MAb9XYUc57ebrW3hYhVfRwzauD9vb7HiZRuqk8.jpg)


If you are around foolish people, after some days, you will start acting, speaking, and mimicking them and you will attract bad people around you in life. 

In this life, we need to be careful of the things we do at times with people, let our yes be yes, no be no.

As a young guy who is into fashion design. I have met different people who are in bad company; some try to lure me, but I had to stand my ground as a believer, looking unto Him as my author.

They kept  coming to establish a friendship with me to join their group but I refused, I remembered in the scripture that says; 


>Proverbs 13:20-21 CEV
[20]  Wise friends make you wise, but you hurt yourself by going around with fools. [21] You are in for trouble if you sin, but you will be rewarded if you live right.

This has been the anchor scripture that keeps me going when it comes to wise friends and foolish friends.

If you work with the wise, you will live rightly; with the foolish, you make foolish decisions that will lead you to be in trouble.

We need to be wise always, because God is a wise God. He never made a foolish decision before because He is Holy and Righteous. He thinks wisely all the time. We ought to be like Him every day.

Thank you.


Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@dearemem/be-wise-hpj)

title.body:
It's been awhile since I had a ramble. Not particularly sure why I ever stopped. I say that every time I create a new ramble I feel like. 

I mildly replaced the rambles with my Chess posts, but I just don't have the energy right now. Or the time. Well, it's sort of a combination of the two. Time and energy. Energy and time. Caffeine and anti-aging. HA. Energy and anti-aging. Two industries that will never go extinct. 

Man, the Internet is such a double edged sword. As much as the Internet can help you save time and energy, it also takes a lot of time and energy. Seemingly limitless things to learn, and limitless ways to waste time. It's strange. 

But I guess life is strange. Verbal records, written records, printing press, books, newspapers, magazines, telegraphs, phones, cameras, Internet, AI, plus a million things in between. Populations rise but we sort of end up becoming both closer and farther apart as people due to many of these technologies, and now many populations are declining LOL. It's as if the more we make life easier, new problems arise. Like a weird version of more money more problems. Once there's a shiny new technology, we all want the shiny new things, and the people with the shiny things seem reluctant to let the common man in. Maybe. I don't know. 

It's entirely too late to still be awake. But I'm just caught up in the whole 'what's the point?' loop. 

Is all of this some deep desire to what, discover immortality? Like these inventions and advancements are amazing and impressive but it's sort of like, what is the endgame?

Progress is great, but doesn't progress sort of imply, at least kind of, an end goal? Am I not ambitious or optimistic enough about life to understand what we're shooting for here?

Inventions are meant to make life easier. Ok, sure. But then why does life feel harder? How does life feel impossible?

I think there's a word or term for this, I can't remember. 

It's like yes, many of these inventions *have* made life easier. But then once these inventions become more common, expectations for production only skyrocket. 

Maybe we should ask squirrels the meaning of life. I don't know. They aren't sitting here wondering why this, or what if that. 

Now I'm just getting old, and I'll probably be asking myself these same questions on my death bed HA. 

Maybe I'm adding to my immortality by rambling like this. Some AI depiction of me will be formed and that version of me will still be wondering what the hell is going on. 

I used to watch this YouTube channel and they spoke about ascension and how highly spiritual folks or like advanced beings live on a higher dimension or something. If that's the case, what's the point of that exactly? 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSsfpTVF2UY8Kf9jhyWvFfw7CD8t68grdB1AuDJR89LWi/1778668736257.png)

I guess it's all for the greater good. Each generation is obligated to be there for the next. Work hard, keep society moving. 

Meh, I guess we're just all destined to become those people from WALL-E. 

Maybe my own problem is fundamentally jealousy. Maybe I am entitled or ungrateful. Meh, I dunno anymore. Maybe I'm just not supposed to notice how unfair everything is. 

Hive on folks.

title.body:
지난 주말, 날씨가 진짜 좋았다.
오랜만에 한강에 가봐야지 했는데, 하늘도 맑고 바람도 적당해서 딱 좋았다.
돗자리를 깔고, 한강을 바라보며, 바람을 쐬다가 출출함이 느껴졌다.

“그래, 오늘은 무조건 한강라면이다.”

편의점 들어갔더니 사람도 엄청 많았다.
라면 고르는 사람, 계산 기다리는 사람,
셀프라면 기계 앞에서 줄 서 있는 사람까지.
다들 한강 오면 생각하는 건 비슷한가 보다.


![IMG_0516.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmb4xib1NeDS6YAaoz3JTcxSyeRyPGMWNC8m9BVLY46piJ/IMG_0516.jpeg)

햇살은 따뜻하고,
시원한 바람은 불고,
앞에는 반짝이는 한강.
그 분위기에서 먹으니까
평범한 라면도 왜 이렇게 맛있는지 모르겠다.

오랜만에 먹어서 더 맛있었던 건지,
날씨 때문인지,
아니면 그냥 한강 감성 때문인지.

어쨌든 왜 한강라면이 계속 핫한지는 다시 한번 제대로 알게 된 주말이었다.

title.title: Are CCD Memories Coming Back? - The Memory Guy Blog
title.body:
# Are CCD Memories Coming Back? - The Memory Guy Blog

**Source:** https://thememoryguy.com/are-ccd-memories-coming-back/

	
	
	
		The Memory Guy was recently contacted by a researcher at imec, the Belgian research consortium, about the rebirth of an old idea.  Back in the late 1970s and early 1980s semiconductor makers had considered using charge-coupled devices (CCDs) for computer main memories.   Probably few readers will even recognize either the name or the abbreviation.  The CCD memory was a good idea that was completely overshadowed by another good idea — DRAM — that ended up taking the market over.
Now that DRAM is having troubles shrinking much farther than its current size, and since DRAM doesn’t easily benefit from any existing 3D processes, the imec researchers decided to investigate ways to use the “Punch & Plug” process that has been so successful with 3D NAND flash (and which is shown in this post’s graphic, courtesy of imec) to make a CCD-based memory that can replace DRAM at a lower cost.
What is a CCD?
A CCD is an interesting device that functions something like a shift register, but with considerably less complexity.  The less complex a memory is, the fewer transistors it takes to make it, and that means that it will be inexpensive.  A good example is DRAM, with its simple memory cell made of one transistor and one capacitor, versus an SRAM that is made up of six transistors per bit.  DRAM is significantly less expensive than SRAM as a result.
Although a CCD doesn’t need DRAM’s capacitor, it does store a charge in a semiconductor layer, but it takes at least three transistors per bit to implement.  The three transistors move the charge through the semiconductor layer somewhat like an electric sign with lights that scroll from one side to the other.
Intel’s 1977 data sheet illustrates a 4-transistor mechanism in the figure below, but a much more intuitive animated presentation is made by a GIF on Wikipedia’s Charge-Coupled Device page.

![Image 1](https://thememoryguy.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/2026-04-23-imec-3D-CCD-150x150.jpg)

In DRAM’s early days, the difference between the Intel CCD’s four transistors and DRAM’s single transistor and capacitor made a DRAM bit smaller than a CCD bit, and DRAM won the market by providing less expensive bits.  But the capacitor didn’t easily shrink beyond a certain point, simply because of the minimum charge it needed to hold.  Today the capacitor is the biggest part of a DRAM bit, and tiny vertical transistors that are made using the Punch & Plug process promise to shrink CCDs smaller than DRAM, so that the CCD is expected to become the less expensive option.
RAM vs. SAM
Here we diverge for a moment to talk about memory naming conventions.  It pertains to the discussion in a way that you probably never knew.
Why is RAM called RAM, as in DRAM and SRAM?  RAM stands for “Random-Access Memory.”  Why do we use that term?  Because in the early 1960s and before, certain memories were serially-accessed.  These included some very different technologies than are used today, including shift registers and even mercury delay lines, where digital data was converted to sound waves that were then sent down a tube of mercury and picked up at the other end to be turned back into digital bits.
These were Serial-Access Memories, or SAMs.  CCDs are Serial-Access Memories.
While SAMs solved a lot of technical problems in their time, they presented challenges.  The biggest one is that the program had to wait for the correct data to arrive.  Consider iterating on a very short software loop in a SAM that was hundreds of times the length of that software loop.  The processor would perform a single iteration, then wait for the code to come back through again to iterate the next time.  Needless to say, programmers learned to write code that managed its way around this issue, but it certainly wouldn’t have been easy code to read!
Today’s processors all have internal caches that fetch data in larger chunks, typically eight addresses at a time.  This is a much better fit for a SAM than in the 1970s when caches were seldom used.  That short software loop is likely to be run out of the cache without requiring repeated accesses to either a DRAM or a SAM, and so it’s not quite as clumsy to use a SAM today as it was back then.  CCDs now make more sense than they did in those days.
Coming Back to 2026
So why does this matter today?  It’s because the introduction of 3D NAND’s unique “Punch & Plug” construction a CCD’s 3-transistor or 4-transistor cell can be built vertically using transistors stacked one above the other to make memories that are denser, and that should be far cheaper, than DRAMs.  That’s what imec’s researchers hope to develop.
The new CCD is under development using a 3D NAND structure, but since the channel must store a charge,  a CCD has different requirements than NAND.  The imec researchers have chosen to replace 3D NAND’s standard amorphous silicon channel, the material that fills the Plug, with a IGZO (Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide) to create a channel with the right properties.
Although they haven’t yet produced a 3D part, which I understand is coming soon, imec researchers presented a planar part at the 2024 IEEE IEDM conference that uses the same materials and that performs very well.  The imec website has a nicely-illustrated blog post that explains how they hope to use this design as a basis for AI-specific compute-in-memory chips.
Objective Analysis keeps watch over new technologies while at the same time focusing on today’s semiconductor memory business issues.  We can bring this to you, helping your company with a strategic edge over its competition.  Please contact us to learn how we can help your company to thrive in today’s and tomorrow’s environments.

title.body:
and you take him birdwatching ![Pajaros.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jcrodriguez/23w2nyupiS9fiUuiCSMASiDX3bfGw1D2rdDQPQKAD2zNLA87UroMYxgdG1j6rYuCZ4ms9.png)

Edited in Photoshop & Canva App
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jcrodriguez/245cUBXzvWF8QVukk8UvqTFX6FutvCzv1TyGDA8ybnR5QKA1v6nMvGS4j6y81Qg9M2HLn.jpg
I saw this film months ago and had forgotten to recommend it. It's a Spanish road movie where two characters with completely opposite personalities, both a mess, meet. Their lives are chaotic. By chance, or rather, by the film's plot, they end up traveling from Valencia, Spain, to a town in Romania. Like any good road trip, besides seeing beautiful landscapes, places they stop, and the typical road scenes, it shows how these two men, who agree that one of them will drive, get to know each other little by little, having their disagreements and arguments, but also forging a friendship: the most beautiful part of this type of film. Mario seems terrified of the road; he doesn't know how to drive. At first glance, he seems quite crazy; he has mental health issues, needs medication, and struggles to speak clearly and answer confidently. Who on earth is this man? Besides always carrying a briefcase, he never wants to be without it. What does he keep in there? Is he a criminal? Where did he get so much money, and why is he so determined to go to a certain place, supposedly to see a bird? Who is he looking for? Although the answers to these questions might suggest a dark and criminal plot, that's not the case at all. On the contrary, what he's doing is a great act of love. He needs to settle accounts with the past, with his mistakes, and with his personal tragedy. Love and guilt consume him. His story is moving. Colombo is the typical cunning man who takes advantage of everyone, a womanizer, a drinker; he enjoys life as if it were his last day, but inside and out he's broken. His son had a birthday, and he couldn't give him a proper gift, or even see him. He has financial problems, but he also feels empty inside. Incapable of being with the person he loves, incapable of being a support to that special person. Is living only for pleasure a way of hiding his sadness? Two magnificent Spanish actors, whose work I admire. Both award-winning: Javier Gutiérrez and Luis Sahera. Just seeing the two of them makes the movie worth watching. They're excellent in their roles, and their unlikely chemistry as a couple is breathtaking. Funny, beautiful, and sad. That's how I'd sum up this film. Watch it and let me know what you think in the comments. ---- > Vi esta película hace meses y se me había olvidado recomendarla. Es una película española de carretera donde dos personajes con personalidades totalmente opuestas, pero ambos un desastre, se encuentran. Sus vidas son un caos. Por azares del destino, o mejor dicho, por la trama de la película, acaban viajando desde Valencia, España, hasta un pueblo de Rumanía. > Como en cualquier buen viaje por carretera, además de ver paisajes preciosos, lugares donde paran y las típicas escenas de carretera, muestra cómo estos dos hombres, que llegan a un acuerdo para que uno de ellos conduzca, se van conociendo poco a poco, teniendo sus roces y discusiones, pero también forjando una amistad: la parte más bonita de este tipo de películas. > Mario parece aterrorizado por la carretera; no sabe conducir. A primera vista, parece bastante loco; tiene problemas mentales, necesita medicación y le cuesta articular palabras y responder con seguridad. ¿Quién demonios es este hombre? Además de llevar siempre un maletín en la mano, nunca quiere separarse de él. ¿Qué guarda ahí? ¿Es un criminal? ¿De dónde sacó tanto dinero y por qué está tan empeñado en ir a cierto lugar, supuestamente para ver un pájaro? ¿A quién busca? > Aunque las respuestas a estas preguntas podrían sugerir una trama oscura y criminal, no es así en absoluto. Al contrario, lo que hace es un gran acto de amor. Necesita saldar cuentas con el pasado, con sus errores y con su tragedia personal. El amor y la culpa lo consumen. Su historia es conmovedora. > Colombo es el típico hombre astuto que se aprovecha de todo, un mujeriego, un bebedor; disfruta la vida como si fuera el último día, pero por dentro y por fuera está destrozado. Su hijo cumplió años y no pudo darle un buen regalo, ni siquiera verlo. Tiene problemas económicos, pero también se siente vacío por dentro. Incapaz de estar con la persona que ama, incapaz de ser el apoyo de esa persona especial. ¿Vivir solo por placer es una forma de ocultar su tristeza? > Dos magníficos actores españoles, cuyo trabajo admiro. Ambos premiados: Javier Gutiérrez y Luis Sahera. Solo con verlos a ellos dos ya vale la pena ver la película. Son excelentes en sus papeles y la química que tienen como pareja, tan improbable, es impresionante. > Divertida, hermosa y triste. Así resumiría esta película. Véanla y díganme qué les pareció en los comentarios.

title.title: Natan De Souza, \
del Betis de Pellegrini / Natan De Souza, \
of Pellegrini's Betis
title.body:
El central brasileño del Betis español está siendo una de las revelaciones de la temporada, pues luego de un paso fracasado por el Napoli italiano, donde sufrió muchas lesiones, que evitaron que se pudiera consolidar en la saga defensiva. Su llegada a España ha cambiado su carrera, siendo indispensable para Pellegrini desde su llegada, jugando gran parte de los minutos disputados en todas las competiciones.

> The Brazilian center-back for Real Betis in Spain has been one of the revelations of the season. After a disappointing spell at Napoli in Italy, where he suffered numerous injuries that prevented him from establishing himself in the defense, his arrival in Spain has transformed his career. He has become indispensable for Pellegrini since his arrival, playing a significant portion of the minutes in all competitions.

<center>![1000675655.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSSRtUcWXSAK8DpfuneBUjsJNxzdET1MWFqyyin6o8oF7/1000675655.jpeg)</center>

<center> <a href=\

>Fuente Sus inicios fueron en las categorías menores del Flamengo, donde llegó a ser una pieza importante, logrando debutar y jugar casi 20 partidos con el primer equipo, aunque no terminó de ganarse un puesto por su inexperiencia. En el 2021 fichó por el Bragantino, donde casi inmediatamente se hizo un puesto en el once, siendo indispensable para que clasificaran ese año a la Libertadores, y aunque el año siguiente se perdió varios partidos por lesiones inorfurtunodas, como una fractura costal, siguió demostrando su nivel. > He began his career in Flamengo's youth ranks, where he became an important player, debuting and playing almost 20 matches with the first team, although he didn't quite secure a regular starting position due to his inexperience. In 2021, he signed for Bragantino, where he almost immediately earned a place in the starting eleven, playing a crucial role in their qualification for the Copa Libertadores that year. Although he missed several matches the following year due to unfortunate injuries, such as a rib fracture, he continued to demonstrate his talent. Para la 2023/24, el Napoli lo fichó por 10 millones de euros, y aunque llegó a sumar muchos minutos en la primera parte de la temporada, compartiendo la saga central sobretodo con el kosovar Amir Rhamani, su pérdida de minutos se vió acentuada luego de una lesión de hombro, lo que provocó que prácticamente fuera borrado del primer equipo, disputando apenas 118 minutos por Serie A en el segundo semestre. Pese hacer la pretemporada con los napolitanos, Antonio Conte no contaba con él, por lo que tuvo que hacer maletas con destino al Sevilla, con un pago previo del Betis de 9 millones de euros. > For the 2023/24 season, Napoli signed him for €10 million, and although he played significant minutes in the first half of the season, primarily sharing the central defensive role with Kosovar Amir Rhamani, his playing time diminished considerably after a shoulder injury. This led to him being virtually dropped from the first team, playing a mere 118 minutes in Serie A during the second half of the season. Despite participating in preseason with Napoli, Antonio Conte didn't count on him, so he had to pack his bags for Sevilla, with Betis paying a fee of €9 million. Con Pellegrini, el carioca volvió a ser importante, pues además de ser uno de los centrales más utilizados por el chileno, ha mejorado en juego y en versatilidad, pudiendo jugar por el lateral zurdo cuando se necesita más contundencia en la marca, ya que su buena calidad técnica le permite sobresalir en posiciones más adelantadas. Otro punto importante ha sido su disponibilidad, pues no ha sufrido lesiones con el Betis, superando esa mala racha que vivió en Italia. > Under Pellegrini, the Brazilian regained his importance, becoming one of the Chilean manager's most frequently used center-backs. He has improved his overall play and versatility, even playing at left-back when more defensive solidity is needed, as his excellent technical ability allows him to excel in more advanced positions. Another key factor has been his availability, as he has remained injury-free for Betis, overcoming the poor form he experienced in Italy.
![natan_napoli.jpg.webp](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQFXNZ3RRcjgXH2DJmvp69xoJRT4nK7AncUNnR2TbjhpN/natan_napoli.jpg.webp)

>Fuente Su envergadura de 1,88 mts también le permite ser bueno en el juego aéreo, aunque le falta pulir un poco su juego ofensivo por esta vía, ya que apenas a marcado un par de goles por esta vía en su carrera. Otro factor interesante, es que más allá de tener un físico corpulento, que le permite ganar muchos duelos por su contundencia defensiva, es relativamente rápido e intenso en la marca, lo que le permite corregir errores y realizar buenos repliegues. > His height of 1.88 meters also makes him good in the air, although he needs to refine his attacking play in this area, having only scored a couple of goals from headers in his career. Another interesting factor is that, beyond his robust physique, which allows him to win many duels thanks to his defensive strength, he is relatively quick and intense in marking, enabling him to correct mistakes and track back effectively. Una de las cosas a mejorar del defensa, es justamente regular esa intensidad, pues suele hacer muchas entradas al límite, ocasionando falta innecesarias, asi como que suele recibir tarjetas amarillas en los partidos, a veces por entradas innecesarias, sufriendo ya suspensión por acumulación tanto en La Liga como en la Europa League este año. Aunque en este curso no ha sufrido ninguna expulsión, el año pasado vió una roja directa apenas a los 7 minutos de haber ingresado contra Osasuna por la liga española, por lo que ya fue muy criticado, poniendo en manifiesto su carácter. > One of the defender's areas for improvement is regulating his intensity, as he tends to make many reckless tackles, committing unnecessary fouls. He also frequently receives yellow cards, sometimes for unnecessary challenges, and has already suffered suspensions for accumulated yellows in both La Liga and the Europa League this year. Although he hasn't been sent off this season, last year he received a straight red card just seven minutes after coming on against Osasuna in La Liga, which drew considerable criticism and highlighted his temperament. En un esquema donde se juegue con una defensa más adelantada, su estilo de anticipación se ve más favorecido, cosa contraria que en equipos con defensas más retrasadas, por lo que es fácil intuir porque no le fue bien en la Serie A. A su favor juego que aún es joven, con lo que podrá mejorar su toma de decisiones, y ya con 25 años, esta a punto de llegar al su peak de rendimiento deportivo. > In a system with a higher defensive line, his anticipation style is more effective, unlike in teams with deeper defenses, which explains why he didn't do well in Serie A. On the plus side, he's still young, which will allow him to improve his decision-making, and at 25, he's about to reach his peak performance.
![natan-partido-betis-villamarin_96.webp](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSnJrQTBaAYVww3xV7kzf918jwGGexBn1i7viVUbx28oj/natan-partido-betis-villamarin_96.webp)

>Fuente Dado lo anterior, ha empezado a sonar para reforzar a varios de los mejores equipos de todo el continente, llamándome especialmente la atención el interés del Barcelona. Muchos argumentan que la primera opción de los cules es Bastoni, pero dado su precio y relevancia en el Inter, otras opciones como el carioca han surgido a la luz, pues cumpliría con el factor mas importante, es zurdo y tiene buena salida de balón, aunque claramente, esta por debajo en la calidad general o la experiencia que atesora el italiano. > Given the above, rumors have started circulating about him joining several of the best teams across the continent, with Barcelona's interest particularly catching my attention. Many argue that Barça's first choice is Bastoni, but given his price and importance to Inter, other options like the Brazilian have emerged, as he would fulfill the most important requirement: he's left-footed and has good ball distribution, although he clearly lacks the overall quality and experience of the Italian.

body.title: Weekend w środku tygodnia
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQP84sNmbbrJDkLBk12CQijKsP8PhYbKgjQr7x6cWMvmc/img_9519.jpg)


Wczoraj po robocie posiadówka z kolegami, z którymi wspólnie jeździmy do pracy wymieniając się co zmianę. Przy 45 kilometrach w jedną stronę to naprawdę robi różnicę. Sam ten dojazd jest męczący i pochłania prawie 2 h z życia licząc w dwie strony. 

Dla nas właśnie wczoraj po pierwszej zmianie zaczął się weekend, który potrwa do jutrzejszej nocki. Weekend w środku tygodnia. Dobrze że pogoda dzisiaj lepsza niż wczoraj.

Niestety od przeprowadzki na wieś czas który tracę na dojazdach nadrabiam poświęcając sen i robi się z tego lekki problem zdrowotny, ale co zrobić, kiedy roboty wszędzie w cholerę. Wszystko rozgrzebane, nic nie dokończone. 

Nic się nie zmieniło. Odpowiedniej ilości snu zaznaje jedynie przy drugich zmianach i ewentualnie w dni wolne, ale też nie zawsze. Pierwsze zmiany i nocki to średnio 5,5-6 h snu dziennie przy intensywnym wysiłku w pracy i pracach domowych, których zamiast ubywać, to wciąż przybywa. Kiedy to się skończy? 

Widzę ten koniec, ale jeszcze jest odległy. Jednak sam fakt, że gdzieś na horyzoncie go widać trochę buduje i daje motywację, żeby to wszystko ogarnąć. 

Z pozytywów tego wszystkiego zdecydowanie warto wymienić, że w zaledwie 7-8 miesięcy od przeprowadzki mamy już gruntownie wyremontowane, ocieplone i wykończone pół piętra wliczając w to nową instalację elektryczną i wodną. Zostało mi jedynie kilka drobnych rzeczy typu gdzieś listwę przykręcić, tam trochę farbą przemalować, coś podregulować. Ale to już wszystko na spokojnie.

Dzisiaj w planach miałem wymianę opon w jednym z samochodów, ale przy okazji chciałem też wymienić na szybko lusterko boczne. Okazało się, że do mechanika dotrze ono dopiero jutro, więc przełożyłem. Zamiast tego dojadę więc do żony w Bielsku kiedy będzie kończyć pracę i wspólnie pojedziemy do galerii na shopping.

title.title: United Kingdom - Discovering The Icons Of London
title.body:
<center>![20140611_183629.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/243WPj1zbx83oE4jZ1tjqVQbNYp6NV3jENtPjP9ZsJqJvTs6ovp2cAxfFHjrfjvD1oWQg.jpg)</center>

Hello there!

Having completed my earlier travel posts on several interesting countries and regions, including Japan, Maldives, Indonesia, US, Europe, New Zealand and the latest one being Australia, it's time to fly over to United Kingdom!

This was a trip I made in 2014, I was there partly for work and partly for leisure as well. At that point in my life, it was one of the further destination that I have travelled all the way from Asia and it was definitely an eye opener to see how United Kingdom, or more specifically London, looked like. One thing that I remembered vividly was how strong GBP was, and everything was so expensive. For example, even though the numerical digits of the prices were small, because 5 or 10 GBP was easily a lot already. Anyway, time to relive those moments as I share the sights and sounds of my experience!

Here are the posts so far:
[United Kingdom - Living The Football Dream With Chelsea](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-living-the-football-dream-with-chelsea)
[United Kingdom - The Beauty Of Art and Shopping In London](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-the-beauty-of-art-and-shopping-in-london)
[United Kingdom - Spectacular Fireworks at Horse Guards Parade](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-spectacular-fireworks-at-horse-guards-parade)
[United Kingdom - Discovering History At The Tower Of London](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-discovering-history-at-the-tower-of-london)
[United Kingdom - Breathtaking Views From The Shard](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-breathtaking-views-from-the-shard)
[United Kingdom - Trooping The Colour Ceremony At Buckingham Palace](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-trooping-the-colour-ceremony-at-buckingham-palace)
[United Kingdom - Spectacular Airshow Over Buckingham Palace](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-spectacular-airshow-over-buckingham-palace)
[United Kingdom - A Relaxing Day Trip To Bath](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-a-relaxing-day-trip-to-bath)
[United Kingdom - Exploring Bath Abbey And Roman Baths](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-exploring-bath-abbey-and-roman-baths)
[United Kingdom - A Journey Through Time At Stonehenge](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-a-journey-through-time-at-stonehenge)
[United Kingdom - A Stadium Tour At Emirates Stadium](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-a-stadium-tour-at-emirates-stadium)
[United Kingdom - Colours Of London’s Streets](https://peakd.com/hive-163772/@relf87/united-kingdom-colours-of-londons-streets)

[//]:# (!worldmappin 51.50181 lat -0.12015 long United Kingdom - Discovering The Icons Of London d3scr)
***
My London work plus leisure trip has come to an end as this will be the final post for my UK and London series, thanks to everyone who have followed my colourful journey in this amazing country and city.

In the final post, I wanted to end with the icons of London, especially those that I haven't mentioned, but still deserved a mention. And it starts with a walk along River Thames. In one of first days, I took this walk during the evening, it was quite a nice walk and there was a lot of sights to soak in. And you could see the ferris wheel, London Eye, in the distance.


<center>![20140611_181159.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/2458LVXLeoFkkmcBVK36p2WNuHmXMv2G6MeX2wRAuQwMutnQ4Cioc1RKEmcCnWLhkxPGn.jpg)</center>


<center>![20140611_181548.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/243frBfJYj8XktPDrCWvzrbzGhkzGVyWoFEV6W5zDgieRdrx6vae3ad6nm3nfELKtU7MX.jpg)</center>


They even had bars on the boats on the river. Would people really want to dine on a platform that sways with the waters? Definitely a no no for people with motion sickness.

<center>![20140611_182138.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23yJCAP7g5GvKXgdtad5jxEZfKcHZeSMpyPZ4hjTukm1nhmKd5mWMTDeBv2uBjSQzPhgb.jpg)</center>

There were many of such bridges on River Thames as we got closer to London Eye.

<center>![20140611_182312.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/245Hj2d38ZQ1eEtdxdU6BRzgMGyvfdUFXQAu2JKGNFiocawMt8MSQew2U8DgXdZmDGNSq.jpg)</center>

Finally we reached! We have a similar one in Singapore, called the Singapore Flyer, so it wasn't a big WOW for me. Still it's nice to look at as the biggest icon in the background of all the photos in this area.

<center>![20140611_183629.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/243WPj1zbx83oE4jZ1tjqVQbNYp6NV3jENtPjP9ZsJqJvTs6ovp2cAxfFHjrfjvD1oWQg.jpg)</center>

<center>![20140614_154909.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/244KRFmyQKJFcCmXN5QXijqaoSXF8CCVNRcbZGwza1wytWWRgzZWdCy2dkkYqnEnsgWzU.jpg)</center>

Another of those bridges as we headed back to the hotel.

<center>![20140611_183909.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23zRwBEGvK8Pe3vTWjFFwN8btXSRytjrN11vsCgNGVMgFv6spqeZ8fXJxji1qsuQpcf6a.jpg)</center>

If you play Monopoly, you definitely would know this place. Advance to Trafalgar Square! Yes, this is the Trafalgar Square! Very crowded and the building behind is National Gallery.


<center>![20140614_140724.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23sdbPsCMBkWq2AHL4RDCgTFqEKB9CGLZU8QZBoCnqWWUYFmxnLVGpwtREZ8Lok74yexV.jpg)</center>

Some historical structures spotted in the area too!

<center>![20140614_140534.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/242rsK8BhWcKaVt8xhS8vk6Qngp7nG4cVUD7UM2bum2ohvMXfhcj875Dk1ySF18fjbbmu.jpg)</center>


<center>![20140614_140530.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23qrLVcCuYvp2aX8r5ND3H75V2V25Vx1yYYy7U5CD6hGcfwGdy1h9gQNfUMkdtQtRZaEq.jpg)</center>

And within walking distance, we arrived at the Big Ben!

<center>![20140614_153353.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/242NgxN4E8qw39YJQk5pogKSjrqJGocTccbW5PMWhhMPJtWHsHRZmociW1gUpPLsqYdwN.jpg)</center>

And that's the Palace of Westminister, which is the meeting place for their Parliament.

<center>![20140614_154641.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/241EzmTXWTM4hdn9hFfvKZPpZakbriEZ9CYzn5hvANar98dJNP4E2mEvAZioQqv19Gd1C.jpg)</center>

Another must visit in London is British Museum! The museum was so big, and I was there on two occasions and I think I didn't manage to cover the entire museum. Here's one of the beautiful halls.



<center>![20140612_170209.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23xefTGEwPwwbjii5PF8PSAj3RohUEbQYWdLUMTeeTBhBeXpsbHf3bGuGSr8HuF9oxRg9.jpg)</center>


<center>![20140612_181119.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23ynWt3TcPvbUjvuc2uocpA2TjvJhTXzucagDpZuyZzPdy7BRk5pR9qZTRcAFbyQiPpra.jpg)</center>


<center>![20140612_181058.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23yws7JHWcy1J2M6gfSVuRN6tZeFjdt8ataQ7K9CC37MzPSAioTdbR14XDJhqpqdz95zQ.jpg)</center>

Finally, a \
. Not so much of an attraction but there were long lines of crowds queueing up to take photo at \

. If you are a Harry Potter fan, you would know how iconic this trolley and platform is.

<center>![20140614_164143.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23xVKEAHFG3fq7dL45Yv2ggzAf9t3Xmnm5DovasZqj4RU1R4j7zTMKiNQzWUxbCa5CwGG.jpg)</center>


<center>![20140614_164308.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23zbRq4hhSgC1UWPjPxV6KaLmyGBLAs2Q89qjgGhKaVJ2wBDnz6PKSPUFsi2ikcmPPEDT.jpg)</center>

They also had a shop which sells Harry Potter merchandise, and of course, it was very crowded as well.

<center>![20140614_165007.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/243BkPVqrqtaicA4vb7e7QGgjTCg3xvh7njVN1GpAWfoyd1kThLfZBC89iQskiDRNKxJp.jpg)</center>


It's been so many years, but definitely brings back memories. I read all their books and watched all the movies, have you?

<center>![20140614_165321.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23wgFgJ6EtMppZtBEJ82sJzZg6uLTnCnLqH16vGUzJ6Qfu7iKBg37KEDR5XVxvefKnksr.jpg)</center>

I was tempted to buy those T-shirts because the me 12 years ago felt there were too expensive. Haha.

<center>![20140614_170316.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23vhwjCTiNPbonieiNsRTejfcLprckUKeZDi8RoWWf5C7T33zomM2ErZjDpqmi7eZFk9x.jpg)</center>

So that's it! 13 posts and a few thousands of words! My posts for the London trip are complete! To be honest, I didn't expect there were so many things to write about, but as I got through the posts and photos, there was indeed a lot of rave about UK and London! So where should we go to next? ;)


And that's all I have today! Have you been to London or United Kingdom? Let me know in the comments below!

Finally, thanks for reading my post in the community under World Map Pin!

body.title: Kladovo - amazing town in Serbia near Romania
body.body: Recently I had a business trip to Kladovo[.](http://Kladovo.It)\n\n

/> It was the first time I visited this town even though I had bad memories because a long time ago ,my defunct father was hospitalized there, in an oncology hospital. There are only few in whole Serbia, and since we were not living in capoital, they decided for him to go there. We were kids and my mum was with him, he spent there about two months after that he unfortunatelly died,very young, at the age of 46. So I didn't want to visit that place, because have very sad memories but the business trip lead me there, and I can say that the place is very beautiful, as I knew by experience of people who were visiting it. but I experienced it by myself, so recommendation for Kladovo.

/> Kladovo is one of those towns in Serbia where you feel like you’re on the sea because of the huge river, but you’re actually right on the border with Romania, where the Danube is perhaps its most powerful. This small town offers the perfect blend of history, nature, and that special peace that a big river brings. It really looks amazing.

/> We couldn't visit all beautiful places recommended by others but I will show photos we took on some places, as well will mention what is good to visit there. Here are some things you definitely shouldn’t miss in Kladovo and the surrounding area: 1. **Fetislam Fortress** This medieval artillery fortress has recently been completely reconstructed and looks fantastic. It’s divided into the Small and Big Towns, and a walk along the ramparts offers incredible views of the Danube. It’s the perfect place for an afternoon stroll and a glimpse of Ottoman architecture.

/>
    
    Archaeological **Museum of Đerdap**  
    Although small, this museum is of immense importance. It houses artifacts that testify to the fact that this area was the cradle of civilization. You can see objects from prehistoric times, as well as important Roman excavations that tell the story of the conquering campaigns of Emperor Trajan.
    
    Trajan’s Bridge and Diana  
      
    Not far from the center are the remains of Trajan’s Bridge, once considered the largest bridge in the world. Although only the pillars are visible today, the very thought of what an architectural masterpiece it was almost 2,000 years ago leaves you breathless. Nearby is the Diana Fortress, one of the largest and best-preserved Roman castra on the Danube.4. Danube Cruise and the Small and Large Cauldrons  
      
    This is probably the most beautiful part of the trip. From Kladovo, you can take a boat ride through the Đerdap Gorge. There you will see:  
      
    **Trajan's Table** (Tabula Traiana): Visible only from the river.  
    **Decebal's Head:** A huge sculpture carved into the rock on the Romanian side.  
    **Mrakonija Monastery:** Located right on the water's edge.
    
    **City Center and Beaches**
    
2.  My friends who were with me on the trip had told me that Kladovo has a beautifully landscaped quay and one of the most beautiful sandy beaches in Serbia. During the summer, the atmosphere is truly summery – the cafes are full,they developed and devoted everything to tourism, so it is beautiful, people are swimming, and the sunsets over the Danube are unforgettable.
    
    I am going to visit this place very soon with my family. We will try to stay at least 4 days in order to have time enough to visit all the places we need .

body.body:
https://youtu.be/TIAgZr_oErQ?si=7cdMHn1OdThM7T2L
Time is of great essence in life. There is nothing that we do that we do not need time. How we use the time that we have made a great impact on our life. This is why we should endeavor to avoid wasting our time. Time is very important. God values time and time means a lot to humanity.

It is not every time that is the opportune time. There are times when what we want to do will not be necessary. There is time for every action under the sun. When we do not do the things that we should do at a particular time we might have ourselves to blame for missing the right thing. There is always the right time as well as there is a wrong time.

In doing the will of God we must understand that God has time for every action under the sun. If you are to go and preach today and you are not doing so, you have not done what God asked you to do. So, doing what God is asking from us is one thing but it is another thing to do it at the right time.

Whenever opportunity come to us, let us use it wisely. Every opportunity that God brings our way He wants us to do good.

body.title: Crispy Dahi Tikki: The Perfect Evening with Friends!

body.title: [生活日记]爸的生日，我却在海边悠闲😜
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbrkayeuP1Gog3jWnExjkP72dEhEftzXrKATMzin4EsA6/1778667034255.jpg)
今天是特别的日子，我老爸生日。因为陪孩子嘛，老爸生日我没有在身边一起庆祝有点遗憾，不过还有明年的生日呢呵呵呵，我给爸妈打了电话。
弟弟弟妹今天给老爸过了非常开心的生日。先是把爸妈接过市里来。然后上午带妈去骨科医院看了手指，妈前一阵不小心摔倒把手指给怼到了，没当回事，结果一直忍忍疼到现在，多次想带她去医院看看，她不肯，这次弟弟还是决定去拍个片子看看。拍片结果是果然小手指骨折了，医生说已经好了很多，不过还没完全好，给开了药，叮嘱要好好包扎好养着，不能再干活了。这回妈知道是骨折了，才肯好好养，听大夫的话啦！
去过医院弟弟弟妹中午就去了餐馆，带老爸老妈吃饭，给爸买定了一个大蛋糕。看这蛋糕我都要流口水啦！弟妹是特意发过来馋我的吗😂😋😋

弟弟今天的事儿办的很不错，真辛苦他啦！妈打电话给我，听到她们说起今天的事情很开心，我心里就舒服多了，毕竟我还真的是第一次没有给爸过生日呢。（不对，我好像是提前给爸红包了，不过没陪伴呀😬）

我今天没有参与其中，自己在这边海边悠闲自在呢哈。下午没事儿的时候又去海边了，海边怎么这么多人？原来天气好都来赶海了，退潮了拾海货。这是我唯一拾到的花蛤。今天喜欢上了海边的岩石，拍了好几张照片。
