links.title: PM appeal moves the market
links.body:
On Sunday Prime Minister of India Mr. Narendra Modi made a speech requesting people of India to become mindful about using resources and to cut back on buying Gold in 2026. His message was simple; Cut back on gold buying, on non-essential foreign travels, on fuel use, if possible do work-from-home and choose local goods. India Rupee has fallen against the dollar in this last 1 month. To think of it how fragile our systems are; one statement from the Prime Minister and all the markets crash.

Everything he said seems to be very practical but by Monday morning there was a major turmoil with all the markets. Gold market was in free-fall, stock market crashed heavily, even the real estate slipped. It felt like something major really happened, where in reality it is just one statement made by him. 

![geralt-stock-exchange-642896_1920.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRtzafdMKMmVA4SQ6JTrD447GrT1jM3BZo9Y8YUXKwMvL/geralt-stock-exchange-642896_1920.jpg)
[Source](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/stock-exchange-bull-bear-securities-642896/)

Last month I wanted to invest some money in mutual funds, hubby told me to wait as he was expecting a fall. There was already a prediction about it. But me as always low on patience in these matters bought it and now, I am feeling bad about it, and hubby also got annoyed with me. Anyways, it was a small amount. I don’t really need to brood about it. The good thing is I also wanted to buy gold, so probably now is the right time for it. I checked the price; the variation is huge at this moment. 24k 1 gm price shows between 15000 to 16000, so if I am going to purchase then I am sure the shop is going to sell me at 16000 only, which is not making much of a difference. Better I will wait for this one for some time for the price to stabilise. 

On a larger scale of things, yes rupee is under pressure right now, so PM made this appeal but guess it made a dramatic impact on the markets. After Covid, I guess people get panicked with this kind of news. Because they feel that first there is an appeal and later there is a mandate. Indians have emotional attachment with Gold and such news creates panic. To look at it, this was not about gold or any other commodity. It is about the challenges of Strait of Hormuz going on for months now. 

For markets, these sentiments rule. Let's see now is this is one of a day sentiment trigger or the first of several many more.

***Thank you for visiting my blog.*** 👼🏻👼🏻💖💖🌹🌺🌸

links.title: Hive Open Mic week 318 || Lion and the Lamb by Pst. Chingtok Ishaku || covered by @sampraise77
links.body:
[![](https://images.3speak.tv/images/1778660266676-ea06caa7115f6c7c.webp)](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=sampraise77/e9b4c74c)

▶️ [Watch on 3Speak](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=sampraise77/e9b4c74c)


---

Hello friends on Hive, I welcome you to Hive Open Mic week 318, I'm @sampraise77 and for this week choice of topic, I will do a rendition of a song titled Lion and the Lamb by Pst. Chingtok Ishaku 
The song really looks up to God, showing how much it respects and adores Him for how truly unique He is. It tells us He's above everyone and everything – all the powerful people, rulers, and authorities – making it clear that nobody else even comes close to Him in terms of glory, wisdom, strength, or holiness. The main point here is God's greatness and how one-of-a-kind He is, staying the same through all generations. It's basically a statement of faith, saying God lasts forever, is always reliable, and is in charge of everything He created.

When the song talks about God as both a lion and a lamb, it's showing us two different sides of who He is. The lion stands for majesty, power, victory, bravery, and His role as King. It paints a picture of God being incredibly strong and unbeatable, someone who fights for His followers and rules with total power. This shows how He can beat darkness, get rid of evil, and make things fair. Then there's the lamb, which represents being humble, making sacrifices, being gentle, merciful, and offering redemption. It highlights how God shows His love by making sacrifices and having deep care for people. Put together, these two symbols perfectly show how God is both strong and gentle. He's powerful enough to run the whole universe, but also loving enough to save and look after all of us.

Calling Him \

in the song really shows His divine power and who He truly is. It tells us that God perfectly reveals what the Father thinks, what He wants, and what He's like to humanity. Through Him, folks can grasp spiritual truths, feel grace, and find salvation. This highlights how close God is to His people, because He's not far away or hiding; instead, He's revealed and easy to reach.

Something else important in the song is how God never changes. People, situations, and even the seasons are always changing, but God stays true forever. His promises always come true, His character never gets weaker, and His power never fades. This gives people who believe a lot of confidence, hope, and a sense of safety, especially when things get tough. The song encourages us to fully trust and give ourselves over to Him because the God we worship is eternal and someone we can always count on.

All in all, the song is a really powerful way to worship, showing how great God is, celebrating His loving sacrifice, and reminding believers that He's always faithful and supreme.

links.title: Fragiled As Life
links.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUcrFRfWx1qmsa3WMuCDBTqY3En71qtchLja3SALGDXxt/screenshot_20260319_205841.jpg)

Sickness and death are the strongest destr0yers of men/women.

A rich man or woman can become helpless on a hospital bed.

Life isn't on repeat, and this moment won't come back around.
If you're unhappy, change something.
If you're stuck, move.
If you're dreaming, start.
Nothing shifts until you do.

A powerful man or woman can suddenly depend on people he once ignored.

A strong man or woman can cry in secret when pain enters his body.

When sickness and death knock,
connections become weak,
money becomes small,
pride disappears.

That is why wisdom is important.

Kindness is important.
Peace is important.

Because at the end of the day, no man or woman is too powerful for sickness, and no human being is bigger than death.

#hivelifestyle #ecency#wave 

Life is truly fragile.

title.title: 岳阳博物馆
title.body:
在公园里认识了位退休的阿姨，给我热心地介绍了家本地饭店，据她说她跟她老公不想做饭的时候，就会去这家饭店去吃，味道很是不错。

我一想这不错，看了下地图，发现离的很近，大约700米左右。从南湖出来，路口处过马路，对面就是这家饭店了。


![IMG20260510121424.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rivalhw/EoK6EAiymikADvJ1iuQq2QBP3vd4zAqmYwvLD39UsVgjhsGxkLRNJrirLJT7VNT2xyE.jpg)

![IMG20260510121438.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rivalhw/EowGaTDn6bxb5pyerAmtMjyxBandwG8Hse5f8QVqGSwuXn3Nh5VQkKeQJWRfJDXoCER.jpg)

![IMG20260510121445.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rivalhw/Eou8fo3izyASLmfhW8kNi36qejdHEq5pZffdkk78h584zRd6GuFFQv2VUcyCGQz2wim.jpg)

![IMG20260510121450.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rivalhw/EoeEpp3u6UcSqCsMwiitzFRCAgmezcgJiSrC8G1K3K5AE9y2R5V5H5BdQnJ5q4PJYkx.jpg)

![IMG20260510124544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rivalhw/23tSamLdgfQb8F9eh8V5Kmc3LoXGmpQsJzRxCkBJk3Vn9ZMcdh9UivXAvMTMJ4zuTgQ5S.jpg)
前一天朋友请吃的回头鱼，味道不错。这次我又再点了份回头鱼。

这锅份量很大，都不用米饭了。

吃完后感觉味道一如既往的赞👍👍👍！

吃的有点撑，在路边站了会。

有个靓女在侧方位停车，停了几次都没停好，我帮她引导了下，方才停好车。

靓女下次后，我看她握方向盘时左右晃动，很明显是不熟悉，便提醒她方向盘不要左右反复晃动。

不过没过几分钟我就对自己说的话感到有些后悔了。我之前给自己定下个规则，不要动辄“好为人师”，这毛病可不好，得改，必须彻底改正！

帮忙就帮忙，干嘛那么多话？以后得注意了，不能再好为人师！😳😳

站了会后，打车去岳阳博物馆，实际上南湖离博物馆很近，约莫1、2公里的样子，只是我刚才那大份鱼🐟吃的有点撑，这会确实不想走了。


![IMG20260510134558.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/rivalhw/Eoc72F62FhHK69wyzZLbphwyFrrJdb5NpYUGTBUMCo3GcVxmp1qKinqGVs9G6uX2Gpp.jpg)
来到岳阳博物馆，门口的路上有个车载卖咖啡的
点了杯咖啡，坐在路边休息下先

title.title: The Last Week of the World Powell Built
title.body:
# The Last Week of the World Powell Built

Friday, May 15. Circle it. Powell's out. Warsh is in.

Eight years of one man's hand on the most powerful monetary lever in human history, and it ends not with a crisis, not with a triumph, but with a calendar date and a Senate committee vote that went 13-11. The narrowest margin in history for a Fed Chair confirmation. Thirteen to eleven. On the eve of a hot inflation print. With Brent crude above $100 and the Strait of Hormuz running at partial capacity. This is the context in which the United States hands the keys to a Hoover Institution fellow who thinks the dot plot is a crime against intellectual honesty.

You could not write it. You'd be told it was too on the nose.

---

Let's slow down on Warsh for a moment, because the market is pricing him as a binary — either a Trump puppet who cuts into a 3.8% CPI print and blows up the Fed's credibility for a generation, or a closet hawk who wraps his inflation-fighting instincts in AI-disinflationary rhetoric and basically continues Powell's hold with better branding. Neither picture is complete and both are dangerous to trade on.

Here is what is actually known: Warsh wants to shrink the balance sheet. The Fed's balance sheet currently sits near $6.7 trillion. Before the financial crisis it was $800 billion. That gap — the chasm between those two numbers — is the accumulated legacy of every QE program, every emergency facility, every \
moment since 2008. Warsh has called this \

He wants it gone. Or at least much smaller.\n\nThe bond market knows what that means. Fewer Fed buyers of Treasuries means more supply relative to demand means higher yields. The 30-year has already crept above 5% — the \

some are calling it — and if the balance sheet rundown accelerates, the move isn't over. Equity risk premiums don't get richer at 5%-handle long bonds. The S&P at 20.9 times forward earnings is a valuation built for a world with $6.7 trillion of central bank support behind it. Remove the scaffolding and the building may still stand. Or it might not. Anyone telling you confidently which outcome occurs is selling something.

---

Then there's the other thing. The strange, almost philosophical position Warsh has staked out: that AI is a disinflationary force powerful enough to justify looser policy even when prices are running hot. He said as much in his confirmation hearing. The tech industry absorbed this like manna. Nvidia touched an all-time intraday high on Tuesday morning, briefly, before the CPI hit and the chip complex fell apart with an almost theatrical synchronicity.

Qualcomm down 12%. Worst session since 2020. Intel off 9%. AMD and Micron bleeding mid-single digits. The SOX dropping 5% on the day. This after a month in which the index had gained 29%. After Intel, of all companies, had run 430% in a year. When the reversal comes in a market like this, it doesn't arrive with a warning. It shows up in the middle of a quiet Tuesday morning alongside a CPI report and a war update and just starts erasing numbers.

The irony is that the SOX is still up 60% year-to-date. What happened Tuesday was a tremor. The question — the one nobody can fully answer — is whether the \

trading at roughly 39 times earnings is a justified premium or a late-cycle hallucination. Dot-com devotees were paying 152 times. Bulls find comfort in that comparison. Bears note that 39 times is still almost double the historical S&P average multiple. The argument goes on. The chips go up. The chips go down. The data centers keep getting built.

---

Somewhere in all this noise, the actual consumer is doing considerably less well than the market's mood would suggest.

For the first time in three years, wage growth is losing the race to inflation. Gas at $4.50 nationally. Beef up 14.8% year over year. Airline fares up 20.7%. The University of Michigan survey now shows households expecting 4.5% inflation over the next year — a number that, if it embeds further into wage negotiations, becomes the Fed's next problem on top of its current ones. Consumer sentiment has hit all-time lows while the S&P 500 sits near all-time highs. These two facts coexist because the stock market is not the economy, and the economy is not the stock market, and 2026 is making that point more brutally than any economics textbook.

Powell, at his last FOMC, sat with four dissents — the most fractious committee since 1992. He held rates and said nothing particularly memorable. That's his legacy in miniature: a man who walked tightropes for eight years without falling, who sometimes moved too slowly and sometimes too fast, who was never beloved by anyone but was trusted by enough people to keep the system functional. History will probably be kinder to him than the room was on Tuesday.

---

Warsh's first press conference will come this week. Every word will be parsed for signals, syllables mapped onto rate trajectories, adjectives interrogated for hidden hawkishness. \

was his phrase from the confirmation hearings — not a term you deploy lightly when you're about to chair an institution whose primary asset is institutional credibility. Either it was a performance for Trump, or he means it. If he means it, the bond market is not done moving.

Barclays data shows the S&P 500 averages drawdowns of 5%, 12%, and 16% in the one, three, and six months following a new Fed Chair taking over — going back to 1930. That's an average. Averages mean nothing in any individual instance. But the number exists, and it exists because transitions are windows of genuine uncertainty, not just political theatre.

GameStop tried to buy eBay this week. eBay's board sent back a letter calling the proposal neither \

Ryan Cohen, who turned a dying video game retailer into something that still somehow commands institutional attention, got publicly rejected by a digital auction platform. This is also a data point, in its way: a symbol of how strange and crowded and restless capital has become when it can't find a clean directional bet.

Everyone is waiting. For the Strait to open or not open. For Warsh to signal or not signal. For May CPI to either confirm or break the inflation trajectory. For Cerebras to price and tell us whether the IPO window is still wide open or beginning to close.

Friday is very close. The world Powell built is almost over. Whatever Warsh builds in its place starts now.

title.title: Balance between studies and sports
title.body:
Greetings Education  Community hive students connect. I hope that by the infinite mercy of God Almighty, you are all well. Today I want to discuss a wonderful topic with you. Basically, our students are becoming more neglected these days. Day after day, they are becoming addicted to mobile games. Moreover, nowadays students are very lazy and they are not able to pay any attention to their studies. And the reason for this abnormal behavior among them is that they do not have enough entertainment. 

Especially a student will study and go to school. Along with studies, he has another responsibility. A student must play sports. 




 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmd5AgoSFu9Gxqjy9FMFxHD6qkVdxBz6ep1e655dLwdGJV/pexels-dhruvrchauhan-13812360.jpg 


[Source](https://www.pexels.com/photo/girls-playing-games-on-the-street-13812360/)

There are many schools where students and learners are only encouraged to study. There is no huge field in front of the school and a school is formed with only a few rooms. In those small schools, there is no field for playing and children cannot play openly. As a result, children become mentally ill and their brains do not develop properly due to only studying. If we want to develop children's brains properly, then what we must do is to give students the opportunity to play sports along with studying. 

 In the current context, schools are built in high-rise buildings. There is not enough free space in front of the school and there is no opportunity for students to play. If students go to school and apply to the teachers to play, the teachers never give permission for sports. As a result, the students are very much affected and their brains are disturbed. 

The only way to get rid of this problem is to arrange a place for sports for children. It is a natural and common characteristic of children to study. However, along with this, sufficient space for sports must be created for students. There must be an open field in front of a school. Students will go to school at a specific time and then they will spend time studying. They must be given opportunities for sports in the middle of the total school hours. That is, if the school runs for 6 hours, then an hour should be created for students to play. 

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmfBZTbxbNS3q3Ga4JCRv6ToTfU1H6vWyzJC8JfjpFm3Go/pexels-rdne-8363047.jpg 


[Source](https://www.pexels.com/photo/children-playing-with-their-toys-inside-the-school-8363047/)


Then the students will again study carefully and they will return home. After returning home, they will freshen up and rest for some time and then go to the school or college grounds or the garden to play again. 

Basically, the afternoon time is very important for students.  The importance of sports in the brain development of students is immense. If students go to school on time, study and get the opportunity to play, it helps in developing their brain. Apart from this, students must be given the opportunity to play in the afternoon. 

I have seen several families. Where students return from school and then they finish some kind of food and drink. After finishing their food and drink, they go back to the coaching center and they focus on various types of studies. But in the afternoon, children must be given the opportunity to play. If they are only attracted to studies, they will never be able to do well in studies. 

Moreover, the school should sometimes arrange entertainment for students. Annual sports events should be organized and sports should be arranged for students on other days. This develops the brain of students and increases their attention to studies. 

So let us, as conscious parents, arrange sports for students. If students study along with sports, their studies will be good and they will be able to focus on studies. At the end of the day, we all wish the students a beautiful and bright future.  But if there is no entertainment, then students cannot improve themselves and their position. 

So I think that students must be provided with sports along with studies. In the afternoon, students should be sent to the field or garden to play. And if the continuity of education is maintained in this way, I think students will definitely be able to do well in their studies. What is your opinion? Of course, don't forget to comment.

title.title: Frigoles, carne de cerdo y arroz blancoºººººFrigoles, pork, and white rice
title.body:
Hola a todos, la verdad amigos como el frio comenzo antes de lo previsto, con esto quiero decirles que todavia estamos en otoño, porque no llego el invierno pero si llego el frio,, ante esta circunstancia, los bueno y en lo personal es de mi agrado, degustar para el almuerzo una comida con muchas calorias, como lo es frigola con carne de cerdo y arroz blanco, pero cuando el antojo apremia, todo es valido jajaja, por eso prepare para el almuerzo todo esto y la verdad es muy facil de cocinarlo todo, ademas el mismo sale muy sabroso.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoeFPzAL5SRhn3TqwZnM4scqrJ85zio9fTPUBroUBkAv7qRELFRiMycvNCa44x7B1Cg.png)

Asi que a los frigoles los dejo de un dia para el otro en remojo, de esa manera se cocina mejor en este caso con la misma agua y mientras se cocina preparo la carne de cerdo, agrego en la olla, un poco de aceite ajo, cebolla y luego dicha carne, cuando la misma esta bien dorada, luego de revolverla bien, la agrego en la olla donde se encuentra los frigoles, los cuales estan casi blando, como se ve es una olla, de esa forma se cocina rapido y sale bien, mas cuando tiene mucho caldo.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoyPVN58MSZKtn4WMmcLQN3n9UsEwZM48XmdZdqiJ59KnsNoZWs9fyLk85zJr2juASg.png)

Para cocinar el arroz, agregamos la olla, en la hornalla de la cocina, le vertemos un poco de aceite, luego unos dientes de ajo, para luego comenzar a verter el arroz, para ir revolviendolo lentamente, luego se le agrega agua caliente, tapamos la olla y dejamos que se asiente y asi queda listo el mismo, como lo podemos ver en esta fotografia, esta todo en proceso.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23tbrkfY8qzvUQNJrNbkLGjv8EqZyVNXA8Nim8gF9Lhe5HHXMLat8RDqwSyA6P3ytktDS.png)

Asi es amigos cuando el frio se hace notar y su presencia comienza a incomodarnos, por el hecho de que nos tenemos que habrigar y muy bien, para de esa manera no contraer un resfriado.

MUCHAS GRACIAS POR SEGUIRME Y LEERME, QUE TENGAN UN BELLO DIA.

ENGLISH

Hello everyone, honestly, friends, since the cold weather started earlier than expected—and by that I mean we’re still in autumn, because winter hasn’t arrived yet, but the cold certainly has— Given this situation, what I personally enjoy is having a high-calorie meal for lunch, like frigola with pork and white rice. But when the craving hits, anything goes, haha. That’s why I made all this for lunch, and honestly, it’s really easy to cook, plus it turns out really tasty.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoeFPzAL5SRhn3TqwZnM4scqrJ85zio9fTPUBroUBkAv7qRELFRiMycvNCa44x7B1Cg.png)

So I soak the black beans overnight; that way they cook better in this case using the same water. While they’re cooking, I prepare the pork: I add a little oil, garlic, and onion to the pot, followed by the pork. Once it’s nicely browned, after stirring it well, I add it to the pot with the beans, which are almost tender. As you can see, it’s a pot, so it cooks quickly and turns out well, especially when there’s plenty of broth.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/EoyPVN58MSZKtn4WMmcLQN3n9UsEwZM48XmdZdqiJ59KnsNoZWs9fyLk85zJr2juASg.png)

To cook the rice, we place the pot on the stove, pour in a little oil, then add a few cloves of garlic, and then begin to pour in the rice, stirring it slowly. Next, we add hot water, cover the pot, and let it simmer until it’s ready, as we can see in this photo—it’s all in progress.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/comandoyeya/23tbrkfY8qzvUQNJrNbkLGjv8EqZyVNXA8Nim8gF9Lhe5HHXMLat8RDqwSyA6P3ytktDS.png)

That’s right, friends, when the cold sets in and starts to bother us, we have to bundle up—and bundle up well—so we don’t catch a cold.

THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR FOLLOWING AND READING MY POSTS. HAVE A WONDERFUL DAY.

title.body:
Триває мій експеримент зі створення квіткового суцільного зеленого килима на ділянці замість газона. Є в мене на присадибній ділянці частина землі, до якої не дотягується подовжувач електричної газонокосарки. І щоб позбутися бур'янів на ній треба було або посадити траву, або спробувати рослину килимового типу. 

І ось минулого року придбали на базарчику за смішну ціну кілька горщиків флоксу і посадили в різних місцях в межах однієї ділянки. Вже за рік рослина розрослась і поступово почав вимальовуватись той бажаний суцільний килим. А цієї весни цей килим ще й перетворився на таку квітку красу, від якої очей не хочеться відриват. 

Думаю, що за цей сезон рослина вкриє заплановану площу і я, нарешті, забуду про бур'ян та косіння трави на довго.

Julley Everyone,

Starting this beautiful day out here today in these beautiful locations in the remote valley around Manali Himachal Pradesh. So was this perfect afternoon that I would say that we spent over here in the forest enjoyed the best time in the shepherds meadows. So we were really lucky enough that we could just drive all the way to this particular spot. As you did. It would take a hike to the place but lucky enough that there was this road that just went all the way to the place so I thought why not to share this moment so today this was the journey and the adventure that I wanted to share it with you guys through this post so which started journey somewhere around 10 AM from my hometown in Manali and then we drove near about 4Starting this beautiful day out here today in these beautiful locations in the remote valley around Manali Himachal Pradesh. So was this perfect afternoon that I would say that we spent over here in the forest enjoyed the best time in the shepherds meadows. So we were really lucky enough that we could just drive all the way to this particular spot. As you did. It would take a hike to the place but lucky enough that there was this road that just went all the way to the place so I thought why not to share this moment so today this was the journey and the adventure that I wanted to share it with you guys through this post so which started journey somewhere around 10 AM from my hometown in Manali and then we drove near about 20 Kms towards Kullu side, where there was this place closer to the village near a place called Patlikuhal.

![IMG_0423.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYbZf1fWMbk6bc8XokFGiMUAo7FeZe5ouWEdxxPTnE2g5/IMG_0423.jpeg)
So after driving all the way to the remote locations in Pangan Road we reached this place called somewhere closer to Shilgli Village. So we reached at this place and every thing looked so beautiful and so peaceful that we could just sit here and do a picnic as it was the best spot that I saw so peaceful, so isolated and kind of remote and that too, it didn't took a lot of time for me to be at this place. So we parked the car by the side of the road and now it was a bit of hiking time. So we just decided to go a bit closer to and explore the place and enjoy the moments in the afternoon.

# The Cozy Hut.
![IMG_0424.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSyUfYkte7gTdvFuBkS6Tsb9qTSM4FWBfevDS1wZDq3Z5/IMG_0424.jpeg)

But as per the time the shepherds around place have been very rare to see as they have travelled to a high altitude place so that they Are a bit away from the city life as they usually prefer to live in the peaceful areas and gaze their Sheeps in the summer time it literally was so peaceful and I just decided how beautiful it would be that I could plan a trip along the shepherds later in the summer time and also shared the moments with you guys through this post and that was the thought that just came out of nowhere when I saw this beautiful shepherds hut that was built in a circular form and looked so beautiful and so peaceful. 

![IMG_0426.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSxnpFdFAeVVDGwtqAKXgobyp91zha7xni3DfmraPjGTq/IMG_0426.jpeg)

![IMG_0427.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbvDymtaji3sCbN3WtJyLKXR1Cgex3suKNMA2rM8X4KaA/IMG_0427.jpeg)

Like this I nearly spent around three hours, just wondering around the place my friends just doing nothing but relaxing and seeing these beautiful clouds forming up in the sky, the sky as blue as the ocean and the clouds as white as snow and just me relaxing in the middle of this beautiful location and spending time in nature and also feeling myself as a part of nature, that every thing felt so peaceful and sore still that I could still remember each and every thing and every moment around the place that would be hard for me to express so that you guys can also feel by the beauty of the place...*

in local Pahadi Language.

title.body: Moin!\n\nHeute möchte ich Euch das aktuelle YouTube-Video von [Robyn Adele Anderson](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCam8VtqRmUKCD-HWZgHtMEg) ans Herz legen. Die Sängerin aus New York hat nämlich auf ihrem Kanal ein traditionelles New-Orleans-Jazz-Cover des Songs __*\

*__ hochgeladen:

https://youtu.be/XU7N9-soWDo?si=Elmy3vaWN_TTACLA

Das Original wurde 1987 von [George Michael](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Michael) produziert. Die bisher bekannteste Cover-Version wurde 1997 auf dem Debütalbum der US-amerikanischen Nu-Metal-Band [Limp Bizkit](https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limp_Bizkit) veröffentlicht. Auch schon wieder mehr als 13 Jahre al ist die Akustik-Version des norwegischen Metal-Spezialisten [Leo Moracchioli](https://www.youtube.com/@leolego):


https://youtu.be/rn-GvPYc3GU?si=-yuJ5ghIUsmqz5W1

Im Juli 2017 präsentierte die Funk-Band [Scary Pockets](https://www.youtube.com/@ScaryPockets/featured) aus Los Angeles ihre Cover-Version:

https://youtu.be/2JI7lX7p-YE?si=jwm6Qj8C6QOwFS3Y

In diesem Sinne wünsche ich Euch einen entspannten Feiertag - egal ob ihr nun Vatertag, Himmelfahrt oder was auch immer feiert.

title.title: The three turtles =/= Die drei Schildkröten 👹🍣🎎 Wonderful Japan ENG-GER
title.body:
![IMG_6803-12.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23yd1r1kNYAyLyBmbdvVQmY5DEMDGnuMvMv96Hrgye4TxYdweSxekMbzTjYKHaBtcmFi6.jpg) Even though the cherry blossoms have now faded, their magic still captivates me. It was simply too beautiful to return to everyday life right away and forget what I had seen and experienced. And on top of that, all of a sudden, so many memories of past cherry blossom seasons come flooding back, and images resurface in my mind that really should have a permanent place there. But it’s not just the cherry blossoms that thrive on their fleeting nature; our memories aren’t immune to it either. And that’s exactly why we should all take a moment to look back every now and then and bring some of these wonderful memories back into the light. I’m doing just that today and have brought along two photos I took a few years ago during this very same glorious season. And to go with them, there’s a little haiku that seems to capture the mood of that day quite well. And that’s all I need today—right now, I’m simply content and cheerful. And I hope I can hold onto this feeling for a while...
__Cherry blossoms drift__
__three turtles bask quietly__
__spring breathes soft and slow.__
![IMG_6789-13.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23wgKcjnFdASk3ckhbYvx3M3qJMRDawGqhn4DzQzVmhLneS5S5kdAhYnHnFRRBCboRxHz.jpg) DEUTSCH Auch wenn die Kirschblüte jetzt weitergezogen hat, beschäftigt mich ihr Zauber doch immer noch. Es war ja auch einfach wieder mal zu schön gewesen, um sofort wieder zum Alltag zurückzukehren und das Gesehene und Erlebte zu vergessen. Und zusätzlich kommen dann auf einmal auch noch ganz viele Erinnerungen an vergangene Kirschblütenzeiten hoch, und Bilder kommen isn Gedächtnis zurück, die dort doch eigentlich einen festen Platz haben sollten. Aber nicht nur die Kirschblüte lebt von ihrer Flüchtigkeit, auch unsere Erinnerungen sind dessen nicht gefeiht. Und eben deshalb sollten wir alle immer mal wieder zurückdenken und ein paar dieser so wundervollen Erinnerungen zurück ans Tageslicht holen. Ich mache dies heute auch und habe uns zwei Bilder mitgebracht, die ich vor ein paar Jahren zu eben dieser so herrlichen Jahreszeit gemacht habe. Und dazu gibt es ein kleines Haiku, was die Stimmung jenen Tages ganz gut einzufangen scheint. Und mehr braucht es dann heute auch nicht, ich bin im Augenblick einfach nur zufrieden und freue mich. Und hoffe, dass ich dieses Gefühl für eine Weile in mir bewahren kann...
__Kirschblüten schweben__
__drei Schildkröten ruhen still__
__Frühling atmet sanft.__
![blog-ende.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxinpower/23tv6H18WKn98nBVkn2MwVhwWsuFRFgjBGwxLEMVhRZD7zRRbFokaNiAn39fUaB3TxVX6.png)

title.title: The views and atmosphere during this year's rainy season, Chiang Mai, Thailand.
title.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVyZwYWgT9AYSLxvNYHtRfFRKqgkcvR9iFkznjZLNso1h/1778658752218.jpg)

Hello everyone. How are you today? I hope all is well with you and your family. I think my country has officially entered the rainy season. Many provinces in Thailand have experienced continuous rain for several days. Especially in my district, it has been raining continuously for a week. So many areas in my district are turning green areas, it's looking incredibly refreshing wherever I look. Now I’d like to take my wife and granddaughter to see and enjoy the scenic rainy season view during my free time, Before my granddaughter's school term starts. And I want to share these rainy season views with everyone this post. So I drove them along the rural roads. This time I will took my wife and granddaughter to our district and another nearby district. We passed through local Thai villages and local farms outside the community area in the countryside. These are some photos of the views we experienced. And I’ve selected some photos of my favorites. Let's enjoy the rainy season views.

Toobit, the award-winning global cryptocurrency exchange, today announces an expansion of its [TradFi offerings](https://www.toobit.com/en-US/tradfi). The exchange is adding 13 new high-demand trading pairs, including Qualcomm (QCOM), IonQ (IONQ), and Oklo (OKLO), to its existing catalog of tokenized traditional assets, bringing the total to 90 pairs.

To mark the rollout, Toobit is launching a new campaign with a 150,000 USDT reward pool. Running from May 12 to May 22, 2026, traders can engage in three activities:

- Activity 1: Participants earn 5 USDT in Trial Funds with 10,000 USDT in cumulative volume on new listings. Hitting a daily volume of 10,000 USDT sustains a check-in streak for lucky draw entries, where rewards like Trial Funds and token airdrops are guaranteed.
- Activity 2: Traders ranking in the top 100 with at least 30,000 USDT in futures volume share a 50,000 USDT prize pool. Those who do not rank still qualify for participation prizes by meeting futures volume milestones.
- Activity 3: Traders ranking in the top 100 with a minimum volume of 25,000 USDT in spot markets claim shares of a 50,000 USDT token airdrop pool. Participation rewards are also available for non-ranking traders who reach designated spot trading milestones.

To participate, traders must register on the [campaign page](https://www.toobit.com/en-US/activity/c/tradfi-listing1). For rules, eligibility requirements, and the full list of supported pairs, please find more details on the [announcement page](https://www.toobit.com/en-US/announcement/new-tradfi-listings-win-150000-usdt-with-aaoi-cohr-be-and-more).

Since its debut, Toobit's Stock Futures has allowed traders to gain exposure to global giants such as Tesla (TSLA), NVIDIA (NVDA), and Apple (AAPL), alongside precious metals and forex. With 90 trading pairs now available in this category, Toobit provides 24/7 liquidity and up to 500x leverage on assets that traditionally operate within restricted market hours.

The expansion comes as the Real-World Asset (RWA) sector sees rapid growth. The total value of tokenized assets on public blockchains grew to $29 billion in April 2026, a 263% increase year-over-year.

Tokenized equities have crossed the $1 billion mark this quarter as institutional demand for blockchain-based settlement infrastructure continues to scale globally.

title.title: Cuadernos de Isabel #14 La ciudad también está cansada. [Esp/Eng]
title.body:
## 📖 Cuadernos de Isabel #14  
### *La ciudad también está cansada*  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcFpFoQxjB4kmgJRa5WDyAGJc5J9nRTVCDfc2oCMbc4TR/nicolas_debray_india_4869731_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/india-woman-look-bus-person-4869731/)

---

Hola querida comunidad @holos-lotus,  

Salí del hospital después de una guardia larga.  

De esas en las que el tiempo deja de sentirse normal. Donde las horas no se cuentan por el reloj, sino por pacientes, por síntomas, por nombres que se mezclan al final del día en algún rincón de la memoria.  

Había visto de todo un poco.  

Cansancio acumulado.  
Estrés convertido en presión alta.  
Insomnio disfrazado de rutina.  
Personas jóvenes con el cuerpo funcionando como si cargaran décadas encima.  

Cuando crucé la puerta del hospital pensé que, por fin, dejaba atrás todo aquello.  

Pero no fue así.  

---

Mientras caminaba hacia la parada, seguía observando. Supongo que una termina acostumbrándose a mirar incluso cuando ya no está trabajando.  

La cola era larga.  

Personas calladas.  
Otras hablando demasiado rápido.  
Algunas con la vista perdida.  
Otras mirando constantemente el reloj como si pudieran obligar al tiempo a avanzar más deprisa.  

Y entonces lo noté.  

---

Los mismos síntomas.  

---

No exactamente iguales, claro. Nadie allí hablaba de diagnósticos ni llevaba resultados médicos en la mano. Pero estaban.  

El cansancio.  
La tensión.  
La ansiedad escondida detrás de conversaciones cotidianas.  

La diferencia era que aquellas personas no estaban en consulta.  

Seguían funcionando.  

---

Una mujer sostenía varias bolsas mientras intentaba mantener tranquilo a un niño pequeño. Un hombre mayor respiraba lento, con esa expresión de quien ha aprendido a soportar el agotamiento sin mencionarlo demasiado. Más atrás, un muchacho no dejaba de mover la pierna con una inquietud que parecía venir de mucho más adentro que la simple espera de un transporte.  

Y pensé algo que me acompañó el resto del camino:  

a veces la ciudad entera parece vivir con síntomas que nadie atiende.  

---

Al poco rato llegó un riquimbili.  

Esos inventos nacidos del ingenio y la necesidad, ensamblados como si el país entero hubiera aprendido a sobrevivir armando soluciones con lo que aparece.  

Subimos ocho personas en aquel cajón metálico improvisado.  

El espacio era pequeño. El calor se acumulaba. El ruido del motor apenas dejaba espacio para hablar.  

Y, aun así, todos parecían acostumbrados.  

---

Miré los rostros a mi alrededor.  

Una mujer apoyaba la cabeza contra la pared metálica con los ojos cerrados, como si cualquier minuto de silencio pudiera servirle de descanso. Un hombre revisaba su teléfono una y otra vez sin realmente mirar la pantalla. Otro pasajero llevaba la mirada fija hacia adelante, perdida en algún pensamiento imposible de adivinar.  

De pronto me di cuenta de algo inquietante.  

Muchas de las expresiones que había visto horas antes en el hospital estaban allí también, dentro de aquel transporte improvisado atravesando la ciudad.  

---

La diferencia era el contexto.  

En el hospital, esos síntomas tenían nombre.  
En la calle, se volvían costumbre.  

---

Quizás por eso tantas personas tardan en buscar ayuda. Porque hay agotamientos que terminan pareciendo normales cuando se viven todos los días.  

El cuerpo se adapta.  
La mente también.  

Hasta que un día algo ya no puede sostenerse igual.  

---

Mientras el riquimbili avanzaba entre calles llenas de ruido y movimiento, pensé en lo extraña que es la resistencia humana.  

La gente sigue.  

Aunque duerma poco.  
Aunque viva preocupada.  
Aunque lleve demasiado tiempo cargando más de lo que debería.  

---

A veces pienso que el hospital no concentra el sufrimiento.  

Solo lo vuelve visible.  

---

Cuando llegué a casa, Bruno seguía acostado sobre el sofá y Max levantó la cabeza apenas escuchó la puerta.  

Me senté unos segundos antes de quitarme los zapatos.  

Y por primera vez en el día, dejé de observar.  

---

Porque hay momentos en que mirar demasiado también pesa.  

---

Gracias por acompañarme en este decimocuarto trazo de mis Cuadernos de Isabel. Nos seguimos encontrando en los pequeños detalles, en los silencios cotidianos y en esas señales invisibles que muchas veces hablan más de una ciudad que cualquier estadística.  

Las imágenes son de Pixabay y la traducción al inglés fue realizada con DeepL Translate.  

---

🇺🇸 **ENGLISH VERSION**  

---

## 📖 Isabel’s Notebooks #14  
### *The City Is Tired Too*  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmcFpFoQxjB4kmgJRa5WDyAGJc5J9nRTVCDfc2oCMbc4TR/nicolas_debray_india_4869731_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/india-woman-look-bus-person-4869731/)

---

Hello dear @holos-lotus community,  

I left the hospital after a long shift.  

One of those shifts where time stops feeling normal. Where hours are not measured by the clock, but by patients, symptoms, and names that eventually blend together somewhere in memory.  

I had seen a little bit of everything.  

Accumulated exhaustion.  
Stress transformed into high blood pressure.  
Insomnia disguised as routine.  
Young people whose bodies already seemed to carry decades of weight.  

When I crossed the hospital doors, I thought I was finally leaving all of that behind.  

But I wasn’t.  

---

As I walked toward the bus stop, I kept observing. I suppose one eventually gets used to looking, even when no longer working.  

The line was long.  

Quiet people.  
Others speaking too fast.  
Some staring into nothing.  
Others checking the time constantly, as if they could force the day to move faster.  

And then I noticed it.  

---

The same symptoms.  

---

Not exactly the same, of course. No one there was talking about diagnoses or carrying medical results in their hands. But they were there.  

The exhaustion.  
The tension.  
The anxiety hidden behind ordinary conversations.  

The difference was that these people were not in consultation.  

They were still functioning.  

---

A woman carried several bags while trying to calm a small child. An older man breathed slowly with the expression of someone who had learned to endure fatigue without mentioning it too much. A young man farther back kept moving his leg restlessly, as if the unease came from somewhere much deeper than simply waiting for transportation.  

And I thought something that stayed with me for the rest of the trip:  

sometimes the whole city seems to live with symptoms no one treats.  

---

After a while, a riquimbili arrived.  

Those improvised vehicles born from necessity and Cuban ingenuity, assembled as if the entire country had learned to survive by building solutions out of whatever appears.  

Eight of us climbed into that improvised metal box.  

The space was small. The heat gathered quickly. The sound of the engine left little room for conversation.  

And still, everyone seemed used to it.  

---

I looked at the faces around me.  

One woman rested her head against the metal wall with her eyes closed, as if even a minute of silence could serve as rest. A man checked his phone over and over without truly looking at the screen. Another passenger stared ahead, lost in thoughts impossible to guess.  

Suddenly, I realized something unsettling.  

Many of the same expressions I had seen earlier in the hospital were also there inside that improvised transport moving through the city.  

---

The difference was the context.  

In the hospital, those symptoms had names.  
On the street, they became routine.  

---

Perhaps that is why so many people delay seeking help. Because some forms of exhaustion begin to feel normal when lived every day.  

The body adapts.  
The mind does too.  

Until one day, something can no longer hold itself together the same way.  

---

As the riquimbili moved through noisy streets full of movement, I thought about how strange human resistance truly is.  

People continue.  

Even when they barely sleep.  
Even when they live worried.  
Even when they carry far more than they should for far too long.  

---

Sometimes I think the hospital does not contain suffering.  

It simply makes it visible.  

---

When I arrived home, Bruno was still lying on the sofa and Max lifted his head as soon as he heard the door.  

I sat down for a few seconds before taking off my shoes.  

And for the first time that day, I stopped observing.  

---

Because there are moments when looking too closely also becomes heavy.  

---

Thank you for accompanying me in this fourteenth entry of Isabel’s Notebooks. We continue meeting in the small details, in everyday silences, and in those invisible signs that often say more about a city than any statistic ever could.  

The images are from Pixabay and the English translation was done with DeepL Translate.

---

title.body:
Ich glaube, genau darin liegt die Schwierigkeit:
Man würde seinem jüngeren Ich vermutlich vieles erklären wollen — aber ob man wirklich darauf gehört hätte, ist eine ganz andere Frage. 

Gerade in den Momenten, in denen man einsam, unsicher oder auf der Suche nach Halt ist, wirken manche Menschen oder Chancen stärker als jede Warnung. Vielleicht sogar stärker als die eigene Vernunft. Manche Erfahrungen muss man leider selbst machen, bevor man sie wirklich versteht.

Und trotzdem fand ich den Gedanken spannend, ob man bestimmte Dinge verhindern würde, wenn man könnte. Verrat, toxische Beziehungen oder Entscheidungen, die einen tief geprägt haben. Wahrscheinlich würden viele spontan „Ja“ sagen.

Aber je länger ich darüber nachdenke, desto mehr frage ich mich etwas anderes:
Wäre ich ohne manche falschen Wege überhaupt derselbe Mensch geworden?

Nicht jeder Schmerz macht stärker und manches hätte niemand gebraucht. Aber einige Erfahrungen verändern den Blick auf Menschen, Freiheit, Ruhe oder das eigene Leben so grundlegend, dass man sie später kaum noch sauber aus der eigenen Geschichte herauslösen kann.

Vielleicht liegt Frieden mit der Vergangenheit nicht darin, alles gutzufinden. Sondern irgendwann aufzuhören, ständig mit ihr verhandeln zu wollen. Und vielleicht ist genau deshalb die Gegenwart das Wertvollste daran: Der einzige Ort, an dem wir tatsächlich noch etwas verändern können.

title.title: Hope's Beach, South Arm, Tassie 🌊
title.body:
It’s quite disorientating, or perhaps weirdly orientating, being in Tasmania.

If you open Google Maps, that little blue dot puts you as close to Antarctica as you’re ever likely to get unless you’ve got a heap of money for a tour down there, which, admittedly, would be pretty incredible. Anyone wanna lend me $20K Australian? If you come from the south of Australia, chances are you've looked out to see a *lot* and imagined that almost mythical icy land mass. You might have even known people to work out there. Admired the Sea Shephard fighting Japanese whalers in its surrounding waters. 


I do love this cold southern ocean. There’s a feeling of standing at the edge of things, like the world just runs out if you keep going south. But it’s not just empty. There’s movement out there too, animals and people, waves, wind, saltstreams. 


![2383.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23sdbK8wsgGMp87pYw4HJf4ChGm8TSdmbzb1nkmSYPDePv4MEwZqBoGYmZb1DXRG1tpeG.jpg)


Every so often, ships pass through - icebreakers and research vessels making their way back from Antarctica toward Hobart. You can stand on a quiet beach and watch something that’s just come from the bottom of the world, cutting a slow line across the horizon. There's sailboats too, breezing along, seals, dolphins, seabirds, clouds. The low Autumnal sun. 


![2390.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23zRvavNUuKQWK6w8Ehx1BujW9eC9Yrnyxo5gMwDmNZ6eitkienNCpZ1s9pSenuxiDqve.jpg)


Even so, there are more mainlanders here now, and plenty of people moving from the bigger part of Australia chasing something quieter, wilder, more beautiful. A place that still feels like it has space in it, wildness, freedom. People used to leave Tassie to get jobs and go to uni on the mainland and never make it back - now it seems people flock there or return to their roots. There's hikers and explorers and climbers and surfers, people drifting, sailing, fighting for the environment. It feels like a last frontier.

Every time I come here, I end up back in that same feeling: just looking out at the sea and thinking about how far away everything else is. How it'd be easy to be cut off from the mainland if a disaster stopped the planes and boats coming. There's understandable a lot of climate fiction set in Tassie.

Here, we're on Hope’s Beach, on the South Arm, Nipaluna (another word for Hobart), is one of those places you wouldn’t find unless you knew it was there. A dirt track leads you down to a wide stretch of sand that feels tucked away from everything - no asphalted carpark or paid for parking. There’s often surf here, usually big, messy waves even when it’s onshore and a bit chaotic. Not like the calmer beaches on the other side of the bay I’ve written about before - and it's a place local surfers will flock to even if it's tiny, particularly when it's clean and offshore like this weekend. 


![2442.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/EqL6L4zmn1QAJNbvN7KDwjNLTWoKTAsZHc4b25e83cFQVii6XE3d5kRrq3D6LpB355r.jpg)



When I go there, it’s usually to watch Tam surf. She’s a strong surfer, much fitter than me, and tends to take on bigger waves without hesitation - her Dad was a big wave surfer. On this particular day though, there’s barely any swell at all. So we just take the dog for a walk and end up swimming in the freezing water anyway. 

It’s icy, a whole 3 degrees colder than home, which makes a difference. Still, it’s refreshing. It knocks the edge off everything, like washing out the red wine from the night before. I tend to just experience cold as a sensation these days not a warning to squeal and get the fuck out. I'm safe, there, held for a moment. 

Tam does end up paddling out into the tiny waves regardless, chasing whatever little ocean fix she can get. I sit on the sand watching, the sun low in the sky all day, warm but with that persistent Tasmanian chill underneath it. The light starts getting afternoony golden way earlier than home - by 3, it feels like it's getting dark. 

The beach is littered with shellsp - pipis, mussels, oyster shells - washed in from the harbour and the bay. We don't know how safe they are to eat, though the air is cleaner than anywhere in teh world.


![2447.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/23xybJWqjJv81evNqhnhYvde9cHSSfEbR1dFNn2S8PvXrNzAqMbsrSWTrLH62qQSyZj3h.jpg)

Looking out to sea, Betsy Island sits low on the horizon, just another marker in a chain of land and water that’s always been about passage, but seems like a cool place to have a shack, if you wanted an island off an island off an island and to be totally isolated. I wonder if it is 'owned'.

We bring the dog down because of his separation anxiety. He’s a sweetheart, mostly, but spends a lot of time staring out at the water waiting for Tam to come back in, and barely tolerates me. Though he does eventually decide I’m useful enough to carry him up the sanddune because he does have very short legs and he is very, very old.


![b384e77d-7665-4142-bdf7-633989d2a67d-1_all_26838.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/riverflows/Eqd7zuopbaETYnHBEVF56Vza22vcVJuqwHTY4L9w6ocwef8SL2V1ueaJzL4nzezePbm.jpg)


On the walk back, black cockatoos move through the pines, breaking open cones. There's more than I've ever seen in one place before - some forty of them, making a noise and chucking pine cones. 

I love Tassie, so much.

![afEthm38vuTUektq_image_1778652579473.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/carolin77/images/afEthm38vuTUektq_image_1778652579473/afEthm38vuTUektq_image_1778652579473.webp)
![7xI4VSiy4QCBuAqL_image_1778652577408.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/carolin77/images/7xI4VSiy4QCBuAqL_image_1778652577408/7xI4VSiy4QCBuAqL_image_1778652577408.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

落英缤纷的五月，五颜六色的五月，只一眼便爱上了这个季节。这是我妈家门口自己种的，我爸是种花高手，平时看我家里不缺鲜切花，爱养花的习惯也算是源于我爸吧。

这个门前的小花园被我爸打理的仅仅有条，过了冬季，迎来了花开时刻，每年的春天到夏天，我爸的小院花开就没断过，各品种的花，接连绽放，也是非常热爱生活的小老头一枚呀。

以前我在家里也养过带根的花，可惜啊，没遗传到这天赋，养啥啥死，连仙人掌都能被我养死了，至此我的花架就空置了，有时候晒晒鞋什么的，真没法养。

一开始养嘎了我就换新的，只要我更换的勤，就没人能看的出我的花嘎了，之后我也不想自欺欺人了，换鲜切花吧，能留住它们的最美时刻也不是一件坏事，也省的我整天丢嘎了的花。

于是之后我就开始在网上淘花，每1-2周买一次，各种鲜切花，我也学会了很多养护的方法，比根系简单，而且每一次收到鲜花，总有一种莫名的欣喜，是开心的心情。

看这些在五月绽放的花朵，竞相齐放，好不艳丽呀，放上一张小桌，一张躺椅，我能坐一下午，心情陶醉在其中。我爸养的花，连虫都没有，他真的好会呵护这些花了，微风拂过，还有淡淡清香呢。

body.title: Cuando alguien recuerda algo que dije al pasar. Cosas pequeñas que me sostienen #18 por veramfund. [Esp/Eng]
body.body:
## Cosas pequeñas que me sostienen #18  
*Cuando alguien recuerda algo que dije al pasar*

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXCkQciZzDc6Dyfk2wBZAxG5psFEEtTKtoeXhpSV7ASVT/silviarita_girl_3528292_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/girl-woman-read-book-sit-nature-3528292/)

---

Hola comunidad @ladiesofhive nuevamente con ustedes con el decimoctavo capítulo de las **Cosas pequeñas que me Sostienen**.

A veces uno dice algo al pasar… sin imaginar que alguien realmente lo escucha.

Recuerdo una conversación entre varios amigos y compañeros de estudio. Éramos muchos, hablando de temas distintos, saltando de una cosa a otra como suele pasar en esos grupos grandes.

En algún momento, alguien mencionó libros de Gabriel García Márquez y la conversación terminó girando alrededor de *Cien años de soledad*.

Yo comenté, un poco apenada, que nunca había podido leerlo.

No porque no quisiera.

Sino porque lo había buscado varias veces y nunca logré encontrarlo.

Lo dije casi sin pensar.

La conversación siguió su curso y aquello quedó atrás. De hecho, estoy segura de que para la mayoría pasó completamente desapercibido.

Incluso para mí.

Por eso me sorprendió tanto lo que ocurrió días después.

Coincidimos en un evento en la universidad y uno de aquellos amigos se acercó directamente hacia mí con un libro en la mano.

Era *Cien años de soledad*.

Sonrió y me dijo algo que todavía recuerdo:

“Alguien que quiere leer este libro no puede quedarse sin hacerlo solo por no encontrarlo. Toma, es tuyo”.

Y me lo regaló.

Recuerdo quedarme sin saber qué decir.

No por el libro solamente.

Sino porque me impresionó que alguien hubiera recordado aquel comentario tan pequeño, dicho casi de casualidad entre tantas voces y tantas conversaciones.

Fue uno de esos momentos que parecen simples… pero se quedan.

Porque a veces no es el regalo en sí lo que emociona.

Es sentir que alguien realmente prestó atención.

Y en un mundo donde tantas cosas se dicen rápido y se olvidan igual de rápido, eso tiene un valor enorme.

Desde entonces, cada vez que pienso en ese momento, recuerdo que hay personas capaces de escuchar incluso lo que uno cree que nadie notó.

Y eso, aunque parezca pequeño…

también me sostiene.

---

 *Esto es Vera, aprendiendo a sostenerse en lo simple.*

Las imágenes son de Pixabay.  
La versión en inglés fue hecha utilizando Google Translate.

- - - 
# *English Version*
- - - 

**Small Things That Sustain Me #18**  
*When Someone Remembers Something I Said in Passing*

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXCkQciZzDc6Dyfk2wBZAxG5psFEEtTKtoeXhpSV7ASVT/silviarita_girl_3528292_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/girl-woman-read-book-sit-nature-3528292/)

---

Hello @ladiesofhive community, once again with you with the eighteenth chapter of **Small Things That Sustain Me**.

Sometimes we say something casually… without imagining that someone is truly listening.

I remember a conversation among several friends and classmates. There were many of us, talking about different things, jumping from one topic to another like large groups often do.

At some point, someone mentioned books by Gabriel García Márquez, and the conversation eventually turned to *One Hundred Years of Solitude*.

I commented, a little shyly, that I had never been able to read it.

Not because I didn’t want to.

But because I had looked for it several times and never managed to find it.

I said it almost without thinking.

The conversation moved on and that moment was left behind. In fact, I’m sure it went completely unnoticed for most people.

Even for me.

That’s why what happened a few days later surprised me so much.

We met again at a university event, and one of those friends walked directly toward me carrying a book in his hand.

It was *One Hundred Years of Solitude*.

He smiled and said something I still remember:

“Someone who wants to read this book shouldn’t miss the chance just because they couldn’t find it. Here, it’s yours.”

And he gave it to me.

I remember not knowing what to say.

Not only because of the book itself.

But because it amazed me that someone had remembered such a small comment, said almost casually among so many voices and conversations.

It was one of those moments that seem simple… but stay with you.

Because sometimes it’s not the gift itself that moves you.

It’s realizing that someone truly paid attention.

And in a world where so many things are said quickly and forgotten just as quickly, that means a lot.

Since then, every time I think about that moment, I remember that there are people capable of listening even to the things we think no one noticed.

And that, even if it seems small…

also sustains me.

---

 *This is Vera, learning to sustain herself in the simple things.*

The images are from Pixabay.  
The English version was made using Google Translate.

Thanks Igor, this means a lot - and your point on outgrowing the DHF is one we think about constantly.

A few things already in motion in exactly that direction: we're building hive-x402 (an x402 payment facilitator on Hive) which positions HBD as a settlement layer for AI agent micropayments - zero fees, 3-second finality, and an active revenue surface that doesn't depend on DHF. The principle we hold firm on: no ads, ever. So the monetization has to come from infrastructure, premium tooling, and AI services that genuinely add value. Fully agree this is the path forward for Hive as a whole, not just Ecency.

The neighbours exclaimed: “What good luck!” Again he said: “Maybe.” Then his son tried to ride one of the wild horses, fell, and broke his leg. The neighbours cried: “What bad luck!” He answered the same. Days later, war broke out and they came to enlist the young man, but with a broken leg he couldn’t go… so then?

ngủ trong những ngày thời tiết nóng bức. Tuy nhiên, trên thị trường hiện nay có
rất nhiều dòng chiếu khác nhau, trong đó phổ biến nhất là chiếu điều hòa 3D và
chiếu điều hòa 5D. Sự khác biệt về cấu tạo, độ êm và khả năng làm mát khiến
nhiều người băn khoăn không biết nên chọn loại nào phù hợp với nhu cầu sử dụng.

Chiếu điều hòa 3D là dòng sản phẩm phổ thông với thiết kế khá đơn giản. Loại
chiếu này thường được cấu tạo từ ba lớp gồm bề mặt làm mát, lớp đệm mỏng và lớp
chống trượt bên dưới. Nhờ thiết kế gọn nhẹ nên chiếu dễ dàng gấp gọn, vệ sinh
và di chuyển khi cần thiết. Đây là ưu điểm lớn giúp chiếu điều hòa 3D trở thành
lựa chọn phù hợp với học sinh, sinh viên hoặc người ở trọ.

Một trong những điểm nổi bật của chiếu điều hòa 3D là mức giá khá rẻ, phù
hợp với người có ngân sách hạn chế hoặc chỉ cần giải pháp làm mát cơ bản trong
mùa hè. Ngoài ra, sản phẩm có trọng lượng nhẹ nên rất thuận tiện trong quá
trình sử dụng hằng ngày. Tuy nhiên, do lớp đệm khá mỏng nên độ êm ái của chiếu
3D không quá cao. Khi nằm lâu, người dùng có thể cảm thấy chưa thật sự thoải
mái, đặc biệt là những ai yêu thích cảm giác mềm mại khi ngủ. Khả năng làm mát
của dòng sản phẩm này cũng chỉ ở mức vừa phải, chủ yếu tạo cảm giác thông
thoáng thay vì làm mát sâu.

Trong khi đó, chiếu điều hòa 5D được xem là phiên bản cao cấp hơn với cấu
tạo nhiều lớp nhằm nâng cao trải nghiệm sử dụng. Thông thường, sản phẩm sẽ gồm
năm lớp như bề mặt làm mát, lớp thoáng khí, lớp đệm dày, lớp định hình và lớp
chống trượt. Nhờ cấu trúc này, chiếu có độ dày lớn hơn và mang lại cảm giác êm
ái rõ rệt hơn so với chiếu 3D.

Ưu điểm lớn nhất của chiếu điều hòa 5D là khả năng nâng đỡ cơ thể tốt, giúp
người dùng cảm thấy dễ chịu khi nằm lâu. Đây là lựa chọn phù hợp với gia đình
có trẻ nhỏ, người lớn tuổi hoặc những ai ưu tiên chất lượng giấc ngủ. Ngoài ra,
khả năng tản nhiệt của chiếu 5D cũng hiệu quả hơn nhờ thiết kế thoáng khí, giúp
bề mặt luôn mát mẻ ngay cả trong những ngày nắng nóng kéo dài. Độ bền của sản
phẩm cũng cao hơn vì ít bị xẹp lún hay biến dạng sau thời gian dài sử dụng.

Tuy nhiên, chiếu điều hòa 5D thường có giá thành cao hơn đáng kể so với dòng
3D. Bên cạnh đó, trọng lượng nặng hơn cũng khiến việc vệ sinh, di chuyển hoặc
bảo quản trở nên kém linh hoạt hơn.

Việc lựa chọn chiếu điều hòa 3D hay 5D sẽ phụ thuộc vào nhu cầu và ngân sách
của từng người. Nếu bạn cần một sản phẩm giá rẻ, nhẹ và dễ sử dụng thì chiếu
điều hòa 3D là lựa chọn phù hợp. Ngược lại, nếu muốn đầu tư cho giấc ngủ với trải
nghiệm êm ái, thoải mái và sử dụng lâu dài thì chiếu điều hòa 5D sẽ đáng cân
nhắc hơn.

body.title: Chandramallika: The Moon-Crowned Flower of Calm Beauty
body.body:
Chandramallika, often known as a variety of chrysanthemum, carries a name that feels poetic even before the flower is seen. Meaning “garland of the moon,” it reflects a quiet radiance rather than bold brilliance. Its layered petals, usually soft white or pale yellow, unfold with a calm symmetry that brings a sense of peace wherever it blooms.

This flower holds deep cultural and emotional significance, especially in South Asia. Chandramallika is often associated with purity, devotion, and gentle remembrance. It appears in moments of prayer, reflection, and respect, where its serene presence helps create an atmosphere of stillness and sincerity. Unlike fleeting blossoms, it lasts longer, symbolizing enduring faith and steady love.

body.title: Study Smarter in 2026: Top AI Homework Helpers Every Student Should Know
body.body:
AI homework got smarter in 2025. Instead of copying answers from random sites, students are now using AI homework helpers as 24/7 study buddies that actually explain concepts, break down steps, and turn messy notes into exam-ready study guides.​

Why AI Homework Helpers Matter

Modern AI homework tools can solve math, analyze essays, summarize lectures, and even turn PDFs or screenshots into step‑by‑step explanations. Used correctly, they save hours every week while helping students understand the “how” and “why” behind every solution instead of just handing over the final answer.​

Examples of Powerful Tools

Some tools focus on visual problem solving, letting you upload photos or screenshots of homework and get clear, guided solutions in seconds. Others act as full study systems that organize textbooks, lecture recordings, and YouTube videos into notes, flashcards, and smart quizzes so exam prep becomes far less stressful.​

How To Use Them Ethically

The smartest students follow a simple rule: try solving the problem yourself first, then use AI only for the last 30% when you are really stuck. Treat the AI like a tutor by asking it to explain each step, show alternative methods, and relate the answer back to what was covered in class, instead of blindly copying solutions.​

body.title: Wednesday Walk - Health benefits of walking
body.body: Greetings to everyone from another Wednesday Walk! It's great to be back here, supporting my experiences with evidence and visuals. I've been in this community for a long time, and I'll be making a great effort to post regularly here for even longer. _Yeni bir Wednesday Walk gününden herkese selamlar. Yeniden burada olmak, yaşadıklarımı kanıtları ile görsellerle desteklemek, kanıtlamak keyif verici. Uzun zamandır bu topluluktayım , çok daha uzun süreler, düzenli şekilde burada gönderi paylaşmak için büyük çaba sarf edeceğim._

/> We've finally started experiencing spring, albeit a little late. The rains have stopped, and the weather has warmed up considerably. I'm now able to go for walks wherever and whenever I want. I've significantly increased both the pace and the duration of my walks. _İlkbahar mevsimini gecikmeli de olsa yaşamaya başladık. Yağışlar durdu, havalar iyice ısındı. Dilediğim yerde, dilediğim zamanda yürüyüşlerimi yapıyorum. Tempoyu ve yürüyüş yaptığım süreyi büyük ölçüde artırdım._

/> I hadn't been to places with historical houses and buildings for a while. I decided to go there. Historical buildings have a very different beauty in every season. Of course, they look most aesthetically pleasing in winter. In spring, the greenery seen between the houses creates a wonderful visual feast. _Bir süredir tarihi evlerin, yapıların olduğu yerlere gitmiyordum. O taraflara gitmeye karar verdim. Tarihi yapılar her mevsimde çok farklı güzelliğe sahip oluyor. Tabii en çok kış mevsiminde daha estetik gözüküyor. İlkbahar mevsiminde de evlerin aralarında görülen yeşillik harika bir görsel şölen oluşturuyor._

/> The castle stands before me in all its grandeur and magnificence. Looking at the castle takes me on a short journey into the past. I took a longer route just to see this side. I also like how secluded the road is. Not many cars pass by, and there aren't many crowds. A stream flows right next to the castle. I can immediately hear the sound of the stream's murmur. _Kale tüm heybeti, iştihamıyla karşımda duruyor. Kaleye baktığımda geçmişe kısa bir yolculuk yapıyorum. Bu tarafı görmek için yolumu uzattım. Yolun tenha olmasını da seviyorum. Çok fazla araç geçmiyor, çok fazla insan topluluğu yok. Kalenin hemen bitişiğinden dere akıyor. Derenin şırıltısını hemen duyuluyor._

/>

Because there is a very serious parking problem in the city center, cars are parked in such secluded places. Car owners have no other alternative for parking.

_Şehir merkezinde çok ciddi anlamda bir park problemi olduğu için araçlar böyle tenha yerlere park ediliyor. Araç sahiplerinin park edecek başka bir alternatifi yok._

That's what I have to say this week. I sleep 6-7 hours a day. I wake up around 5 am. After about an hour of pet care, I take a cold shower. Then I browse the internet for about an hour. After all that, people start waking up. I'm paying more attention to my diet now. Especially my growing belly is causing me discomfort.

body.title: BLOOMING NATURE
body.body:
Today Wednesday, may 13, 2026
There's thia kind of certain peace that lives quietly beneath trees. Not the loud kind of peace, but the soft and peaceful kind that settles gently into the heart. 

In the compound of my school stands collection of ancient trees, stretching their branches across the open field like guardians watching over generations of students. 
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZxvxs7VHJE337jS1bRfbDrayxviC4ncpss12enhuY3Mb/20260512_124023.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXdYHJF4i7rES3q3Q7bQEe8scvfwG2hfWxHXRv17hwLyj/20260512_124019.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQZH2KsynRU3hPY6ougjSDHzcogQe15twsSA5aw24q5uW/20260512_124016.jpg)
Their dark trunks twist with age and wisdom, while their green leaves dance freely with the wind. At certain moments, tiny reddish-orange blossoms appear among the branches like sparks of fire hidden inside nature’s calmness
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmckNH4eVDC8qvxAEEMcA7FJhsneHBhgYKrEqsZ4WMZHsq/20260512_124032.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaGNb86yhxASy2K6w9hVYFZohr6rWGT59VhkBr8VgDwyP/20260512_124046.jpg)
. Every day, students walk past them without fully realizing how much life these trees silently carry.

These trees are more than ordinary plants  in the soil. They are witnesses. They have watched students welcome nervoued on their first day and leave years later carrying dreams bigger than the school 
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV4SapfZ68E6SvttWs9D3yehzP7hD52wL1vqh59q6P9ni/20260512_123907.jpg)
. They have listened to laughter during break time, heard whispered conversations between friends, lovers and stood quietly through rainy mornings, sunny afternoons, and calm evenings.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUu9wtwT2eBbr7a9D2TF4Mos5rtDwGUwHRLmFhAAaQYmC/20260512_124050_001.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmaq6ntxCrGRcPbxpCRQoAPX5w4CiLd5CBDGLiBPHGfBoN/20260512_124107.jpg)
 buildings may crack and paint may fade, these trees remain standing with unmatched dignity.
Whenever the sun shines through the branches, the entire environment changes. The grass glows brighter, the air feels cooler, and the whole school suddenly breathes with life. Sometimes the wind moves so gently through the leaves that it sounds almost like a conversation between nature and the earth itself. Looking at the trees from afar feels like staring into a painting created by time and patience.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmfHXmfj8jwwFWhCBGQkVYQTtrd3rc8vbNwuJJ2b66S62K/20260512_123828.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV4SapfZ68E6SvttWs9D3yehzP7hD52wL1vqh59q6P9ni/20260512_123907.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZ95BUTFbCurz17UfzJMU6arQosiFypWV2QgTjfxd49pu/20260512_123814.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXM9x1UFmKBquZGMWHJUkbDdyTYzHy72LDYP2yrTcvkPT/20260512_124001.jpg)

I remember one afternoon like that after classes had ended. Most students had already gone home, and the school compound became unusually quiet. I sat under one of the largest trees with my notebook on my knees. I had been troubled about many things test, exams, expectations, presentation.The world felt too fast, and my mind was heavy. As I sat there, an elderly cleaner slowly approached with a broom in his hand. He noticed me sitting silently.
“You like this tree?” he asked.

I nodded.

He moved closer towrds me  and said softly, “This tree was already big when I started working here many years ago. Many students sat under it just like you. Some cried here. Some studied here. Some fell in love here. Today many of them are somewhere in the world. But the tree is still here.”

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSLjfnY3gm9k8G1TDPbcL8nAoYts5zWuisWvWbwJNWxhb/20260512_124159.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRmBW6pamTqECgJD2Y8uHC8rKjj826GdDmgvGCKegJDCX/20260512_124241.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeA73f1gF2bRnMZUyWaKpFGMMXV2HLRWCPNkeYUeccpJH/20260512_124139.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmf4yhft6cVxxfTu8RHVUk8jWtMP8Gs3NE3sAnxaTXfgiM/20260512_124148.jpg)

The tree suddenly felt alive in a different way — . The old man continued sweeping slowly while humming a quiet song, and I remained there thinking  about life. Somehow, beneath that shade, my worries became lighter.
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSyZGx6v5vD4T9q1VdbU24LLUvSXSNEB7BM1gvgrw5hvn/20260512_124116.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme72zQUFxiMKVoUJTxXbeMo6rvmHUHkZmkb9kUVfNgs3p/20260512_124133.jpg)

Nature has a strange way of healing people without speaking a single word. Trees do not lecture us, yet they teach patience. They stand through storms without giving up.

The beauty of the trees in my school bring students together. Friends gather beneath them to share food and jokes. Some students read books beneath it. Others simply sit quietly, enjoying the breeze after stressful lectures.Without them, the school would feel incomplete.

What makes nature truly special is its ability to remain humble while offering so much. These trees ask for nothing, yet they give shade, beauty, fresh air, and comfort freely to everyone. In a world where people are often too busy chasing success and, nature reminds us to slow down and breathe. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYN3Y5yKoVNG7URWcv8RL76kpqBGuLL2LNyMdEUhCbQ9j/20260512_125538.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYYZU78KiC9wgEHcR3KYkrG1HSV2vbdwGZdtVK7SLUZnr/20260512_125530.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQykx3yZVc15DyaB3ez8DZ1nLaYnHjTCSTXw9DZzZoCHs/20260512_125523.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS28u2Text4M9ux9j1tAWmPCvacLcUprWUZ9FSFkugL7u/20260512_124234.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZKQCKeryykwx2Ezx5LMkSLLmedEprtFAki4jG3zs4TcR/20260512_124223.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNrSja5WwRUqkXTqC9o2h4NDdEjNCcUaXPKHy7ytFuKZs/20260512_124155.jpg)

I just hope you guys love my little journey around my achool vicinity and also thank you for the love and support guys ❤️🥺

# Crónicas de lo Absurdo #18  
## Los Postes  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX8fLAGzAyYWHXH3xGdfUcRM7rXm5e8YJh1qzqqiYmLJk/joanjocastello_bridge_6314795_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/bridge-lights-car-vehicle-road-6314795/)

---

Hola querida comunidad @holos-lotus, regreso una vez más para compartir una nueva entrega de esta serie:

#### Crónicas de lo Absurdo.

> Esta es una serie de crónicas sobre lo cotidiano, sobre esas escenas que se repiten tanto que dejan de parecernos extrañas. Aquí no hay exageración ni ficción forzada. El absurdo no se inventa, se observa. Son textos nacidos de la experiencia diaria, de la espera, de las normas sin sentido, de los gestos que todos conocemos y que casi nunca cuestionamos. No pretenden dar respuestas, solo detenerse un momento y mirar con atención eso que hemos aprendido a aceptar.

En esta la decimoctava edición el tema es:

#### Los postes.

---

Hay lugares que uno recuerda no por lo que cambian, sino por lo que resisten.

Durante años viví frente al mar, en un edificio construido a finales del siglo pasado. No era una obra llamativa ni moderna en su diseño, pero cumplía su función. Con el tiempo entendí algo que no siempre es evidente: no todo lo antiguo es sinónimo de deterioro, ni todo lo nuevo es garantía de mejora.

El edificio sigue ahí.

Y algo más interesante aún: los postes de alumbrado exterior originales también siguen ahí.

Intactos.

Mientras tanto, la carretera que pasa frente al edificio, con destino a zonas turísticas muy conocidas, ha tenido múltiples intervenciones a lo largo de los últimos años. Primero una reparación general. Luego modificaciones. Después ajustes. Y más tarde, nuevas correcciones sobre lo ya corregido.

Cada etapa parecía tener sentido por separado.

El resultado final, sin embargo, no siempre cuenta la misma historia.

Primero se asfaltó el tramo completo y se construyó un separador central. Todo parecía ordenado, como parte de un plan coherente. Pero poco después, ese mismo separador fue intervenido nuevamente para incluir jardineras con plantas ornamentales.

Más tarde, alguien recordó que hacía falta iluminación.

Entonces se rompieron las jardineras para instalar cableado y colocar nuevos postes de alumbrado.

Y ahí comenzó una nueva etapa dentro del mismo proceso.

Los postes instalados eran modernos, visualmente atractivos, con una apariencia que intentaba armonizar con el entorno. Pero había un detalle que no tardó en aparecer: el ambiente marino no perdona ciertos materiales.

Con el tiempo, comenzaron a deteriorarse. La corrosión avanzó rápido. Algunos se inclinaron. Otros cedieron. Y finalmente, ya no quedó ninguno en pie.

Todos terminaron colapsando.

Mientras tanto, los postes originales del edificio, expuestos al mismo entorno durante décadas, seguían allí.

Firmes.

Entonces apareció una nueva solución.

Otra vez.

Se anunció la instalación de nuevos postes, esta vez con materiales diferentes, posiblemente más resistentes. Una nueva etapa de corrección sobre lo ya corregido.

Y uno no puede evitar preguntarse cómo es posible que un mismo espacio haya pasado por tantas transformaciones sin llegar a una estabilidad clara.

Porque no se trata solo de construir.

Se trata de mantener una coherencia en lo que se construye.

A veces, el problema no es la falta de intervención, sino la acumulación de intervenciones que no terminan de alinearse entre sí.

Y en ese proceso, lo que debía mejorar un espacio termina generando una especie de ciclo en el que cada solución parece necesitar otra solución posterior.

> Lo que se construye para mejorar, a veces termina explicando por qué lo anterior funcionaba mejor.

El absurdo no está en reparar.

Está en reparar sin conservar el equilibrio de lo que ya existía.

---

# Chronicles of the Absurd #18  
## The Poles  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmX8fLAGzAyYWHXH3xGdfUcRM7rXm5e8YJh1qzqqiYmLJk/joanjocastello_bridge_6314795_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/bridge-lights-car-vehicle-road-6314795/)

---

Hello dear @holos-lotus community, I come once again to share a new entry in this series:

#### Chronicles of the Absurd.

> This is a series of chronicles about everyday life, about those scenes that repeat themselves so often that they stop seeming strange to us. Here there is no exaggeration or forced fiction. The absurd is not invented, it is observed. These are texts born from daily experience, from waiting, from meaningless rules, from gestures we all know and almost never question. They do not seek to give answers, only to stop for a moment and look carefully at what we have learned to accept.

In this eighteenth edition the theme is:

#### The poles.

---

There are places you remember not for how they change, but for how they endure.

For many years I lived in front of the sea, in a building constructed at the end of the last century. It was not a particularly modern or striking design, but it worked. Over time, I understood something that is not always obvious: not everything old means deterioration, and not everything new guarantees improvement.

The building is still there.

And something else is still there as well: the original outdoor light poles.

Intact.

Meanwhile, the road in front of the building, leading toward well-known tourist areas, has undergone several interventions over the years. First a general repair. Then modifications. Later adjustments. And afterwards, new corrections over what had already been corrected.

Each stage seemed logical on its own.

But the final result does not always tell the same story.

At first, the entire section was paved and a central divider was built. Everything looked organized, part of a coherent plan. But later, that same divider was modified again to include landscaped areas with ornamental plants.

Then, at some point, lighting was needed.

So the landscaped areas were broken again to install wiring and place new light poles.

And that marked the beginning of another stage in the same process.

The new poles were modern, visually appealing, designed to match the surroundings. But there was one detail that quickly became evident: the marine environment does not forgive certain materials.

Over time, they began to deteriorate. Corrosion advanced quickly. Some bent. Others collapsed. Eventually, none of them remained standing.

All of them failed.

Meanwhile, the original poles of the building, exposed to the same environment for decades, were still there.

Standing.

So a new solution appeared.

Once again.

New poles were announced, this time made with different, more resistant materials. A new attempt to correct what had already been corrected.

And one cannot help but wonder how a single place can undergo so many transformations without ever reaching a stable result.

Because it is not just about building.

It is about maintaining coherence in what is built.

Sometimes, the problem is not the lack of intervention, but the accumulation of interventions that never fully align with each other.

And in that process, what was meant to improve a space ends up creating a cycle where every solution seems to require another solution afterward.

> What is built to improve, sometimes ends up explaining why what existed before worked better.

The absurd is not in repairing.

It is in repairing without preserving the balance of what already existed.

---

This is the end of this eighteenth chronicle. Thank you for reading, and I look forward to your comments. The images are from Pixabay and I used Google Translate for the English version.
